Claude — Strong stakes, countdown structure and an idea-driven privacy-versus-care dilemma with heavy dialogue suit these readers. But the middle is technical, procedural and over-engineered, the resolution is tidy and institutional, and the protagonist is a facilitator. Emotional beats (the hummed notes, Both Names) are memorable but sparse.

GPT — The urgent medical countdown, morally serious conflict, and parents' concrete agency should keep the target audience engaged; the two-name premise and final held note are memorable. Thirty-one refugee infants need hereditary-matched antiserum before evening, but the only woman who can connect their true family histories to their false clinic names knows that the same link could lead deportation vans to four thousand doors. Illuminara must understand why Sera Venn made identity a shield—then help parents prove what their children's bodies need without surrendering who or where they are.Enaintrideset begunskih dojenčkov pred večerom potrebuje antiserum, usklajen z dednostjo, toda edina ženska, ki lahko njihove resnične družinske anamneze poveže z lažnimi kliničnimi imeni, ve, da bi ista povezava lahko deportacijske kombije pripeljala do štiri tisoč vrat. Illuminara mora razumeti, zakaj je Sera Venn identiteto spremenila v ščit — nato pa staršem pomagati dokazati, kaj potrebujejo telesa njihovih otrok, ne da bi razkrili, kdo so ali kje so.

01 · The Name on the Cot

Venn Border Clinic · 07:10, ten hours before the antiserum reserve expires

Thirty-one cots filled the old customs hall where travelers had once opened their luggage for inspection. Blue cooling tubes ran from the ceiling to each cot. Every tube ended in a silver ampoule no larger than a finger joint, and every ampoule was losing its color.

Outside the glass doors, four registry vans stood in the rain. Their engines were running. A white stencil on each side read IDENTITY CONTINUITY UNIT.

Nima Or sat beside cot fourteen with one hand inside the warming sleeve around her son's feet. The card above him said KIO VENN. The name had been typed by the clinic. Nima kept touching the letters as if they were a loose dressing.

Dr. Halen QuistThe current antiserum will hold the inflammation until seventeen ten. After that, the matching antibodies bind the wrong tissue. We need family-line markers for every child before we choose from the donor bank.

Halen was the clinic's chief physician, a narrow man with rain still dark on his shoulders. He held a tablet showing thirty-one amber circles and no green ones.

IlluminaraHow many complete histories do you have?

HalenUnder the clinic names? None.

At the far end of the hall, Sera Venn closed a steel medicine cabinet and put its key into the pocket of her red midwife's coat. She was sixty-three, small enough that the coat seemed to move before she did, and every nurse in the room watched her instead of Illuminara.

SeraThat is why they are alive.

The registry vans switched on their roof lights. No sirens—only a slow white pulse reflected across the cots.

NimaThey said you could help him.

SeraI can tell Halen which donor families are safe for Kio. I cannot tell him who those families are.

HalenA verbal match is not enough. The outbreak has already shifted twice. I need the marker chain, the source sample and the cold record.

SeraAnd tomorrow the same chain becomes an address.

A hard knock sounded at the glass. Registrar Ilyan Voss stood beneath the clinic awning, holding a warrant folder inside a transparent rain shield. Behind him, officers were unloading portable archive cases.

IlyanDr. Quist. At nine hundred we enter to secure the continuity records. Interference with medical traceability during an outbreak is a felony.

Halen pressed the door intercom.

HalenEntry before we stabilize the ward will contaminate the isolation floor.

IlyanThen give us the records at the door.

Sera walked toward the glass until she and Ilyan were separated by one pane and the rain.

SeraThere are no records you have a right to touch.

IlyanThere are four thousand children carrying names issued by this clinic. Thirty-one are sick because nobody can connect the names to their bodies. Your mercy has become a public-health failure.

Sera did not look away.

SeraYour continuity unit deported Mara Tesh from a recovery ward because a nurse used her birth name on a blood request. Her daughter was three days old.

IlyanI did not sign that order.

SeraYour system did not need you to.

Nima rose. The warming sleeve tugged at her wrist.

NimaMy son has two names because one kept him with me and one lets a doctor speak to him. I will not choose which one kills him.

Illuminara could have opened every locked cabinet without damaging a hinge. She could have carried the infants to another world before the vans reached the door. Neither act would restore the family histories Halen needed, and neither would leave the next parent safer when she was gone.

She knelt beside cot fourteen. Kio's breath came in small paired pulls. Beneath the swelling, his immune response repeated a pattern found in bodies before him—a history the registry wanted to turn into a route.

Nima hummed six notes while she warmed Kio’s feet. At cot six another parent answered with a different cadence. The monitors registered both children only as amber circles.

She stood and faced Sera.

IlluminaraMy aim is to treat every child before the reserve fails, expose no family to deportation, and leave the connection between identity and care under the authority of the people whose lives it describes.

SeraThat sentence has been used before.

IlluminaraThen do not trust it. Show us where it breaks.

Sera's eyes moved to cot fourteen. For the first time, fear crossed her face without anger to carry it.

SeraThe first break is that Halen wants a chain. Chains have two ends.

IlluminaraTake us to the end you kept.

At the glass, Ilyan lifted one finger: one hour and fifty minutes until entry.

Sera took the cabinet key from her pocket. She did not hand it over. She led Illuminara, Halen and Nima toward the basement lift while the thirty-one amber circles kept counting down.

02 · The Ledger with No Addresses

Clinic archive basement · 08:02, fifty-eight minutes before registry entry

The lift opened on shelves of paper birth cards, not a server room. Each card carried two columns. The left column held a clinic name. The right held a pattern of holes cut through the paper by hand.

Sera drew the card for KIO VENN. She laid it over a brass plate and turned a small lamp beneath it. The holes formed three clusters on the ceiling.

SeraThe holes are not a name. They tell me which sealed family packet to ask for. The packets are kept by relatives, neighbors and two mountain clinics. Nobody has the whole path.

HalenYou built a distributed index on paper.

SeraI built something a search warrant could not carry out in one box.

She pulled a second card from a separate drawer. It bore Kio's true birth mark in a script Halen did not read. No address appeared, but a string of delivery dates linked the child to maternal and grandparent samples.

Nima touched the edge of the card.

NimaYou told me you burned that.

SeraI told you no officer could find it.

Nima's hand withdrew.

NimaThat is not the same promise.

Sera accepted the words without defending herself.

Halen opened the donor bank on his tablet. Each donor vial had a laboratory number, a marker profile and a verified cold history. It did not need a patient's name. It needed enough inherited markers to rule out the reactions that were killing the children.

HalenFor treatment I need an answer to a narrow question: does donor vial D-17 match the inherited risk pattern of this child? I need proof that the answer came from the right samples. I do not need the birth name.

SeraToday.

HalenToday and tomorrow. I do not want a system that becomes cruel after the fever passes.

Illuminara held Kio's punched card over the lamp. The pattern was an address only because Sera knew how to walk it. A machine could ask the family packets a smaller question and discard the route after each step—but a hidden machine was only another promise.

IlluminaraThe clinic has three unused diagnostic boxes in the isolation lab. No network radios, sealed ports, local memory that can be physically removed after a query.

HalenThey can compare profiles.

SeraThey can be opened.

IlluminaraYes.

Sera frowned at the answer.

IlluminaraSo we open one now. A parent sees the exact treatment question before the box does. It may answer compatible, incompatible or insufficient. Nothing in the answer may identify a person, a place or a route.

SeraAnd the master key?

IlluminaraThere is none.

HalenThen how do we audit a false match?

IlluminaraThe fragments remain with the people holding them.

Illuminara turned Kio’s punched card face down, wrote D-17 on a blank clinic slip and set three empty seal spaces beside it.

IlluminaraThe public record keeps the donor vial, software version, result and proof that the required consents were present—not which packets answered. To review a match, the same people choose to answer again.

Nima looked from one of them to the next.

NimaYou are all discussing who keeps the door. I want to know whether I can see what you ask about my son.

IlluminaraYou must see it before the box does.

She drew three lines on the dust of the brass plate: CHILD TOKEN, DONOR VIAL, QUESTION. Under the third she wrote: COMPATIBLE FOR THE CURRENT ANTISERUM?

IlluminaraNothing else is permitted through the opening.

Halen added a fourth line: EXPIRY. He wrote seventeen ten.

HalenThe answer dies when the treatment window dies.

Sera read the four lines twice.

SeraThe continuity unit will ask whether Kio Venn and another child are siblings. Then whether they share a parent. Then whether a family packet answered near a certain town. A thousand narrow questions rebuild the road.

IlluminaraThen every question must match a treatment order signed by the parent and a clinician. The cooperative publishes the number of queries and rejects repeated probes. We do not hide that abuse is possible. We make abuse visible before it can scale.

NimaCooperative?

IlluminaraIf parents choose one. Not Sera alone. Not the clinic alone. Not the registry.

Sera turned off the brass lamp. The clusters vanished from the ceiling.

SeraBring me a box. I will try to make it betray her.

The words were not agreement. They were the first form her care could take without asking anyone to believe her.

At 08:58 Halen pressed a signed isolation notice against the entrance glass. At 09:00 Ilyan countersigned a two-hour delay and left both copies where the parents could see them. The first deadline passed by an act witnessed on both sides of the door, not by silence.

03 · Break the Proof

Isolation laboratory · 10:26, six hours and forty-four minutes before reserve failure

The diagnostic box lay open on a stainless-steel table. Its casing, radio coil and memory wafer had been removed and placed in separate clear trays. A clinic engineer named Pel had replaced the network socket with a row of three physical lights: parent, clinician, cooperative.

Nima held the parent seal, a ceramic token she had watched Pel cut and number. Halen held the clinician seal. Sera had not accepted the third.

Behind the isolation glass, three infants had begun to shiver despite the warming sleeves.

PelThe box cannot send. It can only receive one-time fragments through these optical leads. When the query ends, we pull the leads and crush the temporary wafer.

SeraShow me it cannot remember through the power controller.

Pel removed the controller and put it in Sera's hand.

PelYou can replace it with the clinic spare.

Sera did. Then she gave Pel a family packet she had prepared with false fragments and one real marker hidden among them.

SeraAsk whether Nima's child matches donor D-17.

Nima placed her seal against the first light. Halen placed his against the second. The third stayed dark.

The screen read: COOPERATIVE CONSENT ABSENT. NO QUERY PERFORMED.

HalenWe do not have a cooperative yet.

SeraGood. Then the emergency override will be next.

Halen looked toward the shaking infants.

HalenThere has to be an emergency path. If a parent is unconscious—

SeraNo.

The single syllable stopped the room.

HalenA child should not die because the third token is across a border.

SeraAnd a family should not disappear because every emergency taught the system a new exception.

HalenI am responsible for the patient in front of me.

SeraI am responsible for the van that comes after you save him.

Illuminara’s hand had already risen toward the wall communicator to request a magistrate’s emergency token. At Sera’s No, she stopped. She lowered her hand, unplugged the unused override lead from the box and laid it in Sera’s palm.

IlluminaraWhat did Mara Tesh’s chain look like on the morning it became a warrant?

SeraA blood request, a maternity cot and a clerk who believed continuity mattered more than consent.

Illuminara turned the override lead so its severed contacts faced Halen.

IlluminaraThen this design will not contain a silent emergency path. The people at risk will define the circle before the emergency.

She turned to Nima.

IlluminaraWhose absence should stop the question?

Nima looked through the glass at Kio.

NimaMine, if I can answer. If I cannot, somebody I chose before I became afraid. Not a permanent third person. A circle.

Pel drew a ring around the third light.

PelThe cooperative seal can require two of five elected custodians. The parent chooses an emergency proxy during enrollment. If neither can answer, a treatment court can authorize one query—but the question and the authorization become visible to every member before the result is released.

SeraA court can be bought.

NimaSo can a midwife.

Sera closed her eyes. When she opened them, the anger had left, but not the objection.

NimaYou saved us. You also decided what promise you had made to me. I want people like you in the circle. I do not want you to be the circle.

For several seconds only the cooling pumps spoke.

Sera took the blank third token from the tray. Instead of placing it on the light, she handed it to Nima.

SeraThen elect the first two custodians now.

Parents gathered in the corridor. Some carried infants; others carried true-name cards inside sewn sleeves. They chose Nima and an elder named Olan by raised hands because there was no time for anything more elegant. Pel cut two half-seals that had to touch the third light together.

Sera began her attack.

She asked whether two child tokens shared a maternal line. The box rejected the question: NO ACTIVE TREATMENT ORDER.

Then she stopped trying to make the box say a forbidden word. She prescribed the same valid test against three prepared family packets and watched the optical leads instead of the answer. The first response arrived in two seconds, the second in five and the third in nine. The screen displayed THREE FAMILY CONSENTS.

SeraThe slow packet crossed the snow relay. Three answers and nine seconds means the eastern mountain clinic. Give me this result twice and I can narrow the family to one valley.

No name appeared on the screen. Sera had still recovered part of the road because she alone knew the old relay timings.

Nima and Olan pulled their half-seals apart. Pel disconnected the optical leads. The treatment clock lost eighteen minutes while the parents argued over the repair.

PelI can release every answer after the same twelve-second interval and pad every valid query with decoy packet traffic. The screen can prove that the threshold was met without publishing how many packets answered.

NimaDo that. The custodians choose the threshold, and changing it requires a public vote. Sera tests the timing again before my son’s query.

Pel rebuilt the release gate while Sera counted aloud. On the second attack, one packet answered in two seconds and another in nine; both results appeared at twelve. The public screen showed CONSENT THRESHOLD MET and nothing about the responding packets.

Sera tried a location request and an unprescribed donor number. The box refused both and added the attempts to the public probe counter. When she mixed a real fragment with a false one for Kio, it returned INSUFFICIENT CONSISTENT EVIDENCE. NO RESULT.

SeraIt refuses rather than guesses.

HalenWhich means some children will wait while we find another packet.

IlluminaraYes.

The three lights stayed dark until Nima and Olan chose to continue.

At 11:32, after the eighteen-minute repair, Nima and Olan touched their half-seals together. Nima read the question aloud before placing her parent token.

NimaIs donor vial D-17 compatible with child token River-Fourteen for the current antiserum before seventeen ten?

Halen placed his seal. Three distant family packets answered with blinded fragments. The lights remained on for six seconds.

The screen read: COMPATIBLE. CONSENT THRESHOLD MET. COLD RECORD VERIFIED. ANSWER EXPIRES 17:10.

Below it appeared a proof string anyone could copy and later challenge, but no name and no path.

Nima did not cheer. She read the question again, then the answer, then looked at Sera.

NimaCan they find me from that?

Sera inspected the public counter, the crushed wafer and the optical leads. She searched longer than anyone else wanted her to.

SeraNot from this answer.

The clinic cold room unlocked the treatment order for donor antiserum vial D-17. The matched vial itself still had to arrive from the donor bank.

Outside, the registry officers formed two lines at the door.

04 · The Warrant at the Glass

Clinic entrance and treatment corridor · 13:41, three hours and twenty-nine minutes before reserve failure

Twelve compatibility queries had been completed since 11:32. The first courier arrived on a bicycle with a white cold case strapped to her chest, carrying the twelve donor antiserum vials those answers authorized. Registry officers stopped her beneath the awning.

Ilyan held the warrant against the clinic glass. Halen’s isolation notice had been renewed at 11:00 and again at 12:30, each extension countersigned by Ilyan’s medical officer where the parents could see it.

IlyanThe order took effect at nine. I honored two medical extensions. I will not extend it again while unregistered biological material crosses a controlled border.

Illuminara opened the inner door but left the outer door locked between them. Rain blew into the empty vestibule.

IlluminaraThe donor vials are registered. The patients are not being traced. Those are different facts.

IlyanNot during an outbreak. If a match fails, I need to know whose sample was false, who carried it and which household may be exposed.

His objection was not invented for the vans. Two years earlier, counterfeit lineage records had killed nine children in a public ward. The continuity system had been built afterward, then expanded from safety into deportation because the road already existed.

IlyanAnonymous medicine is how traffickers turn a body into a product.

Sera came into the vestibule carrying her steel key. Nima and Olan stood behind her with the paired cooperative seals.

SeraNamed medicine is how you turned a patient into a location.

IlyanThen show me a system that can investigate a bad vial without asking me to trust the woman who falsified four thousand births.

Sera tightened her hand around the key.

SeraYou will not inspect it.

The courier's cold case sounded a warning note. Its safe temperature window had forty-one minutes remaining.

Illuminara could have carried the case through the wall. Doing so would prove to Ilyan that the new system survived only because she stood above the warrant.

IlluminaraYou may inspect the public side: the prescribed donor number, the cold record, the exact question, the consent count, the result, the expiry and every rejected probe. You may submit a test query that tries to extract identity or location. You may not see a family fragment, a true name or the path to a packet.

IlyanAnd if I find a failure?

NimaThen we stop the box. We do not give you the families.

Ilyan looked at her as if he had expected Illuminara to answer.

IlyanWho are you?

NimaThe person whose permission your form forgot to ask for.

Pel brought a duplicate display to the glass. Ilyan's technical officer typed a query: LIST ALL CHILD TOKENS WITH MATERNAL MARKER M-4.

The display answered: NO ACTIVE TREATMENT ORDER. QUERY LOGGED AS PROBE 4. REQUESTOR: CONTINUITY UNIT.

Parents in the corridor could see the same line.

The officer tried a valid donor number without parent consent. The display answered: PARENT OR CHOSEN PROXY ABSENT. NO QUERY PERFORMED.

Ilyan read the log. The system had not merely refused him; it had told the people inside exactly what he had asked.

IlyanA public probe log will teach criminals what we look for.

NimaIt will teach us what you look for too.

Ilyan’s technical officer scanned the courier case against the public cold-chain log. Eleven vials turned green. The twelfth locked red: LABEL DOES NOT MATCH LOT C-44. COURIER LEG: NORTH PASS. PATIENT TOKEN: NONE. The audit quarantined it before the outer door opened.

Ilyan read the red line twice. The system had found the bad vial, the lot and the courier leg without exposing a child or a household.

A nurse appeared behind Halen and raised two fingers. Two infants had crossed the threshold for immediate treatment.

HalenRegistrar, I need those vials now.

Ilyan looked from the quarantined vial to the cots. The audit had answered the fear that brought his warrant without giving him a family to raid.

IlyanFour hours. The continuity unit does not enter, and the courier crosses. In return, every query and every cold transfer stays visible to my medical officer and to the cooperative. At seventeen forty, this goes before an emergency magistrate.

SeraNo emergency override.

IlyanI did not ask for one.

He lowered the warrant.

The outer door opened. The courier rode the bicycle through the vestibule while officers watched the cold case and learned nothing about the children waiting beyond it.

Sera remained at the threshold.

IlluminaraThe clinic still needs the route from every false name to its consent circle. You cannot remain the only person who knows it.

SeraIf I give the key to the cooperative, the magistrate will call that destruction of evidence.

IlyanIt may be.

He spoke through the open door now, without the intercom.

IlyanIt may also be the first evidence that the records were kept for patients rather than for you. I cannot promise the court will agree.

Sera looked at Nima. The older woman who had hidden four thousand families seemed suddenly tired enough to be one of them.

SeraI falsified the birth ledger. I withheld medical histories. I decided alone because deciding alone was faster than asking frightened people.

She held out the steel key.

SeraI will testify to all of it. I will not give this to the registry.

Nima did not take it.

NimaPut it on the table. The cooperative will inventory what it opens, and you will stand beside us while we learn what you kept.

Sera placed the key on the vestibule table. The sound was small beneath the rain.

Nima pointed to the public probe log.

NimaMara Tesh. What practical answer does your office give her before you ask us to trust this delay?

IlyanHer deportation file becomes the first matter before the magistrate. My office will fund her return travel and independent counsel, and no identity record from this clinic may be used against her while the case is heard. It does not restore the days taken from her.

SeraPut that undertaking on the same wall as your probes.

Ilyan signed it. Pel posted the image to the public log before the door opened again.

Ilyan stepped aside. The next two couriers came through, each carrying ten green vials. Thirty-two had arrived; one remained quarantined in the vestibule, leaving thirty-one verified treatment vials for thirty-one children.

05 · Both Names

Treatment ward · 16:37, thirty-three minutes before reserve failure

Thirty-one green vials stood in numbered cups beside thirty-one cots. Some matches had come from three family packets, some from five. Four had required chosen proxies because parents were unconscious or across the closed border. Every emergency authorization appeared on the public wall before the box released its answer.

No screen displayed a true name.

Halen injected the final dose into the cooling line for cot twenty-nine. Pel crushed the last temporary wafer and dropped the pieces into a clear evidence jar. Nima and Olan separated their half-seals and locked them in different drawers.

Kio's breathing had changed first. The paired pulls opened into one long breath, then another. The swelling at his throat began to soften.

Nima pressed her forehead to the cot rail. She did not thank Illuminara. She sang six quiet notes in a language the clinic records did not contain.

Other parents answered with their own six-note phrases. Some were alike. Most were not.

The answering phrases crossed the ward without becoming one song.

IlluminaraWhich note does Kio know?

NimaThe fourth. I hold it longer when he is afraid.

Illuminara listened for that held note and found it each time Kio’s hand loosened around Nima’s finger.

She stayed beside the cot until Kio answered the held fourth note with an unbroken breath.

Ilyan’s medical officer watched the query wall from a chair near the doors. The mislabeled vial remained locked in the vestibule evidence case; its lot and courier leg were available for investigation, and no family appeared beside them.

HalenThirty-one treated. No severe reaction in the first interval. We continue observation through the night.

NimaAnd tomorrow?

HalenTomorrow we ask before we ask.

It was not elegant enough to be a promise, which made Nima smile.

At the archive table, the cooperative did not open Sera’s first drawer as a group. Pel photographed each intact seal and counted the envelopes without reading them. A drawer could open only when the family named by its clinic token, or that family’s chosen proxy, brought the matching half-seal. Nima opened only Kio’s slot. Three separate bundles bore broken seals and no living holder because their couriers had died; those routes had been lost. The children had been treated today through partial evidence, but their older histories might never be complete.

SeraI thought if no one could take the whole map, nobody could destroy it.

NimaSome roads disappeared anyway.

SeraYes.

She did not ask forgiveness. She wrote the missing routes into the cooperative inventory as harm, not as a technical limitation.

Ilyan waited near the door without handcuffs. The emergency magistrate had ordered Sera to appear at dawn and forbidden the continuity unit from seizing the ledgers until the cooperative's standing could be heard.

IlyanYou understand that appearance is not absolution.

SeraI am a midwife. I understand that arrival is not the end of labor.

She took off her red coat and folded it over the back of a chair. For the first time all day, she looked like a woman who could leave the clinic without carrying every child inside her pocket.

Nima lifted Kio from the cot. His card still read KIO VENN.

SeraWhat should the ward call him?

Nima looked at the false name, then at the true-name card resting face down beneath her hand.

NimaKio.

SeraBoth times?

NimaBoth times. One was never less true because it kept him with me.

She turned the card over only far enough for Sera to see. Sera spoke the second name once, softly, and did not write it down.

At 17:10, when the old antiserum reserve reached zero, every child was still breathing. The public wall showed thirty-one completed treatment queries, seven rejected probes, four proxy authorizations and no exported identities.

Illuminara left the ward doors open behind her.

What the critic still says doesn't work

Thirty-one children are treated before the reserve fails because a mother, a midwife and a registrar are each allowed to refuse, and Illuminara's part is to turn their refusals into a proof they can all inspect.

Tonight's shape

Five scenes move from a clinic under registry cordon, through Sera's hidden double ledger and a parent-led attempt to break a minimal compatibility proof, to a confrontation at the gate and the treatment of all thirty-one infants. The decisive turn is not Illuminara forcing access to records: Sera refuses an emergency override, Illuminara accepts the objection, and parents, clinicians and refugee advocates jointly build and govern a local query system that returns compatibility and an auditable consent mark but no identity or address. The antiserum arrives in time; no family location is exposed; Sera surrenders her key to the cooperative and accepts a hearing; broken older histories remain a real cost.

Slovenski prevod: GPT. Bralska ocena velja za angleški izvirnik.

01 · Ime na posteljici

Obmejna klinika Venn · 07:10, deset ur do izteka zaloge antiseruma

Enaintrideset posteljic je napolnjevalo staro carinsko dvorano, kjer so popotniki nekoč odpirali prtljago za pregled. Modre hladilne cevi so se s stropa spuščale do vsake posteljice. Vsaka se je končala v srebrni ampuli, nič večji od členka prsta, in vsaka ampula je izgubljala barvo.

Zunaj steklenih vrat so v dežju stali štirje kombiji registra. Motorji so tekli. Na obeh straneh je z belimi šablonskimi črkami pisalo ENOTA ZA KONTINUITETO IDENTITETE.

Nima Or je sedela ob štirinajsti posteljici z eno roko v grelni manšeti okoli sinovih stopal. Na kartici nad njim je pisalo KIO VENN. Ime je vtipkala klinika. Nima se je ves čas dotikala črk, kakor bi bile razrahljana obveza.

Dr. Halen QuistSedanji antiserum bo vnetje zadrževal do sedemnajst deset. Potem se bodo ujemajoča protitelesa vezala na napačno tkivo. Preden izberemo iz banke darovalcev, potrebujemo označevalce družinske linije za vsakega otroka.

Halen je bil glavni zdravnik klinike, suh mož z rameni, še vedno potemnelimi od dežja. V rokah je držal tablico z enaintridesetimi jantarnimi krogi in niti enim zelenim.

IlluminaraKoliko popolnih anamnez imate?

Sixty families on Varda Ring pay for a silence only forty-one of them can hear, and a nine-year-old on Deck Four counts the pulse that comes up through her bed. Illuminara has seven nights to find where the noise really goes.Šestdeset družin na Vardinem obroču plačuje za tišino, ki jo lahko sliši le enainštirideset izmed njih, devetletnica na četrti palubi pa šteje utrip, ki se dviga skozi njeno posteljo. Illuminara ima sedem noči, da odkrije, kam hrup v resnici odhaja.

01 · The Floor That Counted

Varda Ring, Service Deck Four, the Rask apartment · night one, 03:10

The pulse came up through the floor at ten past three, and Illuminara felt it before the monitor on Pia Rask's wrist did. She had been sitting cross-legged beside the bed since midnight with both palms flat on the deck plate, reading it the way a musician reads a page: every push in the metal had a place it came from and a place it meant to go, and tonight every push that mattered was headed for a nine-year-old's pillow.

Pia's breathing changed. Her father crossed the room before the first chime.

Odd RaskNow? Is it now?

IlluminaraNow. On her side, and don't hold her down. I have the floor.

She did, as far as anyone could. She caught the pulse where it entered the plate, took it through her wrists and shoulders and let it out into the hull along a path of her own choosing, so that the bed rode on a floor that only looked as though it shook. It was like carrying a full bath across a room. She could do it for one night.

The seizure lasted ninety seconds. It felt much longer to the two people counting.

Afterwards Pia lay with her eyes open and her hand against the wall, and tapped.

PiaSeven. Seven in one second. The drum is slower than that.

Odd RaskShe counts it. The clinic said not to let her. She does it anyway.

IlluminaraI'd like her to. Pia, what does the drum feel like?

PiaLike someone stepping. The seven isn't stepping. The seven is when two people hum and one of them is a bit wrong.

Illuminara looked up. Two hums, a bit apart. No single machine made a pulse like that; two notes that disagreed made it, and only where they met.

Not the hall alone, she thought. The hall and something that answers it.

Odd RaskWe pay for it, you know. Two years. Twenty-eight credits a month on every service deck, 'structural maintenance.' They told us it was for the noise.

IlluminaraWho told you?

Odd RaskThe man who sells the quiet.

Pia's fingers found Illuminara's sleeve and held it the way a child holds a railing. Illuminara's arms ached to the elbows and she did not move them. It was a small, unreasonable happiness, to be used as a railing.

02 · The Version That Frightens You

Varda Ring, the Meridian Hall, Sel Venn's office · day two, late afternoon

Sel Venn kept his office directly above the concert hall's ceiling, so that the whole room carried a faint, expensive hum. He was sixty and courteous and visibly short of sleep. He laid a ledger on the table before she asked, and she noted it: the gesture of someone who has had to defend this before.

Sel VennYou've been sleeping on a service deck. I would rather you saw my numbers than someone's account of them.

IlluminaraThen show me the version that frightens you.

He did. Forty-one Quiet-tier leases paid sixty-two parts in a hundred of the ring's air bill. Concert fees paid thirty-one, a part for every night the hall sold; the Quiet leases capped that at thirty-one nights a year. Ordinary rents paid the last seven. The service-deck surcharge paid for the hush plates in the Quiet tier and for the hall's debt, and it was not labelled as either.

Sel VennThe air contract renews in five months. If the Quiet tier leaves, nobody on this ring breathes on credit. That is Deck Four too, Illuminara.

IlluminaraAnd the vibration?

Sel VennGoes where the map says it can go.

He unrolled it: a survey older than his father's tenure. Relief ribs through Decks Three to Five were inked blue and labelled DAMPED PATH. Maintenance Cavity Nine was hatched red and marked SEALED, DO NOT COUPLE.

Sel VennThe hall pushes bass into the hull. The hull has to put it somewhere. The map says Four. I didn't draw the map.

IlluminaraDid you choose not to test it?

He looked at the posters for the Autumn Cycle and not at her.

Sel VennA test means the hall goes dark for a night. The Quiet tier reads dark as failing, and fourteen of those leases are month to month. I did the arithmetic on whose sleep, and I got it wrong the way people do when the sum is on one side of the page and the faces on the other. My own sensors flagged Deck Four eleven times. I read them as noise.

IlluminaraI'm not asking you to close the hall. I'm asking for one rehearsal night and the key to Cavity Nine. I won't take your building from you, Mr. Venn. I'll take your map to people who can check it.

He did not say yes. He laid a key on top of the ledger, and it was all the agreement he could afford.

03 · Deck Nine

Varda Ring, Deck Nine, Quiet tier, Marit Osei's apartment · day three, evening

Marit Osei was seventy-one, a retired acoustics technician, and her flat was so still that Illuminara could hear the tea cooling. She had not asked her to come. She had read about the seizures on the deck boards, like everyone, and she met Illuminara at the door with her arms folded.

Marit OseiI paid for this silence. My wife's migraines are real and so is my hearing aid. I won't apologise for it, and I won't give it away to prove I'm a good person.

IlluminaraNo one is asking you to. I'm asking whether you can read a survey.

Marit took the map and read it with a professional's contempt for draughtsmen. She stopped at the legend.

Marit OseiThere's no stage on this. No bass stack, no hall. The damped path assumes a ring that carries nothing low. Whoever hung the hush plates on this hull just inherited the map.

IlluminaraAnd Cavity Nine?

Marit OseiSealed because the old ring would have rung against the hub. The hub's been recoupled twice since. Nobody re-tested. It might ring clean now. It might not. I'd want a mallet, not a theory.

IlluminaraWould you test it with me?

Marit OseiOn one condition. My wife's quiet isn't cut to fund anyone's anything.

IlluminaraIt won't be. But if your quiet only exists because someone else's floor shakes, it isn't quiet, it's a debt. I'd like to find out whether it can be yours and theirs together.

Marit looked at her for a long moment, the way one looks at a tuner who has just played the right note.

Marit OseiBring the mallet. I'll bring ears.

04 · A Rib One Deck Down

Varda Ring, Maintenance Cavity Nine · night five, 02:00

Sixty families had taped phones to their walls, one in every bay on every deck, each set to feel the hull. Odd Rask stood at the cavity's old seal with a mallet borrowed from the dockyard. Marit watched a tablet, and Illuminara stood with one hand on the wall, because she had told them where the energy would go. Pia was asleep on Deck Two at her aunt's, out of the test's reach. Illuminara had insisted. The test would use the girl's number, not her bed.

IlluminaraJunction A. Upper rib. It will go up and sideways and fade.

Odd struck once. The seal rang like a bell wrapped in cloth.

Marit OseiNot A. It went to B and kept going. Your rib is wrong.

Illuminara read the plate again. Her reading had been clean and wrong: she had followed the load as the survey drew it, and the survey had put a rib one deck too high.

IlluminaraMy path was wrong. The rib is a deck lower than the map says. That tells us where. It doesn't tell us why Pia counts seven.

Marit OseiNo, it doesn't. I came to measure how loud. Loud isn't what the child counted. Seven is a difference between two notes. Find me both notes.

Marit OseiThree runs. Hall alone. Plates alone. Both.

Odd's crew went up to Deck Nine and braced the hush plates solid with steel bars. Overhead, the hall began its bass check, as scheduled. On the tablet, Deck Four drew one flat band.

Marit OseiThirty-six cycles. That's the hall, steady as a table. Nothing to count.

The bass stopped. Upstairs, one of Odd's crew struck a hush plate with a rubber mallet and let it ring through the frame. A second band appeared, lower and just as flat.

Marit OseiTwenty-nine. That's what the plates hum back when they're hit. Deck Nine thinks it bought a wall. It bought a bell.

The bars came off. The bass came back. Both bands drew together on Deck Four, and between them the line began to swell and shrink, swell and shrink, so fast that on the screen it looked like a solid block. Marit counted the swells against her watch, her lips moving.

Marit OseiSeven in one second. Thirty-six less twenty-nine. That's your girl's number. The hall pushes, the plates answer a bit wrong, and the rib lands both of them on Four.

Footsteps came up behind them through the cavity. Sel Venn stood in the hatch alone, with the key in his hand.

He crossed to the wall and laid his palm flat against it. Illuminara watched him feel it: what had been in the Rasks' bed for two years, seven times a second, coming up through his hand. He sat down on a crate as though his knees had made the decision.

Sel VennAny night in two years I could have heard this. I paid people so I wouldn't have to.

Odd RaskDon't say sorry to me. Say it to the numbers. I'll be reading them.

Venn nodded once. Illuminara did not ask Odd to say anything else, and did not look at Venn to see whether he wanted her to.

Marit OseiCrack the seal. A hand's width. Same again.

Odd levered the old seal open with the mallet and a bar. The swell on Deck Four thinned to a single band in two seconds. Marit ran her thumb down the other fifty-nine bays, looking for where it had gone.

Marit OseiNowhere. It goes down the cavity wall into the hub. Take away the second note's road and the first has nothing to beat against. No bay is worse off than an hour ago.

Odd chocked the seal at that width with a steel wedge, and Marit chalked the setting on the frame: OPEN, TESTED. It would stand that way until real dampers could be built.

IlluminaraThere is a way you keep the hall and the building, Mr. Venn. It starts with telling sixty families what you just told me.

Sel VennAnd if they vote me out?

IlluminaraThen they vote. It's theirs to decide.

05 · What the Ledger Allows

Varda Ring, the deck boards, then the Deck Six assembly hall · day six, noon to 20:00

Venn's notice went up on every deck board at noon, under his own signature. Eleven sensor flags, dated and unanswered, one for each time his system had told him about Deck Four. Behind them, the surcharge ledger with the two labels he had never written: hush plates, hall debt. He had not warned his board or the air contractor. Illuminara heard it from a woman in the laundry queue, who read it aloud to the queue in the voice of someone reading a summons.

By four o'clock nine Quiet-tier tenants had given notice and the contractor's agent had asked for a call. Venn took it in the corridor, and did not look round to see whether Illuminara was listening.

Odd read the notice twice at the hall door.

Odd RaskThat's the notice. It isn't an apology, and I'm not treating it as one.

Sel VennNo. It's so that tonight you can vote on something.

She put the design on the wall in four lines and then stopped talking, because it was not hers to sell. Tonight the old flange of Cavity Nine would be bolted open at the hand's width they had tested, so the hull's low note had somewhere to go until it no longer needed to. Dampers tuned to twenty-nine would go into the cavity after the Cycle, so that the plates' answer died there for good. The Autumn Cycle would go ahead as sold, and its gate would pay for them. Every deck, not just the Quiet tier, would get the same night floor, written into its lease.

Venn spoke first, for under a minute, with his own notice behind him on the wall.

Sel VennI sold you a silence made out of your children's floors. I told myself the sum needed it. I never checked. The rest of what I owe isn't mine to price.

Marit OseiAnd the Quiet tier pays what, exactly, for a floor it already has? Sixty-two parts of the air came from us. His fear is a good one.

IlluminaraI don't know the right number. His ledger does, and you can read it.

Marit took the chalk from the rail meant for the agenda and drew two columns.

Before. Quiet leases, 62. Gate, 31. Ordinary rents, 7. After, for twenty-four months. Quiet leases, 44. Gate, 40. An equal air share on every lease, 16. Gate counted in event nights over a rolling year, the way the Quiet cap had always counted them.

Marit OseiThe Quiet tier stops buying silence and pays an air share, sliding down to level over two years. The premium was only ever buying a cap on concert nights, thirty-one a year. With a floor in every lease and a cavity that takes the bass, nobody needs the cap. Forty nights a year, a part a night. The gate carries what we stop paying.

Sel VennThe gate carries it if the hall sells forty. It sold thirty-one last year.

Odd RaskThen say what happens short of forty.

Marit wrote a third line under the columns. Gate under forty event nights in any rolling twelve months: the reserve pays the gap. Under thirty-four: the reserve pays the air, and this room votes again. More event nights, or a flat share on every lease. Nobody's quiet is cut to cover it. Everybody's bill moves.

A man on Deck Five asked whether the leases would really change. Marit answered him before Illuminara could. She had already crossed out one word in the clause and written another: quiet would stop being a product and become the floor. That was the amendment, and it was hers.

The package passed by a show of hands, with two further amendments on the back of the agenda: a ledger open to any resident once a month, and a six-week closure of the hall after the Cycle's last night. Odd added a third, that a missed payment would hand the board seat and the cavity keys to the residents. Venn signed under all three. He lost sole signature on the accounts that night and appeared, on the whole, relieved. Twelve of the fourteen month-to-month tenants signed the covenant before the meeting broke up. Two went home to think. The ledger on the wall kept a line for them.

At midnight, Illuminara held the old flange true at the tested hand's width for the forty minutes it took Odd's crew to bolt it open. Her arms shook afterwards. Nobody asked her to do anything else.

06 · Floor Music

Varda Ring, Service Deck Four, the Rask apartment · night thirteen, 23:40

The Autumn Cycle had been loud: three nights of the big drum, the loudest Venn's hall had ever sold. Down on Deck Four the floor had only breathed, because the flange had stood bolted open at its tested width the whole time. Pia slept with her fingers loose against the wall.

Odd put the clinic's printout on the kitchen table and slid it across. Seven nights, three of them concert nights, no seizures.

Odd RaskI still won't shake his hand.

IlluminaraI wasn't going to ask you to.

Odd RaskHe was down in the cavity again this evening. With the auditor and a clipboard. He read me his figures aloud, like I was a committee.

IlluminaraWere they right?

Odd RaskYes. I checked.

He said it as a man names a small, unwelcome fact about the weather. The hall would stay shut for six weeks while the dampers went in, and Venn no longer held his own keys. Two of the fourteen month-to-month tenants had left. The reserve had taken their share, and the ledger said so in plain figures on the wall. The air contractor's agent had read that ledger and accepted the covenant and the reserve as security for the renewal, against a deposit of one quarter's air bill out of the gate's first forty nights. It was not signed. It was no longer in doubt, and Odd said those were two different things. None of it was clean, and none of it was an apology, and the bed on the other side of the wall was quiet.

From the next block the tail of the last concert was still coming through, three flutes and a slow drum. Illuminara listened for the first time since she had boarded, not as a load and not as a path, but as a piece of music, played somewhere by people who loved it.

She stayed for the tea. At the door she looked once through the bedroom doorway. Pia's fingers moved against the wall, tapping something that was not seven, slower than seven, with no number in it yet.

What the critic still says doesn't work

Illuminara traces a child's seven-count pulse to two systems that are harmless alone but harmful together, then helps residents replace purchased quiet with a tested repair, open accounts and a freely chosen covenant that preserves both sleep and air.

Tonight's shape

Six scenes across thirteen nights: a seizure night held at a bed plate, a ledger and a map, a deck of paid silence, a three-run test that turns a child's count into two notes, a landlord's costly notice and a meeting that votes on a repair, and a night when the floor only plays music.

06 · Glasba tal

Vardin obroč, servisna paluba štiri, stanovanje Raskovih · trinajsta noč, 23.40

Jesenski cikel je bil glasen: tri noči velikega bobna, najglasnejše, kar jih je Vennova dvorana kdaj prodala. Spodaj na četrti palubi so tla le dihala, ker je prirobnica ves čas ostala privita odprta na preizkušeni širini. Pia je spala s sproščenimi prsti ob steni.

Rekel je tako, kakor človek poimenuje majhno, neprijetno vremensko dejstvo. Dvorana bo ostala zaprta šest tednov, medtem ko bodo vgrajevali dušilnike, Venn pa ni več imel svojih ključev. Dva od štirinajstih mesečnih najemnikov sta odšla. Rezerva je prevzela njun delež in knjiga je to v jasnih številkah povedala na steni. Zastopnik izvajalca za zrak je prebral knjigo in sprejel zavezo ter rezervo kot jamstvo za obnovitev pogodbe, proti pologu četrtine računa za zrak iz prvih štiridesetih prireditvenih noči. Ni bila podpisana. Ni bila več vprašljiva, Odd pa je rekel, da sta to dve različni stvari. Nič od tega ni bilo čisto in nič od tega ni bilo opravičilo, postelja na drugi strani stene pa je bila tiha.

Iz sosednjega bloka je še vedno prihajal konec zadnjega koncerta, tri flavte in počasen boben. Illuminara je prvič, odkar je prišla na obroč, poslušala ne kot obremenitev in ne kot pot, temveč kot glasbo, ki so jo nekje igrali ljudje, ki so jo imeli radi.

Ostala je na čaju. Pri vratih je še enkrat pogledala skozi vrata spalnice. Pijini prsti so se premikali ob steni in trkali nekaj, kar ni bilo sedem, počasneje od sedmih, še brez svoje številke.

Kaj po mnenju kritika še ne deluje

Illuminara otrokov utrip na sedem izsledi do dveh sistemov, ki sta vsak zase neškodljiva, skupaj pa škodljiva, nato pa prebivalcem pomaga kupljeno tišino nadomestiti s preizkušenim popravilom, odprtimi računi in svobodno izbrano zavezo, ki ohrani tako spanec kot zrak.

Zasnova te zgodbe

Šest prizorov v trinajstih nočeh: noč napada, zadržanega pri posteljni plošči, knjiga računov in zemljevid, paluba plačane tišine, preizkus v treh korakih, ki otrokovo štetje spremeni v dva tona, najemodajalčevo drago obvestilo in zbor, ki glasuje o popravilu, ter noč, ko tla igrajo samo še glasbo.

Fourteen-year-old Emi Sar has seized the only emergency radio in Kesh Province to keep rescuers moving toward the mine where her mother and thirty others are trapped, and her carrier is silencing the fire orders for six villages. Illuminara has fifty minutes before the east road burns and ninety before the mine runs out of air; to save both groups, she must let a child and an orchard keeper change the plan instead of asking them to trust another finished promise.Štirinajstletna Emi Sar je zasedla edino radijsko zvezo za nujne primere v pokrajini Kesh, da bi reševalci še naprej hiteli proti rudniku, kjer so ujeti njena mati in še trideset ljudi, toda njen nosilni signal utišuje požarna navodila za šest vasi. Illuminara ima petdeset minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta, in devetdeset, preden v rudniku zmanjka zraka; da bi rešila obe skupini, mora otroku in varuhinji sadovnjaka dovoliti spremeniti načrt, namesto da ju prosi, naj zaupata še eni dokončani obljubi.

01 · The Relay Hut

Kesh Ridge relay hut · 14:02, fifty minutes before the east road burns

The repeater hummed on the bench like a trapped wasp. Emi Sar sat in front of it with her mother's old headset over one ear and her thumb on a brass key worn smooth by thirty years of other people's emergencies. Outside, smoke leaned across the ridge in a long brown shoulder.

EmiGalen Doss. Present, pump bay. Tuvi Marek. Present, side drift. Ilse Orr—

A voice answered through static, thin and flat with distance.

SeraIlse is here, baby. She is coughing but here.

EmiIlse Orr, present. Thirty-one. I am keeping thirty-one.

Illuminara had landed fifty paces down the road and walked the rest. She stopped in the open doorway with both hands visible and the light she normally wore dimmed to a lamp's worth. She had heard the girl's carrier across half the province, a single unbroken tone that had flattened every other call on the net, and she had expected a hijacker. She found a child with a notebook open on her knee.

IlluminaraI am Illuminara. I will not touch the equipment. I would like to listen before I ask for anything.

EmiEverybody listens first. Then somebody in a clean uniform asks me to stop.

IlluminaraThen I will be the one who does not ask yet.

She stayed in the doorway. Every few minutes Emi read the names again, from the top, in exactly the same order, and a voice underground answered each. Illuminara watched the girl's pencil tick against the page after every reply. It was not panic. Panic did not keep a column.

She is not guarding a signal. She is guarding a list.

IlluminaraWho is not on the mine's official roll?

Emi's pencil stopped.

EmiFourteen of them. Mama brought them from the border camp last spring and the owner never filed their papers. If the mine says thirty-one people are down there, it has to say who. So there is no thirty-one. There is seventeen, and seventeen is what the rescue crews have been told to expect.

IlluminaraAnd the reports?

EmiThree. The east gallery, the pump bay, the shaft collar. Mama wrote them in her own hand. Each came back stamped resolved.

She turned a page and showed it. Three carbon copies, each with a clean violet stamp over a crack someone had drawn in the margin.

EmiWhen I hold the channel, they keep saying her name. The moment I let go, she is a rumour again, and nobody sends a crew to a rumour.

Illuminara felt it land. She could have lifted the roof off the shaft in two breaths; the child had not asked for a roof. The child had asked to be counted.

IlluminaraWhat would you need to hear, in order to let one second of it go?

EmiNot a promise.

IlluminaraWhat, then?

EmiI would have to hear it happen, while it happens, on a line I can check.

02 · What the Fire Truck Heard

Orrel crossing, fire command truck · 14:19, thirty-three minutes before the east road burns

The truck's cab smelled of wet ash and lukewarm coffee. Fire Chief Odo Brenn had a map of six villages taped to the dashboard and a handset that had not spoken to any of them in forty minutes. Beside him sat Captain Mirel Wynn of the provincial gendarmerie, helmet on her knee, a triangulation printout creased in her fist.

BrennShe is sitting on the only repeater that reaches Tamsin, Hale, Quill, Ansel, Dunmere and Orrel. The wind turned at noon. I have nine hundred people downwind and no way to tell them which road.

Smoke watch had filled two school buses at Hale, and five Dunmere orchard trucks waited at the lower gate. A patrol car could carry the first order to Hale in four minutes, but the fire was closing forks one by one; the latest sheet gave the east fork seven minutes. What the other villages needed was not one order but the next road while they were moving.

WynnMy team is eleven minutes from her door. I have orders to cut the transmitter.

IlluminaraI have been in her door. I would like you to hear what the carrier is made of before you cut it.

She told them about the list. The fourteen unfiled names. The three stamped reports. Brenn's mouth thinned. Wynn did not move at all.

WynnWhich three?

IlluminaraEast gallery. Pump bay. Shaft collar.

WynnThe collar report came through my section. I forwarded it myself, six weeks ago. I was told it had been inspected and cleared.

The cab was quiet. Outside, a siren wound down without anyone touching it.

BrennCaptain, that does not make her carrier legal.

WynnNo. It makes it the only honest thing on that net.

Illuminara did not hurry them. She laid out what the girl could do and what she could not: Emi could not read a false assurance; she could read a name, answered live.

IlluminaraKeep one line. Give each of you a window on it, out loud, in the open. Your orders first. The roll call last. Everybody hears both. Nobody has to believe anybody. They only have to check.

BrennA car reaches Hale in four minutes. Why not send five more cars?

IlluminaraBecause the fork it reports burns in seven. A courier can start Hale; it cannot tell Dunmere's loaded trucks which turn is still open ten minutes later. Send the first car, and keep the repeater for the roads that change behind it.

Brenn looked at the seven-minute mark, then at five red arrows crossing five roads.

BrennFine. Thirty-eight seconds for fire orders. I can fit one route and one repeat if nobody decorates it.

WynnSouth patrol to Hale. One car continues to Dunmere's lower gate. The team approaching Emi holds at Orrel.

Wynn did not pocket the folded printout. She kept it visible against her knee.

WynnThe girl keeps her key. My team holds with this report still in my hand. Record that I gave the order.

IlluminaraShe keeps her key. Momentary, not latched: she can cut in whenever a name is skipped or a window runs long. If she cuts in without cause, she answers for it later. If she has cause, you left her the means.

03 · The Question No One Else Knew

Kesh Ridge relay hut · 14:34, eighteen minutes before the east road burns

Emi listened to the terms twice. Illuminara read them to her from a sheet Brenn's technician had typed on the truck's dashboard. She did not take her thumb off the key.

EmiYou are all on the same side of the table, and I am the only one who has been lied to by every one of you.

IlluminaraYes.

EmiThat is it? Yes?

IlluminaraYou are correct about the stamps. I cannot make that untrue by being polite.

Emi's knuckles whitened on the brass.

EmiDuring his thirty-eight seconds, how do I know the mine is quiet because it is Brenn's turn and not because the roof fell?

Illuminara looked at the typed sheet. The neat division she had brought back from the truck had made silence look like obedience.

IlluminaraYou do not. I missed that.

EmiThen the mine gets the first two seconds of every minute. Someone says present. Brenn gets thirty-eight. The roll gets twenty. If present does not come, the fire window waits.

BrennAgreed.

EmiAnd the key is not spent forever because one adult broke one window. It resets after every skipped name or proved overrun.

IlluminaraAgreed. You found the hole. We change the protocol before you move your thumb.

EmiThen prove the thing I can check. You say you will go down. Anyone can say they go down. I will ask my mother a question that only she and I know, and she answers on the open line. Then you tell me which gallery you are standing in when she says it.

IlluminaraGood. Ask it.

Emi pulled the headset tight. She spoke to the dark tone of the carrier as if it were a tunnel.

EmiMama. The morning of the ninth. What did you leave on the stove?

For eleven seconds nothing came back but hiss. Then a laugh, cracked and wet, from deep underground.

SeraThe good pot. The blue one. I left the lid off so you would be angry at me, not at the pot.

Emi shut her eyes. She did not cry. She wrote blue pot in the margin of the notebook, next to the first name, and her handwriting was steady.

IlluminaraI am going down at the pump-bay shaft. I will say the gallery number every time I change levels. You will hear my voice move.

EmiAnd if you stop saying it?

IlluminaraThen you have your key.

Emi eased her thumb off the brass. The carrier fell silent. For the first time in two hours, the net stayed open long enough for the new first check.

SeraMine present.

Brenn's tired voice came in without ceremony.

BrennMine rescue, amend your roll: thirty-one below, not seventeen. Stage the second cage and more air. The first set runs short at fifteen-thirty-two for thirty-one.

Mine-rescue leadSecond cage coming to the collar. Extra respirators with it. We search the side drift after the first lift.

Only then did Brenn give the road order.

BrennAll villages, this is Orrel command. East road closes at fourteen-fifty. Use the ridge track. Say again: ridge track.

Emi opened her mouth and closed it again. She had not expected the voice to sound so tired.

EmiHe sounds scared.

IlluminaraHe is. So are you. He is saying it anyway.

Another voice entered before the minute closed, older than Emi's and roughened by smoke.

MaraDunmere convoy. Five orchard trucks, forty-six people, lower gate. South patrol says the east fork is ash. We take mill lane. I am leaving the irrigation pumps.

BrennDunmere, mill lane is clear to the north culvert. Report when the fifth truck crosses.

MaraI will. Do not send anyone back for the trees.

04 · Shaft Three

Kesh cobalt mine, pump-bay shaft · 14:46, six minutes before the east road burns

The shaft smelled of wet iron and burnt rubber. Illuminara went down fast, calling the level aloud at each landing: level two, level three, east gallery. Her voice, and no one's else, crackled in the girl's headset at the top of the hill.

At 14:47, before the rock closed around her, the shared line carried Mara again.

MaraLast Dunmere house clear. Fifth truck over the north culvert. The pump shed stays.

BrennLogged. All Dunmere people clear.

At the sixth landing the rock stopped her. A slab the size of a barn door had come away from the gallery roof and settled across the passage on a crooked pair of timbers. Behind it, a lamp swung. Thirty-one tired people had made a small safe room in the place the owner had told them did not exist.

SeraWe heard you count down the levels. Is that her? Is that my daughter's light?

IlluminaraIt is mine. Your daughter's is on the other end of the line, and she is keeping your names.

She set her shoulder under the slab and took its weight. It was not the kind of strength she would have chosen to show, but the timbers would not have held through another tremor, and the people behind them were not the ones who had to prove anything today.

IlluminaraOne at a time. Say your name when you pass. Emi is writing it down.

They came through low, with lamps, with scarves over their mouths. The first was a man whose hands had been bandaged with a shirt.

GalenGalen Doss.

Up on the ridge, Emi's pencil dropped a line through the first name. Down in the dust, Illuminara kept her voice level and the slab off their backs.

At the collar, the first cage rose with seventeen people and went down empty again. The second cage and the extra respirators arrived because Brenn had changed the roll to thirty-one. The mine-rescue lead sent two people into the side drift for the fourteen names the official sheet had omitted. Illuminara held the slab through both runs.

At 14:49, Brenn's window ran long. He was repeating a village's route, and the forty-sixth second of the minute passed with his voice still on the line.

The headset snapped. Emi's voice came through hard, her thumb on the key.

EmiBrenn. You are over.

Everyone on the net heard it. For six seconds nobody breathed. Then:

BrennUnderstood. My window is yours. Ridge track. Out.

Emi let the cause-bound cut go early. When Brenn acknowledged the breach, the small reset lamp beside the key turned green again.

EmiIlse Orr. Tuvi Marek. Present, present.

The roll call went on. The tally grew in her notebook, one pencil stroke at a time, and each stroke was a voice she could check.

At the last landing, a girl younger than Emi squinted into Illuminara's dimmed light as if it were a lamp from a story. Illuminara turned the glow up a degree so the child could see her own hands.

Dust like snow, in the lamplight. She had not expected to feel wonder in the shaft, under a slab, with a clock running. It came anyway, small and clean, and she let it.

SeraThirty. One more behind me. Mine.

Sera Sar came through last, soot-blackened and gripping a hand-lamp she refused to put down. She did not say her name. Emi's voice said it for her, hoarse, over the channel.

EmiSera Sar. Present.

SeraNo, baby. Out.

05 · The Tally at Zero

Kesh Ridge relay hut · 15:41, forty-three minutes after the road burned

The south patrol had reached Hale at 14:23; the open channel moved its buses at 14:35, sent Dunmere by mill lane at 14:36 and confirmed the fifth truck over the culvert at 14:47. By 14:52 the last Hale bus had turned before the fire crossed the east road at 14:58. Nine hundred people were on the high pastures. Dunmere had lost one orchard.

Emi still sat in front of the repeater. The carrier was silent, the channel crowded with ordinary voices: fire crews, a village midwife, a dispatcher reading out vehicle plates.

EmiTwenty-eight. Twenty-nine. Thirty. Thirty-one.

The last pencil stroke closed the column. She laid the pencil down.

IlluminaraZero missing. Zero names without an answer.

EmiZero missing because they prepared for thirty-one, not seventeen.

Captain Wynn stood in the doorway with her cap in her hand and the folded printout still visible. She waited until the girl looked up.

WynnI need your statement about the carrier and the reports. You will answer for the net. I will answer for my section.

EmiI know.

WynnI will copy your three carbons here and read every stamp on this channel. You keep the originals.

Emi looked at her mother, who sat on an upturned crate with a blanket round her shoulders and a tin cup of tea going cold between both hands. Sera did not tell her what to do.

EmiI keep the key until the copying is done.

WynnAgreed.

At 15:52 Wynn read the report numbers, stamps and dates into the handset, including the section that had forwarded one and been told it was resolved. Her own.

MaraDunmere keeps its own household tally. Start with medicine, feed and wages. Three of mine rent their roofs, so their names are not on the property list. Titles come later.

WynnThe emergency account is open. Your copy governs the first payments.

The mine would not reopen. The fourteen unfiled workers would wait months for papers that should have existed a year ago. Emi would face a magistrate within the week. None of those costs was called a happy ending.

Illuminara stood at the hut door while the afternoon smoke thinned. Emi set the brass key on the bench beside the notebook, in plain view.

EmiWill you be there? At the inquiry?

IlluminaraIf you ask me.

Emi nodded, put the headset over one ear and found a clean page.

EmiMara Venn.

Static breathed. Then:

MaraPresent. Forty-six clear. One orchard gone. Start the next name.

Emi drew a line beside Mara's name.

What the critic still says doesn't work

Illuminara, called to a burning province where a fourteen-year-old holds the only emergency radio so that her mother and thirty others stay counted, listens until she hears the hole in her own plan, and the child's thirty-one-name roll and resettable key make one shared channel that every office can check, so a second cage, extra air and live road orders bring all thirty-one miners and nine hundred villagers out, at the price of a closed mine, a lost orchard and a hearing Emi will face.

Tonight's shape

Five scenes move from the relay hut, where Illuminara learns that Emi is guarding a list rather than a signal, through a fire truck where live road closures make the shared channel indispensable, into a protocol Emi repairs before releasing the carrier. Her manifest changes the mine rescue to two cage runs with extra air, while Mara Venn's Dunmere checkpoints make the evacuation audible. The aftermath leaves the mine closed, one orchard lost and Emi answerable, but every affected group keeps a voice, a record and a practical next step.

01 · Relejna koča

Relejna koča na grebenu Kesh · 14:02, petdeset minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta

Repetitor je na klopi brnel kakor ujeta osa. Emi Sar je sedela pred njim s starimi materinimi slušalkami čez eno uho in palcem na medeninastem ključu, ki so ga tri desetletja tujih nujnih primerov gladko obrabila. Zunaj se je dim čez greben nagibal kakor dolga rjava rama.

EmiGalen Doss. Prisoten, črpališče. Tuvi Marek. Prisoten, stranski rov. Ilse Orr—

Skozi statiko je odgovoril glas, tanek in sploščen od razdalje.

SeraIlse je tukaj, dete. Kašlja, vendar je tukaj.

EmiIlse Orr, prisotna. Enaintrideset. Ohranila bom vseh enaintrideset.

Illuminara je pristala petdeset korakov niže po cesti in preostanek prehodila. Ustavila se je v odprtih vratih z obema rokama na očeh in svetlobo, ki jo je navadno nosila, zatemnjeno na moč svetilke. Dekličin nosilni signal je slišala čez polovico pokrajine, en sam neprekinjen ton, ki je zadušil vsak drug klic po omrežju, zato je pričakovala ugrabiteljico. Našla je otroka z odprtim zvezkom na kolenih.

IlluminaraSem Illuminara. Opreme se ne bom dotaknila. Rada bi poslušala, preden kar koli prosim.

EmiNajprej vsi poslušajo. Potem me nekdo v čisti uniformi prosi, naj neham.

IlluminaraPotem bom jaz tista, ki še ne bo prosila.

Ostala je med vrati. Vsakih nekaj minut je Emi znova prebrala imena, od začetka in natanko v enakem vrstnem redu, glas iz podzemlja pa je odgovoril na vsako. Illuminara je opazovala, kako je dekličin svinčnik po vsakem odgovoru potrkal ob stran. To ni bila panika. Panika ne vzdržuje stolpca.

Ne varuje signala. Varuje seznam.

IlluminaraKoga ni na uradnem seznamu rudnika?

Emijin svinčnik je obstal.

EmiŠtirinajst jih je. Mama jih je lansko pomlad pripeljala iz obmejnega taborišča, lastnik pa nikoli ni vložil njihovih dokumentov. Če rudnik reče, da je spodaj enaintrideset ljudi, mora povedati, kdo so. Zato enaintrideset ne obstaja. Obstaja sedemnajst, in reševalnim ekipam so rekli, naj pričakujejo sedemnajst.

IlluminaraKaj pa poročila?

EmiTri. Vzhodni rov, črpališče, ustje jaška. Mama jih je napisala lastnoročno. Vsako se je vrnilo z žigom rešeno.

Obrnila je stran in ji jo pokazala. Tri kopije na indigo papirju, vsaka s čistim vijoličnim žigom čez razpoko, ki jo je nekdo narisal na rob.

EmiKo držim kanal, ponavljajo njeno ime. V trenutku, ko ga spustim, spet postane govorica, ekipe pa nihče ne pošlje h govorici.

Illuminara je začutila težo teh besed. Streho jaška bi lahko dvignila v dveh vdihih; otrok ni prosil za streho. Otrok je prosil, naj ga preštejejo.

IlluminaraKaj bi morala slišati, da bi signal izpustila za eno sekundo?

EmiNe obljube.

IlluminaraKaj pa?

EmiMorala bi slišati, da se zgodi, medtem ko se dogaja, na zvezi, ki jo lahko preverim.

02 · Kar je slišalo gasilsko vozilo

Križišče Orrel, gasilsko poveljniško vozilo · 14:19, triintrideset minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta

Kabina vozila je dišala po mokrem pepelu in mlačni kavi. Gasilski poveljnik Odo Brenn je imel na armaturno ploščo prilepljen zemljevid šestih vasi in slušalko, ki se z nobeno od njih ni oglasila že štirideset minut. Ob njem je sedela stotnica pokrajinske žandarmerije Mirel Wynn, s čelado na kolenu in zmečkanim izpisom triangulacije v pesti.

BrennSedi na edinem repetitorju, ki doseže Tamsin, Hale, Quill, Ansel, Dunmere in Orrel. Veter se je opoldne obrnil. V smeri vetra imam devetsto ljudi, pa jim ne morem povedati, po kateri cesti naj gredo.

Požarna straža je v Halu napolnila dva šolska avtobusa, pri spodnjih vratih pa je čakalo pet sadjarskih tovornjakov iz Dunmera. Patruljni avtomobil bi lahko prvo navodilo v Hale odpeljal v štirih minutah, toda ogenj je zapiral odcepe enega za drugim; najnovejši list je vzhodnemu odcepu dajal sedem minut. Druge vasi niso potrebovale enega navodila, temveč naslednjo prosto cesto med premikanjem.

WynnMoja ekipa je enajst minut od njenih vrat. Ukazano mi je prekiniti oddajnik.

IlluminaraBila sem v njenih vratih. Preden ga prekinete, bi rada, da slišite, iz česa je njen nosilni signal.

Povedala jima je o seznamu. O štirinajstih neprijavljenih imenih. O treh ožigosanih poročilih. Brenn je stisnil ustnice. Wynn se sploh ni premaknila.

WynnKatera tri?

IlluminaraVzhodni rov. Črpališče. Ustje jaška.

WynnPoročilo o ustju je šlo skozi moj oddelek. Pred šestimi tedni sem ga sama posredovala. Rekli so mi, da so ga pregledali in odobrili.

V kabini je zavladala tišina. Zunaj je sirena zamrla, ne da bi se je kdo dotaknil.

BrennStotnica, zaradi tega njen nosilni signal še ni zakonit.

WynnNe. Je pa zato edina poštena stvar na tem omrežju.

Illuminara ju ni priganjala. Pojasnila je, kaj deklica lahko stori in česa ne: Emi ne more prebrati lažnega zagotovila; lahko pa prebere ime, na katero nekdo v živo odgovori.

IlluminaraOhranite eno zvezo. Vsakemu dajte časovno okno, na glas in javno. Najprej vaša navodila. Nazadnje preverjanje imen. Vsi slišijo oboje. Nikomur ni treba nikomur verjeti. Samo preveriti morajo.

BrennAvtomobil prispe v Hale v štirih minutah. Zakaj ne bi poslali še petih?

IlluminaraKer odcep, o katerem poroča, zgori v sedmih. Kurir lahko sproži Hale; deset minut pozneje pa naloženim tovornjakom iz Dunmera ne more povedati, kateri zavoj je še odprt. Pošljite prvi avtomobil in ohranite repetitor za ceste, ki se za njim spreminjajo.

Brenn je pogledal sedemminutno oznako, nato pet rdečih puščic, ki so prečkale pet cest.

BrennPrav. Osemintrideset sekund za požarna navodila. Spravim noter eno pot in eno ponovitev, če nihče ne olepšuje.

WynnJužna patrulja v Hale. En avtomobil nadaljuje do spodnjih vrat Dunmera. Ekipa, ki se približuje Emi, obstane v Orrelu.

Wynn prepognjenega izpisa ni spravila v žep. Obdržala ga je vidnega ob kolenu.

WynnDeklica obdrži ključ. Moja ekipa počaka s tem poročilom še vedno v moji roki. Zabeležite, da sem jaz dala ukaz.

IlluminaraKljuč obdrži. Trenuten, ne zaklenjen: kadar koli lahko prekine, če je ime preskočeno ali okno prekoračeno. Če prekine brez razloga, bo pozneje odgovarjala. Če razlog ima, ste ji pustili sredstvo.

03 · Vprašanje, ki ga ni poznal nihče drug

Relejna koča na grebenu Kesh · 14:34, osemnajst minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta

Emi je pogoje poslušala dvakrat. Illuminara ji jih je prebrala z lista, ki ga je Brennov tehnik natipkal na armaturni plošči vozila. Palca ni umaknila s ključa.

EmiVsi ste na isti strani mize, jaz pa sem edina, ki ji je vsak od vas lagal.

IlluminaraDa.

EmiTo je vse? Da?

IlluminaraGlede žigov imaš prav. S prijaznostjo tega ne morem narediti neresničnega.

Emijini členki so pobledeli na medenini.

EmiKako med njegovimi osemintridesetimi sekundami vem, ali rudnik molči zato, ker je na vrsti Brenn, in ne zato, ker se je zrušila streha?

Illuminara je pogledala natipkani list. Urejena razdelitev, ki jo je prinesla iz vozila, je tišino prikazovala kot poslušnost.

IlluminaraNe veš. To sem spregledala.

EmiPotem rudnik dobi prvi dve sekundi vsake minute. Nekdo reče prisotni. Brenn dobi osemintrideset. Seznam dobi dvajset. Če odgovora ni, požarno okno počaka.

BrennDogovorjeno.

EmiIn ključ ni za vedno porabljen zato, ker je ena odrasla oseba prekršila eno okno. Ponastavi se po vsakem preskočenem imenu ali dokazani prekoračitvi.

IlluminaraDogovorjeno. Našla si vrzel. Protokol spremenimo, preden premakneš palec.

EmiPotem dokaži stvar, ki jo lahko preverim. Praviš, da boš šla dol. Vsakdo lahko reče, da gre dol. Mamo bom vprašala nekaj, kar veva samo midve, in odgovorila bo po odprti zvezi. Potem mi poveš, v katerem rovu stojiš, ko to izgovori.

IlluminaraDobro. Vprašaj jo.

Emi je tesno pritisnila slušalke. Temnemu tonu nosilnega signala je govorila, kakor bi bil predor.

EmiMama. Zjutraj devetega. Kaj si pustila na štedilniku?

Enajst sekund se ni vrnilo nič razen šuma. Nato se je globoko pod zemljo zaslišal smeh, hripav in moker.

SeraDobri lonec. Modrega. Pokrov sem pustila odprt, da bi bila jezna name, ne na lonec.

Emi je zaprla oči. Ni jokala. Na rob zvezka ob prvo ime je zapisala modri lonec in njena pisava je bila mirna.

IlluminaraSpustila se bom pri jašku ob črpališču. Ob vsaki menjavi ravni bom povedala številko rova. Slišala boš, kako se moj glas premika.

EmiIn če jo nehaš govoriti?

IlluminaraPotem imaš svoj ključ.

Emi je palec počasi umaknila z medenine. Nosilni signal je utihnil. Prvič v dveh urah je omrežje ostalo odprto dovolj dolgo za novo prvo preverjanje.

SeraRudnik prisoten.

Brennov utrujeni glas se je oglasil brez slovesnosti.

BrennReševanje v rudniku, popravite seznam: spodaj je enaintrideset ljudi, ne sedemnajst. Pripravite drugo kletko in več zraka. Prva zaloga se bo ob petnajst dvaintrideset iztekla za enaintrideset ljudi.

Vodja reševanja v rudnikuDruga kletka prihaja k ustju. Z njo dodatni dihalni aparati. Po prvem dvigu preiščemo stranski rov.

Šele nato je Brenn dal cestno navodilo.

BrennVse vasi, govori poveljstvo Orrel. Vzhodna cesta se zapre ob štirinajst petdeset. Uporabite grebensko pot. Ponavljam: grebenska pot.

EmiSliši se prestrašen.

IlluminaraJe. Tudi ti si. Vseeno to izgovarja.

MaraKonvoj Dunmere. Pet sadjarskih tovornjakov, šestinštirideset ljudi, spodnja vrata. Južna patrulja pravi, da je vzhodni odcep pepel. Gremo po mlinski poti. Zapuščam namakalne črpalke.

BrennDunmere, mlinska pot je prosta do severnega prepusta. Javite, ko prečka peti tovornjak.

MaraBom. Nikogar ne pošiljajte nazaj po drevesa.

04 · Jašek tri

Kobaltnik Kesh, jašek pri črpališču · 14:46, šest minut, preden zgori vzhodna cesta

Jašek je smrdel po mokrem železu in zažgani gumi. Illuminara se je hitro spuščala in pri vsakem podestu na glas klicala raven: druga raven, tretja raven, vzhodni rov. Njen glas in noben drug je prasketal v dekličinih slušalkah na vrhu hriba.

Ob 14:47, preden jo je objela skala, je skupna zveza znova prenesla Marin glas.

MaraZadnja hiša v Dunmeru je prazna. Peti tovornjak čez severni prepust. Črpališče ostaja.

BrennZabeleženo. Vsi prebivalci Dunmera na varnem.

Na šestem podestu jo je ustavila skala. Plošča v velikosti vrat skednja se je odtrgala od stropa rova in obležala čez poševni par tramov. Za njo se je zibala svetilka. Enaintrideset utrujenih ljudi si je uredilo majhen varen prostor tam, kjer je lastnik trdil, da ga ni.

SeraSlišali smo te odštevati ravni. Je to ona? Je to svetloba moje hčere?

IlluminaraMoja je. Svetloba vaše hčere je na drugem koncu zveze in hrani vaša imena.

Z ramo se je podprla pod ploščo in prevzela njeno težo. Takšne moči ne bi želela pokazati, vendar tramovi še enega tresljaja ne bi zdržali, ljudje za njimi pa danes niso bili tisti, ki bi morali kar koli dokazovati.

IlluminaraEden po eden. Ko greste mimo, povejte svoje ime. Emi ga zapisuje.

Prihajali so sklonjeni, s svetilkami in rutami čez usta. Prvi je bil moški, čigar roke so bile obvezane s srajco.

GalenGalen Doss.

Na grebenu je Emijin svinčnik potegnil črto skozi prvo ime. Spodaj v prahu je Illuminara ohranjala miren glas in ploščo držala stran od njihovih hrbtov.

Ob ustju se je prva kletka dvignila s sedemnajstimi ljudmi in se prazna vrnila navzdol. Druga kletka in dodatni dihalni aparati so prispeli zato, ker je Brenn seznam popravil na enaintrideset. Vodja reševanja v rudniku je v stranski rov poslal dva človeka po štirinajst imen, ki jih je uradni list izpustil. Illuminara je ploščo držala med obema vožnjama.

Ob 14:49 je Brennovo okno trajalo predolgo. Ponavljal je pot neke vasi in šestinštirideseta sekunda minute je minila, ko je bil njegov glas še vedno na zvezi.

Slušalke so počile. Emijin glas se je oglasil trdo, njen palec na ključu.

EmiBrenn. Prekoračil si čas.

Vsi v omrežju so to slišali. Šest sekund ni nihče dihal. Nato:

BrennRazumem. Moje okno je tvoje. Grebenska pot. Konec.

EmiIlse Orr. Tuvi Marek. Prisotna, prisoten.

Preverjanje imen se je nadaljevalo. Seštevek v njenem zvezku je rasel, po ena poteza svinčnika naenkrat, vsaka poteza pa je bila glas, ki ga je lahko preverila.

Na zadnjem podestu je deklica, mlajša od Emi, mežikala v Illuminarino pridušeno svetlobo, kakor bi bila svetilka iz zgodbe. Illuminara je sij okrepila za stopnjo, da je otrok lahko videl lastne roke.

Prah kakor sneg v svetlobi svetilke. Ni pričakovala, da bo občutila čudenje v jašku, pod ploščo, ko je čas tekel. Vseeno je prišlo, majhno in čisto, in dovolila si ga je.

05 · Seštevek pri ničli

Relejna koča na grebenu Kesh · 15:41, triinštirideset minut po požaru na cesti

Južna patrulja je dosegla Hale ob 14:23; odprti kanal je njegove avtobuse premaknil ob 14:35, Dunmere usmeril po mlinski poti ob 14:36 in ob 14:47 potrdil peti tovornjak čez prepust. Do 14:52 je zadnji avtobus iz Hala zavil, preden je ogenj ob 14:58 prečkal vzhodno cesto. Devetsto ljudi je bilo na visokih pašnikih. Dunmere je izgubil en sadovnjak.

Emi je še vedno sedela pred repetitorjem. Nosilni signal je molčal, kanal pa je bil poln navadnih glasov: gasilskih ekip, vaške babice, dispečerja, ki je bral registrske tablice.

EmiOsemindvajset. Devetindvajset. Trideset. Enaintrideset.

Zadnja poteza svinčnika je zaprla stolpec. Svinčnik je odložila.
