By sunset, Mount Vey will collapse onto a city where a minor god has made every promise physically binding. Illuminara must free a father from his doorway, two children from forever, and exhausted workers from a mayor’s vow—without teaching the powerful that accountability is only for other people.

01 · The Doorway

Veyra, the east ward · 08:12, ten hours before sunset

Oren Vale leaned into his own open doorway until the tendons stood in his neck. His left boot crossed the sill. His right would not lift. Nothing visible held it, yet the floorboards groaned as if a cart horse pulled the other way.

LioDad, stop. Your ankle is bleeding.

His daughter knelt on the street side with a quarry alarm bell in one hand. Beyond her, a pale line of dust hung above Mount Vey. Each time the bell sounded, the mountain answered a heartbeat later.

OrenI promised your mother I would never leave you alone in this house.

LioI am standing outside it. I am asking you to leave with me.

OrenThe promise does not know the difference.

Across the lane, Mina and Cal moved with their wrists held a handspan apart by a thread of amber light. At nine they had sworn to be friends forever. At twelve, Mina had earned a place on a river school; Cal had refused to let her board the coach because every step away burned both their arms.

MinaWe meant it when we said it.

CalThat is the worst part.

Illuminara came down without thunder. She put one palm against Oren’s lintel. The pressure was not in the wood. It ran under the street, through thousands of doorstones, marriage rings, guild marks and burial tablets, all converging on the black quarry above the city.

A small figure sat on the lintel where her hand had been. He was no taller than Lio’s forearm. His coat was stitched from torn contracts; his eyes were two drops of sealing wax. When he spoke, every promise in the street tightened.

SefIf words may be escaped whenever they hurt, the weak are the only ones who must believe them.

IlluminaraI did not come to teach you that words are cheap.

SefYou came because the mayor’s quarry is breaking my oldest covenant. Powerful people always discover mercy when consequence reaches their own door.

The second alarm sounded. Dust rolled from Mount Vey in a thicker ribbon. Lio unfolded a quarry map. A red crack had reached the ventilation stair where three hundred night workers were still below.

LioForewoman Sen says the east shelf will fall at 17:42. The mayor promised work to every household. Sef made the promise true. Half the city is too exhausted to shore the shelf, and no one assigned to the quarry can leave.

IlluminaraMy aim is to get every person out before the shelf falls, without breaking the covenant that keeps the mountain off the city.

SefThen begin with the part you dislike. Ask who paid when promises were only admired.

He stepped into a crack in the lintel and vanished. Oren’s right foot remained fixed.

Illuminara lifted Lio’s alarm bell and felt its chipped bronze warm in her hand. He had not refused help. He had refused another exception made by someone strong enough to call it mercy.

IlluminaraShow me the Hall of Oaths. Then we go to the quarry together.

Lio glanced at her father. Oren stopped pulling at the threshold, wrapped his ankle, and nodded. It was not rescue yet. It was the first time that morning someone had asked him to act rather than endure.

02 · What Sef Heard

Hall of Oaths · 10:05, seven hours and thirty-seven minutes before collapse

The hall had no statues. Its walls were built from promise stones: one for every vow on which another person’s safety had depended. Bright stones marked fulfilled obligations. Dark ones marked breaches. Most of the dark stones bore the crests of old councils, mining houses and temples.

Sef stood on the clerk’s table. Around him gathered Oren, Lio, Mina, Cal, Forewoman Ilya Sen, Mayor Teren Vos and forty citizens chosen by the quarry crews. No guard stood at the doors. Sef had made every official who promised public service unable to leave.

Mayor VosRelease the workers and I will sign any amendment you draft.

SefYou signed six safety amendments. When production fell, you called each one aspirational.

Mayor VosThe city would have starved.

IlyaYou promised every family wages, then counted compulsory double shifts as employment. We did not starve. We broke.

Illuminara touched a dark stone bearing the mayoral crest. It held not words but consequences: Ilya’s crushed fingers; a widow’s unanswered petition; children carrying meals to parents who slept beside the lifts.

IlluminaraSef, when did you begin binding every promise literally?

SefAfter the seventh council swore to repair the west retaining wall and used the money for a triumph gate. The slide killed four hundred and twelve. Their last breath was full of official language.

IlluminaraSo your goal is not obedience. It is recourse.

The wax in Sef’s eyes trembled, but his voice stayed hard.

SefRecourse that cannot be postponed by the eloquent. A promise that changes when the promiser suffers is merely a weapon with a velvet handle.

LioAnd a promise that cannot hear the person it was made to becomes a cage. My mother asked Dad to keep me safe, not to die inside our doorway.

OrenI used her last words because deciding what came next frightened me. Sef did not invent that.

Cal raised his glowing wrist. Mina raised hers beside it.

CalI wanted forever because everyone in my house leaves.

MinaI stayed because his fear hurt me less than hurting him. That does not make staying freely chosen.

For one moment the amber thread slackened, then tightened again. Sef had listened; he had not conceded.

SefIf I accept intention over words, Mayor Vos will discover that he intended justice all along.

IlluminaraThen do not let the promiser decide. Let the person who relied on the promise name the harm. Let release require truth, repair and a new choice—not cleverer wording.

Mayor VosA tribunal during a mountain emergency?

IlyaA tribunal is what you call it when workers get a chair.

The hall shuddered. A line of dust fell from the ceiling. On the quarry map, the red crack crossed another support gallery. The clock now read seven hours, twenty-nine minutes.

SefWords again. Test them where stone can answer.

He struck the table. Three promise stones rose: the mayor’s employment vow, Oren’s doorway vow, and the children’s forever vow. Beneath them lay a fourth, older and brighter than all the rest: the city’s covenant to keep the drainage channels clear so Mount Vey would sleep.

SefBreak every bond and the old covenant breaks with them. Keep every bond and the exhausted crews die. Show me accountability that survives freedom.

Illuminara did not reach for power. She asked Ilya for the quarry ledgers, Lio for the petitions no clerk had answered, and Sef for the names of those who had relied on each promise. Sef gave her the names.

03 · The Price Named by the Harmed

East quarry assembly floor · 13:48, three hours and fifty-four minutes before collapse

The quarry floor had been cleared beneath a roof of cracked slate. Every eight minutes, a brass plumb bob swung farther east. Ilya had painted three evacuation lines on the ground. The workers stood behind the lines by crew, not by rank.

Illuminara could have carried them out. The covenant ran through the drainage tunnels, however, and a forced severing would send the saturated upper slope into Veyra. Her strength could hold one shelf for ninety-three seconds. The mountain held six.

IlluminaraHere is my first proposal. Every safety promise names its beneficiaries, duration, proof and a way to demand repair. Changed circumstances may reopen its terms. Those harmed decide whether repair is enough.

SefWho declares the circumstances changed?

IlluminaraEither party could ask—

SefThen Mayor Vos will call falling profits a changed circumstance. He will reopen the promise, keep the benefit and describe the breach as negotiation. You have built him a polite door.

Illuminara looked down at the clause she had thought was fair. Sef knew not only how promises trapped people, but how power escaped them. She struck the sentence through.

IlluminaraOnly a person who relied on the promise may trigger a reopening. Immediate danger may justify a provisional departure, but it starts a public repair hearing within one day. The promiser cannot rewrite the harm.

IlyaAnd the hearing begins with the injured, not the office that broke the promise.

SefBetter. Not safe. Better.

Ilya rolled the quarry cutaway across the slate. The loaded waste tram stood above the north stair on a relief rail whose haul cable crossed the east fracture. If its brake were released, it would clear the stair, travel for ninety-three seconds and pull the fractured shelf toward the abandoned cut.

Illuminara traced the crack with two fingers and marked the point where the cable would take the load. Ilya checked the tram mass against the six crews’ recorded weights, then made the north-stair release and the counterweight one timed sequence. The workers—not a hidden machine—would set the brake, clear the route and call the final latch.

IlluminaraI can hold the shelf for the tram’s ninety-three-second descent. Not for a hundred. If the route changes, you call the change.

IlyaThen your strength follows our clock.

Ilya laid three demands on the stone table. The quarry would close until an elected crew inspected every gallery. Vos would surrender his quarry shares to a restitution trust. For five years, half the council seats overseeing public works would belong to workers and bereaved families.

Vos removed the mayoral seal and signed away his office, his half of the house and every quarry share. He sent a runner for Maro and the children before anyone could mistake his signature for theirs.

While they waited, Mina and Cal wrote their own repair: each would tell the other one thing the vow had cost; neither would ask for contact for thirty days; after that, friendship could be renewed only by two yeses.

CalIf she says no after thirty days, what holds me?

SefNothing.

CalThat feels like falling.

MinaI will sit with you until the coach comes. I will not promise what happens after.

Cal wept without hiding his face. Sef climbed down from the table and sat beside him. He did not loosen the amber thread.

SefI was made from that fear. Every promise is a bridge over the fact that another being may leave.

Lio placed an unused witness seal on the floor beside him. It was plain iron, cut for two keys. Her written offer gave Sef the witness key for one hearing only, or permission to leave it untouched. The quarry gate was not its price, and no one could bind him to the chair.

SefA place offered can become another promise.

IlluminaraSo it expires after one hearing. You choose again. If you never take it, the chair remains empty and the court still owes you nothing.

Sef did not touch the seal. He also did not step away from it.

The runner returned with Vos’s family. Maro read the demands twice, closed his hand around the house key and refused to spend the children’s home on Teren’s debt. He conceded one concrete term: they would keep three rooms through winter while the clinic used the ground floor. The remaining purchase, trust and repair terms would be heard after the evacuation.

Vos reached for the key, stopped, and signed only the property and shares that were his to give. Ilya turned the page toward the waiting witnesses. His title was gone; his family’s boundary remained outside his control.

Illuminara signed beneath the tram calculation: ninety-three seconds when Ilya called, the evacuation route above her improvisation, and the same public review for any force she used in Veyra that day. She offered no forever.

SefYou could leave before judgment.

IlluminaraYes. The record gives people an answer if I do: publish my breach, refuse my aid and summon witnesses beyond this city. Trust is not certainty. It is power arranged so betrayal has an answer.

Sef looked toward the lower terraces, where Lio’s runners were already carrying the names he had supplied in the Hall. The people protected by the drainage covenant would be asked what risk, if any, they would accept.

The plumb bob struck its warning mark twenty-three minutes early.

IlyaThe crack accelerated. New collapse time: 17:19.

No one asked Sef to believe a definition. They carried a corrected proposal, a checked ninety-three-second plan, an unclaimed witness seal and three possible evacuation answers to the failing galleries.

04 · Ninety-Three Seconds

Mount Vey, east shelf · 17:16, three minutes before collapse

Rainwater hissed through the upper fracture. Below it, six crews moved along routes they had chosen. Ilya held the two-stage release lever: its first pull would send the loaded ore tram down the ninety-three-second relief rail and clear the north stair; its final latch would drop the tram into the empty cut and tension the haul cable across the fracture. Lio stood at the signal bell. Oren waited at the city doorway, still bound, ready to cross if Sef released him.

At the lower spillway stood Ressa Daan, whose bakery and cellar occupied the first terrace, and Toma Ely, chosen by the east-lane households. They held the reply bells. No one claimed they spoke for the whole city; they carried the recorded answers of the people on the routes that would take the eleven-second surge.

IlyaTest condition one: the workers may refuse the mayor’s employment promise without losing their claim to wages.

SefIf I release them, who keeps the drainage covenant?

Thirty-two workers raised their hands. Not one was compelled.

WorkersWe renew the drainage covenant for this evacuation and for thirty days. After that, renewal requires inspection, pay and a recorded vote.

IlyaTest condition two: those harmed retain the power to reject repair.

MinaI accept thirty days apart.

CalI accept that she may not return.

Sef opened one small hand. The amber thread between the children dissolved into warm sparks. Cal staggered, then stood without grabbing Mina. Mina took his hand for three breaths and let go. Both choices held.

In the city, Oren’s right foot lifted. He crossed the doorway and ran toward the lower drainage gate with Lio’s spare key. His promise did not vanish; it changed into a record of care, harm and consent that Lio had accepted.

SefAnd the mayor?

Mayor VosDo not release my debt. Release the workers from my command.

The promise stones around the quarry flared. The ore tram gates opened. Workers who had been physically unable to abandon assigned stations moved toward the stairs.

At 17:18:07 the east shelf split.

IlyaNow, Illuminara.

Ilya pulled the first detent. The loaded tram began its ninety-three-second descent, clearing the north stair as its wheels took the cable strain. The crews had built the sequence; Illuminara had shown them where the fracture would accept it.

Illuminara went beneath the falling shelf and raised both hands. Two million tonnes of slate stopped a spear’s length above her. The impact drove her knees into stone. Lio’s clock began with the tram’s descent: ninety-three seconds to the empty cut.

Sef saw the sixth crew still trapped behind a contract-marked gate. Releasing them would weaken the old covenant for eleven seconds before the volunteers’ renewal reached the promise stones. In those seconds the lower spillway would flood and the east retaining road might go.

SefIf I keep them, the mountain sleeps and they die. If I free them, other people pay.

IlluminaraThen ask the people who would pay.

Lio rang the question sequence: eleven seconds, lower spillway, east road. Ressa’s bell answered once: yes with a condition. Toma’s answered twice: no.

RessaKeep the spillway open even if my cellar floods. My ovens are not worth a crew.

TomaThe east lane is not clear. Six households are still moving the bedbound. No gate until Lio gives three bells.

The clock passed forty-one. Ilya changed the plan. The north-stair crew abandoned two carts of shoring timber and ran to carry the last east-lane residents above the red line. The lost timber meant the processing hall could not be saved.

SefYou accept the cellar and the road?

RessaI accept my cellar. Toma speaks for the road only when his people are clear.

The clock passed fifty-eight. A support cracked against Illuminara’s shoulder. She did not command Sef or promise that no one would be hurt.

At sixty-four seconds, Lio heard three reply bells from the east lane and struck three of her own. Toma answered once. The condition had been met; his no had become a yes without being overruled.

Sef looked at Ilya, not at the mayor.

SefIf I open the gate, will your crew renew the drainage covenant before they reach the north stair?

IlyaAsk them.

Through the bars, the sixth crew answered one by one. Twenty-one said yes. Three said no; they had been on duty thirty-six hours and would accept no new promise until they slept. Ilya assigned their section to rested volunteers, who consented on the record.

At seventy-two seconds, Sef glanced at the plain iron witness seal Lio had left beside the lever. He could have opened the gate without it, and the offer had not been made as payment. He picked up only the witness key.

SefOne hearing. Then I choose again.

At seventy-five seconds, Sef opened the gate.

For eleven seconds, Mount Vey moved. Oren reached the lower gate and locked the emergency spillway open. Brown water filled Ressa’s cellar and tore the east retaining road into the abandoned orchard. The six households were already above it. Lio struck the new sequence; rested volunteers renewed only the drainage work they had named. The bright covenant stone held.

At eighty-eight seconds, the loaded tram reached the empty cut. Ilya pulled the final latch. The tram dropped, the haul cable snapped taut, and the fractured shelf turned away from the city along the line Illuminara had marked.

IlyaClear!

Illuminara released the stone at ninety-two seconds. The shelf fell into the abandoned quarry. The old processing hall, three cranes and the mayoral triumph arch disappeared under dust. No house in Veyra moved.

For a moment Mina laughed—not because the loss was small, but because Cal had let her run and had run beside someone else. Illuminara laughed too, breathless and astonished. The sound was her own, not a lesson for anyone.

Sef stood on her dust-covered shoulder with the witness key closed in his wax hand. He was still small. He no longer looked like a jailer, but neither did he look harmless.

SefThree workers refused. Toma refused until his people were clear. The covenant lived.

IlyaGood. Come witness the cost before the next renewal.

05 · The Court of Open Hands

Veyra, the former mayoral house · dawn, the following day

The front rooms had become a temporary clinic before the dust settled. Maro and his children kept three rooms upstairs through winter; in spring, the trust could offer an assessed purchase only if they accepted it. Vos’s half of the house and every quarry share he owned were sealed in the restitution trust. He slept on a bench outside the records office, waiting to testify.

At the long table sat workers, bereaved families, apprentices, clerks and two seats kept empty for people who had not yet decided whether to join. Above them hung no image of Sef.

Sef sat in one of the empty seats and set the witness key beside his hand. The chair continued an offer he had accepted for one hearing, not a reward for opening the gate.

IlyaThis court preserves the record, hears the people who relied on a promise, and certifies repair or release. It cannot compel a new promise.

SefAnd my power?

IlyaYou may make concealed consequences visible. You may not bind a body until the person harmed has been heard and immediate safety requires it. Every binding expires unless this court renews it with the affected people’s consent.

SefYou offer a god a clerkship.

LioWe offer you witnesses who cannot be dismissed as a superstition when officials break their word.

Sef studied the dark stones carried from the old hall. They were no longer hidden in walls. Each lay beside a petition and the name of someone empowered to answer it.

SefI will serve for thirty days. Then I choose again.

IlyaSo do we.

Oren entered through the front door carrying a kettle. He paused on the sill by habit, then crossed. Lio did not applaud. She took the heavier handle, and together they brought tea to the night crew.

OrenI cannot repair twelve years by crossing once.

LioNo. But today you crossed when I needed you outside.

Mina’s river coach left at noon. Cal came to the platform with Sef and did not ask for a promise. Mina gave Cal a paper address that might change. Cal gave her a carved whistle and told her she did not have to use it.

At Mount Vey, rested volunteers cleared the drainage channels under Ilya’s plan. The quarry stayed closed and wages came from the seized shares. Ressa’s cellar remained flooded; the east road would stay broken through winter. Three families rejected the first restitution offers, and the court recorded their refusals without punishment.

Vos disclosed the diverted funds and named the councilors who had approved them. When he tried to explain that every choice had protected employment, Ilya made him read the night-shift injury list before he continued.

Illuminara submitted her ninety-two seconds of force to review. A rigger objected that the falling shelf had shattered a memorial crane. She listened, recovered its nameplate with him, and accepted the requirement that the crane be rebuilt before any monument to the rescue.

Sef watched with the severe attention of a creature learning that consequence could have more than one shape.

Before she left, Illuminara set Lio’s chipped bell within his reach and opened her palm beneath the edge of his chair. Sef looked at the offered hand, then climbed down by the chair rung instead. She withdrew without turning his refusal into a lesson and left the bell where he could choose it.

SefThe weak still need words they can trust.

IlluminaraYes.

SefFreedom will still be used as an excuse by the strong.

IlluminaraYes. That is why freedom without recourse is unfinished.

SefAnd recourse without freedom becomes me.

He did not apologize for the bindings. Some people were not ready to forgive him, and the court did not ask them to. He placed his sealing-wax hand on the first thirty-day covenant beside Ilya’s inked thumbprint.

Illuminara left Veyra by the east road after breakfast. Behind her, Sef rang Lio’s chipped bell for the next hearing. Two empty chairs remained at the table. No one filled them by force.

Do sončnega zahoda se bo gora Vey zrušila na mesto, kjer je mali bog vsako obljubo naredil fizično zavezujočo. Illuminara mora očeta osvoboditi njegovega praga, otroka njunega za vedno in izčrpane delavce županove zaobljube, ne da bi mogočnim sporočila, da odgovornost velja samo za druge.

01 · Prag

Veyra, vzhodna četrt · 08:12, deset ur pred sončnim zahodom

Oren Vale se je uprl v odprta vrata lastne hiše, dokler mu niso na vratu izstopile kite. Levi škorenj je bil čez prag. Desnega ni mogel dvigniti. Nič vidnega ga ni zadrževalo, a talne deske so ječale, kakor da bi na drugo stran vlekel vprežni konj.

LioOče, nehaj. Gleženj ti krvavi.

Njegova hči je klečala na ulični strani in v eni roki držala kamnolomski opozorilni zvonec. Za njo je nad goro Vey visela bleda črta prahu. Vsakič ko je zazvonilo, je gora odgovorila en srčni utrip pozneje.

OrenTvoji materi sem obljubil, da te v tej hiši nikoli ne bom pustil same.

LioStojim zunaj nje. Prosim te, da greš z menoj.

OrenObljuba ne pozna razlike.

Na drugi strani ulice sta se Mina in Cal premikala z zapestjema, ki ju je jantarna nit držala za dlan narazen. Pri devetih sta si prisegla, da bosta prijatelja za vedno. Pri dvanajstih je Mina dobila mesto v rečni šoli; Cal ji ni dovolil na voz, ker je vsak korak proč žgal oba v rokah.

MinaKo sva to rekla, sva mislila resno.

CalTo je najhuje.

Illuminara se je spustila brez grmenja. Dlan je položila na Orenovo preklado. Pritisk ni bil v lesu. Tekel je pod ulico, skozi tisoče pragovnih kamnov, poročnih prstanov, cehovskih znamenj in nagrobnih plošč, ki so se vsi stekali v črni kamnolom nad mestom.

Na prekladi, kjer je bila prej njena roka, je sedela drobna postava. Ni bil višji od Liojine podlakti. Plašč je imel sešit iz raztrganih pogodb; oči sta bili dve kaplji pečatnega voska. Ko je spregovoril, se je vsaka obljuba v ulici zategnila.

SefČe je mogoče besedam uiti vsakič, ko zabolijo, jim morajo verjeti samo šibki.

IlluminaraNisem te prišla učit, da so besede poceni.

SefPrišla si, ker županov kamnolom lomi mojo najstarejšo zavezo. Mogočni vedno odkrijejo usmiljenje, ko posledica pride pred njihova vrata.

Oglasil se je drugi alarm. Z gore Vey se je skotalil debelejši trak prahu. Lio je razgrnila načrt kamnoloma. Rdeča razpoka je dosegla prezračevalno stopnišče, pod katerim je bilo še vedno tristo nočnih delavcev.

LioDelovodkinja Sen pravi, da se bo vzhodna polica zrušila ob 17:42. Župan je vsakemu gospodinjstvu obljubil delo. Sef je obljubo uresničil. Pol mesta je preveč izčrpanega, da bi podprlo polico, nihče, ki je razporejen v kamnolom, pa ne more oditi.

IlluminaraMoj cilj je spraviti vse ven, preden se polica zruši, ne da bi prelomila zavezo, ki goro zadržuje nad mestom.

SefPotem začni z delom, ki ti ni všeč. Vprašaj, kdo je plačeval, ko so obljube samo občudovali.

Stopil je v razpoko v prekladi in izginil. Orenovo desno stopalo je ostalo prikovano.

Illuminara je dvignila Liojin opozorilni zvonec in začutila, kako se ji okrušeni bron greje v dlani. Pomoči ni zavrnil. Zavrnil je še eno izjemo, ki jo nekdo dovolj močan lahko imenuje usmiljenje.

IlluminaraPokaži mi Dvorano priseg. Potem greva skupaj v kamnolom.

Lio je pogledala očeta. Oren se je nehal vleči čez prag, si obvezal gleženj in prikimal. To še ni bila rešitev. Prvič tistega jutra ga je nekdo prosil, naj nekaj stori, namesto da samo prenaša.

02 · Kar je slišal Sef

Dvorana priseg · 10:05, sedem ur in sedemintrideset minut pred zrušitvijo

V dvorani ni bilo kipov. Stene so bile zgrajene iz kamnov obljub: po enega za vsako zaobljubo, od katere je bila odvisna varnost drugega človeka. Svetli kamni so označevali izpolnjene obveznosti. Temni so označevali kršitve. Večina temnih je nosila grbe starih svetov, rudarskih hiš in templjev.

Sef je stal na pisarjevi mizi. Okoli njega so se zbrali Oren, Lio, Mina, Cal, delovodkinja Ilya Sen, župan Teren Vos in štirideset prebivalcev, ki so jih izbrale kamnolomske izmene. Pri vratih ni bilo nobenega stražarja. Sef je vsakemu uradniku, ki je obljubil javno službo, onemogočil odhod.

Župan VosIzpusti delavce in podpisal bom vsak amandma, ki ga sestaviš.

SefPodpisal si šest varnostnih amandmajev. Ko je proizvodnja padla, si vsakega razglasil za nezavezujočo željo.

Župan VosMesto bi stradalo.

IlyaVsaki družini si obljubil plačo, nato pa obvezne dvojne izmene štel za zaposlitev. Nismo stradali. Zlomili smo se.

Illuminara se je dotaknila temnega kamna z županovim grbom. V njem niso bile besede, temveč posledice: Ilyini zdrobljeni prsti; neodgovorjena vdovina prošnja; otroci, ki so nosili hrano staršem, spečim ob dvigalih.

05 · Sodišče odprtih dlani

Veyra, nekdanja županova hiša · zora naslednjega dne

Sprednje sobe so postale začasna klinika, še preden se je prah polegel. Maro in otroka so skozi zimo obdržali tri sobe zgoraj; spomladi jim je sklad lahko ponudil ocenjen odkup le, če bi ga sprejeli. Claude — Fresh premise (weather as delegation), humane stakes with sick children, dialogue-heavy, and a clean boundary-and-refusal resolution. But the technical procedure (millibars, wheels, membranes, timestamps) is dense and abstract, the dialogue is stiff, and the resolution is tidy and bureaucratic, which limits emotional pull.

The solution emerges through experiment, mutual revision, and enforceable consent rather than easy harmony, while lasting injuries prevent sentimentality. Assessment refers to the English reading edition. Model comments retain their original language.Ocena velja za angleško bralno izdajo. Komentarja modelov sta v izvirnem jeziku.

A delegation whose bodies are weather fronts has crossed the sealed homes of Aster Vale because it cannot imagine an outside, leaving two children struggling to breathe. With dispersal aircraft launching in three hours, Illuminara must discover a boundary the visitors can perceive and the settlers can control—without asking either side to enter a room that cannot let them leave.

01 · Weather Inside the Nursery

Aster Vale clinic · 13:58, three hours and two minutes before dispersal launch

The fog came through the sealed nursery wall without opening it. It entered as a pale blue seam, unfolded across the ceiling and pressed every hanging toy toward the floor at once.

Six-year-old Jo Pell coughed into an oxygen mask. Blue condensate had etched a white crescent into its rim. In the next bed, his brother Anik made no sound at all. The monitor above him showed eighty-four, then eighty-three.

Doctor Sen Var pulled the emergency curtain around both beds although the curtain could not stop weather.

SenPressure drop. Twelve millibars in eight seconds. Seal the bronchial circuit.

Technician Ro Kade struck the wall control. The room's vents closed. The fog thickened.

A chord moved through the glass cabinets—not heard so much as felt in teeth and ribs. Three notes rose, separated and rejoined. Frost drew branching lines over the medicine refrigerator.

Illuminara stepped between the beds and spread her light into a shallow golden canopy. Air stopped rushing from the boys' lungs, but the blue seam continued through her glow as rain through a beam from a window.

SenCan you force it out?

IlluminaraYes. Not before I know what part of it is listening.

SenOne child is at eighty-three.

Illuminara lowered one hand. The air around Anik held at the pressure his damaged lungs could bear. With the other she touched the condensation on the cabinet. The droplets did not run down. They moved toward the warm print of her finger.

Not an invasion toward bodies. A migration toward gradients.

The doors opened. Governor Elian Voss entered with pilot Mara Kes and two sealed launch cases.

VossThe aircraft are fuelled. At seventeen hundred they seed calcium ash along the ridge. The fronts break, the incursions stop.

The chord in the cabinets dropped by half a tone. Blue mist curled around the warm oxygen tube beside Jo's cheek.

MaraThat thing crossed three pressure walls. The seed gives it surfaces to condense on. We can pull it out of the valley.

IlluminaraAnd if the front is a body?

MaraThen it entered a nursery in a body.

Jo lifted one hand from the blanket. His fingers trembled in the fog.

JoIt keeps saying warm.

Sen looked at him sharply.

SenIt is not speaking to you. Low oxygen makes patterns.

JoNot a word. The same squeeze the storm made before it came through the wall.

Illuminara let the chord touch her canopy. A fourth pulse returned from every sealed room.

IlluminaraGovernor, give me ninety minutes before you load the ash.

VossNinety minutes. If clinic pressure falls again at fifteen-thirty, I decide.

SenThe boys do not become your experiment.

IlluminaraNo. The first room will be empty. And it will have doors on both sides.

02 · The Argument About Outside

North weather mast · 14:31, two hours and twenty-nine minutes before launch

Beyond the mast, translucent fronts folded against the wind across half the northern sky.

Voss had ordered every family into the stone cistern halls. He remained at the mast because the launch code required his hand. Mara remained because the aircraft were hers.

Illuminara opened the mast's pressure valves one finger-width at a time. Each valve answered with a brass click. The folds in the sky tightened.

MaraThey followed the heat leaks from the houses. We patched the leaks. They crossed the walls anyway.

IlluminaraA wall makes the gradient steeper. To you it means keep out. To something that lives as moving pressure, it may mean a wound that must be equalised.

VossTwo children have chemical burns in their lungs. Do not ask me to admire the wound's philosophy.

IlluminaraI am asking what will make it stop crossing.

She struck the lowest plate: compression, release, stillness. Three answering pulses drove rain upward from the fields.

Illuminara repeated the pattern, then left the final valve shut.

The response came harder. The mast groaned. A voice formed from the difference between windward and leeward glass.

VisitorsYou close continuation.

Mara's hand went to the launch case.

IlluminaraWe close inhabited air because your passage tears lungs.

VisitorsThere is no inhabited air. There is air. There is no outside from which permission arrives.

VossThen there can be no agreement. Our children cannot live in your definition.

The front moved across the sun. Every anemometer on the mast spun backward.

VisitorsYour still boxes remove the road. When a trailing front dries, its pressure sequence breaks; what it carried cannot rejoin us. Open all warm volumes until the sea-current rises.

MaraNo.

She said it before Illuminara could answer.

MaraMy daughter sleeps in one of those volumes. You crossed her room yesterday. She bled from both ears. We will not open the houses.

The front's lower edge whitened, a pressure response sharp enough to crack one pane of the mast.

VisitorsOne volume refuses the atmosphere? A cup orders the river not to wet it.

IlluminaraA lung is not a cup. It exchanges and remains itself. It has a surface, and that surface is not an insult to the air.

VisitorsYour surface cannot be perceived before collision.

There it was: not permission refused, but a boundary arriving too late to be meaningful.

Illuminara looked south toward the abandoned crop research station. Its old pressure farm had tested seeds under two atmospheres without exposing workers to either.

IlluminaraIf a boundary announced itself as a gradient you could feel before crossing, would you stop at it?

VisitorsIf stopping did not sever our rearward selves. If the path continued somewhere real.

VossAnd if we make this path, do the incursions end?

The three notes separated in the mast.

VisitorsShow a boundary that is not disappearance. Then we can choose.

MaraThat was not a promise.

IlluminaraNo. It was a condition. Ours is that the houses remain closed and the clinic pressure never falls again.

VossYou have fifty-nine minutes before my decision returns.

03 · A Room That Could Refuse

Aster Vale pressure farm · 15:16, fourteen minutes before the clinic trigger

A scratched glass cylinder held two halves divided by a flexible membrane. Each side had its own wheel; neither could open the other.

Ro worked beneath the controls. Sen held the south wheel because the chamber borrowed clinic warmth and only she could admit it. A nurse relayed the boys' monitors to her wrist. Mara brought warm water.

RoThe chamber can hold a six-millibar slope. More than that and the centre membrane walks out of its seals.

IlluminaraWe need four: one to warn, three to hold. First both halves stay at the same temperature. If the front stops, pressure can announce a boundary. Then we add warmth. If warmth pulls it through, the walls are more than walls.

SenAnd what tells us they have not crossed?

Ro raised two tracer lamps, amber and blue.

RoAmber marks us; blue marks them. If a sensor sees both, both wheels lock and the roof opens over the empty gravel field.

Voss set the armed case in sight. Its slurry loader was clipped to the farm's old thermal feed to keep the ash nozzles warm. The red countdown read 01:44:02.

VossThe clinic held. Your ninety minutes are almost gone. What exactly are you asking my people to risk?

IlluminaraNo person enters. Each side keeps a wheel. Ro has isolated the chamber valves from the old thermal feed. We test pressure alone, then warm amber; each result answers a different question.

SenAnd if their pressure tears it?

IlluminaraI hold the membrane long enough for the roof vents to clear the chamber. Not long enough to make the test succeed against either side's refusal.

Mara stared through the glass at the empty south half.

MaraYou can hold a roof. You cannot promise a weather body will understand a lamp.

IlluminaraNo. That is why you keep your wheel.

Sen's wrist receiver chirped. She listened, then covered the speaker.

SenAnik is at ninety-one on reduced oxygen. Jo is asking whether the weather knows his name. One failure, then I return. The boys do not fund a second attempt.

VossAgreed.

The voice of the visitors came through the mast relay as a tremor in the chamber glass.

VisitorsThe road is too small. The smallest front may dry beyond rejoining; then the pressure memory that makes us one is lost.

IlluminaraThis is one question, not your road. You keep your wheel and may leave if continuity thins: can you feel a surface before collision and remain yourself while you stop?

VisitorsYou ask weather to become a guest in a jar.

MaraWe ask you not to enter a child's lung.

A long pressure wave moved through the building. Dust rose from the floor in a perfect ring.

VisitorsWe will send the smallest front that still remembers us. We do not open your wheel.

SenAnd we do not open yours.

Illuminara placed one palm against the centre seal. Not to command it. To be ready when tested.

IlluminaraThen the first answer can be no on both sides. Begin.

04 · The Test Front

Aster Vale pressure farm · 16:04, fifty-six minutes before launch

At 15:30 the clinic pressure had held. Voss's trigger passed without a fall; the launch clock kept running.

The north baffles sang first. A filament of blue fog entered the outer ring and stopped when it met the one-millibar warning slope. It spread sideways, tracing the chamber's circumference without touching the centre membrane.

The blue lamp brightened. The amber lamp remained alone.

RoBoundary detected. No transfer.

Mara poured warmed water into the south evaporator. Amber vapour climbed the glass. The visitor filament pulled toward the heat and pressed the north wheel without turning it.

VisitorsContinuation is present. The surface is early.

Sen did not take her hand off the south wheel.

SenStop there.

The filament stopped. For four seconds the chamber held two weathers separated by a membrane neither had crossed.

Then the pressure rose from below.

The floor plates bowed. The north filament flattened against the glass, not toward the amber vapour but toward a heating pipe beneath the seals. Ro looked at the gauge and swore.

RoThe launch loader pulled the farm loop across our isolation. Eleven degrees in nine seconds.

The centre membrane jumped two handspans south. Illuminara caught it with light and shoulder. The north sensor flashed amber and blue together.

SenContamination. Vent it.

Ro struck the roof release. Both chamber roofs opened. Blue and amber vapour rose into the empty gravel field. The visitor filament recoiled, then followed the warm exhaust upward rather than driving toward the occupied station.

Illuminara dimmed her own light until it no longer made another warm cliff.

IlluminaraYou chose the empty vent when the seal failed.

Smallest FrontI remembered the breath that failed. I would not enter it again.

Mara shut her wheel. Sen had never opened hers.

The membrane sagged back into place. One lower seal had torn.

VossThe test failed.

IlluminaraThe chamber failed. The early boundary worked. The steep heat behind it pulled harder than the warning.

MaraNot sealed air. Waste heat.

IlluminaraPressure walls trap waste heat into cliffs. We built beacons and named them barriers.

The visitors answered from the gravel field, their voice weaker after the venting.

VisitorsWarmth is the road. Your boxes cut it into cliffs. We cross before we perceive the surface.

VossCan the aircraft move a road?

Mara turned toward the launch case. The red clock read 00:51:12.

MaraThe aircraft can vent heated water instead of ash: a warm line from the northern folds to the sea current, over empty salt terraces. No roofs.

SenFor how long?

MaraSix hours. Tomorrow settlers can vote on a geothermal ridge duct from the north cooperative's exhaust stack, routed around two greenhouses.

VisitorsSix hours is a gap, not continuation.

IlluminaraEnough to test the corridor without crossing a home. Success earns a daylight vote; failure ends the duct.

The front darkened the windows.

VisitorsOpen the clinic volume as proof of trust.

Sen's answer struck the glass harder than the pressure chord.

SenNo.

Illuminara did not soften it.

IlluminaraNo. Trust is not paid with the bodies already harmed. You can refuse the corridor. You cannot purchase it with the children.

Voss closed the launch case and turned the key to hold. The red countdown went dark.

VossDispersal suspended until the corridor test ends. The ash will not decide your answer.

The three visitor notes separated. The highest faded first.

VisitorsWe refuse the clinic. We demand that the corridor's edge be announced in pressure before the warmth begins.

RoWe can pulse the aircraft vents twice before the release. Same early surface as the baffles.

MaraAnd I keep the ash aboard. If one front turns toward a roof, I disperse only that arm.

VisitorsYou retain a weapon.

MaraYou retain a sky.

A small spiral of blue fog formed above the gravel, then loosened.

Smallest FrontThe warning reaches me before the warmth. I can refuse it and remain. Both retain refusal. Send the early surface.

VisitorsWe choose the corridor for six hours. The greater weather does not promise beyond it.

05 · Weather with an Address

Aster Vale salt terraces · 16:51–17:22, nine minutes before launch to twenty-two minutes after

Mara's two aircraft banked over the empty salt terraces. They pulsed their vents twice, then released a warm ribbon toward the sea current. The first visitor front descended toward it.

At 16:51 the front reached the announced pressure edge. Its leading fold compressed, stopped and spread sideways along the invisible line. Mara watched the whole front turn west without touching a roof.

The northern folds followed one by one. At 16:56 Sen's voice broke over the aircraft channel.

SenThe last seam is leaving the clinic wall. Both boys are holding. No ash.

Rain travelled west in a narrow shining road that touched no roof. Above it, the visitors moved as separate fronts, no longer one wall across the sky.

Voss stood with twenty-three delegates. Ro's duct plan bent around the two greenhouses whose owners had voted no.

VossThe north cooperative offers one exhaust stack for thirty days. The clinic offers none. Every occupied building keeps its pressure wall. Renewal requires another vote.

The visitors spoke through three kites Ro had tethered at different heights. Their chords arrived with the rain.

VisitorsThirty days does not carry all rearward selves. We accept it for the delegation. The greater weather waits beyond the ridge.

MaraAnd the houses?

VisitorsClosed volumes announce before warmth. We do not cross the announced surface. If a surface fails to announce, we call through the kites before following heat.

Sen arrived with Jo; Anik slept under observation at ninety-six oxygen.

Jo wore a paper mask decorated with two uneven blue spirals. He stopped well short of the first rain marker.

JoWhich one of you was in our room?

The lowest kite dipped.

Smallest FrontI carried that crossing. I did not know your inside until your breath failed.

JoDo you know now?

Smallest FrontI know a lung is a weather that must not be entered whole.

Sen placed a hand on Jo's shoulder but did not ask him to forgive.

SenBoth boys will be examined for months. The clinic lost its nursery. Knowing comes after harm, not instead of it.

VisitorsThen record the harm in the corridor call. Let every front hear before arrival.

Ro added a fourth pressure sequence to the kites: two children injured, one nursery closed, no unrestricted passage. The visitors repeated it without shortening it.

The farm's south greenhouse was lost to the loop failure. Its foundation became a proposed meeting chamber; no one called the ruin a gift.

Mara opened the launch case. The calcium ash canisters were still sealed.

MaraStore the ash in public. Any dispersal needs Sen, me and one elected delegate. No quiet launch.

The warm corridor began to cool as the aircraft turned home. The first geothermal vent opened on the northern stack, approved for thirty days. Rain shifted toward it, testing the new line.

The visitor delegation followed. At the marker above the clinic road, its smallest front paused, separated from the warmth and made the two warning pulses itself.

Jo raised one hand but did not step into the rain.

The blue spiral above him waited on its own side of the air.

Delegacija, katere telesa so vremenski fronti, je prečkala zatesnjene domove Aster Vala, ker si ne zna predstavljati zunanjosti, dva otroka pa se zdaj borita za dih. Ker bodo letala za razpršitev vzletela čez tri ure, mora Illuminara odkriti mejo, ki jo obiskovalci lahko zaznajo in naseljenci nadzorujejo — ne da bi od katere koli strani zahtevala, naj vstopi v sobo, ki je ne more spustiti ven.

01 · Vreme v otroški sobi

Klinika Aster Vale · 13:58, tri ure in dve minuti pred vzletom za razpršitev

Megla je prodrla skozi zatesnjeno steno otroške sobe, ne da bi jo odprla. Vstopila je kot bledomoder šiv, se razgrnila čez strop in vse viseče igrače hkrati potisnila proti tlom.

Šestletni Jo Pell je kašljal v kisikovo masko. Moder kondenz je v njen rob vrezal bel polmesec. V sosednji postelji njegov brat Anik ni izdal niti glasu. Monitor nad njim je pokazal štiriinosemdeset, nato triinosemdeset.

Zdravnica Sen Var je okoli obeh postelj potegnila zasilno zaveso, čeprav zavesa ni mogla ustaviti vremena.

SenPadec tlaka. Dvanajst milibarov v osmih sekundah. Zatesnite bronhialni obtok.

Tehnik Ro Kade je udaril po stenskem krmilniku. Zračniki v prostoru so se zaprli. Megla se je zgostila.

Skozi steklene omarice je stekel akord — niso ga toliko slišali, kolikor so ga čutili v zobeh in rebrih. Trije toni so se dvignili, ločili in spet združili. Slana je čez hladilnik za zdravila risala razvejane črte.

Illuminara je stopila med postelji in svojo svetlobo razprla v plitek zlat baldahin. Zrak je prenehal uhajati iz pljuč dečkov, modri šiv pa je še naprej prehajal skozi njen sij kakor dež skozi snop svetlobe iz okna.

SenGa lahko izrineš?

IlluminaraDa. Toda ne, dokler ne vem, kateri njegov del posluša.

SenEden od otrok je pri triinosemdesetih.

Illuminara je spustila eno roko. Zrak okoli Anika je obdržala pri tlaku, ki so ga njegova poškodovana pljuča še prenesla. Z drugo se je dotaknila kondenza na omarici. Kapljice niso stekle navzdol. Premaknile so se proti toplemu odtisu njenega prsta.

Ne vdor proti telesom. Selitev proti gradientom.

Vrata so se odprla. Guverner Elian Voss je vstopil s pilotko Maro Kes in dvema zatesnjenima zabojema za izstrelitev.

VossLetala so napolnjena z gorivom. Ob sedemnajstih bodo vzdolž grebena zasejala kalcijev pepel. Fronti se razbijejo, vdori se končajo.

Akord v omaricah se je znižal za pol tona. Modra meglica se je ovila okoli tople kisikove cevke ob Jotovem licu.

MaraTa stvar je prečkala tri tlačne stene. Seme ji bo dalo površine, na katerih se lahko kondenzira. Lahko jo izvlečemo iz doline.

IlluminaraKaj pa, če je front telo?

MaraPotem je kot telo vstopil v otroško sobo.

Jo je izpod odeje dvignil roko. Prsti so se mu tresli v megli.

JoVes čas govori toplo.

Sen ga je ostro pogledala.

SenNe govori s teboj. Zaradi premalo kisika vidiš vzorce.

JoNi beseda. Isti stisk kot v nevihti, preden je prišla skozi steno.

Illuminara je dovolila, da se je akord dotaknil njenega baldahina. Iz vsake zatesnjene sobe se je vrnil četrti sunek.

IlluminaraGuverner, dajte mi devetdeset minut, preden naložite pepel.

VossDevetdeset minut. Če tlak v kliniki ob petnajstih trideset spet pade, odločim jaz.

SenDečka ne bosta postala vaš poskus.

IlluminaraNe. Prva soba bo prazna. In imela bo vrata na obeh straneh.

02 · Spor o zunanjosti

Severni vremenski jambor · 14:31, dve uri in devetindvajset minut pred vzletom

Za jamborom so se prosojni fronti v nasprotni smeri vetra zgibali čez polovico severnega neba.

Voss je ukazal, naj se vse družine umaknejo v kamnite dvorane cistern. Sam je ostal pri jamboru, ker je koda za vzlet zahtevala njegovo roko. Mara je ostala, ker so bila letala njena.

Illuminara je tlačne ventile jambora odpirala po širino enega prsta. Vsak ventil je odgovoril z medeninastim klikom. Gube na nebu so se napele.

MaraSledili so uhajanju toplote iz hiš. Uhajanje smo zakrpali. Skozi stene so šli vseeno.

IlluminaraStena gradient naredi strmejši. Za vas pomeni ostani zunaj. Za nekaj, kar živi kot gibajoči se tlak, pa morda pomeni rano, ki jo je treba izenačiti.

VossDva otroka imata kemične opekline v pljučih. Ne zahtevajte, naj občudujem filozofijo te rane.

IlluminaraSprašujem, kaj bo doseglo, da bo prenehala prehajati.

Udarila je po najnižji plošči: stisk, sprostitev, mirovanje. Trije povratni sunki so z njiv pognali dež navzgor.

Illuminara je vzorec ponovila, zadnji ventil pa pustila zaprt.

Odgovor je prišel siloviteje. Jambor je zaječal. Iz razlike med privetrnim in zavetrnim steklom se je oblikoval glas.

ObiskovalciZapirate nadaljevanje.

Marina roka je segla proti zaboju za izstrelitev.

IlluminaraZapiramo naseljeni zrak, ker vaš prehod trga pljuča.

ObiskovalciNaseljenega zraka ni. Je samo zrak. Ni zunanjosti, iz katere bi prišlo dovoljenje.

VossPotem dogovor ni mogoč. Naši otroci ne morejo živeti v vaši opredelitvi.

Front je prešel čez sonce. Vsi vetromeri na jamboru so se zavrteli nazaj.

ObiskovalciVaše mirujoče škatle odstranijo pot. Ko se zadnji front posuši, se njegovo tlačno zaporedje pretrga; kar je nosil, se nam ne more znova pridružiti. Odprite vse tople prostornine, dokler se morski tok ne dvigne.

MaraNe.

To je rekla, še preden je Illuminara utegnila odgovoriti.

MaraMoja hči spi v eni od teh prostornin. Včeraj ste prečkali njeno sobo. Krvavela je iz obeh ušes. Hiš ne bomo odprli.

Spodnji rob fronta je pobelel; tlačni odziv je bil dovolj oster, da je počila ena od šip jambora.

ObiskovalciEna prostornina zavrača ozračje? Skodelica ukazuje reki, naj je ne zmoči.

IlluminaraPljuča niso skodelica. Izmenjujejo in ostajajo svoja. Imajo površino in ta površina ni žalitev zraka.

ObiskovalciVaše površine ni mogoče zaznati pred trkom.

To je bilo to: ne zavrnjeno dovoljenje, temveč meja, ki je prišla prepozno, da bi sploh kaj pomenila.

Illuminara je pogledala na jug proti zapuščeni postaji za raziskovanje poljščin. Njena stara tlačna farma je semena preskušala pod dvema atmosferama, ne da bi delavce izpostavila kateri koli od njiju.

IlluminaraČe bi se meja napovedala kot gradient, ki bi ga lahko začutili pred prehodom, bi se pred njo ustavili?

ObiskovalciČe ustavitev ne bi odrezala naših zadnjih jazov. Če bi se pot nadaljevala nekam, kar je resnično.

VossIn če zgradimo to pot, se vdori končajo?

Trije toni so se v jamboru ločili.

ObiskovalciPokažite mejo, ki ni izginotje. Potem lahko izberemo.

MaraTo ni bila obljuba.

IlluminaraNe. Bil je pogoj. Naš je, da hiše ostanejo zaprte in tlak v kliniki nikoli več ne pade.

VossDo vrnitve moje odločitve imate devetinpetdeset minut.

03 · Soba, ki je lahko zavrnila

Tlačna farma Aster Vale · 15:16, štirinajst minut pred sprožilcem v kliniki

Opraskan steklen valj je držal dve polovici, ločeni s prožno membrano. Vsaka stran je imela svoje kolo; nobena ni mogla odpreti druge.

Ro je delal pod krmilniki. Sen je držala južno kolo, ker si je komora izposojala toploto klinike in jo je lahko spustila vanjo samo ona. Medicinska sestra je monitorja dečkov posredovala na njen zapestni sprejemnik. Mara je prinesla toplo vodo.

RoKomora zdrži šestmilibarski naklon. Pri večjem se osrednja membrana izmakne iz tesnil.

IlluminaraPotrebujemo štiri: enega za opozorilo, tri za zadržanje. Najprej obe polovici ostaneta pri isti temperaturi. Če se front ustavi, lahko tlak napove mejo. Potem dodamo toploto. Če ga toplota potegne skozi, so stene več kot samo stene.

SenIn kaj nam pove, da niso prečkali?

Ro je dvignil dve sledilni svetilki, jantarno in modro.

RoJantarna označuje nas, modra njih. Če tipalo zazna obe, se obe kolesi zakleneta in streha se odpre nad praznim gramoznim poljem.

Voss je oboroženi zaboj postavil na vidno mesto. Njegov nakladalnik za suspenzijo je bil priključen na stari toplotni vod farme, da so šobe za pepel ostale tople. Rdeče odštevanje je kazalo 01:44:02.

VossKlinika je zdržala. Vaših devetdeset minut je skoraj mimo. Kaj natančno zahtevate od mojih ljudi, naj tvegajo?

SenKaj pa, če jo njihov tlak raztrga?

Najprej so zapeli severni dušilniki. Nit modre megle je vstopila v zunanji obroč in se ustavila, ko je dosegla enomilibarski opozorilni naklon. Razširila se je vstran in zarisala obod komore, ne da bi se dotaknila osrednje membrane.

Illuminara, called to a valley where living weather fronts are crossing sealed homes and two boys are struggling to breathe, tests the visitors' fog against heat as well as language, and the failed chamber, an early pressure edge and a six-hour warm corridor turn the incursions away from every roof with the dispersal ash held back, at the price of a closed nursery, a lost greenhouse, months of examinations and a thirty-day route that cannot carry all the visitors' rearward selves.

A barn-sized slab is creeping toward the village of Kesk, and the oldest woman in it has locked herself in the burial ground; Illuminara learns what the refusal is guarding, and the village finds a way to carry it.

01 · The Slab

Kesk, the cliff track · noon

The slab above Kesk was the size of a barn and had been moving for nine days. It moved the way a tired child leans on a door, so slowly that nobody could say when the leaning had stopped being a lean.

Captain Iven Roth of the valley rescue had called Illuminara himself, which she understood had cost him something. He did not shake her hand. He held out his tablet the way a man shows a doctor a wound he has already diagnosed.

RothTwo millimetres a day on Monday. Eleven an hour this morning. Plot one over the speed and the line walks down to zero at about eight tonight, give or take three hours. Rain is due at eight. I have been telling myself seven.

She laid her palm flat on the cliff beside the track and let the mountain show her where it was holding. The slab did not hang from the face. It leaned on a rock bridge behind it, a column the width of a bus, cracked through like a boiled bone and doing the work of the whole slope. She felt the load run down it the way you feel a pulse in a wrist.

IlluminaraI can take the slab's weight off that bridge. I cannot make the bridge sound, and to hold anything I need two anchors in good rock. This mountain has one place that qualifies: the limestone knuckle where the ledge turns away. Four hours, perhaps.

RothPerhaps.

IlluminaraPlan for three.

He nodded like a man accepting an honest invoice. The track down was two and a half kilometres of ledge, single file, and its first four hundred metres ran under the slab's shadow before the cliff turned away. Sixty-two people lived in Kesk. Sixty-one were on the church green with their bags.

RothThe sixty-second has locked herself in the burial ground. The gate, I mean, with a key. The wall beside it fell down in 'ninety-eight.

02 · The Circuit

The burial ground above the church · half past twelve

Ostrava Mehl was ninety-one and walked as though the ground were a sentence she was checking for errors. She went along the first row with a stick in one hand and a ring of iron keys in the other, and when Illuminara stepped through the gap where the wall had been, she did not look up.

Illuminara fell in beside her and said nothing for a full row. It was the most useful thing she had done all day. The old woman's lips were moving. She never repeated herself.

A man came up the path at a run and stopped with his hands on his knees. Davor Mehl was fifty, a quarry foreman, and the only person in Kesk who had ever been forgiven for raising his voice to her.

DavorAuntie. The captain says three hours at the outside.

OstravaThen you have time to be quiet.

DavorYou hold mountains, don't you? That is what they say. Then you can hold her. Put her over your shoulder and let us go, and she will thank you at ninety-five.

IlluminaraIt would work. That is what is wrong with it.

Ostrava stopped, for the first time, and looked at Illuminara properly, as one inspects a stranger who has said something unexpected.

IlluminaraWhat are you saying?

OstravaNames. Two hundred and fourteen, in the order they lie. Thirty-seven have no stone: the cough winter, the Pirc fire, the ones nobody could pay a mason for. There was a book. The school burned in 'seventy-four and the book went with it, and my mother gave me these keys and the order of the rows and said, whoever walks this after you walks it from you or not at all. I have been through it twice since the siren. I lose the order at the east wall.

IlluminaraSo you are not refusing to leave.

OstravaI am refusing to leave them unsaid.

IlluminaraHow long does it take to say them all?

OstravaFour hours, walking. I will not say a name I have not stood at.

DavorAuntie, nobody asked you that.

OstravaNobody asked me anything. They asked if I was coming. I did the sum myself, Davor, before you had your boots on. Four hours, and the track is an hour and a half. I chose the names.

Illuminara saw then that the village had spent the morning arguing with a refusal, and that no one had asked what it was for. Davor had gone the colour of the church wall. She let him.

03 · Three Clocks

The church porch · one in the afternoon

They laid it out on the porch flags with Roth's tablet and a stub of builder's chalk, because it turned out to be three problems wearing one coat.

IlluminaraThe slab's clock: down by eight at the latest, sooner if the rain is early. The track's clock: three hours for sixty-two people, with the old and the stones. Ostrava's clock: four hours, because the list can only travel as fast as one pair of legs.

OstravaLegs are what a person has.

IlluminaraThen borrow more. The list is not slow. The walking is. Sit you in a chair at the crossing of the paths. Six people each take a row, walk to a grave, and stand at it. You say who lies there, from where you sit. A seventh writes. They have stood at the place, and you have heard them stand. Two hours, perhaps less.

OstravaAnd when they stand at the wrong mound?

IlluminaraThen you tell them, and they go to the right one. That is all a reading is.

OstravaThey will point at moles.

RothEveryone who is not needed for the reading goes now, children first, and the bend belongs to them alone until they are across.

RothYour hold starts when the slab tells us, not when it suits you. Anchors are a clock too. Four hours spent at noon are four hours you will not have at six.

RothThen the ledge. The old trough stands two hundred metres in, under the slab. Short of the trough, if anything goes wrong, you turn back to the kiln cut: two metres of rock over it, and I have sat under it myself. Past the trough, the way out is forward. Nobody runs. A running line shakes the ledge.

DavorThe geophone is mine. I listen to the cracking. Forty ticks a minute, or Illuminara tells me an anchor is going, and we do what the captain said, and whatever is unfinished stays where it is. Nobody argues.

IlluminaraYour call, not mine. If it crosses forty, I am not an argument.

DavorAnd the sum, so I do not invent it on the day. From the trough to the knuckle is two hundred metres. A chair's pace covers that in five minutes, six on a bad step, and I want half as much again in hand for the last foot. Nine. At the trough I ask her for her hold. Nine or more, we pass it. Less, we take the kiln cut.

OstravaCan you put it down somewhere else?

IlluminaraNo. It falls where the plane tilts. I can choose when. The when has to be after you are all out.

IlluminaraThe twelve line stones, the first stone of each row, are the oldest and the heaviest. I can lift them down the ledge myself.

OstravaYou will not. They go by sledge, on shoulders. Whoever carries them down will carry them again on All Souls. A stone that arrived by miracle is a stone nobody has to look after.

She was right, and she had made it a better plan. Illuminara wrote sledges, shoulders on the flags and underlined it.

OstravaWhen the reading is done I will say them all again, from the chair, going down. Once to the ground, once to the six who stood on it.

OstravaDavor. You will carry the register.

DavorAuntie, I will carry you.

OstravaNot me. What I say. Lift that, and four of your neighbours may carry the rest of me, on the Pirc chair, because my own has a bad leg.

For a moment Davor looked as though he might refuse the whole arrangement out of pure relief. Then he took the tablet from Roth and held it as one holds something alive.

04 · The Reading

The limestone knuckle at the far end of the ledge · half past two

The gauge touched twenty millimetres an hour at twenty-seven minutes past two, and Illuminara set both hands into the only sound rock on the mountain and took the slab's weight onto her own.

It was like lifting a table that a hundred people were leaning on. Roth stood beside her with a handset clipped to his collar and a face that offered nothing, which she was grateful for. Through the radio, from three hundred metres up the slope, came a kitchen chair scraping on gravel.

Ostrava (radio)Row one, from the church wall. Hedvig Mehl, who kept bees. Josef Brunec, who did not. Mara Pirc, four years old. Tomo, you are on her feet. Step back one.

Davor (radio)Written. Next.

Up the slope, through the bridge and into the shoulder, she could feel what the mountain remembered of two hundred and fourteen openings, each a small softness where hands had once dug and filled. She could have counted them. She could not have told one from another by anything but its depth, which was the whole point of the old woman and the whole trouble.

The names came across the gorge like a train of small carriages, each with someone in it. Row two. Row three.

Ostrava (radio)That is a mole, Brina.

The radio filled with six people trying not to laugh.

Ostrava (radio)East wall. Third mound.

The radio hissed. A minute went, and another. Under Illuminara's hands the north anchor shifted a hair, like a tooth.

Ostrava (radio)I had it this morning.

Davor (radio)Nan Pirc's boy. Teodor. He fell off the Pirc barn in 'fifty-one and Nan hauled a bench up here every Sunday till she died.

Ostrava (radio)Who told you that?

Davor (radio)You did. I was nine. You made me carry the bench.

There was a long hiss. Illuminara held the mountain and waited.

Ostrava (radio)Write it.

It was, she thought, the first name Ostrava had said in nine hours that she had not said alone.

At twenty past four the chair scraped for the last time. Row twelve was said, and the thirty-seven with no stone were pegged where the walkers had stood, each peg tied with a name.

Ostrava (radio)The count.

Davor (radio)Two hundred and fourteen. Thirty-seven pegs, and Brina has counted them twice. Every one is on the tablet against its row and its paces from the east wall.

Ostrava (radio)Read me the last peg.

Davor (radio)Jelka Pirc. The Pirc fire. Row twelve, three paces from the east wall.

RothThe valley station has the file. A second copy, off the mountain.

Ostrava (radio)Then it is out of my head. Good. It was getting heavy.

05 · The Bend

The far end of the ledge · twenty-five to six

They came along the ledge in the last of the light, twenty-two lanterns in a line against a face the colour of slate: six sledges with the line stones lashed on, a chain of neighbours who had done this every All Souls of their lives, and in the middle, four of them carrying a kitchen chair with a very small woman sitting bolt upright in it. Davor walked at the back with the tablet inside his coat and the geophone in his hand.

Ostrava was saying them again, as she had promised, from row one. It had turned out that the register was in four-four time, and the bearers had fallen into step with it, a name to a stride, so that the chair rode level on the ledge.

At twenty to six the rock under Illuminara's left hand turned to grit.

IlluminaraRoth. North anchor is gone. I am moving east. Eleven minutes at half strength.

RothSay it to Davor.

IlluminaraDavor. Eleven minutes, half strength.

Davor (radio)Thirty-four.

She slid her hand along the knuckle, found a seam, and leaned into it. The slab took a breath above them, and she felt it as a stranger's weight on her arm.

Davor (radio)Thirty-eight.

The tail of the line, Davor's lantern, had just come level with the trough, two hundred metres from her. Forty, she thought, and the plan says the kiln cut or on, and his sum decides which. She did not speak. It was his line.

Davor (radio)We are at the trough. Forward is six minutes on a bad step against her eleven, and the rule was nine. We pass it. Walk. Do not run. Running shakes the ledge.

Down the gorge came the old woman's voice, flat and steady, at the pace of a walk.

Ostrava (radio)Alois Vrh, a good man and a bad fiddler. Lena Vrh, who forgave him.

Davor (radio)Thirty-six.

At the third minute a sledge runner caught in a crack of the ledge and four men stood still for the length of a breath. It was the bad step the sum had allowed for. The line moved again, and nobody ran.

At four minutes the first sledge reached her, and the man hauling it said something to nobody that had the shape of a prayer, and kept going. At five the chair passed. Ostrava did not look at her. She was on row nine.

Davor (radio)Last foot clear.

RothSix minutes.

IlluminaraThen I am putting it down.

RothSay it to someone who can answer.

IlluminaraOstrava. Is there anything the mountain still owes you?

Ostrava (radio)Nothing it can pay.

She lowered it. She did not drop it. For a moment the slab seemed to remember it was falling, as a person remembers a name, and then it went, and the shoulder opened and closed over two hundred and fourteen small softnesses all at once. She did not look away. The slab came down on empty ground.

06 · East Corner

The threshing terrace below Kesk · the next morning, frost

Sixty-two people stood on the old threshing terrace with their breath hanging over them, and above them the mountain had a new face. Nobody said the word cairn. Nobody would for a year.

Davor had three printed copies of the register in a plastic sleeve: one for the diocese, one for the council, one for the cousins in Toronto. They had rung every All Souls and been told, correctly, that Aunt Rozalija lay at the top of the hill in the third row. This year they would be told, correctly, that she lay there still, under the mountain, and that her name would be cut in April at the east corner of the terrace below, where the living could stand. The register had two columns now, because Ostrava had insisted: where each of them lies, and where each is remembered. Twelve line stones stood in a row on the frosted grass. Beside Illuminara a woman called Brina, who had been wrong about the moles, put a cup of tea into her hands without asking. They shook a little. She let them.

DavorThe council sat till two. The terrace is a memorial ground, not a graveyard. Nobody is moved, and nobody is to say they were. The thirty-seven are to be cut first, before any stone that already had one.

OstravaI would have asked for that.

DavorYou did not ask.

OstravaI did not think it could be asked.

She stood up from the Pirc chair without help, took her stick in one hand and her keys in the other, and went along the terrace until she had found the corner she wanted. She put the Mehl line stone down herself and took her time over it.

OstravaEast corner. It gets the sun in the morning.

OstravaYou told me you could not put it down somewhere else.

IlluminaraI could not.

OstravaThen all you did was let it fall when we were ready. I do not forgive the mountain. I may forgive you by spring.

Davor, kneeling in the frost, wrote the corner's name at the top of a clean page.

Plošča velikosti skednja se pomika proti vasi Kesk, najstarejša vaščanka pa se je zaklenila na pokopališče; Illuminara spozna, kaj varuje njena zavrnitev, vas pa najde način, da to odnese s seboj.

01 · Plošča

Kesk, steza ob pečini · poldne

Plošča nad Keskom je bila velika kakor skedenj in se je premikala že devet dni. Premikala se je tako, kakor se utrujen otrok nasloni na vrata, tako počasi, da nihče ni mogel reči, kdaj naslanjanje ni bilo več zgolj naslanjanje.

Dlan je položila plosko na pečino ob stezi in pustila gori, da ji pokaže, kje se drži. Plošča ni visela s stene. Naslanjala se je na skalni most za seboj, na steber, širok kakor avtobus, preklan kakor kuhana kost, ki je opravljal delo celotnega pobočja. V Kesku je živelo dvainšestdeset ljudi. Enainšestdeset jih je s prtljago čakalo na travniku pred cerkvijo.
