Forty goats in a dale byre have voted, unanimously, for something nobody can name, and a sale is about to fence off the hill; Illuminara spends two evenings in the straw until she hears what the vote is a translation of, and lets the herd correct her answer.

01 · The Byre

Marrick Farm, Brannoch Dale · evening, eleven days before the sitting

The goats had called the meeting, and Odile Marrick wanted that understood before anything else. They had called it by walking into the byre at dusk, all forty, and standing in the straw in the patient way of animals who have listened to people for a long time. A veterinary trial that went wrong eleven years ago had left them able to follow an argument. It had not left them quick about it.

OdileThey voted last Tuesday. Forty on the left side of the byre, and then eleven walked across to the right and back again, and the vet wrote that down as a recount. I think it was a joke.

IlluminaraWhat did they vote for?

Odile held out the vet's notepad. It carried three phrases, copied down over three nights: the hill, the count, the going-up.

OdileThe assembly sits in eleven days to decide whether they are livestock or residents. The cooperative has voted to sell the high pasture, as one lot, through a Mr Pruett, to people who want to put cabins on it. I have been asked to bring the goats' position, and I do not have one. I have three phrases.

IlluminaraWhy did you send for me?

OdileBecause I am afraid of being wrong in either direction. Call them persons and the assembly may take them from a farm that loves them. Call them stock and I have said exactly what the sale needs me to say. And I will not hand forty living creatures to a court on the strength of what a goat said in a barn.

At the far end of the byre an old nanny with a grey muzzle got up out of the straw, one leg at a time, and came the length of the floor. The others made room without being asked.

BrackenYou are the one who listens. Sit. Sit down. Down in the straw.

Illuminara sat. It seemed to be the first item of business, and the sigh that went through the herd told her she had guessed right.

02 · The Count

The byre · the second evening

Illuminara spent two evenings in the byre before she asked anyone anything. She had asked Odile to come without her clipboard, and Odile sat on an upturned bucket by the door with an expression somewhere between suspicion and relief.

She ate what the kids ate, which was oat cake pressed with something bitter and green, and found she liked it, and that the kids found her liking it very funny. She learned that the herd did not so much talk as take turns: one word, then a pause long enough to hold a whole thought, then another. She learned that a goat in conversation says the same thing three times, so that nobody has to ask twice. She had also noticed, without quite noticing, that every time one of the three phrases was spoken the whole herd leaned a little toward the east door.

At bedtime the kids played a game. One said a name, the next said it again and added another, and so on down the straw, and a small brown kid with one folded ear always got furthest.

TansyByre Gate. Split Ash. Byre Gate, Split Ash, the Wet Step. Byre Gate, Split Ash, the Wet Step, Tolly's Rise.

IlluminaraWhat is the game called?

TansyThe count.

She said it the way a child says the alphabet. Illuminara sat very still, because something in her head had come loose and she did not want to knock it off the shelf.

Not goats. Places.

IlluminaraTansy, what comes after Tolly's Rise?

Fourteen names came out of the straw in order, ending at a place called the Long Look. The vet had written down three demands. They were one. The hill was where the rhyme went. The count was the rhyme. The going-up was the walking of it.

IlluminaraWho taught you the count?

TansyBracken. Bracken's mother. Bracken's mother's mother. The count.

03 · The Registry

The Brannoch Dale registry, back room · the fourth morning

The registrar listened to Odile without a word and then wheeled out a flat drawer. The enclosure award of 1844 was a map the colour of weak tea, and across the high ground ran a dotted line labelled in a hand like barbed wire: Common Way, as anciently used, for the going-up and coming-down of beasts to the common grazing above the Lamb Wall. Fourteen waymarks were pencilled along it. Illuminara read them aloud, once, and Odile sat down on a box of ledgers.

OdileSplit Ash. Tolly's Rise. My grandfather said that in the lambing shed. I thought it was a nursery rhyme.

IlluminaraIt is a survey. The award only wrote down a road that was already old. They have been saying the bounds of it since before the ink, and calling it a game, because nobody else was listening.

OdileThen why is it not in Pruett's title?

RegistrarBecause there are two ledgers. The award book keeps a right alive by an entry, and nothing else. A holder's claim is an entry. A walk that I or a holder sets down is an entry. Twenty years with none, and the right lapses. Pruett's title is drawn from the parcel index, and the index carries only what a holder has entered against a parcel. The last entry in the award book is nineteen years old, a lambing-week walk my predecessor happened to see. Nobody has ever entered the Way against the land.

IlluminaraSo the right is alive in one book and invisible in the other. The herd has kept the road alive on foot, and the paper has let it go quiet. Eleven months left on the clock.

RegistrarAnd a goat cannot lodge a claim. The sale particulars were drawn from the index as it stands.

He slid a second sheet across the desk. It offered the high pasture as an unencumbered single lot.

OdileSo I enter a claim for the holding, and the Way goes onto the title before the lot is divided, and the sale cannot close as written. But to do that I must say it is the holding's herd that uses it. Which is the word they did not want said. A thing people do to them.

IlluminaraYes. I could draft it tonight, and it would be correct, and it would win. I think we ask first.

OdileAsk whom?

IlluminaraThe people whose road it is.

04 · The Correction

The byre · that night

She laid it out the slow way, a sentence and then a wait, for as long as it took. The way was in the award. The right belonged to the holding. The cooperative would claim it, the herd's going-up would stand as the use, and forty goats would keep the hill without anyone having to rule on what they were.

It was a good plan. She was a little proud of it, and had not hidden that well. Bracken heard it out to the end. Then she said, three times over, the word Illuminara had hoped not to hear.

BrackenNo. No. No.

IlluminaraTell me where it is wrong.

BrackenFor these forty. Forty die, the way is gone. Not for us. For the kids who are not yet. For whoever the herd is.

Illuminara's pride went out of her all at once, and what came in behind it was more useful. She had written the right for the animals in front of her. The herd had asked for a road that would outlast them.

IlluminaraThe right runs with the herd, whoever it is. Kids born, strays taken in. Not forty names.

BrackenGood. And a road to a shut gate is no road. The grass at the end of it is the end of the road. We want the hearing. When the way changes, the cooperative counts us first. We say. We say before.

OdileYou want a veto over my own land?

BrackenOver the road. Not the farm. The road is the road.

OdileAnd where it goes?

BrackenA road goes somewhere.

Odile looked at the old nanny for a long time. Then she looked at the straw, where Tansy lay asleep with her mouth still moving on the count.

OdileThen the sale loses the top of the hill. The grass above the Lamb Wall stays in the cooperative's name, out of every lot, and I put that to people who voted for the whole of it. I will write more than you asked. Neither the Way nor the grass it goes to can ever be sold, and nothing on either is changed without your speakers heard first. Not in a bad year. Not ever.

BrackenThat is more than we asked. Good. It is not enough. A road no one walks is a road in a drawer. The way must be walked. Every spring. Kids at the front. If it is walked and the book sees it, it is used. If it is used, it is not lost. The hill remembers if we walk.

Illuminara wrote that down and understood what Bracken had just done. The right had come within eleven months of lapsing because nobody could claim it. It would not come near again, because the entry was a morning walk the herd would make whether or not anyone asked, and the registrar had only to be there to see it.

05 · The Gate

The high pasture gate · afternoon, four days before the sitting

Mr Hale Pruett was not a villain, which Illuminara found inconvenient. He was a tidy man in a waterproof the colour of porridge, acting for a buyer who had paid a deposit, with a lender who wanted a clean title behind her, and the look of someone who has read a great many documents carefully and is now being shown one that was not in the file. He had read the award twice.

PruettYou are asking my client to accept, for ever, forty goats walking through his scheme twice a year, on the strength of a nursery rhyme.

IlluminaraOn the strength of an award, which the rhyme matches stone by stone. I walked the line last night with my palm flat on the air. The old groove is still there under the gorse, four hundred years of the same weight on the same line.

PruettAnd the lot is halved.

IlluminaraIt is. The grass above the Lamb Wall leaves the sale. Your client keeps the lower meadow, the road frontage, the water, and seven of his eleven plots. The Way is a four-metre lane along the wall, outside the plots, mapped and entered on the title on the first day instead of found by your lender's solicitor in March.

PruettThe price falls.

IlluminaraIt does. She will lend against a lane she can read. She cannot lend against a claim in the registrar's drawer that nobody has told her about.

PruettAnd if the goats change their minds?

IlluminaraThen they say so, in the count, to the cooperative, before anything moves. It is the only change to that lane you will ever have to deal with, and it will come with notice.

He looked up the hill for a while.

PruettMy guests will ask what the noise is.

IlluminaraTwice a year, a fine one. Bring your lender to the walk.

PruettI agree to nothing. I will carry a mapped lane, seven plots and a walk to my client, and they will say what they say.

He wrote spring walk, autumn walk in the margin of the particulars, which is how a careful man marks what he expects to have to defend.

06 · The Going-Up

The Common Way · dawn, the morning of the sitting

They went up in the grey: forty goats, the whole membership of the cooperative and the registrar with a notebook, and Tansy at the front, because the kids go first.

TansyByre Gate, Split Ash, the Wet Step, Tolly's Rise, the Lamb Wall.

At the Wet Step she stopped, put one hoof in the water to prove it was wet, and went on, and forty animals lifted their feet over the same stones in the same order. A hollow the width of a goat ran through the gorse under the frost. Odile walked at the back with her hands in her pockets, saying the names under her breath and getting two of them wrong. The registrar walked beside the kids and wrote, after each waymark, a line.

Pruett had come, in the porridge-coloured waterproof, with his phone in his hand. At the Lamb Wall he stood and looked at it while the herd went past him, and then he read aloud, to nobody, a message that had come in at five.

PruettFrom my client. Seven good plots and a story no other cabins in the county have, beats eleven plots and a lawsuit. Sign it.

He dialled the other number. Illuminara, last in the line, heard only his half, which was enough: Yes. A registered lane. Seven plots. The ground above the wall out of the sale. A long listening. Forty. The kids go first. Another. He laughed once, unwillingly.

PruettShe will lend against a lane on the title, not against a surprise. And she wants to know whether they walk on Sundays.

Illuminara walked last of all, and was surprised by how much she minded being last. She had decoded a rhyme and found a map and lost an argument to a goat, and none of it had felt like this: a hill being gone up by those it belonged to, one name at a time, at the speed of the smallest.

At the Long Look Bracken stopped, and the herd stopped behind her. The whole dale lay below them in the first sun with its roofs smoking, and the registrar closed his notebook on the first entry of the next twenty years.

BrackenNow the hill knows who is coming.

TansyAgain?

BrackenAgain. Next spring. And the spring after.

07 · What the Assembly Left Open

Brannoch Dale assembly hall · noon

The assembly's question was whether forty goats were livestock or residents, and it spent an hour discovering that it had not been asked the right one. Odile Marrick stood up with no notes. She said the cooperative was not asking for a category. It was claiming the Common Way in the award of 1844 for its holding, with that morning's walk entered in the award book as use and the claim entered against the title before the lot was divided. It was covenanting that neither the Way nor the grass it went to would ever be sold, and that nothing on either would change until the herd's chosen speakers had been heard. She had filed the covenant that morning, with a hoof-print inked beside her signature, because Bracken had insisted on a mark.

The chair asked whether this decided what the goats were. Odile said it decided what they could count on. The assembly adjourned the other question, as she had hoped, and nobody much minded, since the hill was no longer for sale in the form that had made the question urgent. The cooperative kept the high pasture above the Lamb Wall in its own name, and the herd would go on grazing it as it always had, on ground the cooperative had bound itself never to sell. Pruett's client signed the amendment at the gate before ten: the lower meadow and seven plots, at a lower price, with the lane along the wall written into the title as the Common Way, and a lender who asked only that the spring walk be put in the brochure.

It cost something. Two members of the cooperative resigned that week, one of them a man who had wanted the sale money and who would not forgive Odile for choosing the goats' road over his drains. The question of what the herd was remained open, and Bracken's speakers would have to defend the covenant at the count for years.

That night in the byre Tansy said the count, the whole fourteen, and did not lose a name. Illuminara found she was saying it with her, under her breath, the way and not the goats. Odile stood in the doorway with the cooperative's book and no clipboard, and when the last name was done she wrote under the date, in her small square hand, Count taken.

Štirideset koz v hlevu v dolini je soglasno glasovalo za nekaj, česar nihče ne zna poimenovati, prodaja pa bo kmalu ogradila hrib; Illuminara preživi dva večera v slami, dokler ne zasliši, kaj glasovanje prevaja, in dovoli čredi, da popravi njen odgovor.

01 · Hlev

Kmetija Marrick, dolina Brannoch · večer, enajst dni pred zasedanjem

Sestanek so sklicale koze in Odile Marrick je hotela, da se to razume še pred vsem drugim. Sklicale so ga tako, da je vseh štirideset ob mraku vstopilo v hlev in obstalo v slami na potrpežljiv način živali, ki ljudi poslušajo že dolgo. Veterinarski poskus, ki je šel pred enajstimi leti narobe, jim je omogočil slediti argumentu. Ni pa jim podaril hitrosti.

OdileGlasovale so prejšnji torek. Vseh štirideset na levi strani hleva, nato pa jih je enajst prešlo na desno in nazaj, veterinar pa je to zapisal kot ponovno štetje. Mislim, da je bila šala.

IlluminaraZa kaj so glasovale?

Odile ji je podala veterinarjevo beležnico. V njej so bile tri zveze, prepisane v treh nočeh: hrib, štetje, vzpenjanje.

OdileSkupščina zaseda čez enajst dni, da odloči, ali so živina ali prebivalke. Zadruga je glasovala za prodajo visokega pašnika kot ene parcele prek gospoda Pruetta ljudem, ki želijo na njem postaviti koče. Prosili so me, naj predstavim stališče koz, jaz pa ga nimam. Imam tri zveze.

IlluminaraZakaj ste poslali pome?

OdileKer me je strah, da se bom zmotila v eno ali drugo smer. Če jim rečem osebe, jih lahko skupščina vzame kmetiji, ki jih ima rada. Če jim rečem živina, sem povedala natanko to, kar potrebuje prodaja. In štiridesetih živih bitij ne bom izročila sodišču na podlagi tega, kar je koza rekla v hlevu.

Na skrajnem koncu hleva je iz slame vstala stara koza s sivim gobcem, eno nogo za drugo, in prehodila vso dolžino poda. Druge so ji naredile prostor, ne da bi jih kdo prosil.

BrackenTi poslušaš. Sedi. Sedi dol. V slamo.

Illuminara je sedla. Videti je bilo, da je to prva točka dnevnega reda, vzdih, ki je šel skozi čredo, pa ji je povedal, da je pravilno uganila.

02 · Štetje

Hlev · drugi večer

Illuminara je v hlevu preživela dva večera, preden je kogarkoli karkoli vprašala. Odile je prosila, naj pride brez svoje podloge za papir, zato je Odile sedela na obrnjenem vedru pri vratih z izrazom nekje med sumničavostjo in olajšanjem.

Jedla je, kar so jedli kozlički: ovseno pogačo, stisnjeno z nečim grenkim in zelenim. Ugotovila je, da ji je všeč, kozličkom pa se je zdelo zelo zabavno, da ji je všeč. Spoznala je, da čreda ne govori toliko, kolikor si jemlje besedo: ena beseda, nato dovolj dolg premor za celo misel, nato druga. Spoznala je, da koza v pogovoru isto stvar pove trikrat, da nikomur ni treba vprašati dvakrat. Opazila je tudi, ne da bi zares opazila, da se je ob vsaki od treh zvez vsa čreda nekoliko nagnila proti vzhodnim vratom.

Pred spanjem so se kozlički igrali igro. Eden je izrekel ime, naslednji ga je ponovil in dodal še eno, in tako naprej po slami; majhen rjav kozliček z enim prepognjenim uhljem je vedno prišel najdlje.

TansyHlevska vrata. Razcepljeni jesen. Hlevska vrata, Razcepljeni jesen, Mokra stopnica. Hlevska vrata, Razcepljeni jesen, Mokra stopnica, Tollyjev vzpon.

IlluminaraKako se igra imenuje?

TansyŠtetje.

Izgovorila je tako, kakor otrok reče abeceda. Illuminara je sedela povsem pri miru, ker se ji je nekaj v glavi sprostilo in ni hotela, da pade s police.

Ne koze. Kraji.

IlluminaraTansy, kaj pride za Tollyjevim vzponom?

Iz slame je po vrsti prišlo štirinajst imen, zadnje za kraj, ki se je imenoval Dolgi razgled. Veterinar je zapisal tri zahteve. Bile so ena sama. Hrib je bil tam, kamor je vodila izštevanka. Štetje je bilo izštevanka. Vzpenjanje je bilo njeno prehojenje.

IlluminaraKdo te je naučil štetja?

TansyBracken. Bracknina mati. Mati Bracknine matere. Štetje.

03 · Register

Register doline Brannoch, zadnja soba · četrto jutro

Matičar je Odile poslušal brez besed, nato pa izvlekel ploski predal. Zemljevid iz odločbe o ograditvi iz leta 1844 je bil barve šibkega čaja, čez visoki svet pa je tekla pikčasta črta z napisom v pisavi, podobni bodeči žici: Skupna pot, kakor se uporablja od davnine, za vzpenjanje in spuščanje živine do skupne paše nad Jagnječjim zidom. Ob njej je bilo s svinčnikom označenih štirinajst mejnikov. Illuminara jih je enkrat prebrala na glas, Odile pa je sedla na zaboj z glavnimi knjigami.

OdileRazcepljeni jesen. Tollyjev vzpon. Moj ded je to govoril v jagnjetnici. Mislila sem, da je otroška izštevanka.

IlluminaraTo je popis. Odločba je le zapisala pot, ki je bila stara že takrat. Njene meje izgovarjajo že od časa pred črnilom in temu pravijo igra, ker jih nihče drug ni poslušal.

OdileZakaj je potem ni v Pruettovem naslovu?

MatičarKer sta dve glavni knjigi. Knjiga odločbe ohrani pravico živo z vpisom in z ničimer drugim. Zahtevek imetnika je vpis. Hoja, ki jo vpišem jaz ali imetnik, je vpis. Dvajset let brez enega in pravica ugasne. Pruettov naslov je vzet iz parcelnega registra, ta pa vsebuje le tisto, kar je imetnik vpisal ob parceli. Zadnji vpis v knjigi odločbe je star devetnajst let, hoja med tednom jagnjitev, ki jo je po naključju videl moj predhodnik. Poti ni še nihče vpisal ob zemljišče.

IlluminaraPravica je torej živa v eni knjigi in nevidna v drugi. Čreda je pot ohranila živo z nogami, papir pa jo je pustil utihniti. Na uri je ostalo enajst mesecev.

MatičarKoza pa zahtevka ne more vložiti. Prodajni pogoji so bili sestavljeni po registru, kakršen je.

Čez mizo je potisnil drugi list. Visoki pašnik je ponujal kot neobremenjeno enotno parcelo.

OdileTorej vložim zahtevek za posestvo, Pot se vpiše v naslov, preden se parcela razdeli, prodaja pa se ne more končati, kakor je zapisana. Toda za to moram reči, da jo uporablja čreda posestva. To je beseda, ki je niso hotele slišati. Nekaj, kar jim ljudje naredijo.

IlluminaraDa. Lahko bi zahtevek pripravila nocoj, bil bi pravilen in zmagal bi. Mislim, da najprej vprašamo.

OdileKoga?

IlluminaraTiste, katerih pot je.

04 · Popravek

Hlev · tisto noč

Razložila je počasi: stavek in nato čakanje, kolikor dolgo je bilo potrebno. Pot je bila v odločbi. Pravica je pripadala posestvu. Zadruga bi jo uveljavila, vzpenjanje črede bi veljalo kot uporaba in štirideset koz bi obdržalo hrib, ne da bi moral kdorkoli razsoditi, kaj so.

Načrt je bil dober. Bila je malce ponosna nanj in tega ni najbolje skrivala. Bracken ga je poslušala do konca. Nato je trikrat izrekla besedo, za katero je Illuminara upala, da je ne bo slišala.

BrackenNe. Ne. Ne.

IlluminaraPovej mi, kje je napačen.

BrackenZa teh štirideset. Štirideset jih umre, poti ni več. Ne za nas. Za kozličke, ki jih še ni. Za kogarkoli, ki je čreda.

Illuminarin ponos je iz nje ugasnil naenkrat, kar ga je nadomestilo, pa je bilo uporabnejše. Pravico je zapisala za živali pred seboj. Čreda je prosila za pot, ki jih bo preživela.

IlluminaraPravica pripada čredi, kdorkoli jo sestavlja. Rojeni kozlički, sprejeti potepuhi. Ne štirideset imen.

BrackenDobro. Pot do zaprtih vrat pa ni pot. Trava na njenem koncu je konec poti. Hočemo zaslišanje. Ko se pot spremeni, nas zadruga prešteje prve. Mi povemo. Povemo prej.

OdileHočete veto nad mojo zemljo?

BrackenNad potjo. Ne nad kmetijo. Pot je pot.

OdileIn nad tem, kamor vodi?

BrackenPot nekam vodi.

Odile je dolgo gledala staro kozo. Nato je pogledala v slamo, kjer je Tansy spala, usta pa so se ji še vedno premikala ob štetju.

OdilePotem prodaja izgubi vrh hriba. Trava nad Jagnječjim zidom ostane v lasti zadruge, zunaj vsake parcele, in to bom predložila ljudem, ki so glasovali za celoto. Zapisala bom več, kot ste zahtevale. Niti Pot niti trava, h kateri vodi, ne smeta biti nikoli prodani, na nobeni od njiju pa se nič ne spremeni, ne da bi prej zaslišali vaše govorke. Ne v slabem letu. Nikoli.

BrackenTo je več, kot smo zahtevale. Dobro. Ni dovolj. Pot, po kateri nihče ne hodi, je pot v predalu. Po poti je treba hoditi. Vsako pomlad. Kozlički spredaj. Če je prehojena in jo knjiga vidi, je uporabljena. Če je uporabljena, se ne izgubi. Hrib si zapomni, če hodimo.

Illuminara je to zapisala in razumela, kaj je Bracken pravkar naredila. Pravica je prišla na enajst mesecev do ugasnitve, ker je nihče ni mogel uveljaviti. Nikoli več se ji ne bo tako približala, saj bo vpis jutranja hoja, ki jo bo čreda opravila, ne glede na to, ali jo kdo prosi, matičar pa bo moral biti le tam, da jo vidi.

05 · Vrata

Vrata visokega pašnika · popoldne, štiri dni pred zasedanjem

Gospod Hale Pruett ni bil zlikovec, kar se je Illuminari zdelo neprijetno. Bil je urejen mož v nepremočljivi jakni barve ovsene kaše, zastopnik kupca, ki je plačal aro, s posojilodajalko, ki je za njim želela čist naslov, in z videzom človeka, ki je skrbno prebral veliko dokumentov, zdaj pa mu kažejo enega, ki ga ni bilo v spisu. Odločbo je prebral dvakrat.

PruettMojo stranko prosite, naj za vedno sprejme štirideset koz, ki dvakrat letno hodijo skozi njegov projekt, na podlagi otroške izštevanke.

IlluminaraNa podlagi odločbe, ki se z izštevanko ujema kamen za kamnom. Sinoči sem prehodila črto z dlanjo plosko v zraku. Stara brazda je še vedno tam pod uleksom, štiristo let iste teže na isti črti.

PruettParcela pa je prepolovljena.

IlluminaraJe. Trava nad Jagnječjim zidom se umakne iz prodaje. Vaša stranka obdrži spodnji travnik, dostop do ceste, vodo in sedem od enajstih parcel. Pot je štiri metre širok pas ob zidu, zunaj parcel, kartiran in vpisan v naslov prvi dan, namesto da ga marca odkrije odvetnica vaše posojilodajalke.

PruettCena pade.

IlluminaraPade. Posodila bo proti poti, ki jo lahko prebere. Ne more posoditi proti zahtevku v matičarjevem predalu, o katerem ji ni nihče povedal.

PruettKaj pa, če si koze premislijo?

IlluminaraPotem to s štetjem povedo zadrugi, preden se karkoli premakne. To je edina sprememba te poti, s katero boste kadarkoli imeli opravka, in prišla bo z obvestilom.

Nekaj časa je gledal v hrib.

PruettMoji gostje bodo spraševali, kaj je ta hrup.

IlluminaraDvakrat letno bo lep. Pripeljite posojilodajalko na hojo.

PruettZ ničimer ne soglašam. Kartirano pot, sedem parcel in hojo bom predstavil svoji stranki, oni pa bodo povedali svoje.

Na rob prodajnih pogojev je zapisal spomladanska hoja, jesenska hoja, tako pa skrben človek označi tisto, za kar pričakuje, da bo moral zagovarjati.

06 · Vzpenjanje

Skupna pot · zora, jutro zasedanja

V sivo jutro so se vzpenjali: štirideset koz, celotno članstvo zadruge in matičar z beležnico, Tansy pa spredaj, ker gredo kozlički prvi.

TansyHlevska vrata, Razcepljeni jesen, Mokra stopnica, Tollyjev vzpon, Jagnječji zid.

Pri Mokri stopnici se je ustavila, položila eno kopito v vodo, da bi dokazala, da je mokra, in nadaljevala; štirideset živali je dvignilo noge čez iste kamne v istem vrstnem redu. V uleksu je pod slano tekla vdolbina, široka kakor koza. Odile je hodila zadaj z rokami v žepih, si potiho ponavljala imena in dve izgovorila narobe. Matičar je hodil ob kozličkih in po vsakem mejniku zapisal vrstico.

Pruett je prišel v nepremočljivi jakni barve ovsene kaše in s telefonom v roki. Pri Jagnječjem zidu je obstal in ga gledal, medtem ko je čreda hodila mimo njega, nato pa je na glas, nikomur posebej, prebral sporočilo, ki je prišlo ob petih.

PruettOd moje stranke. Sedem dobrih parcel in zgodba, kakršne nima nobena druga koča v okrožju, je boljše od enajstih parcel in tožbe. Podpišite.

Poklical je drugo številko. Illuminara, zadnja v vrsti, je slišala le njegovo polovico, kar je zadoščalo: Da. Vpisana pot. Sedem parcel. Zemljišče nad zidom zunaj prodaje. Dolgo poslušanje. Štirideset. Kozlički gredo prvi. Še eno. Enkrat se je nehote zasmejal.

PruettPosodila bo proti poti v naslovu, ne proti presenečenju. In vedeti želi, ali hodijo ob nedeljah.

Illuminara je hodila čisto zadnja in presenetilo jo je, kako zelo jo je motilo biti zadnja. Razvozlala je izštevanko, našla zemljevid in izgubila argument s kozo, toda nič od tega se ni zdelo tako: hrib, po katerem se vzpenjajo tisti, ki jim pripada, eno ime za drugim, s hitrostjo najmanjšega.

Pri Dolgem razgledu se je Bracken ustavila, za njo pa čreda. Vsa dolina je ležala pod njimi v prvem soncu, iz streh se je kadilo, matičar pa je zaprl beležnico nad prvim vpisom naslednjih dvajsetih let.

BrackenZdaj hrib ve, kdo prihaja.

TansySpet?

BrackenSpet. Naslednjo pomlad. In pomlad za njo.

07 · Kar je skupščina pustila odprto

Skupščinska dvorana doline Brannoch · opoldne

Vprašanje skupščine je bilo, ali je štirideset koz živina ali prebivalke, in porabila je uro, da je odkrila, da ji niso postavili pravega vprašanja. Odile Marrick je vstala brez zapiskov. Povedala je, da zadruga ne prosi za kategorijo. Uveljavlja Skupno pot iz odločbe iz leta 1844 za svoje posestvo; jutranja hoja je bila v knjigo odločbe vpisana kot uporaba, zahtevek pa je bil vpisan ob naslovu, preden se je parcela razdelila. Zavezala se je, da niti Pot niti trava, h kateri vodi, ne bosta nikoli prodani in da se na nobeni nič ne bo spremenilo, dokler ne bodo zaslišane govorke, ki jih izbere čreda. Zavezo je vložila tisto jutro, z odtisom kopita ob svojem podpisu, ker je Bracken vztrajala pri znamenju.

Predsedujoči je vprašal, ali to odloča, kaj so koze. Odile je odgovorila, da odloča, na kaj se lahko zanesejo. Skupščina je drugo vprašanje preložila, kakor je upala, in to ni nikogar posebej motilo, saj hrib ni bil več naprodaj v obliki, zaradi katere je bilo vprašanje nujno. Zadruga je visoki pašnik nad Jagnječjim zidom obdržala v svojem imenu, čreda pa se bo na njem pasla naprej, kakor se je vedno, na zemljišču, za katero se je zadruga zavezala, da ga ne bo nikoli prodala. Pruettova stranka je spremembo podpisala pri vratih pred deseto: spodnji travnik in sedem parcel po nižji ceni, s pasom ob zidu, zapisanim v naslovu kot Skupna pot, in posojilodajalko, ki je zahtevala le, naj bo spomladanska hoja navedena v brošuri.

Nekaj je stalo. Tisti teden sta iz zadruge izstopila dva člana; eden je želel denar od prodaje in Odile ni mogel odpustiti, da je izbrala pot koz namesto njegovih odtokov. Vprašanje, kaj je čreda, je ostalo odprto, Bracknine govorke pa bodo morale zavezo ob štetju braniti še leta.

Tisto noč je Tansy v hlevu povedala celotno štetje, vseh štirinajst imen, in ni izgubila niti enega. Illuminara je ugotovila, da ga govori z njo, potiho, pot in ne koze. Odile je stala pri vratih z zadružno knjigo in brez podloge za papir; ko je bilo izrečeno zadnje ime, je pod datumom s svojo majhno oglato pisavo zapisala: Štetje opravljeno.

Illuminara learns that the herd's vote is a living survey and refuses to file the easy answer until Bracken corrects it; the goats retain a walked, registered road and its high pasture, while the cooperative, buyer and lender freely accept a smaller durable bargain with its costs disclosed.

A river god has not answered either of two opposing prayers in six weeks, and the valley is drying around its silence; nine days before the Lift, Illuminara walks the river with it and finds that nobody has ever asked for what they actually need.

01 · The Dry Bend

The Veshra bed below the old weir · dawn of the first day

Illuminara had been hired to measure a weir, and she had spent the night doing it: three sluice gates of black oak, the third rusted fast in its slot, a gauge post notched in hands from the pool floor to the lip. At first light she walked downstream to see where the water went, and the water went nowhere, because there was hardly any. The Veshra had shrunk to a brown thread. Where the bend should have run deep, something the height of a tall man stood in the cracked mud with its arms at its sides.

It looked like a very tired person. That was the kindest description she could make. Its edges were damp and did not hold.

OunYou are the survey. Pell said one would come. I would offer you water, but it is the one thing I am not giving anyone.

IlluminaraThen I'll offer you my name. Illuminara. Are you the river?

OunI am what answers to it. Oun. Six weeks I have heard two prayers and answered neither.

It opened one hand, and the two prayers came out of the air between them the way a name comes out of a crowd. From upstream, Upper Shale: Oun, lift the river, our seed is thirsty. From downstream, thinner and just as certain, Lowmere: Oun, hold the river, our eggs are in the gravel.

OunOne wants the river up and one wants it down. Do not tidy it. I have done that sum ten thousand times and it comes out as a drowned village.

She looked at the bed it stood in. Under the mud, in the shadow of a crack, ran a line of squared foundation stones.

OunAldmere. Two prayers then as well, and I chose. I reached past my banks to make the choosing good, and the river that reached came into its houses at night. I stand here because it is the one place that is entirely mine to be ashamed in.

IlluminaraWhere have you stood since?

OunNowhere. I am in the river, and I cannot see past the next bend of it. I hear prayers the way you would hear a shout from a house you have never been inside.

IlluminaraThen walk it with me. Source to sea, on foot. The Lift is nine days off and you have six weeks of silence, and I would like to see what each of them is praying for before either of us decides what you owe.

Oun looked at its own hand for a while, as if checking that it was still attached.

OunI have never walked it.

IlluminaraI know. Mind the cracks.

02 · Hill Water

The Upper Shale terraces · the second day, mid-morning

Six terrace lines climbed the hill above the weir, and the barley beds on them had gone the colour of old paper. Ketterin Osk met them at the lowest wall with a trowel in her belt and the stance of a woman who had been braced for visitors for six weeks. She saw the surveyor, not the damp tall shape at the surveyor's shoulder; Oun had asked to stay unseen until it knew what it was looking at.

Illuminara knelt and pushed her fingers into a bed. The crust broke in plates. Under it the soil was dry to the knuckle, then to the wrist.

Ketterin OskThe seed is gone by the sixth morning. Sown on the Lift's promise, like every year. My mother's mother lost a line to a late Lift and taught me to count mornings.

IlluminaraWhat would stop the count?

Ketterin OskWater standing a hand deep in the beds for five days, begun before the sixth morning. That is all the barley wants. The river is the only road we have ever had to ask for it, so we ask for the river.

Illuminara looked up the wall. At the top of every terrace a stone gutter ran from the hillside into the bed behind it, swept clean and bone dry.

IlluminaraSomebody keeps those swept.

Ketterin OskMy duty, from my grandmother's. Hill drains, for hill water. Rain has never come on the hill in my life. It comes up the river, if at all.

At Illuminara's shoulder, Oun made a sound like gravel settling, and spoke for her alone.

OunI do not rain on hills. A river god that rains on hills has forgotten where its banks are. That is how Aldmere began.

IlluminaraNobody has asked you to.

OunThen no one has asked for anything I could do.

She hasn't asked for a flood, Illuminara thought. She's asked for a number: a hand deep, five days. The flood is only the road she knew.

03 · Gravel

The Lowmere spawning channels · dawn of the third day

Lowmere's channels were shallow cuts of clean gravel beside the main bed, and under a hand of clear water the gravel glittered. Illuminara crouched before she understood why. Eggs, thousands of them, each the size of a lentil, each holding a dark fleck that would be a fish. She had watched galaxies resolve and had been steadier for it; this stopped her breath in a smaller, more dangerous way, as if she had stepped on something not meant to be seen and it had let her.

Daro Venn stood waist-deep at the channel mouth with a notched stick, reading the water the way a man reads a sleeping child's breathing.

Daro VennTwo hands of river at the weir, no more, and the channel runs gentle. Past two, the current lifts the gravel and the eggs go with it. Six days to hatch: the ninth morning. After that the fry need the river high, four hands for two days, to carry them over the bar before it closes. Everyone on the Veshra eats ashfin through the winter, even the ones upstream who think we steal their water.

Behind the surveyor, Oun was looking at the gravel. Illuminara had not seen it look at anything yet; it had only looked toward.

OunI have been a river for ten thousand years, and I have never once seen an egg.

IlluminaraYou were never asked to look.

OunI was asked to hold. I held. The barley wants a hand of water on a hill for five days. These want the river no higher than two until they hatch. Nobody has asked me for two things that cannot happen. They have asked me for one thing each, and I have heard them as a quarrel.

IlluminaraYes.

OunDo not look so pleased. I still cannot rain on a hill.

04 · Two Columns

The old weir, the gauge post · evening of the third day

Illuminara had chalked a slate and set it on the lip of the weir, and now four people stood around it in the last light: Ketterin Osk and Daro Venn, who had not stood within ten paces of each other since the spring, Pell the weir-keeper with his oil-can, and the surveyor. The sixth morning was three dawns off. Oun stood among them now, visible at last as a wet shimmer where the air was thicker. Nobody mentioned it. Everybody had decided not to be the first.

On the slate, in two columns:

Upper Shale: a hand of water standing in the beds, five days, begun before the sixth morning. Lowmere: the river at two hands or under until the ninth morning; then four hands for two days. A finger either way is the post breathing. Past that, stop.

Ketterin OskSo I am to trust that when my beds are wet your people will not simply open the weir and drain the pool.

Daro VennAnd I am to trust my eggs to rain on a hill that has never rained. Last Lift your canal-takers held the weir three days past the mark and my channel ran silt for a week.

Ketterin OskBecause your nets choked the tail.

IlluminaraI am not asking you to like each other. I am asking you to read two numbers off the same post. One of you stands at the pool and one at the tail. Over the line, either of you says stop. Not to me. To the water.

Ketterin OskI can say stop for my lines. I cannot say yes for them. That is a vote, and I will not put a god to them in the dark.

Daro VennNor I for the nets.

PellAnd who lifts gate three for the pulse? That gate has not moved in sixty years. If it lets go, it lets go all at once, onto Lowmere.

IlluminaraThen it will not be allowed to. Oak pins in the guide post, at three hands, three and a half, four. The gate rises to a pin and no further, and you pull the pin, not I. An hour's hold at each, and the tail reads before you draw the next. If either watcher says stop, your pawl drops it to the pin below and Oun draws the river back. Your gate, its water, their word.

PellIt is my gate, and I want it said.

Daro VennAnd if the god overshoots?

Oun spoke aloud for the first time to anyone but her. Its voice was low, and the pool shivered with it.

OunI have overshot once. I would rather not discover that I can do it twice. I will answer you tomorrow. First I must speak to the surveyor about my banks.

05 · Where My Banks Are

The weir top, night · the same evening

The pool was black and almost still. Pell had gone down to his gate with a lantern and his oil-can, muttering about slots. Oun stood at the edge of the stonework with its feet in the little water that remained.

OunYou have drawn two columns, and they fit. I can see that. Now I will tell you what the columns do not show. To rain on that hill, I must go past my banks, and I have done that once, and the village is a line of stones. Every mercy I give is a drought someone else is praying through. Tell me what you would give up.

Illuminara took the question as seriously as it was asked. She did not reach for comfort.

IlluminaraThe right to be the one who says where your banks are. I could. I could stand at the ridge and hold the border with my own body, and the rain would fall where I told it. And you would learn that someone else keeps your edges, and the next time no one was there, you would do what you did at Aldmere.

OunThen who keeps them?

IlluminaraThe two who pray against each other. One on each bank, every dawn, reading the post. You were never wrong to love both. You were alone with a border.

For a time Oun did not answer. Under the stone, water ticked.

OunThere is a term I will add. They say where my banks are, aloud, each dawn, before any rain. And either may say stop, and I will stop, and neither will need the other's leave. If only one can say it, it is a leash on the other. And they say the name first. Aldmere. Every dawn. I will not rain on a hill for a village that has been left out of the count.

IlluminaraThat is a better rule than mine.

OunI know. It is mine.

IlluminaraOne job I will do with my hands, and I say it now so nobody finds it out at the bend. If the flood comes to Aldmere with a head on it, it will swing for the oldest bed it remembers. I will go and look at what lies there. Whatever it is, it is timber or stone, not your border. Moving it is mine. Saying stop is theirs.

OunThen we look together.

Down at the third gate, the lantern flickered, and Pell's voice came up the stonework, flat and clear.

PellSlot is rough. I will not call it true until I have oiled it three nights. You will wait.

IlluminaraI will wait.

It was, she reflected, the most useful sentence anyone had said to her all week.

06 · The Count

The weir, the terraces and the tail · the fourth to the ninth day

The fourth day was for asking. Oun went up to the terrace-house at dusk and down to the net shed afterward, and said the same in both: what it would do, what it had done at Aldmere, and the word that would stop it. Both villages argued for the length of a lamp, and came to the post with their answers.

Ketterin OskUpper Shale says yes to five days, not to a season. Nine lines for, three against. The three want the watcher chosen again every Lift, not handed down like a trowel.

OunThen I am bound for a year, not an age. That is fair.

Daro VennFourteen nets say yes to the trial. Four say no, and will stand on the tail bank to watch, and I told them they may call stop as loud as I do. Old Maran's grandfather had a house at Aldmere. He wants the name said before the readings, not after. And the Lift is a second question. Lowmere will answer it on the ninth morning, with the eggs in front of it.

Ketterin OskThen the name first, and the Lift unpromised.

OunBoth.

On the fifth dawn Ketterin Osk stood on the pool bank and Daro Venn on the tail, forty paces of grey water between them, and neither would look first.

Daro VennAldmere.

Ketterin OskAldmere. Here, at the post. One hand.

Daro VennHere, at the tail. One hand and a finger.

Nothing happened for the space of ten breaths. Then the air over the Shale slope darkened along a line so straight that Illuminara laughed aloud. The rain fell as if drawn with a rule: heavy on the five upper terraces, nothing on the track beside them, a hard bright edge at the ridge where the cloud stopped as though it had been told. She stood on the weir with her head tipped back, a person watching weather do what weather did not do, wet to the collarbone and delighted.

The gutters, swept clean for three generations, ran for the first time in anyone's life. At the sixth dawn, the seed morning, Ketterin Osk's stake in the top bed stood a hand deep, and she cut the first of five notches into it. She walked the terraces from the top down, touching the walls, and stopped at the lowest. The sixth line sat in the lee of the ridge, and the rain that fed the five above it had passed overhead. She crouched there with her trowel and told the truth.

Ketterin OskThis one is lost. Half a soak is a rot.

Daro VennLowmere has seed barley in the granary. I will lend it to you for a second sowing.

Ketterin OskLend.

Daro VennA sack back in the autumn, and you hold the weir mark with me for a season.

Ketterin OskA sack and a half, and you keep your nets out of the tail.

Daro VennDone.

Illuminara said nothing, and thought it was the most hopeful bargain she had witnessed in a year of far larger ones.

The count held. On the seventh night the wind shifted and the cloud edge slid a hundred paces toward the river; at the post the gauge crept to two hands and a finger. Daro Venn did not wait for anyone. He called into the dark.

Daro VennStop.

The rain stopped. It stopped in the middle of a drop, Ketterin Osk said afterwards, who had been under it.

Ketterin OskIt did not even ask me.

Daro VennIt did not ask me either. That was the term.

At the eighth dawn they chalked the ridge on the post, so that both of them could read the cloud, and began again, a morning's rain only. The tail read one hand and two fingers; the stake, a hand and a finger, and a third notch. On the ninth morning Daro Venn knelt in the gravel and held his stick very still. In every egg a dark fleck had grown a tail, and the tails were moving.

07 · The Lift

The old weir and the Aldmere bend · noon of the tenth day to noon of the twelfth

Pell had called the slot true on the seventh morning, before witnesses, so that it could not later be said otherwise, and had oiled it every night since. The three oak pins sat in the guide post. On the ninth evening Illuminara and Oun had walked the Aldmere bend together and found what the river would swing toward: a jam of drowned timber in the old street-bed, heavy as a barn roof. It was on the slate now, under the two columns: Jam: I lift it at the second hold, before the head comes. Stop is theirs. Lowmere had answered the Lift that morning, eleven nets to seven. The seven stood on the tail bank with their hands raised to say stop, and none of them did.

PellFirst pin.

He drew it. The gate rose a third of its span and stopped on the next, and sixty years of rust gave up along a line Illuminara could have drawn with her eyes shut. The pool ran out under it, brown and then white.

Ketterin OskThree hands.

Daro VennThree. The gravel is staying.

They held an hour. At the second pin, with the river at three and a half, Illuminara went down the bank in four strides and stood in the Aldmere bend. The water leaned on her. She took the jam in both hands, the great sodden mass of it, and set it on the bank with a care she would have used for a sleeping animal.

Oun stood at the stones beside her and did not move.

OunIt wanted to swing there. I could feel it wanting.

The river stood at three and a half for the second hour. Then Daro Venn waded out to the tail mark, read his stick against the post, and called it across the water.

Daro VennThree and a half at the tail, and the gravel holding. Lowmere says proceed.

Ketterin OskUpper Shale says proceed. We are not past a finger.

PellPawl is set. If either of you says stop, it drops the gate to this pin before the word is out, and Oun needs one breath to draw the river back. Third pin.

At the third pin the head of the flood came down, and found no door where it had expected one, and ran between its banks.

Ketterin OskFour hands!

Daro VennFour and a finger! That is the post breathing. Say it again anyway!

Ketterin OskFour and a finger! Here! This is the bank!

Daro VennAnd here!

OunI felt it. I felt where the banks were. They were not mine. They were being said.

Down the Lowmere channels went a silver thread of fry, carried out on the Lift, over the bar, into the lagoon. Both villages had come down to the water, and for the first time in six weeks they prayed in one voice, not for the river up or the river down, but for the river to stay where it was told.

The pulse held through the night. On the eleventh dawn Ketterin Osk read her stake before she read the post: five notches, a hand deep, five days standing. At noon of the twelfth day Pell let the gate down pin by pin, and Oun drew the river in behind it, and the tail read two hands, and the fry were over the bar.

By dusk the sixth line stood bare and dark, ready for a second sowing in lent seed, and on the dry bend where Aldmere had been, someone had begun to set a stone upright, and someone else had begun to chalk a name on it, and neither of them was the same someone.

OunSay it again, tomorrow, at dawn.

Ketterin OskAldmere. Here.

Daro VennAldmere. And here.

IlluminaraAnd Aldmere.

Oun looked at the three of them for a long time, with the plain astonishment of a being that has just seen the other side of its own river, and then it walked downstream to find out what was past the next bend.

Rečni bog že šest tednov ni odgovoril na nobeno od dveh nasprotujočih si molitev in dolina se suši okoli njegovega molka; devet dni pred Dvigom Illuminara z njim prehodi reko in odkrije, da nihče še nikoli ni prosil za tisto, kar v resnici potrebuje.

01 · Suhi zavoj

Struga Veshre pod starim jezom · svit prvega dne

Illuminara je bila najeta, da izmeri jez, in s tem je preživela noč: tri zapornice iz črnega hrasta, tretja zarjavela in negibno ujeta v svojem utoru, merilni steber z zarezami v dlaneh od dna tolmuna do roba. Ob prvi svetlobi je odšla po toku navzdol, da bi videla, kam odteka voda, vendar voda ni odtekala nikamor, ker je skoraj ni bilo. Veshra se je skrčila v rjavo nit. Tam, kjer bi moral biti zavoj globok, je v razpokani glini z rokama ob telesu stalo nekaj, visoko kakor visok človek.

Videti je bilo kakor zelo utrujen človek. To je bil najprijaznejši opis, ki ga je zmogla. Njegovi robovi so bili vlažni in niso držali oblike.

OunTi si meritev. Pell je rekel, da bo nekdo prišel. Ponudil bi ti vodo, vendar je to edino, česar ne dajem nikomur.

IlluminaraPotem ti ponudim svoje ime. Illuminara. Si ti reka?

OunJaz sem tisto, kar se odzove nanjo. Oun. Šest tednov poslušam dve molitvi in nisem odgovoril na nobeno.

Razprl je dlan in molitvi sta se pojavili v zraku med njima tako, kakor se iz množice pojavi ime. Od zgoraj, iz Upper Shale: Oun, dvigni reko, naše seme je žejno. Od spodaj, iz Lowmere, tišja in prav tako odločna: Oun, zadrži reko, naše ikre so v produ.

OunEni hočejo reko višje, drugi nižje. Ne olepšuj tega. Ta račun sem izračunal deset tisočkrat in rezultat je utopljena vas.

Pogledala je strugo, v kateri je stal. Pod glino je v senci razpoke tekla vrsta klesanih temeljnih kamnov.

OunAldmere. Tudi tedaj sta bili dve molitvi in izbral sem. Segel sem prek svojih bregov, da bi bila izbira dobra, reka, ki sem jo poslal, pa je ponoči vstopila v njihove hiše. Tu stojim, ker je to edini kraj, kjer je moj sram povsem moj.

IlluminaraKje si stal od takrat?

OunNikjer. Sem v reki in ne vidim čez njen naslednji zavoj. Molitve slišim tako, kakor bi ti slišala krik iz hiše, v kateri še nikoli nisi bila.

IlluminaraPotem jo prehodi z menoj. Od izvira do morja, peš. Do Dviga je devet dni, za teboj pa je šest tednov molka; rada bi videla, za kaj pravzaprav molijo, preden se kdorkoli od naju odloči, kaj jim dolguješ.

Oun je nekaj časa gledal svojo dlan, kakor da preverja, ali je še vedno pritrjena nanj.

OunNikoli je nisem prehodil.

IlluminaraVem. Pazi na razpoke.

02 · Voda za hrib

Terase Upper Shale · drugi dan, sredi dopoldneva

Šest vrst teras se je vzpenjalo po hribu nad jezom, ječmenove grede na njih pa so dobile barvo starega papirja. Ketterin Osk ju je pričakala pri najnižjem zidu z zidarsko lopatico za pasom in držo ženske, ki se je šest tednov pripravljala na obiskovalce. Videla je geodetinjo, ne pa vlažne visoke postave ob njeni rami; Oun je prosil, naj ostane neviden, dokler ne bo razumel, kaj gleda.

Illuminara je pokleknila in porinila prste v gredo. Skorja se je lomila v ploščah. Pod njo je bila zemlja suha do členkov, nato do zapestja.

Ketterin OskSeme je izgubljeno do šestega jutra. Posejano je bilo na obljubo Dviga, kakor vsako leto. Mati moje matere je zaradi poznega Dviga izgubila eno vrsto in me naučila šteti jutra.

IlluminaraKaj bi ustavilo štetje?

Ketterin OskVoda, ki bi pet dni stala eno dlan globoko v gredah in bi prišla pred šestim jutrom. To je vse, kar ječmen potrebuje. Reka je edina pot, po kateri smo lahko kadar koli prosili zanjo, zato prosimo za reko.

Illuminara je pogledala po zidu navzgor. Na vrhu vsake terase je kamnit žleb vodil s pobočja v gredo za njim, pometen do čistega in suh kakor kost.

IlluminaraNekdo skrbi, da so ti žlebovi pometeni.

Ketterin OskMoja dolžnost, podedovana od babice. Hribovski odtoki za hribovsko vodo. Dež na hribu ni padel še nikoli v mojem življenju. Če sploh pride, pride po reki navzgor.

Ob Illuminarini rami je Oun zazvenel kakor polegajoči se prod in spregovoril samo zanjo.

OunNa hribih ne dežujem. Rečni bog, ki dežuje na hribih, je pozabil, kje so njegovi bregovi. Tako se je začel Aldmere.

IlluminaraNihče te ni prosil za to.

OunPotem nihče ni prosil za nič, kar bi lahko storil.

Ni prosila za poplavo, je pomislila Illuminara. Prosila je za število: dlan globoko, pet dni. Poplava je bila le edina pot, ki jo je poznala.

03 · Prod

Drstitveni kanali Lowmere · svit tretjega dne

Kanali Lowmere so bili plitve zareze čistega proda ob glavni strugi in prod se je bleščal pod dlanjo bistre vode. Illuminara je počepnila, preden je razumela zakaj. Ikre, na tisoče, vsaka velika kakor leča in v vsaki temna pikica, iz katere bo nastala riba. Opazovala je razreševanje galaksij in pri tem ostala mirnejša; to ji je vzelo sapo na manjši, nevarnejši način, kakor da je stopila na nekaj, česar ne bi smela videti, pa ji je to dovolilo.

Daro Venn je stal do pasu v vodi ob ustju kanala z zarezano palico in bral vodo tako, kakor človek bere dihanje spečega otroka.

Daro VennDve dlani reke pri jezu, nič več, pa kanal teče nežno. Nad dvema tok dvigne prod in ikre odnese z njim. Šest dni do izvalitve: deveto jutro. Nato mladice potrebujejo visoko reko, štiri dlani dva dni, da jih ponese čez pregrado, preden se zapre. Vsi ob Veshri pozimi jedo pepelne ribe, tudi tisti zgoraj, ki mislijo, da jim krademo vodo.

Za geodetinjo je Oun gledal prod. Illuminara ga še ni videla pogledati ničesar; doslej je gledal le proti nečemu.

OunReka sem že deset tisoč let in še nikoli nisem videl ikre.

IlluminaraNikoli te niso prosili, da pogledaš.

OunProsili so me, naj zadržim. Zadržal sem. Ječmen potrebuje dlan vode na hribu pet dni. Te ikre potrebujejo reko največ dve dlani visoko, dokler se ne izvalijo. Nihče me ni prosil za dve stvari, ki se ne moreta zgoditi. Vsak me je prosil za eno stvar, jaz pa sem ju slišal kot prepir.

IlluminaraDa.

OunNe bodi videti tako zadovoljna. Še vedno ne morem deževati na hribu.

04 · Dva stolpca

Stari jez, merilni steber · večer tretjega dne

Illuminara je s kredo popisala tablico in jo postavila na rob jezu, zdaj pa so v zadnji svetlobi okoli nje stali štirje: Ketterin Osk in Daro Venn, ki od pomladi nista stala manj kot deset korakov drug od drugega, jezovni čuvaj Pell s svojo oljnico in geodetinja. Do šestega jutra so ostali trije sviti. Oun je zdaj stal med njimi, naposled viden kot moker migljaj, kjer je bil zrak gostejši. Nihče tega ni omenil. Vsi so se odločili, da ne bodo prvi.

Na tablici, v dveh stolpcih:

Upper Shale: dlan vode, ki pet dni stoji v gredah, z začetkom pred šestim jutrom. Lowmere: reka pri dveh dlaneh ali nižje do devetega jutra; nato štiri dlani za dva dni. Prst v eno ali drugo smer je dihanje stebra. Čez to mejo se ustavi.

Ketterin OskTorej naj zaupam, da vaši ljudje, ko bodo moje grede mokre, ne bodo preprosto odprli jezu in izpraznili tolmuna.

Daro VennJaz pa naj svoje ikre zaupam dežju na hribu, kjer še nikoli ni deževalo. Ob zadnjem Dvigu so vaši upravljavci kanalov zadrževali jez odprt tri dni čez oznako in moj kanal je teden dni nosil mulj.

Ketterin OskKer so vaše mreže zadušile odtok.

IlluminaraNe prosim vaju, da se imata rada. Prosim vaju, da odčitata dve števili z istega stebra. Eden stoji pri tolmunu, drugi pri iztoku. Če gre čez črto, lahko kdorkoli od vaju reče stop. Ne meni. Vodi.

Ketterin OskZa svoje vrste lahko rečem stop. Ne morem pa namesto njih reči da. O tem se glasuje in boga jim ne bom pripeljala v temi.

Daro VennTudi jaz ne bom govoril za ribiče.

PellIn kdo dvigne tretjo zapornico za val? Ta vrata se niso premaknila šestdeset let. Če popustijo, popustijo vsa naenkrat, naravnost proti Lowmere.

IlluminaraTega jim ne bomo dovolili. Hrastovi zatiči v vodilnem stebru, pri treh dlaneh, treh in pol, štirih. Zapornica se dvigne do zatiča in nič dlje, zatič pa izvlečeš ti, ne jaz. Na vsaki stopnji eno uro zadržimo in iztok se odčita, preden izvlečeš naslednjega. Če katerikoli opazovalec reče stop, tvoja zaskočka spusti zapornico do zatiča pod njo, Oun pa reko potegne nazaj. Tvoja vrata, njegova voda, njuna beseda.

PellTo so moja vrata in hočem, da je to izrečeno.

Daro VennKaj pa, če bog preseže mero?

Oun je prvič spregovoril na glas komurkoli razen njej. Njegov glas je bil globok in tolmun se je ob njem stresel.

OunEnkrat sem presegel mero. Raje ne bi odkril, da to zmorem dvakrat. Odgovoril vam bom jutri. Najprej moram z geodetinjo govoriti o svojih bregovih.

05 · Kje so moji bregovi

Vrh jezu, noč · isti večer

Tolmun je bil črn in skoraj negiben. Pell je odšel k zapornici z laterno in oljnico ter mrmral o utorih. Oun je stal na robu kamnitega zidu z nogami v tisti mali količini vode, ki je še ostala.

OunNarisala si dva stolpca in ujemata se. To vidim. Zdaj ti bom povedal, česa stolpca ne kažeta. Da dežujem na tistem hribu, moram iti prek svojih bregov; to sem že storil in vas je postala vrsta kamnov. Vsaka milost, ki jo dam, je suša, skozi katero moli nekdo drug. Povej mi, čemu bi se ti odpovedala.

Illuminara je vprašanje vzela tako resno, kakor je bilo zastavljeno. Ni segla po tolažbi.

IlluminaraPravici, da jaz odločam, kje so tvoji bregovi. Lahko bi. Lahko bi stala na grebenu in mejo držala z lastnim telesom, dež pa bi padal, kamor bi mu ukazala. Ti bi se naučil, da nekdo drug varuje tvoje robove, in naslednjič, ko tam ne bi bilo nikogar, bi storil to, kar si storil Aldmereju.

OunKdo jih bo potem varoval?

IlluminaraTista dva, ki molita drug proti drugemu. Vsak na svojem bregu, vsako jutro, ko bereta steber. Nikoli se nisi motil, ker si imel rad oba. Le sam si bil z mejo.

Oun nekaj časa ni odgovoril. Pod kamnom je kapljala voda.

OunDodal bom pogoj. Vsako jutro pred dežjem na glas povesta, kje so moji bregovi. Kdorkoli lahko reče stop, jaz pa bom ustavil, ne da bi potreboval dovoljenje drugega. Če to lahko reče samo eden, je to povodec na drugem. In najprej izgovorita ime. Aldmere. Vsako jutro. Ne bom deževal na hribu za vas, ki je bila izpuščena iz štetja.

IlluminaraTo je boljše pravilo od mojega.

OunVem. Moje je.

IlluminaraEno delo bom opravila s svojimi rokami in to povem zdaj, da tega nihče ne odkrije šele na zavoju. Če poplavni val pride do Aldmereja z grebenom, bo zavil proti najstarejši strugi, ki se je spomni. Šla bom pogledat, kaj leži tam. Karkoli je, je les ali kamen, ne tvoja meja. Premakniti to je moje delo. Reči stop je njuno.

OunPotem pogledava skupaj.

Spodaj pri tretji zapornici je laterna zatrepetala in Pellov glas se je po kamnitem zidu dvignil raven in jasen.

PellUtor je hrapav. Ne bom rekel, da je varen, dokler ga ne bom mazal tri noči. Počakali boste.

IlluminaraPočakala bom.

Pomislila je, da je bil to najkoristnejši stavek, ki ji ga je kdorkoli izrekel ves teden.

06 · Štetje

Jez, terase in iztok · od četrtega do devetega dne

Četrti dan je bil namenjen vprašanjem. Oun je ob mraku odšel do hiše na terasi in nato do ribiške lope ter v obeh krajih povedal isto: kaj bo storil, kaj je storil Aldmereju in katera beseda ga bo ustavila. Obe vasi sta se prepirali ves čas gorenja ene svetilke, nato pa prišli k stebru s svojima odgovoroma.

Ketterin OskUpper Shale je rekel da petim dnem, ne celemu letnemu času. Devet vrst za, tri proti. Tiste tri hočejo, da opazovalca ob vsakem Dvigu izberemo znova, ne pa da se dolžnost deduje kakor zidarska lopatica.

OunPotem sem zavezan za eno leto, ne za večnost. To je pravično.

Daro VennŠtirinajst ribičev je za preizkus. Štirje so proti in bodo stali na bregu pri iztoku ter opazovali; povedal sem jim, da lahko zavpijejo stop prav tako glasno kakor jaz. Ded starega Marana je imel hišo v Aldmereju. Hoče, da ime izgovorimo pred odčitki, ne po njih. Dvig pa je drugo vprašanje. Lowmere bo nanj odgovoril deveto jutro, pred ikrami.

Ketterin OskPotem najprej ime, Dvig pa ni obljubljen.

OunOboje.

Ob petem svitu je Ketterin Osk stala na bregu tolmuna, Daro Venn pa pri iztoku; med njima je bilo štirideset korakov sive vode in nobeden ni hotel pogledati prvi.

Daro VennAldmere.

Ketterin OskAldmere. Tukaj, pri stebru. Ena dlan.

Daro VennTukaj, pri iztoku. Ena dlan in en prst.

Deset vdihov se ni zgodilo nič. Nato je zrak nad pobočjem Shale potemnel po črti, tako ravni, da se je Illuminara glasno zasmejala. Dež je padal, kakor bi bil narisan z ravnilom: močno na pet zgornjih teras, nič na stezo ob njih, oster svetel rob na grebenu, kjer se je oblak ustavil, kakor bi mu nekdo tako ukazal. Stala je na jezu z glavo nagnjeno nazaj, človek, ki gleda vreme početi tisto, česar vreme ne počne, mokra do ključnice in navdušena.

Žlebovi, tri generacije pometani do čistega, so prvič v življenju kogarkoli stekli. Ob šestem svitu, jutru semena, je kol Ketterin Osk v najvišji gredi stal dlan globoko in vanj je zarezala prvo od petih zarez. Prehodila je terase od vrha navzdol, se dotikala zidov in se ustavila pri najnižji. Šesta vrsta je ležala v zavetrju grebena in dež, ki je napajal pet višjih, je šel čeznjo. Počepnila je s svojo lopatico in povedala resnico.

Ketterin OskTa je izgubljena. Polovična namočitev pomeni gnitje.

Daro VennLowmere ima semenski ječmen v kašči. Posodil ti ga bom za drugo setev.

Ketterin OskPosodil.

Daro VennJeseni vrneš vrečo in eno sezono z menoj držiš jezovno oznako.

Ketterin OskVrečo in pol, ti pa svoje mreže umakneš iz iztoka.

Daro VennDogovorjeno.

Illuminara ni rekla ničesar in pomislila je, da je bil to najbolj obetaven dogovor, ki mu je bila priča v letu veliko večjih dogovorov.

Štetje je držalo. Sedmo noč se je veter obrnil in rob oblaka je zdrsnil sto korakov proti reki; pri stebru se je merilnik povzpel do dveh dlani in enega prsta. Daro Venn ni čakal nikogar. Zaklical je v temo.

Daro VennStop.

Dež je prenehal. Ustavil se je sredi kaplje, je pozneje povedala Ketterin Osk, ki je stala pod njim.

Ketterin OskNiti vprašal me ni.

Daro VennTudi mene ni vprašal. Tak je bil pogoj.

Ob osmem svitu sta na steber s kredo narisala greben, da bi oba lahko brala oblak, in začela znova, samo za eno dopoldne dežja. Iztok je kazal eno dlan in dva prsta; kol dlan in en prst ter tretjo zarezo. Deveto jutro je Daro Venn pokleknil v produ in svojo palico držal povsem mirno. V vsaki ikri je temni pikici zrasel rep in repi so se premikali.

07 · Dvig

Stari jez in zavoj pri Aldmereju · od poldneva desetega dne do poldneva dvanajstega

Pell je sedmo jutro pred pričami razglasil utor za varnega, da pozneje ne bi mogel nihče trditi drugače, in odtlej ga je mazal vsako noč. Trije hrastovi zatiči so sedeli v vodilnem stebru. Deveti večer sta Illuminara in Oun skupaj prehodila zavoj pri Aldmereju in našla tisto, proti čemur bi reka zavila: gmoto potopljenega lesa v stari ulični strugi, težko kakor streha skednja. Zdaj je bilo zapisano na tablici pod obema stolpcema: Zastoj: dvignem ga ob drugem zadržku, preden pride greben vala. Stop je njun. Lowmere je tisto jutro odgovoril na vprašanje o Dvigu, enajst ribičev proti sedmim. Sedmerica je stala na bregu pri iztoku z dvignjenimi rokami, pripravljena reči stop, vendar ni tega rekel nihče.

PellPrvi zatič.

Izvlekel ga je. Zapornica se je dvignila za tretjino svoje višine in se ustavila na naslednjem, šestdeset let rje pa je popustilo vzdolž črte, ki bi jo Illuminara lahko narisala z zaprtimi očmi. Tolmun je pod njo stekel, najprej rjav in nato bel.

Ketterin OskTri dlani.

Daro VennTri. Prod ostaja na mestu.

Zadržali so eno uro. Pri drugem zatiču, ko je bila reka pri treh dlaneh in pol, je Illuminara v štirih korakih prišla po bregu navzdol in stopila v zavoj pri Aldmereju. Voda se je uprla vanjo. Z obema rokama je prijela zastoj, veliko premočeno gmoto, in jo položila na breg tako previdno, kakor bi ravnala s spečo živaljo.

Oun je stal pri kamnih ob njej in se ni premaknil.

OunHotela je zaviti tja. Čutil sem, kako je hotela.

Reka je drugo uro stala pri treh dlaneh in pol. Nato je Daro Venn zabredel do oznake pri iztoku, odčital svojo palico glede na steber in zaklical čez vodo.

Daro VennTri in pol pri iztoku, prod drži. Lowmere dovoli nadaljevanje.

Ketterin OskUpper Shale dovoli nadaljevanje. Meje nismo presegli niti za prst.

PellZaskočka je nastavljena. Če kdorkoli od vaju reče stop, spusti zapornico do tega zatiča, še preden je beseda izrečena do konca, Oun pa potrebuje en vdih, da reko potegne nazaj. Tretji zatič.

Pri tretjem zatiču je prišel greben poplavnega vala, ni našel vrat tam, kjer jih je pričakoval, in stekel je med bregovoma.

Ketterin OskŠtiri dlani!

Daro VennŠtiri in en prst! To je dihanje stebra. Vseeno povej še enkrat!

Ketterin OskŠtiri in en prst! Tukaj! To je breg!

Daro VennIn tukaj!

OunČutil sem ga. Čutil sem, kje so bregovi. Niso bili moji. Izgovarjali so jih.

Po kanalih Lowmere je stekla srebrna nit mladic, ki jih je Dvig ponesel čez pregrado in v laguno. Obe vasi sta prišli k vodi in prvič v šestih tednih molili z enim glasom: ne za reko višje ali reko nižje, temveč naj reka ostane tam, kjer ji je bilo rečeno.

Val je držal vso noč. Ob enajstem svitu je Ketterin Osk prebrala svoj kol, preden je prebrala steber: pet zarez, dlan globoko, pet dni stoječe vode. Opoldne dvanajstega dne je Pell spustil zapornico zatič za zatičem, Oun je za njo povlekel reko vase, iztok je kazal dve dlani in mladice so bile čez pregrado.

Do mraka je šesta vrsta stala gola in temna, pripravljena na drugo setev s posojenim semenom; na suhem zavoju, kjer je nekoč stal Aldmere, je nekdo začel postavljati kamen pokonci, nekdo drug pa nanj s kredo pisati ime, in to nista bila ista človeka.

OunJutri ob svitu povejte še enkrat.

Ketterin OskAldmere. Tukaj.

Daro VennAldmere. In tukaj.

IlluminaraIn Aldmere.

Oun jih je dolgo gledal z odkritim začudenjem bitja, ki je pravkar videlo drugo stran lastne reke, nato pa je odšel po toku navzdol, da bi izvedel, kaj leži za naslednjim zavojem.

Illuminara helps Oun understand that the two villages are asking for bounded, measurable needs rather than a divine choice between winners, then protects a staged and freely governed release in which Oun, both communities and Pell retain the right to stop.
