Sael has lit three inhabited moons for six billion years. In nineteen days the conscious star intends to spend itself in a flare that will seed a silent nebula—and strip eight billion living people from the worlds already in its light. Illuminara must protect the present without turning a godlike parent into a prisoner.

01 · Nineteen Days of Light

Assembly vault beneath Lume, innermost moon of Orison · Nineteen days before flare threshold

Sael filled half the sky through the vault's polar glass. The old star was amber at its quiet edge and white where a magnetic arch rose six hundred thousand kilometres above the surface. Every eleven minutes the arch brightened. Every eleven minutes the vault floor gave a low answering hum, as if the moon had become a tuning fork held against a god's throat.

Eight billion people lived on Lume, Vey and cold Harrow. Their governments had sent twelve delegates, four admirals and one empty chair for the being they had only learned to hear three days ago.

The empty chair spoke first. Its voice came from helioseismic tones translated by instruments around all three moons. The words were not perfectly timed. Sael began some sentences before the translator finished the last, because a star did not think in the order a room preferred.

SaelNineteen of your days remain before I cross the useful threshold. Remove your ships from the eastern magnetic road. The particles there will be needed elsewhere.

Minister Aro Venn laid both hands on a black case beside him. Inside it rested the authorization keys for the Quiet Crown, a belt of superconducting stations designed to flatten Sael's magnetic speech and hold the flare below ignition.

Aro VennNeeded to kill us.

SaelNeeded to make what comes after me possible.

Behind the delegates, a wall map showed the neighboring Oriel Nebula: a dark red wound seven light-years long, rich in hydrogen and poor in everything that could build rock, water or blood. Sael's models said a narrow stream of carbon, oxygen and iron could change that. The same ejection, released all at once, would peel the atmospheres from the moons before it left Orison.

Illuminara stood between the case and the empty chair. She could feel the forces the instruments rendered as coloured lines: the pressure gathering below Sael's photosphere, the magnetic cage waking station by station, the small trembling loads in the vault's roof. Force was legible. Intention was not.

IlluminaraMy aim is plain. The three moons keep their atmospheres and every person gets the chance to live. Sael keeps the right to choose what its death means. I will not trade one of those for the other before I understand what is actually required.

Aro opened the black case. The keys were ordinary metal, worn at the edges by rehearsals nobody had expected to use.

Aro VennA conscious catastrophe is still a catastrophe. The Crown buys us eighty years. In eighty years we can evacuate or learn to govern it safely.

SaelYou have consumed my light for six billion years and call another eighty years restraint. The nebula has waited without a voice. Its worlds cannot petition your assembly because I have not yet made them.

IlluminaraAnd the people under your light? What are they to you?

A chain of sunspots crossed Sael's face. The translator hesitated, discarded two approximations and chose a third.

SaelPassengers. Beautiful ones. Brief ones. They built homes on stones that circle me. They did not ask what I meant to build.

The word passengers moved through the chamber more dangerously than the rising magnetic arch. Harrow's delegate left his seat. In the public gallery, foundry workers began shouting. Aro's thumb settled over the first key.

Illuminara did not ask them to forgive the word. She asked the roof to hold while the shouting found its shape, setting one hand against the vault's central spar as the old stone took a thermal jolt from Sael's brightening arch. Her strength kept dust from falling. It did not make anyone agree.

Wren Odira placed a small mechanical clock on the table. Deep contact with Sael would fold Illuminara's protection inward. During it, she could not hold the vault, stop the Crown or shield a moon. The clock's red hand was set to eight minutes.

WrenEight minutes. At seven I call you. At eight I pull the solar link, whether the star has finished its sentence or not.

Aro VennAnd while you listen, what stops it crossing the threshold?

SaelI do.

For the first time, the translator caught something like anger without delay.

IlluminaraThen that is the first thing you can do for the living: hold the arch for eight minutes because you choose to, not because the Crown makes you. If you cannot, there is no conversation to enter.

Sael's arch continued to rise for six long seconds. Then it bent sideways, poured its fire into a harmless loop and dimmed.

Aro removed his thumb from the key. He did not close the case.

SaelEight minutes. Do not ask me to pretend silence is not a life merely because it has not begun.

02 · The Silent Shore

Solar observatory Thren, high orbit above Sael · Seventeen days before threshold

The wide window opened only after Sael accepted its terms in three different forms: a magnetic sequence it could verify, a spoken explanation from Illuminara, and the uninterrupted right to end contact. Wren waited outside with the red clock. Aro waited beside the Crown controls. No fleet moved toward the star.

Illuminara entered no human room. She found pressure, convection and time. Sael's thought lived in loops that took weeks to rise and centuries to close. The window did not compress them into human memory; it let her stand near their scale without claiming it as her own.

She saw Orison before the moons had cooled: dark stones crossing a young star's light. She felt six billion years of fusion turn simple matter into the heavier elements Sael carried in its core and shell. Far beyond the system lay Oriel, a cold shore that gathered hydrogen, lost it, gathered it again. In Sael's long attention the nebula was not empty. It was unfinished.

No future people appeared. The field could not certify them. There were only models, patience and Sael's fierce interpretation of what a star owed the universe.

SaelYou will say they are imaginary because they cannot answer.

IlluminaraNo. I will say possibility is not permission to kill. Those are different claims.

A convective wall turned beneath them. Its sound was the sound of a continent boiling.

SaelYour moons cut metals from my children before they cool. They net my wind. They drink the gradient between my heat and their night. They call this living. When I spend what I made on a future they cannot own, they call it death.

IlluminaraThey call eight billion deaths death. You keep changing the scale so you do not have to use the number.

The window narrowed. For an instant Illuminara felt Sael preparing to end it. She did not reach for the star's inner force or widen the contact without consent.

SaelEight billion present voices against uncounted silent ones. Your arithmetic has already chosen its favorite tense.

It was Sael's strongest argument, and it was not foolish. Every assembly in Orison could promise only the safety of voters who already existed. A magnetic cage would preserve them by taking the only generative choice Sael believed remained. Simple persuasion would ask a being older than their species to treat a century as morally serious while refusing to treat a million years that way.

Illuminara stopped arguing with the flare and examined its work. Sael had shaped it as a broad shell. The breadth was not needed to reach Oriel; it kept the heavy elements together after they crossed the system's chaotic wind. Along the shell's inner edge, each emitting magnetic loop rolled a fraction as it opened, and Sael kept turning the release beneath it so the elements did not drift apart. A wide gift could hide that motion inside its width. A narrow one would remember exactly where the loop had faced. Sael wanted continuity, not explosion for its own sake.

Below them, the inhabited moons moved through the star's memory as three recurring shadows. Around Lume and Vey, freight mirrors already passed fragile loads from one sail to the next. Illuminara followed the handoff in her mind: a chain of catcher sails could do for a narrow pulse what Sael's breadth did for the shell, refocusing each separated band before the system's wind could scatter it. Harrow's foundries could make the mesh. No single sail had to govern the whole journey.

IlluminaraIf the elements reached Oriel over a century instead of one day, would their meaning change?

SaelA century is an oath your species uses for ceremonies and breaks for budgets.

IlluminaraThen do not accept an oath. Accept a mechanism you can stop. One small pulse. One sail. Then another only when the next generation has built its part and asks for it. You keep the power to refuse us. The living keep the power to renew or end the labor.

Sael showed her the weakness at once. The first pulse required a magnetic throat wider than any foundry sail. Constructing it in seventeen days would need the very superconductors already committed to the Crown. The moons would have to surrender their best weapon before they knew the alternative worked.

SaelThey will ask you to build it and call their fear a contribution.

IlluminaraI can lift the first frame and hold it through launch. I cannot manufacture a century of consent. I will not aim your descendants for you. If the foundries and the assemblies will not carry the work, you will know the offer is false.

The red hand reached seven minutes. Wren's voice entered as a thin external line.

WrenOne minute, Nara.

Sael's pressure moved against the edge of the window, curious rather than violent.

SaelNara.

IlluminaraMy mother still calls me that.

SaelA name from before your power. You kept it.

IlluminaraKeeping is not the same as refusing to change.

She left before Sael answered. The red hand struck eight as the window closed. Outside, Aro stood over untouched controls. Sael still held the magnetic arch below threshold.

For the first time since arriving, Illuminara felt joy without relief attached to it. The solution was not yet real.

03 · What a Century Costs

Harrow polar foundry and the linked assemblies · Fourteen days before threshold

The Quiet Crown's final throat-coil hung over Foundry Nine like a black halo. Melt it down and the foundry could spin the first heliosail: a web two hundred kilometres across, thin enough to move under a controlled pulse and strong enough to sort charged iron from the flare. Keep it intact and the Crown could begin numbing Sael within six hours.

Rian Vale, elected master of the foundry guild, stood under the coil with six hundred workers. Half wore the silver band of the sail proposal. Half wore the black band of the Crown. Her own wrists were bare.

Rian ValeThe sail takes four percent of Orison's foundry output every year for a century. Harrow's east habitats wait eleven more months for radiation roofs. Vey postpones two ocean pumps. Lume gives up half its storm reserve. Do not call this a beautiful promise. Name the people who pay for it.

On the assembly screens, names appeared beside the costs. Habitat cooperatives. Pump crews. The children scheduled to move out of Harrow's oldest caverns. Illuminara had asked for the ledger before asking for a vote. If love for unborn worlds required making living workers invisible, it would repeat Sael's mistake in smaller language.

Aro VennA century compact is theatre. The unborn cannot bind themselves. The star can stop the pulses whenever it chooses, while we cannot recover a melted Crown in time.

IlluminaraThen the compact must not bind the unborn. Every eleven years each moon renews its contribution separately. If one refuses, no punishment, no forced pulse. The material already built remains theirs. Sael receives no claim on future labor—only evidence each generation may offer again.

Aro VennYou have made the chain optional. That makes it incredible to Sael.

Rian turned to the workers rather than the screens.

Rian ValeAnd the first sail? Honesty will not spin two hundred kilometres of mesh in fourteen days.

Illuminara unfolded a physical plan across the floor. Foundry Nine would spin forty modular ribbons. Existing storm tugs would carry them sunward. Illuminara could hold the joining frame against Sael's wind for sixty-one seconds during launch, no longer; after that, ordinary tension and the guild's control vanes had to keep it open. Three unmanned catcher sails would trace the outbound stream. If captured mass fell below ninety-nine point seven percent, or radiation at any moon rose above its ordinary storm limit, Sael would end the pulse and the experiment would count as failed.

The proof had a clock. Sael would emit the test pulse on threshold day. The sail would have six minutes to separate its charge bands and forty hours to show a stable course toward Oriel. The Crown would remain partly assembled until the moment the throat-coil was needed for the sail.

Tavi Sen, a young rigger from Harrow's east habitats, raised a black-banded wrist.

Tavi SenMy family has moved their roof date three times. You want us to delay it for worlds that may never exist. What do we receive besides the honor of being reasonable?

A murmur ran through the workers. Rian did not silence it.

IlluminaraA real roof date funded first from Lume's storm reserve, and a veto if it slips. No moon gets to buy the future with Harrow's present. The sail design also returns its induced current to the east grid after each pulse. Not enough to erase the cost. Enough to make the same structure protect the people building it.

Tavi SenAnd if Lume votes no after we melt our coil?

Aro VennThen I have failed at the one job for which this case was put in my hands.

Aro touched the authorization case. He had been a child during the Red Eruption, when an ordinary storm burned Vey's northern sky and killed his older sister in a shelter whose door fused shut. The Crown was not a politician's appetite for control. It was the only answer he had spent thirty years making ready.

Aro VennYou ask me to place eight billion people behind a test whose other party can become angry enough to boil rock.

SaelYou planned to make me unable to be angry and named that safety.

The translated voice came through the foundry floor. Workers stepped away from the coil as its shadow trembled.

Aro VennI planned to keep children from learning the sound a shelter makes when its door melts.

SaelAnd I planned to keep a nebula from remaining a shelter with no children in it.

The argument did not reconcile them. Illuminara did not turn Aro's grief into a reason he had to yield. She put his condition into the test: until capture crossed ninety-nine point seven percent, three Crown stations would remain active as emergency deflectors under separate keys held by the moon assemblies. They could protect the moons from the trial pulse but could not reach deep enough to silence Sael.

Rian called the votes. Lume accepted. Vey accepted after its patient councils won priority on the returned sail current. Harrow divided exactly in half.

Tavi removed his black wristband. He did not put on silver.

Tavi SenShow us the star can spend power on our safety before it asks us to spend our roof on its future.

The vote remained tied. No coil melted. The proposal had met the one objection no design could solve on paper.

Sael's magnetic arch brightened above the polar glass. It had listened to the cost being named. Whether it had understood was still unproved.

04 · The Pulse Sael Kept

Sunward construction orbit · Nine days before threshold

They built a smaller demonstrator without the throat-coil. It could not launch material toward Oriel. It could only prove that Sael and the foundries could shape a pulse together without harming the moons.

Rian called it a toy. Aro called it insufficient. Tavi volunteered to rig it because neither word made the test useless.

Four storm tugs stretched the mesh into a shining square thirty kilometres wide. Illuminara held the central frame while the riggers locked its vanes. Sael lowered a filament of charged carbon toward it, gentle by stellar measure and large enough to turn night into blue day across Harrow.

Wren counted down from the observatory while the Crown deflectors and Harrow shelters reported ready. At forty seconds, her voice left only the clock in Illuminara's ear.

Aro VennIf the pulse exceeds the agreed band, I call for all three keys.

SaelIf you turn them before it does, I end this conversation.

IlluminaraBoth statements stand. No one improves them by pretending trust already exists.

At twenty-one seconds, the outer ribbon twisted. A manufacture seam that had passed every cold inspection began to unzip under solar charge. The failure travelled inward faster than the tugs could release tension. Tavi and two riggers were clipped to the failing quadrant.

Illuminara could keep the frame open or gather the three workers into her protection. Deep in Sael's wind, she could not do both. She released the frame.

The square folded. She crossed thirty kilometres before the torn ribbon completed its first turn, wrapped her field around the riggers and pushed their tug clear. Behind her, the uncontrolled mesh presented its full conductive face to the incoming filament.

At Aro's call, Lume's assembly turned its key. Lume's deflector woke. The other two keys waited for Vey and Harrow.

Aro VennSael, end the pulse.

SaelIts structure is already above you. Ending the source does not end what travels.

Aro VennThen turn it.

SaelThat carbon took eleven thousand years to raise into this loop.

Tavi's suit spun within Illuminara's field. Through the transparent faceplate, his eyes stayed fixed on the blue-white filament bearing down on the moons.

Tavi SenMinister, turn the rest.

Vey's key turned. Harrow's did not. Rian held it in the foundry chamber, waiting the final second the test allowed Sael to choose.

Through the bounded window, Sael felt Illuminara's field fold tight around three brief lives and saw, in Tavi's faceplate, fear aimed past himself toward the moons; behind them, the frame she had promised to hold tumbled free.

Sael changed.

The convective road Illuminara had entered days before contracted around the filament. Magnetic arches fell across one another, not as a cage imposed from outside but as a hand closing over its own gift. The filament spread into a pale aurora too thin to damage atmosphere or sail. Eleven thousand years of gathered material diffused into light that no nebula would inherit.

The torn demonstrator drifted harmlessly past Harrow. The Crown's instruments measured the result: less radiation than an ordinary winter storm.

Rian took her hand off the third key.

For six minutes Sael did not speak.

Tavi SenYou could have let the deflectors take it.

SaelTwo were awake. One was waiting to know me.

Tavi SenI was waiting to know you.

SaelNow we have each wasted something irreplaceable on the other's uncertainty.

Tavi laughed once, breathlessly. It was not forgiveness, but it was the first sound in the exchange that belonged to neither fear nor grandeur.

Rian reconvened Harrow's vote. Aro asked to speak before it.

Aro VennKeep two Crown stations as deflectors. Melt the throat-coil for the full sail. Renew the compact every eleven years, exactly as proposed. If any assembly withdraws, Sael suspends the next pulse. If Sael breaks the capture limit, the stations protect the moons.

SaelYou still prepare against me.

Aro VennYes. Keep both shields. Test the compact again in eleven years.

The arch over Sael's surface rose and settled.

SaelKeep the Lume and Vey shields.

Harrow voted sixty-one percent for the sail. Tavi voted yes after the habitat roof fund transferred into an account the east cooperatives controlled. Rian gave the order. Foundry cutters entered the black throat-coil and began turning a weapon of silence into forty ribbons of listening metal. They ran three shifts and carried the demonstrator's repaired seam pattern into every ribbon to recover the five days the tied vote had cost.

05 · A Gift That Can Be Refused

The first heliosail beyond Harrow · Threshold day and forty hours later

The full sail opened like a dark flower against Sael. Forty ribbons joined at a ring built from the throat-coil. Ordinary tugs held thirty-nine. Illuminara held the last while Rian's crews repaired the demonstrator's failed seam pattern across two hundred kilometres of mesh.

At sixty-one seconds, Illuminara released the frame.

It stayed open.

No cheer came yet. The proof remained the one Harrow had voted on: capture at or above ninety-nine point seven percent, no moon exposed beyond an ordinary storm, and a course the catchers could hold. The three assemblies, the foundry guild and Sael each retained a stop signal. The Lume and Vey Crown stations waited as shields, their deep-field circuits dismantled.

WrenAll parties show green. Sael, the path is yours to begin and yours to end.

SaelNot mine alone.

A warm pressure touched the sail. Carbon arrived first, then oxygen, silicon and a thin bright thread of iron. The mesh sorted their charges into nested bands while amber light crossed the night side of every moon.

The sail's induced current poured into Harrow's east grid. In the oldest cavern, radiation-roof printers started months before their revised schedule. Tavi watched their load line from a tug, one hand still resting over the patched seam.

The capture line climbed past its red mark. The lost fraction dispersed above the moons' orbital plane, and radiation stayed below winter-storm level. One by one the catcher sails took the separated bands and began the long bend toward Oriel.

Still no one cheered. The course display needed forty hours to distinguish a stable path from a beautiful mistake.

Sael used the wait to slow the deeper magnetic arch. District by district, the evacuation alarms went dark, but the work inside the star was not quiet. Great loops that Sael had spent ages arranging collapsed into harmless light.

SaelI made one day carry everything I meant by parent. I am taking it apart layer by layer. Your instruments call that safety. They cannot name what disappears.

Illuminara did not answer with another design. She asked Wren to pass the navigation watch to Aro, opened the same bounded solar window Sael could end, and stayed while the first arch fell.

IlluminaraThen let me witness it without renaming it. Tell me what you meant each part to become.

For most of an hour Sael showed her no future people, only intended elements, pressures and distances. One collapsed loop had been tuned to send iron last into a young world's turning core, keeping its first ocean warm beneath a faint sun. Illuminara held the sequence without compressing it and asked why the iron must arrive after the silicates. Sael showed her the timing twice.

When the window closed, the assemblies' displays showed three separate eleven-year commitments, each with its own renewal light. Nebula advocates took seats beside habitat cooperatives, and Sael and every moon kept a stop signal.

At hour thirty-nine, the projected stream began to wander. On the display, the nested bands stepped sideways in the same cadence Illuminara had felt inside Sael: the pulse was remembering the magnetic loop that had released it.

IlluminaraIt did not leave a point. The loop turned beneath it. Aro, use the final angle Sael showed the sail.

Aro was already laying the rotation over the catcher geometry. His correction kept the second sail inside its remaining reach.

Aro VennThe second catcher can still hold it if Sael gives us the loop's final angle.

SaelYou intend to improve my aim.

Aro VennI intend to keep your gift from becoming empty weather.

Sael transmitted the angle. Aro sent the correction. At forty hours, the three catcher sails settled onto a stable path whose uncertainty cone lay entirely inside Oriel's hydrogen shelf.

Then the system cheered. It began in Foundry Nine, where cutters struck their tools against the empty supports of the Crown. It crossed assembly galleries and hospital corridors. It reached the old cavern as the first roof panel came hot from its printer. Even the translator carried the vibration back to Sael.

SaelIs this how passengers sound when they decide where the vessel goes?

IlluminaraListen to them. They chose the course with you.

SaelDo not call the silent worlds less real now that you have saved the speaking ones.

IlluminaraI will not. And do not call the speaking ones passengers again.

Sael took seven human seconds to answer, a deliberate delay from a mind that could use centuries.

SaelCrew, then. Difficult crew.

The first pulse was too small to make a planet, and no one could prove Oriel would ever wake. Four percent of Orison's foundries would serve the chain. Sael would die earlier than the moons wanted. Aro kept two shields because one brave choice did not erase the reason he had built them. Tavi's family still had months of roofing ahead.

Wren found Illuminara seated on the observatory hull after the celebrations thinned, both hands against the warm metal. Wren said nothing; she set her palm beside one of Illuminara's.

Sael was correcting the next pulse with Aro's navigation team; each adjustment came through the metal as a low warm hum. Far beyond sight, three small sails held their line toward Oriel.

Sael že šest milijard let osvetljuje tri naseljene lune. Čez devetnajst dni se namerava zavestna zvezda porabiti v izbruhu, ki bo zasejal tiho meglico — in osmim milijardam živih ljudi odvzel svetove, ki so že v njeni svetlobi. Illuminara mora zaščititi sedanjost, ne da bi bogovsko starševsko bitje spremenila v ujetnico.

01 · Devetnajst dni svetlobe

Zbornični obok pod Lume, najbolj notranjo luno Orisona · devetnajst dni pred pragom izbruha

Sael je skozi polarno steklo oboka zapolnjevala polovico neba. Stara zvezda je bila ob mirnem robu jantarna, tam, kjer se je magnetni lok dvigal šeststo tisoč kilometrov nad površino, pa bela. Vsakih enajst minut je lok zasijal močneje. Vsakih enajst minut je tla oboka napolnil nizek odgovor, kakor da je luna postala glasbene vilice, pritisnjene ob grlo boga.

Na Lume, Vey in mrzlem Harrowu je živelo osem milijard ljudi. Njihove vlade so poslale dvanajst delegatov, štiri admirale in en prazen stol za bitje, ki so se ga naučili slišati šele pred tremi dnevi.

Prazen stol je spregovoril prvi. Njegov glas je prihajal iz helioseizmičnih tonov, ki so jih prevajali instrumenti okoli vseh treh lun. Besede niso bile povsem časovno usklajene. Sael je nekatere stavke začela, še preden je prevajalnik končal prejšnjega, kajti zvezda ni razmišljala v zaporedju, ki bi ustrezalo sobi.

SaelŠe devetnajst vaših dni, preden prestopim uporabni prag. Umaknite ladje z vzhodne magnetne poti. Tamkajšnji delci bodo potrebni drugje.

Minister Aro Venn je obe dlani položil na črn kovček ob sebi. V njem so ležali ključi za odobritev Tihe krone, pasu superprevodnih postaj, zasnovanih tako, da zravnajo Saelin magnetni govor in zadržijo izbruh pod točko vžiga.

Aro VennPotrebni, da nas ubijejo.

SaelPotrebni, da omogočijo tisto, kar pride za menoj.

Za delegati je stenski zemljevid kazal sosednjo meglico Oriel: temno rdečo rano, dolgo sedem svetlobnih let, bogato z vodikom in revno z vsem, iz česar bi bilo mogoče zgraditi skalo, vodo ali kri. Saelini modeli so kazali, da bi jo ozek tok ogljika, kisika in železa lahko spremenil. Isti izmet, sproščen naenkrat, bi lunam odtrgal ozračje, še preden bi zapustil Orison.

Illuminara je stala med kovčkom in praznim stolom. Čutila je sile, ki so jih instrumenti risali kot obarvane črte: pritisk, ki se je zbiral pod Saelino fotosfero, magnetno kletko, ki se je prebujala postajo za postajo, drobna trepetajoča bremena v strehi oboka. Silo je bilo mogoče brati. Namere ne.

IlluminaraMoj cilj je jasen. Vse tri lune obdržijo svoja ozračja in vsak človek dobi možnost živeti. Sael obdrži pravico odločiti, kaj pomeni njena smrt. Nobenega od tega ne bom zamenjala za drugo, preden ne razumem, kaj je dejansko potrebno.

Aro je odprl črni kovček. Ključi so bili iz navadne kovine, njihovi robovi pa obrabljeni od vaj, za katere nihče ni pričakoval, da bodo kdaj potrebne.

Aro VennZavestna katastrofa je še vedno katastrofa. Krona nam kupi osemdeset let. V osemdesetih letih se lahko evakuiramo ali naučimo, kako jo varno obvladovati.

SaelŠest milijard let ste uživali mojo svetlobo, dodatnih osemdeset let pa imenujete zadržanost. Meglica je čakala brez glasu. Njeni svetovi ne morejo prositi vaše skupščine, ker jih še nisem ustvarila.

IlluminaraKaj pa ljudje pod tvojo svetlobo? Kaj so zate oni?

Čez Saelin obraz je zdrsnila veriga sončnih peg. Prevajalnik je okleval, zavrgel dva približka in izbral tretjega.

SaelPotniki. Čudoviti potniki. Kratkotrajni. Domove so zgradili na kamnih, ki krožijo okoli mene. Niso vprašali, kaj sem nameravala zgraditi jaz.

Beseda potniki je prešla skozi dvorano nevarneje kot dvigajoči se magnetni lok. Harrowov delegat je vstal. V javni galeriji so livarski delavci začeli vpiti. Arov palec je obstal nad prvim ključem.

Illuminara jih ni prosila, naj besedo odpustijo. Prosila je streho, naj zdrži, medtem ko je kričanje dobivalo obliko, in eno roko naslonila na osrednji nosilec oboka, ko je stari kamen sprejel toplotni sunek Saelinega vse svetlejšega loka. Njena moč je preprečila, da bi padal prah. Nikogar ni prisilila v strinjanje.

Wren Odira je na mizo postavila majhno mehansko uro. Globok stik s Sael bi Illuminaričino zaščito obrnil navznoter. Med njim ne bi mogla držati oboka, ustaviti Krone ali zaščititi lune. Rdeči kazalec ure je nastavila na osem minut.

WrenOsem minut. Ob sedmih te pokličem. Ob osmih prekinem sončno povezavo, ne glede na to, ali je zvezda dokončala stavek ali ne.

Aro VennIn kaj ji med tvojim poslušanjem preprečuje, da prestopi prag?

SaelJaz.

Prevajalnik je prvič brez zamude ujel nekaj, kar je spominjalo na jezo.

IlluminaraPotem je to prva stvar, ki jo lahko narediš za žive: lok zadrži osem minut, ker si se tako odločila, ne zato, ker te Krona sili. Če tega ne zmoreš, ni pogovora, v katerega bi lahko vstopili.

Saelin lok se je še šest dolgih sekund dvigal. Nato se je upognil vstran, izlil svoj ogenj v neškodljivo zanko in potemnel.

Aro je umaknil palec s ključa. Kovčka ni zaprl.

SaelOsem minut. Ne prosi me, naj se pretvarjam, da tišina ni življenje samo zato, ker se še ni začela.

02 · Tiha obala

Sončni observatorij Thren, visoka orbita nad Sael · sedemnajst dni pred pragom

Široko okno se je odprlo šele potem, ko je Sael njegove pogoje sprejela v treh različnih oblikah: z magnetnim zaporedjem, ki ga je lahko preverila, z Illuminaričino govorjeno razlago in z neprekinjeno pravico, da stik konča. Wren je čakala zunaj z rdečo uro. Aro je čakal ob upravljanju Krone. Nobena flota se ni premaknila proti zvezdi.

Illuminara ni vstopila v nobeno človeško sobo. Našla je pritisk, konvekcijo in čas. Saelina misel je živela v zankah, ki so potrebovale tedne, da so se dvignile, in stoletja, da so se sklenile. Okno jih ni stisnilo v človeški spomin; omogočilo ji je stati ob njihovem merilu, ne da bi ga razglasila za svojega.

Videla je Orison, preden so se lune ohladile: temni kamni so prečkali svetlobo mlade zvezde. Začutila je šest milijard let fuzije, ki je preprosto snov spreminjala v težje elemente, ki jih je Sael nosila v jedru in lupini. Daleč onkraj sistema je ležal Oriel, mrzla obala, ki je zbirala vodik, ga izgubljala in znova zbirala. V Saelini dolgi pozornosti meglica ni bila prazna. Bila je nedokončana.

Nobeni prihodnji ljudje se niso prikazali. Polje jih ni moglo potrditi. Obstajali so samo modeli, potrpežljivost in Saelina silovita razlaga tega, kar zvezda dolguje vesolju.

SaelRekla boš, da so namišljeni, ker ne morejo odgovoriti.

IlluminaraNe. Rekla bom, da možnost ni dovoljenje za ubijanje. To sta različni trditvi.

Pod njima se je obrnila konvekcijska stena. Zvenela je kot celina, ki vre.

SaelVaše lune režejo kovine iz mojih otrok, še preden se ohladijo. Lovijo moj veter. Pijejo razliko med mojo vročino in svojo nočjo. Temu pravijo življenje. Ko porabim, kar sem ustvarila, za prihodnost, ki je ne morejo posedovati, temu pravijo smrt.

IlluminaraSmrt osmih milijard sedanjih glasov imenujejo smrt. Nenehno spreminjaš merilo, da ti ni treba uporabiti številke.

Okno se je zožilo. Illuminara je za hip začutila, da se Sael pripravlja stik končati. Ni segla po zvezdini notranji sili niti brez soglasja razširila stika.

SaelOsem milijard sedanjih glasov proti nepreštetim tihim. Tvoja aritmetika si je že izbrala najljubši čas.

To je bil Saelin najmočnejši argument in ni bil neumen. Vsaka skupščina v Orisonu je lahko obljubila samo varnost volivcem, ki so že obstajali. Magnetna kletka bi jih ohranila tako, da bi Sael odvzela edino ustvarjalno izbiro, za katero je verjela, da ji je ostala. Preprosto prepričevanje bi bitje, starejše od njihove vrste, prosilo, naj ima stoletje za moralno pomembno, hkrati pa zavračalo, da bi enako obravnavalo milijon let.

Illuminara se je nehala prepirati z izbruhom in preučila njegovo delo. Sael ga je oblikovala kot široko lupino. Širina ni bila potrebna, da bi dosegel Oriel; težke elemente je držala skupaj, potem ko so prečkali kaotični veter sistema. Ob notranjem robu lupine se je vsaka magnetna zanka ob odprtju malo zavrtela, Sael pa je sproščanje pod njo obračala naprej, da se elementi niso razpršili. Široko darilo je lahko to gibanje skrilo v svoji širini. Ozko bi si natančno zapomnilo, kam je bila zanka obrnjena. Sael je hotela zveznost, ne eksplozije zaradi nje same.

Pod njima so naseljene lune potovale skozi zvezdin spomin kot tri ponavljajoče se sence. Okoli Lume in Veya so tovorna zrcala že predajala krhka bremena z enega jadra na drugo. Illuminara je v mislih sledila predaji: veriga lovilnih jader bi lahko za ozek sunek storila to, kar je Saelina širina naredila za lupino, in znova zbrala vsak ločeni pas, preden bi ga veter sistema lahko razpršil. Harrowove livarne bi lahko izdelale mrežo. Nobenemu posameznemu jadru ne bi bilo treba upravljati celotne poti.

Illuminara breaks open a buried engine chamber and finds Oru, the stone giant whose breathing powers six hospitals. He refuses to leave. With nine hours before the damaged turbines stop, she must protect the patients, expose the city's old crime and make staying unnecessary—without turning liberation into one more order given to him.

01 · The Wall That Opened

Cauldron Nine beneath the city of Vale · Nine hours before hospital reserve exhaustion

Illuminara tore the last iron rib from the buried wall and caught three hundred tonnes of cracked masonry before it could fall inward. Cold air rushed past her into a chamber built around a sleeping body.

The giant was forty metres long. Dark stone plates rose and fell along his chest. With every breath, six bronze bellows beside him compressed. Far above, six hospitals took the pulse through pipes older than any living engineer.

The restraint rings around his wrists had rusted open generations ago. Their scars had not.

Rava Sen, leader of the Open Earth collective, climbed over the broken sill with a red liberation cord around her arm. Behind her came Director Kes from the city energy office and Dr Anik Ilyan, elected by the six hospital patient councils.

RavaOru, the wall is open. You can come out.

The giant's eyes opened like two lamps behind rain-dark glass.

OruClose it.

A pressure alarm began to howl. Illuminara felt the broken chamber losing the dense air that made the bellows efficient. Each breath now delivered less force than the one before.

IlluminaraI believed this was an active prison. I opened it before I asked you.

OruYes.

She waited. An apology that hurried toward forgiveness would only ask him to carry her discomfort too.

IlluminaraI am sorry. I will repair what I broke. I will not touch you again without your permission.

KesThe west seal cannot be restored in time. At current leakage the hospital turbines fall below safe output in nine hours.

RavaThen evacuate the hospitals. We are not putting him back in a cage because your city made slavery convenient.

Dr AnikFour hundred patients cannot be moved. Thirty-two are on blood oxygenators. You may call that convenience after you have carried them through the upper tunnels.

Rava flinched, but did not retreat.

RavaAnd how many more centuries do you prescribe for him?

Oru placed one palm against the chamber floor. The turbines answered with a low, steady vibration.

OruI prescribe nothing. I am not your patient.

IlluminaraWhat do you want in the next nine hours?

OruThe children breathing. The truth spoken. No one using my departure as proof that they have finally understood me.

Kes stared at the open restraints rather than at Oru.

KesThe current arrangement was ratified eighty-three times.

OruBy people who never put my name on the question.

Illuminara lowered the suspended masonry into a stable arch instead of rebuilding the wall. Fresh air could enter. Oru could see the opening. Emergency fabric sealed the pressure gap around it without closing the way out.

IlluminaraMay I enter far enough to listen to the machinery through the floor? Not to your mind. Not to your body unless you show me how.

Oru studied the open arch, the red cord, the city official and the physician whose hands trembled with nine hours of arithmetic.

OruYou may listen where the stone listens. If you call the sound consent, I will stop speaking.

02 · The Shape of a Breath

Lower turbine gallery under Oru's chamber · Eight hours before reserve exhaustion

The gallery smelled of hot oil and mineral rain. Each of Oru's breaths pushed air through six separate turbine trunks. The trunks were not merely pipes. Their old valves turned his slow inhale and faster exhale into a pressure pattern the hospital generators used to stay synchronized.

Illuminara knelt with both hands on the floor. She listened to iron, not to Oru's thoughts. A hairline fault in the fourth trunk clicked every thirty-seven seconds. The giant altered his next breath before the fault could strike.

IlluminaraYou have been correcting the machinery.

OruSince before Kes's grandmother learned to lie politely.

Kes opened his mouth and then closed it.

Dr AnikOur manuals call the pressure self-balancing.

OruYour manuals call me geological assistance.

Rava ran a finger over a brass plate. Someone had chiseled away the first line. Under the scratches remained three words: CAPTIVE RESPIRATORY PRIME.

RavaWe publish this now.

KesIf the city hears it while the hospitals are failing, the lower districts will riot.

OruThey may be angry in the same hour they are useful.

Illuminara traced the pressure rhythm outward while Kes opened the city's archived utility map. Beneath Vale ran compressed-air reservoirs once used by tram lines, now kept half full for freight brakes. Deeper still, geothermal wells heated homes and baths, but their steam bypassed the turbine district because an old mineral separator could not handle pulsed flow. On Kes's map, the abandoned east interchange still held freight locks and timing drums. A second line crossed beneath it: LAUNDRY STERILIZER RETURN—ACTIVE. Maintenance had marked the floor above it WARM IN EVERY SEASON.

Illuminara could see only the outline: tram pressure for the fast exhale, geothermal flow for the slow refill, and the hospital turbines already in place. The missing interval between them still belonged to Oru's body.

IlluminaraThe city has enough stored pressure to begin and enough geothermal flow to continue. But the separator floods whenever demand pulses. I do not yet know what his body does that the circuit does not.

KesA new separator takes six months.

KesEast Interchange still has the freight locks, six check valves and the old timing drums. The inventory was written off, not removed.

RavaAnd who builds it? The same office that hid his name?

IlluminaraAnyone Oru accepts. Your crews, hospital engineers, city workers. The design belongs to all of them. The test belongs to the patient councils.

Oru's next exhale slowed. The fourth trunk clicked twice.

OruYou heard the shape. You did not hear the ache.

Illuminara lifted her hands from the floor.

IlluminaraWill you show me where it begins?

Oru guided her without contact. He breathed once while she watched the pressure gauges, then stopped midway. The chamber's south brace pulled against a stone plate beneath his ribs. The machinery required him to twist every exhale around a support installed after the restraints had rusted.

OruThey say I chose to remain. They do not say the choice hurts in the shape their gratitude prefers.

Dr AnikHow long?

OruThe city has used my breathing for three hundred years. This brace has hurt for forty-one.

Anik removed the hospital council badge from her coat and set it on the stained floor.

Dr AnikThen the patient councils have been voting on a lie too.

IlluminaraThe bridge must match the turbines without matching your pain. Give me three breaths you choose, with a pause between them. We will record the pressures, not your body. You can end the measurement at any moment.

Oru gave one breath, then another. Before the third, he looked through the open arch at the first strip of daylight to reach the chamber in generations.

OruTwo are enough. Let the machine learn there is no entitlement to a third.

03 · No One Owns the Door

Vale assembly rotunda and six linked hospital wards · Six hours before reserve exhaustion

The erased brass plate filled every public screen. Beside it appeared the first contracts: Oru purchased as a war captive, his name replaced by ENGINE SOURCE NINE. Kes had released the records after Oru demanded that no transition begin under a clean lie.

The rotunda divided before anyone spoke. Open Earth members held red cords. Turbine workers wore blue. Hospital patients appeared from beds through wall-sized links. Oru's voice came through the chamber floor.

KesMy office concealed the founding records. I signed the last three renewals without asking Oru directly. The archive is public, and I have placed my authority under council review.

RavaReview is late. The restraint is not.

Dr AnikImmediate disconnection kills patients before transfer can be completed. I will not call that treatment.

A boy in the north children's ward raised his hand. His name was Pell. A clear tube carried blood from his chest to an oxygenator.

PellIs Oru listening?

OruYes.

PellThank you for today. I don't want you to have to do tomorrow.

PellI also want you to stay. I know morning has started by the change in your breathing. I know that is not a fair reason.

Oru's fingers tightened once against the chamber floor. The pressure trace carried the movement into every ward.

OruI am glad the sound kept you company. I cannot promise to make my body your clock. If I visit, it will be because I chose the road to you.

Oru closed his eyes. The next turbine pulse arrived late, then recovered.

RavaThat is why we disconnect him now. No more compromises made over his body.

OruYou speak as if the only door out is the one you choose for me.

RavaI am trying to make sure they cannot choose for you again.

OruThen stand beside my door. Do not own the direction I walk through it.

The red cords lowered. Rava's objection did not disappear.

RavaIf you stay while they still depend on you, how can anyone know the choice is free?

OruThey cannot. That is why the dependence must end before you ask what I choose next.

Illuminara projected the bridge plan. Tram pressure would run the hospitals during the first test. Geothermal steam would refill the reservoirs through a dry chamber assembled at East Interchange. If the bridge failed, Oru's trunks could reconnect in eleven seconds without sealing the open wall.

IlluminaraThe proof has three parts. First, all six hospitals run on the bridge for one full hour while Oru's valves are physically open to the chamber, not to the turbines. Second, pressure remains within two percent through an unannounced hospital load change chosen by the patient councils. Third, Oru walks beyond the old restraint line before anyone asks him to return.

A refusal flashed across the tram union's board: no reservoir transfer until the founding archive was public, paused crews were paid, and lower-district delegates controlled two valve seats. Kes moved the executive contingency fund to wages and surrendered the seats. The lower districts did not riot. Their pipe crews arrived with hammers and elected valve keepers. The board turned amber, then green.

KesThe tram reservoirs will empty in four hours if the geothermal chamber misses its mark.

IlluminaraThen the test fails honestly, the hospitals return to Oru's breathing, and we learn what must change. We do not rename failure liberation.

Dr AnikThe councils require one more condition. If the bridge works only by closing emergency wards, it does not work.

RavaOpen Earth requires independent valve keepers at every trunk and an alarm Oru controls from inside or outside the chamber.

OruI require the old support removed before I give another working breath. Not after the crisis. Now.

Kes looked at the clock.

KesRemoving it costs forty minutes.

OruIt has cost me forty-one years.

Illuminara did not offer to rip it out alone. She held the chamber roof while turbine workers cut the brace in view of Oru, Rava and the patient councils. Kes carried the first severed piece into the rotunda and laid it beside the erased plate.

When Oru breathed again, the pressure rose four percent with less effort.

The four-percent rise appeared at once on six ward screens. Oru released a long breath that did not drag against iron.

04 · Borrowed Breath

East Interchange and North Children's Hospital · Two hours before reserve exhaustion

The temporary manifold occupied the abandoned tram hall: a ring of six salvaged valves, two timing drums and a dry chamber made from freight locks. A strip of floor above the active laundry return stayed warm even before steam entered the system. Illuminara held the warped upper seam together while ordinary welders closed it. She could keep the metal aligned. She could not make a bad circuit breathe.

At North Children's, Pell watched the pressure line climb toward transfer. Dr Anik stood beside his bed. Rava held the manual valve key. Kes had placed the city's master key on the floor beyond his reach.

IlluminaraOru, we are ready to take the first hospital. You set the count.

OruNot ready. The third drum is early.

KesThe instruments show synchronization.

OruThe instruments have never had ribs.

Illuminara listened again. The third drum struck at the correct moment, but its valve opened too quickly. Oru's breathing had always cushioned that edge with the slight flex of his chest. A metal bridge would send a hard pressure wave into the oldest hospital turbines.

IlluminaraHe is right. Add a water buffer before the third valve.

RavaThe nearest tank is part of the fire line.

PellOur roof has a rain cistern.

Anik checked the hospital plan. The cistern was full, isolated and high enough to answer pressure without a pump.

Dr AnikUse ours. Fire reserve remains above code for three hours.

Rava and two hospital engineers opened the old roof line. The patient council, not Kes, authorized the temporary risk.

The first transfer began. Oru's trunk valve opened to the chamber. East Interchange sent its measured exhale through the north line. The turbine caught it cleanly.

Then the dry chamber flooded.

Mineral water struck the timing drums. Two valves jammed half open. At North Children's the lights dimmed and Pell's oxygenator changed to battery.

KesReconnect Oru.

RavaWait. Twenty seconds of battery margin.

Dr AnikSeventeen now.

Illuminara held the dry chamber above the flood and looked for the wrong assumption. Steam entered dry. Water was condensing after the pressure drop, faster than the drain could carry it.

IlluminaraOru, what do you do with the cold in the return stroke?

OruI keep it in my heels.

RavaMeaning?

OruThe return air warms through the lower rock before I draw it again. Your bridge has no heel.

Pell pressed the call switch from his bed.

PellThe laundry return makes that strip of tram floor warm. Maintenance complains every winter. Can it warm the pipe?

Kes reopened the archived map. The line they had noticed beneath East Interchange was marked obsolete at the manifold but active from two hospital sterilizers.

KesWe can wrap the return line. Ninety seconds.

Dr AnikBattery margin is twelve.

OruUse one breath of mine. Not because you failed to free me. Because Pell asked the right question.

Rava turned Oru's valve for exactly one cycle. His exhale restored the hospital line while crews cut into the laundry heat pipe. No wall closed. No restraint engaged.

The interruption and rebalancing cost eleven minutes of tram reserve. When Oru's valve closed again, the patient councils reset the one-hour proof clock to zero. The reserve board showed one hour and thirty-two minutes.

The warm return cleared the condensate. East Interchange took the next pulse, then the next. North Children's lights steadied before Pell's battery reached five minutes.

PellDid it work?

OruThe return is warm. The pulse is stable.

IlluminaraThe proof starts again now.

She released the seam. The weld held without her.

05 · After the Turbines Let Go

Oru's open chamber and Vale's western ridge · Dawn after the full-load test

After the flood the councils reset the clock. They transferred the hospitals in pairs while the tram reserve declined and geothermal refill slowed the loss. Once all six were on the repaired bridge, it carried them for one uninterrupted hour. Midway through that hour the councils changed the load without warning: two sterilizers, a magnetic theatre and every oxygenator in the south ward at once. Pell watched the green lamp beside his blood line hold steady. Anik watched one pressure needle tremble and return; Rava kept her palm above the valve key and did not touch it. Pressure stayed within one point six percent. When the hour ended, the tram reserve board showed eighteen minutes.

Oru's six trunk valves stood open to the chamber. Air moved through them in both directions, useless to the turbines. For the first time since the founding contract, a hospital's survival did not rise and fall with his chest.

Rava removed the last red cord from the doorway and tied it around the public archive case instead.

RavaThe door is yours.

OruIt always was. Now it leads somewhere.

He rose slowly. Stone dust fell from joints held in one position longer than the city had kept any constitution. Illuminara offered her shoulder and waited.

OruYes.

Turbine workers walked beside him as he placed one foot, then the other, beyond the old restraint line. Kes stood aside. Anik watched the hospital readings and did not ask him to hurry.

His chosen weight settled through her shoulder. Warm stone dust touched her cheek, and joy rose in her, quick and quiet, at being trusted with exactly that much.

Outside, dawn struck the upper plates of Oru's face. He stopped so long that the crowd mistook stillness for uncertainty.

OruIt is smaller than I remembered.

IlluminaraThe sky?

OruThe city. They built it very large inside my chamber.

He walked to the western ridge, where an unfinished quarry house had been widened overnight by stonecutters, activists and turbine crews. It had no pipes leading to a hospital. Its door opened from either side.

Only after Oru had slept there for six hours did the assembly ask what he wanted next.

KesThe bridge can carry the hospitals, but it closes two tram lines and most night foundry work. Permanent geothermal redundancy takes six weeks. The city has no claim on your help.

RavaOpen Earth will keep independent watch whether you return or not.

Dr AnikThe patient councils will fund the redundancy before any ceremonial project. We also request a direct seat for you, not a geological advisory category.

Oru looked at Illuminara.

OruWhat do you want me to choose?

IlluminaraNothing that proves I was right. I want the hospitals safe, the old crime impossible to hide, and you able to change your mind without punishment.

A smile moved through the seams of his face like light entering a canyon.

OruThen I will give one shift each third day for six weeks. Four hours, never sleeping in the chamber, and Rava keeps the valve key. Not because Vale needs my body. Because the children asked me to stay until the replacement grows roots.

RavaI still dislike it.

OruGood. Stand beside the door.

Kes signed the transition charter, then signed his resignation and the release of every founding record. The assembly created Oru's independent home and an unconditional right to disconnect that no emergency declaration could suspend. None of that erased the original enslavement. It changed what the city could demand next.

Six weeks later the permanent geothermal ring took the hospital load. Oru did not attend its dedication. Pell's bed had been wheeled into the North Children's courtyard, where Oru was teaching patients how to hear faults in stone through the soles of their feet.

PellAre you a doctor now?

OruNo.

He set one broad finger against the courtyard paving. A pump beneath the hospital slab clicked out of rhythm.

OruI am someone who knows what a machine sounds like when it hurts.

Pell placed his bare foot beside Oru's hand. Far below, a pump skipped once; both of them looked up at the same instant.

Illuminara razpre zasuto strojnico in najde Oruja, kamnitega velikana, čigar dihanje poganja šest bolnišnic. Oditi noče. Do ustavitve poškodovanih turbin je devet ur; zaščititi mora bolnike, razkriti stari zločin mesta in poskrbeti, da njegovo bivanje tam ne bo več nujno — ne da bi osvoboditev spremenila v še en ukaz, namenjen njemu.

01 · Zid, ki se je odprl

Kotlovnica devet pod mestom Vale · Devet ur do izčrpanja bolnišnične rezerve

Illuminara je iz zasute stene iztrgala zadnje železno rebro in ujela tristo ton razpokanega zidu, preden bi se zrušil navznoter. Mimo nje je v dvorano, zgrajeno okoli spečega telesa, planil hladen zrak.

Velikan je meril štirideset metrov. Temne kamnite plošče na njegovih prsih so se dvigale in spuščale. Z vsakim vdihom se je stisnilo šest bronastih mehov ob njem. Daleč zgoraj je šest bolnišnic prejemalo njegov utrip po ceveh, starejših od vsakega živečega inženirja.

Obroči za vklenitev okoli njegovih zapestij so že pred rodovi prerjaveli in se razprli. Njihove brazgotine ne.

Rava Sen, vodja kolektiva Odprta zemlja, je z rdečo osvobodilno vrvico okoli roke splezala čez razbiti prag. Za njo sta prišla direktor Kes iz mestnega urada za energijo in dr. Anik Ilyan, ki jo je izvolilo šest svetov bolnikov.

RavaOru, zid je odprt. Lahko prideš ven.

Velikanove oči so se odprle kakor dve svetilki za od dežja potemnelim steklom.

OruZaprite ga.

Tlačni alarm je zatulil. Illuminara je čutila, kako iz poškodovane dvorane uhaja gost zrak, zaradi katerega so mehovi delovali učinkovito. Vsak naslednji dih je dal manj sile od prejšnjega.

IlluminaraMislila sem, da je to delujoč zapor. Odprla sem ga, preden sem te vprašala.

OruDa.

Počakala je. Opravičilo, ki bi hitelo proti odpuščanju, bi od njega zahtevalo le še, naj nosi tudi njeno nelagodje.

IlluminaraŽal mi je. Popravila bom, kar sem zlomila. Brez tvojega dovoljenja se te ne bom več dotaknila.

KesZahodnega tesnila ne moremo pravočasno obnoviti. Ob sedanjem uhajanju bodo bolnišnične turbine čez devet ur padle pod varno moč.

RavaPotem evakuirajte bolnišnice. Ne bomo ga vrnili v kletko zato, ker je vaše mesto suženjstvo naredilo priročno.

Dr AnikŠtiristo bolnikov ni mogoče premakniti. Dvaintrideset jih je priključenih na krvne oksigenatorje. Temu lahko rečete priročnost, ko jih boste odnesli skozi zgornje predore.

Rava je trznila, vendar ni odstopila.

RavaIn koliko stoletij mu predpisujete še?

Oru je eno dlan položil na tla dvorane. Turbine so odgovorile z nizkim, enakomernim tresljajem.

OruNičesar ne predpisujem. Nisem vaš bolnik.

IlluminaraKaj želiš v naslednjih devetih urah?

OruDa otroci dihajo. Da je resnica izrečena. Da nihče mojega odhoda ne uporabi kot dokaz, da me je končno razumel.

Kes je gledal odprte okove namesto Oruja.

KesSedanja ureditev je bila potrjena triinosemdesetkrat.

OruPotrdili so jo ljudje, ki mojega imena niso nikoli zapisali v vprašanje.

Illuminara je viseče zidovje spustila v stabilen lok, namesto da bi zid znova zgradila. Svež zrak je lahko vstopal. Oru je videl odprtino. Zasilna tkanina je zatesnila tlačno režo okoli nje, ne da bi zaprla izhod.

IlluminaraSmem vstopiti dovolj daleč, da skozi tla poslušam stroje? Ne tvojih misli. Ne tvojega telesa, razen če mi sam pokažeš kako.

Oru je premeril odprti lok, rdečo vrvico, mestnega uradnika in zdravnico, ki so se ji roke tresle od deveturne računice.

OruPoslušaš lahko tam, kjer posluša kamen. Če boš zvok imenovala privolitev, bom nehal govoriti.

02 · Oblika diha

Spodnja turbinska galerija pod Orujevo dvorano · Osem ur do izčrpanja rezerve

V galeriji je dišalo po vročem olju in mineralnem dežju. Vsak Orujev dih je potisnil zrak skozi šest ločenih turbinskih vodov. Vodi niso bili le cevi. Njihovi stari ventili so njegov počasni vdih in hitrejši izdih spreminjali v tlačni vzorec, s katerim so bolnišnični generatorji ostajali usklajeni.

Illuminara je pokleknila z obema dlanema na tleh. Poslušala je železo, ne Orujevih misli. Lasasta razpoka v četrtem vodu je kliknila vsakih sedemintrideset sekund. Velikan je naslednji dih prilagodil, še preden bi razpoka lahko udarila.

IlluminaraVes čas popravljaš delovanje strojev.

OruOd časa, preden se je Kesova babica naučila vljudno lagati.

Kes je odprl usta in jih nato zaprl.

Dr AnikNaši priročniki tlak opisujejo kot samouravnalnega.

OruVaši priročniki mene opisujejo kot geološko pomoč.

Rava je s prstom zdrsnila čez medeninasto ploščico. Nekdo je izklesal prvo vrstico. Pod praskami so ostale tri besede: UJETNIŠKI DIHALNI POGON.

RavaTo objavimo zdaj.

KesČe mesto to izve med odpovedovanjem bolnišnic, se bodo spodnja okrožja uprla.

OruV isti uri so lahko jezni in koristni.

Illuminara je sledila tlačnemu ritmu navzven, medtem ko je Kes odprl arhivski zemljevid mestnih vodov. Pod mestom Vale so tekli rezervoarji stisnjenega zraka, nekoč namenjeni tramvajskim progam, zdaj pa napol polni za tovorne zavore. Globlje so geotermalni vodnjaki ogrevali domove in kopeli, vendar je njihova para obšla turbinsko okrožje, ker stari ločevalnik mineralov ni zmogel pulznega toka. Na Kesovem zemljevidu so v opuščenem Vzhodnem križišču še vedno bile tovorne zapornice in časovni bobni. Pod njim je prečkala druga cev: POVRATEK PRALNIŠKEGA STERILIZATORJA — DEJAVEN. Vzdrževalci so tla nad njo označili z VSE LETNE ČASE TOPLA.

Illuminara je videla le obris: tramvajski tlak za hitri izdih, geotermalni tok za počasno polnjenje in že postavljene bolnišnične turbine. Manjkajoči razmik med njimi je še vedno pripadal Orujevemu telesu.

IlluminaraMesto ima dovolj shranjenega tlaka za začetek in dovolj geotermalnega toka za nadaljevanje. Toda ločevalnik poplavi ob vsakem sunku porabe. Še ne vem, kaj naredi njegovo telo, česar vezje ne.

KesZa nov ločevalnik potrebujemo šest mesecev.

KesVzhodno križišče ima še vedno tovorne zapornice, šest nepovratnih ventilov in stare časovne bobne. Inventar so odpisali, ne odstranili.

RavaIn kdo ga bo zgradil? Isti urad, ki je skril njegovo ime?

IlluminaraKdorkoli, ki ga Oru sprejme. Vaše ekipe, bolnišnični inženirji, mestni delavci. Zasnova pripada vsem. Preizkus pripada svetom bolnikov.

Orujev naslednji izdih se je upočasnil. Četrti vod je dvakrat kliknil.

OruSlišala si obliko. Bolečine nisi.

Illuminara je dvignila dlani s tal.

IlluminaraMi boš pokazal, kje se začne?

Oru jo je vodil brez dotika. Enkrat je vdihnil, medtem ko je opazovala merilnike tlaka, nato pa se je na polovici ustavil. Južna opora dvorane je vlekla kamnito ploščo pod njegovimi rebri. Stroji so od njega zahtevali, da vsak izdih zavije okoli opore, nameščene po tem, ko so okovi prerjaveli.

OruPravijo, da sem se odločil ostati. Ne povedo, da izbira boli v obliki, ki jo ima njihova hvaležnost najraje.

Dr AnikKako dolgo?

OruMesto moje dihanje uporablja tristo let. Ta opora me boli enainštirideset.

Anik je z ogrinjala snela značko sveta bolnikov in jo položila na umazana tla.

Dr AnikPotem so tudi sveti bolnikov glasovali o laži.

IlluminaraPremostitev se mora ujemati s turbinami, ne da bi posnemala tvojo bolečino. Daj mi tri dihe po svoji izbiri, s premorom med njimi. Zabeležili bomo tlake, ne tvojega telesa. Merjenje lahko kadarkoli končaš.

Oru je dal en dih, nato drugega. Pred tretjim je skozi odprti lok pogledal prvi trak dnevne svetlobe, ki je po rodovih dosegel dvorano.

OruDva sta dovolj. Naj se stroj nauči, da do tretjega nima pravice.

03 · Nihče si ne lasti vrat

Rotunda zbora mesta Vale in šest povezanih bolnišničnih oddelkov · Šest ur do izčrpanja rezerve

Izbrisana medeninasta ploščica je napolnila vsak javni zaslon. Ob njej so se pojavile prve pogodbe: Oru, kupljen kot vojni ujetnik, njegovo ime nadomeščeno z POGONSKI VIR DEVET. Kes je zapise objavil, potem ko je Oru zahteval, da se noben prehod ne začne pod očiščeno lažjo.

Rotunda se je razdelila, še preden je kdo spregovoril. Člani Odprte zemlje so držali rdeče vrvice. Turbinski delavci so nosili modro. Bolniki so se iz postelj prikazali prek povezav v velikosti stene. Orujev glas je prihajal skozi tla dvorane.

Kes je izvršni rezervni sklad prenesel v plače in prepustil sedeža. Spodnja okrožja se niso uprla. Njihove cevne ekipe so prispele s kladivi in izvoljenimi varuhi ventilov. 05 · Ko so turbine popustile

Orujeva odprta dvorana in zahodni greben mesta Vale · Zora po preizkusu polne obremenitve

Oru, a stone giant whose breathing has powered six hospitals for three hundred years, is neither dragged out nor kept in: Illuminara listens where he can feel it, the city's crews and patients build a bridge he corrects, and he leaves the chamber by his own step to a home of his own while every patient stays powered.
