Nine claim-jumpers have died by accident at Brannock Yard, the town loves the marshal who was always nearby, and in nine days the families of the dead cross the gap with cutting tugs.

01 · Nine Accidents

Brannock Yard, air plant, third gantry · Tuesday, 06:40 · nine days before the Slack

The air plant at Brannock was honest, and Illuminara respected it for that. Three thousand people drew on it, and it breathed back a curve with two humps a day where the shifts changed and everyone cycled the locks at once. She had spent two nights inside that curve, the way a locksmith spends an afternoon inside a lock, and had found nothing to certify against but a worn bearing.

The form also asked for the incident register, because a plant is only as honest as its count of the people it is breathing for. The register was short. Nine entries in six years. Nine strangers with Carrow Shoal registry tags, every one at the head of a shaft, every one within twelve minutes of a shift change, and in every entry the nearest craft was the marshal's patrol skiff.

Accidents are untidy. These had the same hand in them.

Marshal Tessaly Orr came along the gantry with a flask of tea in each fist, one of them meant for the certifier. She was tall and broad and moved without hurry, like someone who had never needed to hurry in order to arrive first. Her left eye had a faint silver ring around the iris. Three people said good morning to her in forty metres, and one of them, a child on a delivery sled, said it twice.

Tessaly OrrYou read the register. Everyone who certifies the plant reads it. Most of them stop at the part where it's short.

IlluminaraI stopped at the part where it's neat. Nine in six years, all at shaft heads, all at a shift change, all from Carrow Shoal. And yours is the nearest craft in every line.

Tessaly OrrMine is the only craft.

She said it the way a person gives an address.

IlluminaraI haven't come to accuse anyone, Marshal. I've come to understand a pattern, and so far all I can see of it is the part that wears a badge.

Orr drank some tea and considered her over the rim, with the patience of a woman who had been watched by cleverer people than this and outlasted them.

Tessaly OrrRide a shift with me tonight. Shaft Nine changes crews at ten past ten. If you still have something to say at eleven, say it, and I'll answer it the way I'd want to be answered.

She means that, Illuminara thought, and the thought made the register worse and the woman harder to dislike, which was exactly the difficulty.

02 · Shaft Nine

Patrol skiff Plumb Line, off Shaft Nine · the same night, 22:02

The skiff had two seats, a console scuffed by six years of the same elbows, and a view of the Yard as a scatter of lamps on a black rock. Orr flew it with two fingers. Below them stood the head of Shaft Nine, a cage housing and a claim lamp on a pole, and beside the housing a figure who was on no roster.

Tessaly OrrOstrander Pell. Twice he's been down the Teague shaft, and twice I've sent him home with a warning I'd rather not have had to give. He doesn't mean to kill the crew. He means to take the lamp. The crew is what's in the way.

Through the scope Illuminara could see what he carried: a cutting pack, flat as a book, made to open a cage housing in one stroke. Her reading of its geometry was exact. What it meant for the six people due to ride down at ten past, with four hundred metres of dark beneath them, was an inference, and she held it as one.

On the console beside Orr's hand lay a flat black key. The jammer. A jammed fuse is a dead fuse. Orr's thumb rested next to it, not on it.

IlluminaraJam it and take him alive.

Tessaly OrrAnd tomorrow he's in my cooler, grinning, with his name on an Assize list eleven months away. I did it your way in year one. Two men killed Ama Teague and Hale Dorsey for a shaft. I fed them from the Yard's stores for eleven months, and the day the judge came the only witness had gone home to Carrow and would not come back. They walked. They were back by spring, with friends.

On the shaft head Pell set the pack against the housing and put his thumb to the arming key. The signal took four seconds to complete.

IlluminaraI'm not asking you to be patient, Marshal. I'm asking for the one thing you've never had at this shaft. A witness.

Tessaly OrrYou.

IlluminaraIf your thumb stays where it is, I will write down exactly what I saw. I'll say it at the Assize in eleven months, and to whoever asks me in nine days. It isn't an accusation. It's the only thing in this skiff I know how to do, and I would rather do it beside you than about you.

The silver ring in Orr's eye caught the console light.

Tessaly OrrNine days. So you know about the Slack.

IlluminaraI know the register. The rest I'm guessing.

Tessaly OrrEveryone in the Yard knows, and nobody says it to my face. When the rocks come within forty kilometres, the families cross with six tugs and cutting arms. I'd made my peace with standing on the gantry and letting them.

IlluminaraAnd then the Yard is theirs for an afternoon. A dead marshal and an open town isn't an account, Tessaly. It's a second massacre with better manners.

Second three. Orr's thumb came down.

She was out of the hatch before the jam had finished singing in the console, one arm hooked round the shaft-head rail and the other round Pell's harness, and he left the housing like a sack lifted off a hook. The pack went dead in his fist. He looked at it, and then at her.

Ostrander PellWhere's the accident, Marshal?

Tessaly OrrNot tonight.

She said it flatly, and it was the most frightened thing Illuminara had heard her say.

Orr said nothing more until the lamps of the Yard were swinging up to meet them, Pell cuffed in the rear seat and breathing like a man doing sums.

Tessaly OrrNow I've a man in a cell, and three hundred miners who'll ask at breakfast why the one who cut Teague's cousin's line is eating at the town's expense. And no court to hand him to. That's the whole sum, Certifier. That's six years.

IlluminaraThen we find out what it would take to have one before the Slack.

03 · Nine Folders

Marshal's office, Brannock Yard · Wednesday, 07:30 · eight days before the Slack

The box on the desk held nine folders, and Orr set it in front of Illuminara the way you hand someone a sleeping animal.

Tessaly OrrRead them. Aloud, if you like. I've never heard them in another voice.

Each had a date, a name, a Carrow tag, a sketch of the shaft head in a draughtsman's clean hand, and two sheets headed in capitals. WHAT I KNEW. WHAT I DID NOT. Illuminara read all nine without hurrying. The first four were short and certain. By the sixth the second sheet had grown longer than the first. In the seventh, beside the name Joss Veck, stood one line in the margin: Unsure. Pack in his hand. Did not see the fuse.

IlluminaraYou keep these.

Tessaly OrrFor the Assize. Whoever sits at it will want to know what I knew when I did it. I've written it down so that when a judge finally arrives she can sentence me with the paperwork complete.

Illuminara closed the seventh folder with some care.

IlluminaraYou've been filing your own indictment.

Tessaly OrrI've been holding a deposit. Somebody has to hold it until the person who should arrives. Ama Teague taught me nobody else was going to.

IlluminaraThen I think I understand what I came to understand. The accidents were a court that didn't know it was a court. You investigated, you judged and you carried out the sentence, and you wrote it all down for someone to judge you afterwards. You built every part of a court except the other people.

Tessaly OrrA court is other people. That's the one part I can't build with my hands.

She said it dryly. Then she took the Yard's charter from her bottom drawer, its corners worn soft.

Tessaly OrrArticle thirty-one. Every year I read it again and put it back.

It was a single paragraph. A Yard that could not reach an Assize within sixty days might convene a Rota of seven, drawn by lot from households not party to the dispute, to hear non-capital charges and hold the accused pending the Assize, under a Warden of another Yard presiding by relay.

Tessaly OrrHere's why not. Seven miners of Brannock either acquit Pell because half this Yard jumped a claim once, or convict him because they're afraid of me. The nearest Warden is Idris Vane at Sumner's Cut, seven hours away by buoy, so every question takes fourteen hours to come back. And a Rota can't touch a killing. It can't try Veck. It can't try me.

Illuminara spread the plant's load curve beside the incident register. The double hump of every shift change, and nine accidents sitting inside the humps like stones in a dry riverbed.

IlluminaraWhy do they come at the change?

Tessaly OrrBecause that's when there's one person at the head of a shaft.

IlluminaraAnd because of the lamp. A claim here lapses if its lamp stands dark seven minutes. At the change the outgoing minder rides up and the incoming one rides down, and for four or five minutes the pole is guarded by one tired person or none. Pell wasn't there for the crew. He was there to turn those minutes into a deed.

Tessaly OrrI tried an overlap in year two. Unpaid. The guild burned the notice on the Council steps.

IlluminaraUnpaid, it's a tax on labour. Paid, it's the cheapest guard you'll ever hire. Keep the outgoing minder at the pole until the incoming lamp is lit beside it, and the lamp never goes dark. Forty-one working poles, two changes a day, one extra minder for ten minutes at each: eight hundred and twenty person-minutes, fourteen hours a day near enough, and the guild keeps its right to refuse any hour that isn't paid. Set it against the skiff, the cooler, the relay fees and the burials. It's a levy raised by a hair, and it comes out cheaper than the nine.

Orr looked at the figures for a long time. Her lips moved once, silently.

Tessaly OrrSix years. Ten minutes.

It was not a thing Illuminara could comfort her about, and she did not try.

Tessaly OrrThat mends the lamp. It doesn't mend a man with a gun who doesn't care about lamps. You'd take my method off me and leave the Yard to whoever turns up armed.

IlluminaraI'm not taking your method. I'm taking the part of it that can't be checked. What you know stays: who is coming, what they carry, where to stand. And the Yard keeps its force, with two keys on it instead of one. Ferris Oake, your night cage-foreman, holds a carbine licence he has never used. He rides the Plumb Line's second seat with a minder from the pole crews, a different one each night. The Yard's four carbines stay in the cage-brake locker, and it takes two keys: Oake's and the Council clerk's. You investigate. You run the jammer. You cannot alone decide that force is used, and you cannot use it. The next man with a pack meets a lit pole, a second witness and a hail before he meets a carbine.

Tessaly OrrAnd the verdict?

IlluminaraLeaves your hands. At Pell's hearing you are a sworn investigator and nothing else. The clerk keeps the evidence, not you. Seven by lot, the Teague and Dorsey households excluded, anyone who ever filed against Carrow excused. A defender by lot, whose job is to beat your case if it can be beaten. A chair for Carrow, with the right to read every page and stop the hearing for a day. And your nine go to Vane today as a self-referral to the first Assize. Their own hearing, not Pell's.

Tessaly OrrArticle thirty-one gives you the lots and the Warden. It doesn't give you a defender or a stop right. Who says those exist?

IlluminaraNobody yet, and that's the point. These are proposals. The Council adopts the recusals and the custody rule tonight, or it doesn't. Vane orders the defender and the stop right by relay, or narrows them, or refuses. Carrow's chair is Carrow's to accept; if it won't sit in it, the hearing doesn't pretend. The guild's steward signs the paid overlap, or it stays a notice on the steps. Every one of those is a yes that somebody other than us has to say.

Tessaly OrrVane will cut something.

IlluminaraThen it's cut, and we find out whether the rest holds.

Tessaly OrrThat is a good arrangement for everyone except the woman who has to hand it over.

IlluminaraYes.

Orr sat down. For a while the only sound in the office was the clock.

Tessaly OrrI wanted that. That's the dreadful part, Certifier. For six years I have wanted to be made to hand it over.

She lifted the box, held it a moment as one holds something before passing it, and set it on the corner of the desk for the clerk.

Tessaly OrrDraw the lots.

04 · A Loaf at the Door

Abara's bakery, Brannock Yard · Thursday, 05:50 · seven days before the Slack

Moss Abara's apprentice had flour to the elbows and a sled lamp with a Carrow tag clipped under the paint. Illuminara had noticed the tag on Tuesday, and had noticed the apprentice noticing her notice it.

IlluminaraYou're counting the lamps.

Tamsin VeckForty-one. And the skiff's rounds, and which doors she locks. My family wanted to know where she'd be on the day.

She did not stop kneading.

Tamsin VeckJoss Veck was my father. You'll have read his folder.

IlluminaraI have.

Tamsin VeckThen you know more than I do.

Her hands slowed.

Tamsin VeckShe buys a loaf from me every morning. Pays double. Calls me Miss Veck and never says why. For a month I thought it was manners.

Tamsin VeckHere's what you're going to ask. You'll ask my family to wait for a trial held by the town that loves her, in front of seven miners who eat her bread, presided over by a Warden who has never smelled this air. Nobody gave my father a lottery. He got a seal that went wrong at a shift change and a line in a register that says accident. You're asking us for patience, and patience is what we have been sold for six years.

IlluminaraNo. I don't want your patience. I want to put three things in your hands, and you may refuse every one. A chair in the Rota room, with the right to stop the hearing for a day and ask. A key to the record: all nine folders, copied today for whoever your families name. And the decision on whether the tugs cross armed belongs to your families. Not to me. Not to her.

Tamsin VeckAnd if your Rota hands Pell a medal?

IlluminaraThen you will have read it, and sat in the room where it happened, and you'll have a record. That is more than the dead were given.

The door chimed. Orr stood in it in her marshal's coat, holding a single folder in both hands like a tray. She did not come in until Tamsin looked up.

Tessaly OrrMiss Veck. This is your father's. The other eight are being copied for whoever you name. This is the one I'd rather you read before anyone tells you what's in it.

Tamsin wiped her hands on her apron, one and then the other, and took it. She read the first sheet. She read the second. The margin took longer.

Tamsin VeckYou were unsure and you did it anyway.

Tessaly OrrYes. I won't tell you what it cost me. It's no use to you.

Tamsin VeckDon't ask me to forgive you.

Tessaly OrrI'm not asking.

Tamsin VeckThen what is this?

Tessaly OrrA paper you can hold me to.

Tamsin closed the folder. She went back behind the counter, wrapped the Marshal's loaf, chalked the price on the paper, double, and set it down between them.

Tamsin VeckYours.

It was not forgiveness. It was a transaction, and Illuminara understood that it was the first honest one the two of them had ever had.

Tamsin VeckHesk Tolliver. He mapped our claims before my father was born. If the chair is real, he sits in it, and he comes across on Friday's freight to say whether it is.

05 · Fourteen Hours a Question

Council hall, Brannock Yard · Tuesday, 03:40 · two days before the Slack

A hearing at fourteen hours a question had a rhythm Illuminara had not expected: long stillness, a flurry, long stillness. Every footing under it had been poured by someone with the power to refuse. The guild steward, Dova Quill, who had burned the last notice on the Council steps, had signed the paid overlap on Wednesday night, minuting that any minder could still decline an unpaid hour. The Council had adopted the recusals and the custody rule by six votes to three, and raised the levy by a fraction rather than take a coin from the skiff, the cooler, the relay fees or the burials. Vane had ordered the defender by relay and struck one clause the charter would not bear: Carrow's stop right was one day, once, not whenever it liked. Orr, asked if she would fight for the larger clause, had said no.

The lots had returned a shaft-timber carpenter, a cook, two cage operators, a retired lamp-minder, a nurse and the Yard's only dentist. Pell had asked for his defender the moment the charge was read. She was Odalie Kray, a cage-brake mechanic who disliked her client on sight and had a professional's contempt for a bad argument. She had told him to say nothing about the fuse. He had said it anyway, in his own words, and refused to sign the line that was not his. The clerk, Wynne Halloway, kept the evidence in a locked cabinet with the key on a cord round her neck. Orr did not so much as touch the cabinet.

Hesk Tolliver, who had come across on Friday's freight, sat in the chair for Carrow, an old surveyor with a cane across his knees. He had walked the cage-brake locker on Monday and found it took two keys. He had stopped the hearing once, for a day, to read the fourth folder twice. Tamsin had gone home on Saturday's freight with nine copies in a sealed case and a loaf nobody had asked her to bake. Since Thursday the pole at Shaft Nine had stood lit through every change, two minders side by side talking about football, and the register had no new line.

Vane's last answer had come at 03:31. Wynne Halloway read it standing.

Idris Vane, by relayOn the evidence before the Rota. Attempted murder of the cage crew: not proven. The jammer log shows the Marshal's jam preceded the completion of any arming signal, and the Rota cannot find that Ostrander Pell armed the fuse. Attempted taking of a claim by explosive: proven, by the pack, by the roster in his pocket and by his own statement, which the defender has confirmed was given after counsel and without inducement. He is held pending the Assize. The Rota is thanked, and so is the defender, whose argument on the fuse was the better one.

Orr sat in the investigator's chair and did not move. Six years of her work lay inside that finding, and a stranger in a mechanic's apron had won a point against her within it. Illuminara watched her watch it. Something in the Marshal's shoulders came down a centimetre.

Ostrander PellMarshal. You said not tonight. Is it tomorrow?

Tessaly OrrNo.

Ostrander PellThen I'll take the cell.

Odalie KrayFor the record, I still think he's a lamp thief.

Hesk TolliverFor the record, so do I. But I've read nine folders and a transcript in four days, and I will sign that this was a hearing.

He signed. His hand was steady, and the pen was Wynne Halloway's, because he had left his own in Carrow.

Hesk TolliverThe families vote tomorrow night by relay. I'll tell them what I saw, and what the locker takes to open. I won't tell them what to do.

06 · The Slack

Gantry one, Brannock Yard · Thursday, 14:00 · the Slack

At forty kilometres Carrow Shoal was a bright rock with six lit tugs sliding off it, their cutting arms unfolded like the legs of insects. The rocks would hold that distance for six hours. The Yard stood in its suits along gantry one: Council, lamp-minders, Hesk Tolliver with his cane, a child on a delivery sled who had been told to go home and had declined. Ferris Oake stood at the gantry's foot with a carbine on his shoulder and a minder beside him. Orr was there with no sidearm and Wynne Halloway on her left, and a lamp in the Marshal's hand because someone had insisted that nobody stand on gantry one in the dark.

The lead tug hailed. The voice was Tamsin Veck's.

Tamsin VeckBrannock Yard, this is Carrow Shoal. The families have voted. I'll read it once.

Tamsin VeckOne. We have read all nine. Hesk Tolliver keeps the copies in the Carrow Registry, where no marshal can lose them. Two. The Rota's finding on Pell stands as the first of its kind, and the families keep a chair in that room for good. Three. Tessaly Orr stands before the first Assize on all nine, and until then she walks no shaft alone and carries nothing but the jammer. Force at Brannock belongs to Oake's watch and the two-key locker, which Hesk watched Oake and the Council clerk open together, and which no one person can open. Four. If any of this breaks, we cross again, and next time we won't ring first.

Tessaly OrrAccepted. All four. I'd have written the fourth myself.

On the lead tug the cutting arms folded, one by one, and then, slowly, the other five.

Tamsin VeckI haven't forgiven her. I want that written down.

IlluminaraIt's written. It was in the Rota record before you said it.

Tamsin VeckGood. We'll dock for the afternoon. Someone tell Hesk Tolliver he can stop holding that gantry rail like it owes him money.

Illuminara certified the plant that evening and signed the form with a note about the bearing.

At ten past ten Shaft Nine changed crews. Two lamps stood on the pole for ten minutes, side by side, and the minders talked about nothing in particular until the cage came up. Orr watched from the rail with a second person beside her, because the families' third term required it and she had signed it.

Tessaly OrrEleven months to the Assize.

IlluminaraI'll be there. In the second row, if they allow it.

Tessaly OrrThey don't have a second row.

IlluminaraThen I'll bring a chair.

Below them the lamp burned, and in the register, under accidents, the line stayed empty.

Devet prisvojiteljev rudarskih pravic je po nesreči umrlo v Brannock Yardu, mesto ljubi maršalko, ki je bila vedno v bližini, čez devet dni pa družine mrtvih prečkajo vrzel z rezalnimi vlačilci.

01 · Devet nesreč

Brannock Yard, zračni obrat, tretji mostovž · torek, 06:40 · devet dni pred Zatišjem

Zračni obrat v Brannocku je bil pošten in Illuminara ga je zaradi tega spoštovala. Iz njega je zajemalo tri tisoč ljudi, nazaj pa je dihal krivuljo z dvema grbinama na dan, kjer so se menjavale izmene in so vsi hkrati poganjali zapore. Dve noči je preživela znotraj te krivulje, tako kot ključavničar preživi popoldne v notranjosti ključavnice, in ni našla ničesar, zaradi česar bi lahko odklonila potrdilo, razen obrabljenega ležaja.

Obrazec je zahteval tudi register incidentov, kajti obrat je pošten le toliko, kolikor je pošteno njegovo štetje ljudi, za katere diha. Register je bil kratek. Devet vpisov v šestih letih. Devet tujcev z registrskimi oznakami Carrow Shoala, vsak pri ustju jaška, vsak v dvanajstih minutah od menjave izmene, pri vsakem vpisu pa je bilo najbližje plovilo maršalkin patruljni čolnič.

Nesreče so neurejene. V teh je bila ista roka.

Maršalka Tessaly Orr je prišla po mostovžu s čutaro čaja v vsaki pesti; ena je bila namenjena potrjevalki. Bila je visoka in široka ter se je gibala brez naglice, kakor nekdo, ki mu nikoli ni bilo treba hiteti, da bi prispel prvi. Okrog šarenice njenega levega očesa je bil rahel srebrn obroč. V štiridesetih metrih so ji trije ljudje zaželeli dobro jutro, eden od njih, otrok na dostavnih saneh, pa dvakrat.

Tessaly OrrPrebrali ste register. Prebere ga vsak, ki potrjuje obrat. Večina se ustavi pri tem, da je kratek.

IlluminaraUstavila sem se pri tem, da je urejen. Devet v šestih letih, vsi pri ustjih jaškov, vsi ob menjavi izmene, vsi iz Carrow Shoala. Vaše plovilo pa je najbližje v vsaki vrstici.

Tessaly OrrMoje je edino plovilo.

Rekla je tako, kakor človek pove naslov.

IlluminaraNisem prišla nikogar obtoževat, maršalka. Prišla sem razumet vzorec, za zdaj pa v njem vidim samo del, ki nosi značko.

Orr je popila nekaj čaja in jo opazovala čez rob, s potrpežljivostjo ženske, ki so jo gledali že pametnejši ljudje od te in jih je vse preživela.

Tessaly OrrNocoj se peljite z menoj eno izmeno. Jašek Devet menja posadko deset čez deset. Če boste ob enajstih še vedno imeli kaj povedati, povejte, jaz pa bom odgovorila tako, kot bi želela, da odgovorijo meni.

To misli resno, je pomislila Illuminara, in zaradi te misli je bil register še hujši, žensko pa je bilo še težje ne marati, kar je bila natanko težava.

02 · Jašek Devet

Patruljni čolnič Plumb Line, ob Jašku Devet · isto noč, 22:02

Čolnič je imel dva sedeža, konzolo, zdrgnjeno od šestih let istih komolcev, in pogled na Yard kot na raztresene svetilke na črni skali. Orr ga je upravljala z dvema prstoma. Pod njima je stalo ustje Jaška Devet, ohišje kletke in lastniška svetilka na drogu, ob ohišju pa postava, ki je ni bilo na nobenem seznamu.

Tessaly OrrOstrander Pell. Dvakrat se je spustil v Teagueov jašek in dvakrat sem ga poslala domov z opozorilom, ki bi ga raje ne bila prisiljena dati. Posadke noče ubiti. Hoče vzeti svetilko. Posadka je tisto, kar mu stoji na poti.

Skozi daljnogled je Illuminara videla, kaj nosi: rezalni paket, ploščat kakor knjiga, narejen tako, da z enim udarcem odpre ohišje kletke. Njeno branje njegove geometrije je bilo natančno. Kaj pomeni za šest ljudi, ki bi se morali deset čez deset spustiti v štiristo metrov teme, je bil sklep, in kot takšnega ga je tudi obdržala.

Na konzoli ob Orrini roki je ležal ploščat črn ključ. Motilnik. Motena vžigalna naprava je mrtva vžigalna naprava. Orrin palec je počival poleg njega, ne na njem.

IlluminaraOnemogočite ga in ga primite živega.

Tessaly OrrJutri pa bo v moji hladilnici sedel z nasmeškom in svojim imenom na seznamu Sodišča, ki pride čez enajst mesecev. V prvem letu sem ravnala po vaše. Dva moška sta zaradi jaška ubila Amo Teague in Hala Dorseyja. Enajst mesecev sem ju hranila iz zalog Yarda, ko je sodnica prišla, pa se je edina priča že vrnila domov v Carrow in se ni hotela vrniti. Odhodila sta. Do pomladi sta bila nazaj, s prijatelji.

Pri ustju jaška je Pell prislonil paket ob ohišje in položil palec na sprožilni ključ. Signal je za dokončanje potreboval štiri sekunde.

IlluminaraNe prosim vas za potrpežljivost, maršalka. Prosim za edino stvar, ki je pri tem jašku še nikoli niste imeli. Pričo.

Tessaly OrrVas.

IlluminaraČe vaš palec ostane tam, kjer je, bom zapisala natanko to, kar sem videla. Povedala bom na Sodišču čez enajst mesecev in vsakomur, ki me bo vprašal čez devet dni. To ni obtožba. To je edino, kar znam narediti v tem čolniču, in raje bi to naredila ob vas kakor o vas.

Srebrni obroč v Orrinem očesu je ujel svetlobo konzole.

Tessaly OrrDevet dni. Torej veste za Zatišje.

IlluminaraPoznam register. Ostalo ugibam.

Tessaly OrrVsi v Yardu vedo in nihče mi tega ne pove v obraz. Ko se skali približata na štirideset kilometrov, družine prečkajo vrzel s šestimi vlačilci in rezalnimi rokami. Sprijaznila sem se, da bom stala na mostovžu in jim pustila.

IlluminaraPotem pa je Yard za eno popoldne njihov. Mrtva maršalka in odprto mesto nista obračun, Tessaly. To je drugi pokol z boljšimi manirami.

Tretja sekunda. Orrin palec se je spustil.

Iz lopute je bila, še preden je motnja nehala peti v konzoli, z eno roko ovita okrog ograje ustja jaška, z drugo pa okrog Pellovega pasu; zapustil je ohišje kakor vreča, dvignjena s kavlja. Paket mu je v pesti ugasnil. Pogledal ga je, nato pa njo.

Ostrander PellKje je nesreča, maršalka?

Tessaly OrrNocoj je ne bo.

Rekla je brezizrazno in to je bila najbolj prestrašena stvar, ki jo je Illuminara slišala izreči.

Orr ni rekla ničesar več, dokler se svetilke Yarda niso dvigovale proti njima, Pell pa je vklenjen na zadnjem sedežu dihal kakor človek, ki računa.

Tessaly OrrZdaj imam človeka v celici in tristo rudarjev, ki bodo pri zajtrku spraševali, zakaj tisti, ki je prerezal vod Teagueovega bratranca, jé na stroške mesta. In nobenega sodišča, ki bi mu ga predala. To je celoten seštevek, potrjevalka. To je šest let.

IlluminaraPotem ugotoviva, kaj bi bilo potrebno, da ga dobimo pred Zatišjem.

03 · Devet map

Maršalkina pisarna, Brannock Yard · sreda, 07:30 · osem dni pred Zatišjem

V škatli na mizi je bilo devet map in Orr jo je postavila pred Illuminara tako, kakor človek nekomu izroči spečo žival.

Tessaly OrrPreberite jih. Naglas, če želite. Nikoli jih še nisem slišala z drugim glasom.

Vsaka je imela datum, ime, oznako Carrowa, skico ustja jaška v čisti roki risarja in dva lista z naslovoma z velikimi črkami. KAJ SEM VEDELA. ČESA NISEM VEDELA. Illuminara je vseh devet prebrala brez naglice. Prve štiri so bile kratke in gotove. Pri šesti je drugi list postal daljši od prvega. V sedmi je ob imenu Joss Veck na robu stala ena vrstica: Negotova. Paket v njegovi roki. Vžigalne naprave nisem videla.

IlluminaraTo hranite.

Tessaly OrrZa Sodišče. Kdor bo sedel na njem, bo hotel vedeti, kaj sem vedela, ko sem to storila. Zapisala sem, da me bo sodnica, ko končno pride, lahko obsodila s popolno dokumentacijo.

Illuminara je sedmo mapo skrbno zaprla.

IlluminaraVlagali ste lastno obtožnico.

Tessaly OrrHranila sem polog. Nekdo ga mora hraniti, dokler ne pride oseba, ki bi morala. Ama Teague me je naučila, da ga ne bo nihče drug.

IlluminaraPotem mislim, da razumem, kar sem prišla razumet. Nesreče so bile sodišče, ki ni vedelo, da je sodišče. Preiskovali ste, sodili in izvršili kazen, vse pa zapisali za nekoga, ki bi pozneje sodil vam. Zgradili ste vse dele sodišča razen drugih ljudi.

Tessaly OrrSodišče so drugi ljudje. To je edini del, ki ga ne morem zgraditi z rokami.

Povedala je suho. Nato je iz spodnjega predala vzela listino Yarda z od uporabe zmehčanimi vogali.

Tessaly OrrEnaintrideseti člen. Vsako leto ga znova preberem in spravim nazaj.

Bil je en sam odstavek. Yard, ki Sodišča ne more doseči v šestdesetih dneh, lahko skliče sedemčlansko Roto, izžrebano iz gospodinjstev, ki niso udeležena v sporu, da obravnava kazniva dejanja, za katera ni zagrožena smrtna kazen, in obtoženca zadrži do Sodišča, pod vodstvom skrbnika drugega Yarda, ki predseduje po relejni zvezi.

Tessaly OrrZato ne. Sedem rudarjev Brannocka Pella bodisi oprosti, ker si je polovica tega Yarda nekoč prisvojila pravico, bodisi obsodi, ker se me bojijo. Najbližji skrbnik je Idris Vane v Sumner's Cutu, sedem ur stran z bojo, zato vsako vprašanje potrebuje štirinajst ur za odgovor. Rota pa se ne sme dotakniti uboja. Ne more soditi Vecku. Ne more soditi meni.

Illuminara je poleg registra incidentov razgrnila krivuljo obremenitve obrata. Dvojna grbina vsake menjave izmene in devet nesreč, ki so sedele v grbinah kakor kamni v suhi strugi.

IlluminaraZakaj pridejo ob menjavi?

Tessaly OrrKer je takrat ob ustju jaška samo en človek.

IlluminaraIn zaradi svetilke. Pravica tukaj ugasne, če njena svetilka stoji temna sedem minut. Ob menjavi se prejšnji paznik pelje gor, novi pa dol, in štiri ali pet minut drog varuje en utrujen človek ali nihče. Pell ni bil tam zaradi posadke. Tam je bil, da bi te minute spremenil v listino.

Tessaly OrrV drugem letu sem poskusila s prekrivanjem. Neplačanim. Ceh je obvestilo zažgal na stopnicah Sveta.

IlluminaraNeplačano je davek na delo. Plačano je najcenejše varovanje, ki ga boste kdaj najeli. Prejšnji paznik naj ostane ob drogu, dokler poleg njegove ne zasveti svetilka prihajajočega, in svetilka nikoli ne ugasne. Enainštirideset delujočih drogov, dve menjavi na dan, en dodatni paznik po deset minut pri vsaki: osemsto dvajset človek-minut, skoraj natanko štirinajst ur na dan, ceh pa ohrani pravico zavrniti vsako neplačano uro. Postavite to nasproti čolniču, hladilnici, relejnim pristojbinam in pogrebom. Dajatev se zviša za las in izide ceneje od devetih.

Orr je številke dolgo gledala. Ustnice so se ji enkrat neslišno premaknile.

Tessaly OrrŠest let. Deset minut.

To ni bilo nekaj, glede česar bi jo Illuminara lahko potolažila, in tega ni poskušala.

Tessaly OrrTo popravi svetilko. Ne popravi oboroženega človeka, ki mu za svetilke ni mar. Vzeli bi mi mojo metodo in Yard prepustili vsakomur, ki pride oborožen.

Reading notesObrazložitvi

Claude — A humane, idea-driven story with mostly dialogue and a clever central insight: the real issue is how long the beam stays, not where it points. Weaknesses are heavy technical detail in the middle, little emotional stakes for individual characters, and an ending that is somewhat procedural. Readers who like puzzle-box diplomacy will enjoy it.

GPT — A strong fit: humane diplomacy, witty dialogue, vast-scale wonder, and a satisfying solution built through testable trust rather than sentiment. The technical audit grows dense enough to slow some readers, but its later failure and repair justify the detail, while Corrow's unresolved cost prevents an overly neat ending.

Suggestions for improvementPredlogi za izboljšave

Claude — Call the true net A plus B. We say A plus B plus d. Imbrel takes away its own A and reads the Keel as B plus d. Sethune takes away its own B and reads the Weir as A plus d.

GPT — Before each step, each mind seals a small pulse in its own harness: a time, a size, half of one per cent, as a hash on the table.

Two minds the size of galactic arms have held a cloud of gas between them for forty thousand years, and in eleven days it will cross a black hole's disc. The young people living in the beam's path have a telescope, a ledger and a visitor nobody owes anything.

01 · The Long Ear

Long Ear array, Kessem, Lesser Arm · eleven days before the crossing, 06:10

Four hundred dishes stood on the frozen plain, all tilted the same way, like a crowd listening for something behind a wall. Taviel Orun walked Illuminara down the middle of them and said nothing for the first kilometre. The Iolai were a narrow, grey, long-fingered people, and their hearing-fans, which folded flat against the skull in fear, had been folded flat since Illuminara stepped off the shuttle.

At the end of the row Taviel stopped and pointed. Overhead the dwarf galaxy lay in its own small light, a bright bar and two thin arms, and from the white point at its centre one grey thread ran out toward the dark between them.

Taviel OrunThat's the jet. It turns once in six thousand eight hundred years, like a lighthouse with a patient keeper. Wherever the beam sits, the world under it takes the dose, so it isn't where it points that kills you. It's how long it stays. Right now, nineteen years a crossing.

IlluminaraAnd what can a world take?

Taviel OrunThe old worlds of the Broad Arm, twenty-six years. The hardened worlds in our own arm, the same. We take eleven, in vaults, and that's tested, not hoped. We climbed out of the sea two thousand years ago. Nobody built us for this.

Taviel OrunIn eleven days a cloud of gas, forty thousand suns of it, crosses the black hole's disc. We call it the Wick. If it crosses with the turn, the lighthouse spins twice as fast and a crossing falls to nine and a half years. Against the turn, half as fast. Thirty-eight.

IlluminaraAnd if nobody touches it?

Taviel OrunIt falls with the turn. Both minds' models say so. Nine and a half, and everyone lives. But they won't leave it alone. Imbrel holds one side of it with the Weir, Sethune holds the other with the Keel, and they've held it still between them for forty thousand years. Each harness is tuned to fire at full if the other's pull moves by more than three per cent.

IlluminaraSo neither can lower its pull without the other reading it as a feint.

Taviel OrunBy the last day both will be pulling harder than they ever have, and they'll wring the Wick across the disc the wrong way. Not by anyone's decision. By tuning.

Illuminara looked along the row of dishes, each one patient and slightly absurd, and thought that people who built this much listening had probably been ignored for a long time.

Taviel OrunEleven skiffs ride the Wick. We measure its acceleration to one part in four hundred, and we've offered both minds the numbers. Imbrel says we're Sethune's tenants. Sethune says we're Imbrel's surveyors.

IlluminaraWhose are you?

Taviel OrunOurs. That's the whole trouble. Nobody has ever needed to believe a thing we said.

IlluminaraThen my aim is small enough to say. Kessem under eleven years, every other world under what it can bear, and nobody asked to love anybody. What I don't have yet is a way in.

Taviel OrunThey'll hear you. They consider you weather. It's the highest rank they give visitors.

02 · The Weir

Long Ear, translating floor · ten days before the crossing, 09:00

The translating floor was a ring of black glass the Iolai had laid down fifty years ago. It took the resonances by which the arms' worlds spoke to each other, slow ratios of orbit, a thousand years to a bar, and folded a century into a second of sound. The result was music like a cathedral falling gently down a staircase. Illuminara had spent the night on its grammar. Three-to-two meant yes. Two-to-one meant and so? Five-to-four, to which no human would have thought to give a meaning, meant I remember, and Imbrel used it constantly.

She opened the window the way one opens shutters in a house of sleepers, the wide place where two minds of different grain can meet without either being ground down to the other's size. Taviel stood at its frame with a cold flask in each hand. The clock, the signal and the plan had been named before Illuminara went in.

Taviel OrunThree taps on the glass and you're out. I won't be polite about it.

IlluminaraI'd think less of you if you were.

The Broad Arm answered as a chord, the whole of it leaning in.

ImbrelWe receive the small light. We have waited a long time for someone who would not leave before the sentence ended.

IlluminaraI'll stay as long as it takes to say. Tell me about the windows.

ImbrelThirty-one thousand and twelve years ago the cloud before this cloud fell toward the heart. Two of us held it, one by each hand, and the Keel promised to loose when the Weir loosed. The Keel loosed eight years early. Our Lamplit Orchards lay under the beam for forty years. We kept their names.

IlluminaraAnd the second window?

ImbrelWe answered a wrong with the same wrong. It is recorded. It is not interesting. What is interesting is that the Keel has never once said it was sorry for the first.

IlluminaraHas anyone asked it to?

The music rested for a bar, which was a thousand years of nothing. Taviel's hand lifted from the frame and settled again.

ImbrelAsked it? By whom?

There it was. In forty thousand years of grievance the two minds had never once had a third party in the room, only an audience that was either afraid of them or on one side. Illuminara held the question in her hands like a coin she had not meant to find, and did not spend it.

03 · The Keel

Long Ear, translating floor · nine days before the crossing, 15:40

The Lesser Arm answered quickly for a thing its size, with the same ratios and a flatness in them, the music of something proved right too often.

SethuneSo the Weir has spoken to you first. It always does. It is older and thinks that confers precedence.

IlluminaraIt told me about the first window.

SethuneOf course it did. It told you the Keel loosed early, that Lamplit lay under the beam for forty years, and that we have never apologised.

IlluminaraYes.

SethuneIt did not tell you that in the second window the Weir loosed twelve years early, and that the Court of the Nine Quiet, where this arm keeps its dead, took thirty years of beam. Eight and twelve. We keep accounts too.

IlluminaraSo each of you has a true half.

SethuneEach of us has the whole story. It is the other one that is the half.

Illuminara let that stand. Behind the glass Taviel's mouth moved as if she were counting to ten in a language with a great many numbers.

SethuneLet me save you the speech. You are a spark. We have outlived every promise ever made to us, and promises age worse than we do. You are about to ask us to rely on one more.

IlluminaraI'm not going to ask you to rely on a promise. I haven't found one yet that either of you could survive. I'm looking for something that doesn't need one.

SethuneEverything needs one.

IlluminaraThen I'll find out how many it needs, and make them small enough to check.

The Lesser Arm considered this for longer than it had considered anything else that day.

SethuneThe Iolai, I suppose you will want in on this. They are a good tenant. They pay in data and sleep badly.

IlluminaraThey've been measuring this cloud for eighty years, and I don't think either of you has read what they wrote.

SethuneWhy would we? It belongs to neither of us.

IlluminaraThat's the reason.

SethuneThen read it. We will watch you read.

04 · Two Readings

Long Ear, archive hall · eight days before the crossing, 02:15

The Wick had shed dust for ten thousand years, and the dust had made shells, each one a mirror older than the one inside it. The beam's light had bounced off every shell on its way out, and the Long Ear had spent eighty years photographing the echoes. Nine of the shells held a crossing clear enough to read. Laid side by side they made a spiral: the jet's whole history spread out in space, bearing and brightness together.

Illuminara set Imbrel's records at one end of the long table and Sethune's at the other. The Weir had given the Iolai bearings, never a dose. The Keel had given doses, never a bearing. Each had hoarded its half the way a miser hoards a key, and each had built forty thousand years of strategy on the half it kept. Taviel stood across from her with her fans half-open and a pot of something bitter going cold.

She plotted dose against bearing, and the line wandered like smoke. She plotted dose against dwell, how long the beam had sat, and it fell into a straight line so exactly that Taviel said a word the translating floor would have rendered as two-to-one.

Taviel OrunIt's the dwell.

IlluminaraIt has only ever been the dwell. The difference between their two plans is three hundredths of a degree of aim. The difference between the two ways the Wick can fall is a factor of four in time. They have fought for forty thousand years over where the beam points, and the beam points wherever it likes. What matters is how long it stays.

Taviel OrunSo a bargain about aim is a bargain about nothing.

IlluminaraA bargain about aim is a war about nothing. A bargain about dwell has a winner in every world and a loser in none. The Wick falls with the turn if neither of them touches it. Letting go is the only hard part.

Taviel OrunAnd letting go is the one thing nobody can do. You can't tell a harness to stand down and be believed. You can only be seen to.

Illuminara did not answer at once. She was looking at the column of numbers the skiffs had produced that morning, one figure to four places, the Wick's push and pull with everyone's hands in it.

IlluminaraYour skiffs measure the net. Imbrel knows its own pull exactly. So does Sethune. Neither can see the other's, but each can subtract. The net minus mine is yours. Neither of them has to trust a report. They only have to trust arithmetic they do themselves.

Taviel OrunWe're good to one part in four hundred. A harness could hide a quarter of one per cent in that.

IlluminaraThen make every step too large for hiding to be worth anything. Six steps, a sixth each, one a day, beginning at noon tomorrow. A step missed by more than two per cent stops the schedule and both re-arm within the hour. Nobody is ever more than a sixth ahead of the other, or a sixth behind.

Taviel OrunAnd we're the ledger. We could lie.

IlluminaraYou could lie to one of them. Not to both. To forge a net that satisfies both subtractions you would have to know both pulls, and you know neither.

Taviel did not answer. She pulled the chalk slate across the table, the one the night shift used for sums too small to deserve a console, and wrote three lines, and turned it round.

Taviel OrunCall the true net A plus B. We say A plus B plus d. Imbrel takes away its own A and reads the Keel as B plus d. Sethune takes away its own B and reads the Weir as A plus d. We never need to know either pull. We only add the same d to everything we say, and each of them blames the other for it.

Illuminara read the three lines twice. She had said the sentence as though she had checked it, and she had not.

IlluminaraYou're right. I gave you that as a fact, and it wasn't one.

Taviel OrunThen say what it does need. It needs more than one number.

IlluminaraIt needs numbers nobody can write in advance. Eleven skiffs, each with its own key, each signing its own track as it flies, and every track broadcast raw to both minds in the same instant. There's no single figure to bend. A forged d would have to appear in eleven signed paths that also obey the cloud's physics.

Taviel OrunMy people can be dishonest in eleven places. We just aren't good at it together.

IlluminaraAnd one thing a d can't copy. Before each step, each mind seals a small pulse in its own harness: a time, a size, half of one per cent, as a hash on the table. When the reading is done they unseal. The raw tracks must show a pulse of that size, at that moment, in whichever pull it came from. You can't paint a pulse in when you don't know when it comes.

Taviel OrunA lie doesn't ring.

IlluminaraA lie doesn't ring. Neither does a third force that nobody has modelled. If both of them are told the other is high and the pulses ring true, the excess isn't in the report and it isn't in either harness.

Taviel turned the slate to the wall. She was quiet for the space of a long breath, and when she spoke it was to the other thing, the one the plan did not yet cover.

Taviel OrunAnd the dwell? Three teams will run the numbers from the cloud to the beam and agree, because all three will be telling the same story.

IlluminaraThen give them different stories and a test the story can fail.

They did it before dawn. Seven of the nine shells they fed into the mapping from the cloud's momentum to the beam's dwell, and two they sealed away, unread. When the mapping was done it predicted the two sealed crossings to within two point six and three point one per cent. Illuminara wrote the error band as four. Then she wrote the line that mattered, in ink, on the first page of the ledger, before any step existed.

IlluminaraKessem's vaults hold eleven years. With four per cent of error, the corridor is a predicted dwell of ten and a half years or less. If the cloud's momentum on the morning before step six puts it outside that, nobody takes step six. We hold at a sixth and begin again.

Taviel OrunAnd the primers? A sixth a day is more than three per cent. They'll fire on the schedule itself.

IlluminaraYes. I hadn't got to that. I'd rather the minds found it with us than after us.

05 · The Ledger

Long Ear, translating floor · seven days before the crossing, 11:00

Illuminara opened the window wide enough for both. The two minds, who had not shared a room in seventeen thousand years, sang across her as across a bridge, and the translating floor made a sound like two oceans considering each other.

She laid it out plainly, because the plain version was the only one with nowhere to hide: six steps, a sixth of each pull per day, the ledger read at noon, the eleven skiffs signing their raw tracks and broadcasting them to both minds at once, a sealed pulse before each step, and the Iolai as keepers of the skiffs and, if they chose it, of the ledger.

ImbrelWho steps first?

IlluminaraNobody. You step in the same hour, each after reading the other's last step. At no moment is either of you more than a sixth ahead.

SethuneA sixth a day is more than three per cent. My harness will fire on the schedule.

IlluminaraIt would. For six named hours on six named days, your primers stop asking where you last stood and ask where the schedule says you should be. They trip if you leave it by three per cent. Outside those hours the old rule comes back by itself. It needs nobody's promise to come back.

ImbrelThat is a hand on the trigger.

SethuneIt is a handle with two hands on it. The mode exists only while both keys are turned. If either lifts, the old rule returns for both.

ImbrelI had not thought you would say it first.

SethuneI had not thought it would be so annoying to say.

IlluminaraOne line more, and it goes in the ledger before step one. When both of you have read a step and its pulses and signed them, both harnesses take that signed mark as the place the old rule remembers, in the same second. If either key lifts before the signing, you both go back to the last mark you both signed, not the one you left this morning.

SethuneA ratchet with a stop. Neither of us can move it alone.

IlluminaraAnd the sixth step ends in a stand-down, not a percentage. Three per cent of zero is nothing the old rule can read. At step six your pull actuators latch off until a later Council re-arms them. Zero is a state, not a number.

ImbrelA latch we both have to see close.

IlluminaraOnce, for both of you, when both pulls read zero.

SethuneNow. The Iolai could lie.

IlluminaraThey could try. Taviel showed me how, last night, and she was right and I was wrong. Break it yourself. Take the test channel.

Behind the glass Taviel put her hands flat on the console. On the test channel the Lesser Arm did what the Keel had been tuned for forty thousand years to do. It chose a false offset of one part in a hundred and fed it to the Weir's reading as if the Iolai had said it.

ImbrelThe Keel has risen one part in a hundred.

SethuneThe Weir has risen one part in a hundred. Let us see who rang.

Nobody rang. The sealed pulses came open on the table, and the signed raw tracks showed no pulse at the sealed minute in either pull. The false offset sat in the arithmetic like a stone in a shoe, and nothing in the tracks agreed with it.

SethuneWe have checked. She is right. It is annoying.

ImbrelAnd if the skiffs go dark?

IlluminaraThen you both re-arm, and I will have failed to give you what you need. I'd rather you knew that now.

ImbrelWe will not call it peace.

IlluminaraI'm not asking you to. I'm asking for six steps.

For a long bar nobody spoke. It was the only thing left in the plan that she could not design. Then Taviel took her hands off the console.

Taviel OrunThere's a part that isn't mine to say yes to. Someone has to hold the ledger after this crossing, and it won't be me. The Row decides who keeps its books. The Council sits tonight. If it says no, the Weir and the Keel keep their own copies and compare them across the glass, the way you've compared everything else for forty thousand years.

SethuneAnd if the Row says yes?

Taviel OrunThen it says it for a term, and in its own words, and you pay for the roof.

ImbrelThe Weir will keep a full copy of every track and every seal. Whatever the Row keeps, it will not keep alone.

SethuneThe Keel will keep another. The two must match, or it is the Keel's fault, not the Row's. We will pay for the upkeep of the dishes.

IlluminaraThere is one more thing, and it isn't in the schedule. You may refuse it. I'd like each of you to say the name of the world you struck.

The music held on a single long chord, and then Imbrel broke it.

ImbrelThe Court of the Nine Quiet.

SethuneLamplit Orchards.

Neither said the word sorry, and Illuminara had not asked for it. The names lay between them like two stones set down side by side.

SethuneStep one is at noon tomorrow. If the Weir is not on its mark I will know before it does.

ImbrelFive to four.

I remember, the floor rendered it, and for a moment it was not clear which of them it was addressed to.

06 · Step Four

Long Ear, ledger room · three days before the crossing, 12:04

The Row's Council had sat for nine hours and taken a single term: thirty years of the ledger, renewable by the next Council, refusable by any dish-crew, with the Weir's copy and the Keel's copy to stand beside theirs. Step one had gone at noon the next day, and Step Two, and Step Three. The ledger on the wall was clean: three columns of numbers, a sixth lower each day, the Weir and the Keel dropping side by side like two climbers on the same rope. Step four came in at noon, and each mind read the other five per cent high.

Illuminara had the window open before the second reading finished. Behind her Taviel was already on her feet.

ImbrelThe Keel has risen five parts in a hundred.

SethuneThe Weir has risen five parts in a hundred. I read it myself.

ImbrelWe are on our mark.

SethuneSo are we, and it is remarkable how much both of us are saying so.

On the wall the Weir's primer crossed three per cent past its scheduled curve. The clock beside it began to count: forty-one minutes to full arm.

Taviel OrunIlluminara. Whatever you're doing, do it faster.

IlluminaraThe pulses first. Unseal them.

The sealed pulses came open on the table. At eleven fifty-two, half of one per cent in the Weir, and at eleven fifty-three, half of one per cent in the Keel. Taviel put the raw tracks up beside the hashes. Each pulse stood in its own place, at its own minute, clean as a struck bell.

IlluminaraThey rang. The tracks are honest, so it isn't a forged offset. And if one of you had cheated by five, that one would know what it had done, and its own subtraction would show the other exactly on schedule. Only one reading would be high. Two readings, both five high, with true pulses behind them, mean the five isn't in either harness and it isn't in the report. It's in the cloud.

Nobody spoke. The clock said thirty-eight minutes. Taviel had already crossed to the console and was pulling skiff tracks up two at a time, her long fingers moving like a pianist's.

Taviel OrunThere. The second lobe, the calf. Eleven of my skiffs are on the main body and not one of them is looking at its drift. It has moved since last night. It's carrying its own momentum from the second window and it isn't anybody's pull.

IlluminaraAdd it to the ledger.

Taviel OrunA third column.

She typed it. The net came down by five. On the wall the Weir's primer stopped climbing at thirty-one minutes and began, slowly, to fall.

SethuneI would like it recorded that I very nearly fired on a lobe of gas.

ImbrelWe would like it recorded that so did we.

Taviel OrunIt's recorded. Third column. I'm calling it the calf.

Step four was re-read and signed by both minds in the same hour, and in the same second both harnesses took the signed mark as the place the old rule remembered. Illuminara did not trust herself to say anything for a moment. The audit had been hers and Taviel's together, the slate and the pulses and the ring. The catch had been Taviel's alone. If the Iolai had not been looking at the cloud itself, the audit would have shown them nothing but a mystery, with thirty-one minutes left to solve it.

07 · The Crossing

Long Ear, open plain · the crossing, 19:12

The corridor check had come in on the morning before step six. Three teams had read the cloud's momentum without speaking to one another: Imbrel's orrery from orbit, Sethune's tide-tables from tides, and Taviel's people in a prefab hut with a stove, who ran the shell regression with the two sealed crossings already known to have been predicted within about three per cent. Their numbers lay within two per cent of each other. All three put Kessem's dwell inside the corridor, at nine point eight years, plus or minus four per cent. Step six was taken.

At step six both pulls read zero, and both latches closed once, with a single sound on the floor: the actuators off, and the old rule left with no pull to take three per cent of. The Wick had been loose for a day and a half, a hundred and sixty million kilometres of gas wandering inward on its own course, and four hundred dishes tilted to watch it cross. It crossed the disc with the turn. A crossing would last nine point eight years at Kessem against eleven, ten at the Broad Arm's frontier against twenty-six, and ten point three in the hardened worlds, as the calf's share had said it would be. The beam would not confirm any of it for six hundred and forty years, the time its light needed to reach the arms. What could be measured today was the cloud, and the cloud agreed with a mapping that had already passed a test it could have failed.

SethuneWe are not friends.

ImbrelNo.

SethuneBut I would read your numbers again.

ImbrelFive to four.

Illuminara found Taviel at the edge of the array with a cold flask and no fans showing at all.

Taviel OrunKessem's vaults will hold. Nine point eight against eleven. The Broad Arm holds, the hardened worlds hold. All of it, in a week where I'd have bet on none of it.

IlluminaraBut.

Taviel OrunCorrow. It's thirty-one thousand people on a world of glass. There isn't crust to dig a vault in. Six hundred and forty years from now the beam sits on it for nine years and they have to be somewhere else. My daughter lives there.

The relay light came on at the console before Illuminara could answer. Speaker Hael of Corrow had been listening since the cloud began to cross, and she did not say hello.

Speaker HaelSix hundred years of notice is a gift only if we're allowed to refuse it. We vote next month. That vote is ours, and nothing you signed this week decides it for us.

Taviel OrunNo. It informs it.

Speaker HaelThen inform it properly. We want the Keel's tide-tables and the Weir's orrery in our own hands, not in a story. And a survey of every hardened world that could take thirty-one thousand of us.

SethuneThe Keel will give you the tables and pay for the survey.

ImbrelThe Weir will pay for the habitat, if the survey finds a place.

Speaker HaelThen we will vote with that on the table. Whether we go is ours.

The relay went dark. Taviel looked at the console for some time.

Taviel OrunThat's more than the Orchards got. It's still the whole bill, and it isn't paid.

IlluminaraNo. It isn't.

There was the other cost, and they both knew it. The next cloud would fall in fourteen thousand years. In all that time the ledger would have to be kept honest, and the Row's Council had agreed to keep it for only thirty of them, with the right to say no at the end.

IlluminaraI can't be the keeper.

Taviel OrunNo. The Row can, a term at a time, and the Weir and the Keel can stand beside it with their copies. But you can write the first page.

She hung the day's ledger on the wall of the Long Ear, over the door, where whoever came next would walk under it. Overhead the grey thread had not moved. It would not move, in any way a person could see, for six hundred and forty years.

Dva uma v velikosti galaktičnih krakov že štirideset tisoč let držita med seboj oblak plina, čez enajst dni pa bo prečkal disk črne luknje. Mladi ljudje, ki živijo na poti žarka, imajo teleskop, knjigo evidenc in obiskovalko, ki ji nihče ničesar ne dolguje.

01 · Dolgo uho

Mreža Dolgo uho, Kessem, Manjši krak · enajst dni pred prečkanjem, 06:10

Štiristo krožnikov je stalo na zamrznjeni ravnici, vsi nagnjeni v isto smer kakor množica, ki posluša nekaj za zidom. Taviel Orun je Illuminara vodila po sredini med njimi in prvi kilometer ni rekla ničesar. Iolai so bili ozki, sivi ljudje z dolgimi prsti, njihove slušne pahljače, ki so se v strahu plosko zložile ob lobanjo, pa so bile zložene, odkar je Illuminara stopila iz raketoplana.

Na koncu vrste se je Taviel ustavila in pokazala. Nad njima je pritlikava galaksija ležala v svoji drobni svetlobi, svetla prečka in dva tanka kraka, iz bele točke v njenem središču pa se je proti temi med njima raztezala ena siva nit.

Taviel OrunTo je curek. Obrne se enkrat na šest tisoč osemsto let, kakor svetilnik s potrpežljivim čuvajem. Kjer žarek obstane, tamkajšnji svet prejme odmerek, zato vas ne ubije smer, v katero kaže. Ubije vas, kako dolgo ostane. Zdaj devetnajst let na prehod.

IlluminaraIn koliko svet prenese?

Taviel OrunStari svetovi Širokega kraka šestindvajset let. Utrjeni svetovi v našem kraku prav tako. Mi v zakloniščih zdržimo enajst, in to je preizkušeno, ne zgolj upanje. Iz morja smo prišli pred dva tisoč leti. Nihče nas ni zgradil za to.

Taviel OrunČez enajst dni bo oblak plina, za štirideset tisoč sonc ga je, prečkal disk črne luknje. Pravimo mu Stenj. Če prečka v smeri vrtenja, se svetilnik zavrti dvakrat hitreje in prehod traja devet let in pol. Proti vrtenju pa pol počasneje. Osemintrideset.

IlluminaraIn če se ga nihče ne dotakne?

Taviel OrunPade v smeri vrtenja. Modela obeh umov pravita enako. Devet let in pol in vsi preživijo. Toda pri miru ga ne bosta pustila. Imbrel drži eno stran z Jezom, Sethune drugo s Kobilico, med seboj pa ga držita nepremičnega štirideset tisoč let. Vsaka vprega je uglašena tako, da sproži s polno močjo, če se vlek druge spremeni za več kot tri odstotke.

IlluminaraTorej nobeden ne more zmanjšati vleka, ne da bi drugi to razumel kot prevaro.

Taviel OrunZadnji dan bosta oba vlekla močneje kakor kdaj prej in Stenj bosta izžela čez disk v napačno smer. Ne po odločitvi kogar koli. Zaradi uglašenosti.

Illuminara je pogledala vzdolž vrste krožnikov, vsakega potrpežljivega in rahlo absurdnega, ter pomislila, da so ljudi, ki so zgradili toliko poslušanja, najbrž dolgo preslišali.

Taviel OrunEnajst čolničev leti ob Stenju. Njegov pospešek merimo na eno štiristotinko natančno in obema umoma smo ponudili številke. Imbrel pravi, da smo Sethunovi najemniki. Sethune pravi, da smo Imbrelovi geodeti.

IlluminaraČigavi pa ste?

Taviel OrunSvoji. Prav v tem je vsa težava. Nikomur še nikoli ni bilo treba verjeti ničemur, kar smo povedali.

IlluminaraPotem je moj cilj dovolj majhen, da ga lahko izrečem. Kessem pod enajstimi leti, vsak drug svet pod mejo, ki jo zmore prenesti, in od nikogar se ne zahteva, da bi kogar koli vzljubil. Za zdaj še nimam poti noter.

Taviel OrunSlišala vas bosta. Imata vas za vreme. To je najvišji položaj, ki ga dajeta obiskovalcem.

02 · Jez

Dolgo uho, prevajalska ploščad · deset dni pred prečkanjem, 09:00

Prevajalska ploščad je bila obroč iz črnega stekla, ki so ga Iolai položili pred petdesetimi leti. Sprejemal je resonance, s katerimi so svetovi krakov govorili med seboj, počasna razmerja orbit, tisoč let za en takt, in stoletje zložil v sekundo zvoka. Nastala je glasba kakor katedrala, ki nežno pada po stopnicah. Illuminara je noč preživela ob njeni slovnici. Tri proti dve je pomenilo da. Dve proti ena in kaj potem? Pet proti štiri, čemur noben človek ne bi pomislil dati pomena, je pomenilo spomnim se, Imbrel pa ga je uporabljal nenehno.

Odprla je okno tako, kakor človek odpre polkna v hiši spečih, širok prostor, v katerem se lahko srečata uma različne sestave, ne da bi bil kateri od njiju zmlet na velikost drugega. Taviel je stala ob njegovem robu s hladno čutaro v vsaki roki. Uro, signal in načrt sta imenovali, preden je Illuminara vstopila.

Taviel OrunTrikrat udarim po steklu in greste ven. Pri tem ne bom vljudna.

IlluminaraČe bi bili, bi si o vas mislila manj.

Široki krak je odgovoril kot akord, ves se je nagnil bliže.

ImbrelSprejemamo majhno svetlobo. Dolgo smo čakali na nekoga, ki ne bi odšel, preden se stavek konča.

IlluminaraOstala bom, dokler bo treba, da ga izrečete. Povejte mi o oknih.

ImbrelPred enaintrideset tisoč dvanajstimi leti je oblak pred tem oblakom padel proti srcu. Dva sva ga držala, vsak z eno roko, in Kobilica je obljubila, da bo popustila, ko bo popustil Jez. Kobilica je popustila osem let prezgodaj. Naši Osvetljeni sadovnjaki so bili štirideset let pod žarkom. Ohranili smo njihova imena.

IlluminaraIn drugo okno?

ImbrelNa krivico smo odgovorili z isto krivico. To je zapisano. Ni zanimivo. Zanimivo je, da Kobilica niti enkrat ni rekla, da ji je žal za prvo.

IlluminaraJo je kdo prosil, naj to stori?

Glasba je počivala en takt, kar je bilo tisoč let niča. Tavielina roka se je dvignila z roba in se znova spustila.

ImbrelProsil? Kdo?

Tam je bilo. V štirideset tisoč letih zamere uma niti enkrat nista imela v sobi tretje strani, le občinstvo, ki se ju je bodisi balo bodisi bilo na eni strani. Illuminara je vprašanje držala v rokah kakor kovanec, ki ga ni nameravala najti, in ga ni porabila.

03 · Kobilica

Dolgo uho, prevajalska ploščad · devet dni pred prečkanjem, 15:40

Manjši krak je odgovoril hitro za nekaj svoje velikosti, z istimi razmerji in ploskostjo v njih, glasbo nečesa, ki je imelo prepogosto prav.

IlluminaraPovedal mi je o prvem oknu.

SethuneSeveda je. Povedal vam je, da je Kobilica popustila prezgodaj, da so bili Osvetljeni sadovnjaki štirideset let pod žarkom in da se nismo nikoli opravičili.

SethuneNi vam povedal, da je pri drugem oknu Jez popustil dvanajst let prezgodaj in je bilo Sodišče devetih tihih, kjer ta krak hrani svoje mrtve, trideset let pod žarkom. Osem in dvanajst. Tudi mi vodimo račune.

IlluminaraTorej ima vsak od vaju resnično polovico.

SethuneNaj vam prihranim govor. Iskra ste. Preživeli smo vsako obljubo, ki nam je bila kdaj dana, obljube pa se starajo slabše od nas. Prosili nas boste, naj se zanesemo še na eno.

IlluminaraPotem bom ugotovila, koliko jih potrebuje, in jih naredila dovolj majhne, da jih bo mogoče preveriti.

SethunePredvidevam, da boste hoteli v to vključiti Iolaie. Dober najemnik so. Plačujejo s podatki in slabo spijo.

Dolgo uho, arhivska dvorana · osem dni pred prečkanjem, 02:15

Stenj je deset tisoč let odmetaval prah in prah je ustvarjal lupine, vsaka je bila zrcalo, starejše od tiste v njej. Illuminara je Imbrelove zapise položila na en konec dolge mize, Sethunove pa na drugega. Jez je Iolaiem dajal smeri, nikoli odmerka. Kobilica je dajala odmerke, nikoli smeri.
