A ring habitat of fourteen thousand has seventy hours to decide whether its star is attacking it, and the only evidence that it is not is a silence nobody had thought to measure.

01 · Seventy Hours

Calloway Reach, Ring Council chamber · Day 1, 06:10

The clock on the chamber wall read 70:00:00. Someone had put it there so that it would be read aloud, and nobody had. Outside the long window the ring turned slowly under a red sun the size of a coin, with fourteen thousand people on its inner face, and the room smelled of cold tea and of a council that had not slept.

Illuminara had come aboard three weeks earlier on an ice tender, hired by the Rakel cooperative to model how heat and light loaded the cutting quays. She was in the chamber because her models were the only ones nobody had yet argued with. She stood at the back, beside the water jug.

Teodora VanceThe Wick has thrown six dangerous bursts in eleven days. In nine years of records it threw about one a month. Eleven days is two hundred and sixty-four hours; six bursts in that time is one every forty-four, and that is not a fluctuation I can fold into the background. They cluster after our evening traffic peaks. The next natural alignment is due at about four in the morning on Day Four. Under ordinary traffic the shield office forecasts one point three times the rating of our parasol. Ferries need twenty-six hours to finish loading, and I will not cut a two-hour margin out of a ring's lives. The order has to go out by hour forty-two.

Pell RourkeThe parasol takes one burst. I will not promise it takes that one.

IlluminaraWhat does leaving cost?

Teodora VanceRakel. Everything we mine. A ring that leaves carries eight months of water, and after that it's a very large cup.

Vance was sixty and square-shouldered, with the habit of putting the worst number first so that no one could accuse her of hiding it. She turned from the window to face the back of the room.

Teodora VanceDon't tell me it's talking. We have no way to know it is speaking at all, and you are asking fourteen thousand people to stay under a possible weapon on the strength of a pattern. If I'm wrong about the weapon we lose the ice and a year. If you're wrong we lose the ring.

IlluminaraI won't tell you it's talking. I haven't seen enough to say so, and you would be right not to believe me if I did. I'd like your dock-clock traffic log, Dr. Brannock's flare record, the specifications of every detector, and the room until the evening session.

Teodora VanceThe council sits at eighteen hundred. At eighteen hundred I put the evacuation to a vote.

IlluminaraThen I'll bring you something you can test before you vote.

Vance looked at the clock and then at her. Curiosity did not soften her face; it made the responsibility in it more exact.

Teodora VanceTest it with what? We have sixty-nine hours and fifty-one minutes.

02 · Nine Years of Margins

Ring observatory, Brannock's office · Day 1, 09:30

Ilse Brannock kept the flare record in a ledger as well as on the network, because the ledger could not be edited by anyone who disliked it. Nine years of the Wick filled it, night by night, in a small upright hand with questions in the margins. A few were underlined twice.

Ilse BrannockYou're the ice woman with the thermal models.

IlluminaraToday I'm the ice woman who read your flare record. It's very clean. Who keeps it?

Ilse BrannockI do. Nobody else wanted to. A flare is a flare.

IlluminaraYou don't think so.

Ilse put a hand flat on the ledger as one might on a sleeping animal.

Ilse BrannockI showed this to two people. One laughed, kindly, which was worse. I said the Wick grows louder when we do. After every busy evening the next burst is larger by about the same fraction. A star's flares don't care about our trade. I knew how it sounded, so I stopped saying it.

IlluminaraAnd the timing?

Ilse BrannockAlways in a gap. I called it the small hours because that was the gap we kept giving it.

Illuminara laid the traffic log over the flare record on the glass table. The observatory clock and dock clock were three minutes apart. Nobody had held the records together because the exchange net carried private trade.

She slid one trace by three minutes. The bright marks dropped into the troughs of the traffic like coins into a purse.

Ilse BrannockFour-oh-five. Shift change. The ring goes quiet for twenty minutes while the crews swap.

IlluminaraThe size follows the loudness before the gap. The timing follows the gap itself. If there is an intention here, the least extravagant account is not anger. It is turn-taking: something raising its voice over a crowd, then waiting not to be overwritten. But the same trace could still come from a rotating spot, a precursor that suppresses our band, or chance.

Ilse BrannockSay what you want to do.

IlluminaraMove the gap. Fill four-oh-five with ordinary traffic, open a new gap at seven, and write every prediction before we touch the switches.

Ilse BrannockThe exchange monitor shares the band. A precursor could fool it.

IlluminaraWhat does not share it?

Ilse BrannockThe old bolometric plate. Hard wire, separate clock, nothing in the exchange band. Rourke wanted it scrapped.

IlluminaraThen it stays. And you present the test. I will not borrow nine years of your listening and call it my discovery.

Ilse looked at the double-underlined question in her ledger. Hope is not evidence, Illuminara thought. But shame can hide evidence for years if nobody makes room for the person carrying it.

Illuminara turned the ledger's pages back to the worst flares and forward to the Day Four forecast, and stopped. The test would tell them whether the star kept time. It would not shrink the burst already coming.

IlluminaraOne more thing, and it is a question about your own margins. If the size follows the loudness before the gap, then the Day Four burst is not fixed. It is being sized right now by what we do on the evening of Day Three. What happens to the flare after a quiet evening?

Ilse turned eight pages without looking for them. The smallest flares in the book were all there: the nights after the ring had gone dark for the harvest festival, when the trade band was nearly empty by dusk.

Ilse BrannockSmall. They're the smallest in the book. I put them down to the calendar.

IlluminaraThen the lever is the dusk peak, not the gap. If the council can cap one evening's traffic before the Day Four alignment, the parasol may meet something near eight-tenths instead of one point three. Pell will have to model it. I can't promise it. I can tell you which number to try to move.

Ilse BrannockI will present it if the envelope contains the ways I may be wrong.

IlluminaraPut them first.

03 · The Case for Flight

Council chamber · Day 1, 18:00

Vance opened the session by reading the clock aloud: fifty-eight hours, ten minutes. Then she gave the floor to Rourke, who stood with his hands behind him, like a man giving evidence in a trial he hoped to lose.

Pell RourkeThe dangerous dawn alignment on Day Four, ordinary traffic, one point three of rating. Our two requested test gaps may draw smaller responses before it. If they do, that is new behavior, not the seventh and eighth members of the old sequence. It may strengthen the case for turn-taking, or mean the experiment itself is increasing the hazard.

Teodora VanceThat's the case for flight, and I will make it myself so nobody thinks I haven't. Evacuations fail when they start late. A star that changes because we ask it to is not automatically safer than a star that does not.

Gideon Farrow rose from the guild benches. He was round and beautifully dressed and had been counting something in his head for the whole session.

Gideon FarrowWho pays if we flee from a weather event? The ice is my guild's wages and the ring's drinking water. It can't be that nobody may ask whether the star is just a star.

Teodora VanceNobody has forbidden it. Dr. Brannock?

Ilse stood. Her hands were steady on the lectern, and Illuminara, three rows back, saw her find the notes she had meant not to need.

Ilse BrannockI have nine years of flares, three instruments and three clocks. The timing sits in the quiet of our traffic, and the size follows the loudness before it. I have three rivals: a spot rotating every twenty-four-point-one hours, a lull caused by a precursor rather than chosen by us, and chance.

Teodora VanceHow much chance?

Ilse BrannockI kept the clustering and the one-a-month background of the nine-year record, and shuffled ten thousand pairs of gaps with the same widths and traffic levels. Seven pairs caught bursts in both timing windows and both amplitude bands. Seven in ten thousand is not zero. It is also not an argument I would throw away.

Dov AchterbergA calculation built from the same ledger that suggested the question. And your windows are fifty minutes wide.

Ilse BrannockYes. Which is why the spot and precursor predictions are sealed beside ours. If the spot fires at the old hour, we lose. If the exchange band fails while the independent plate stays quiet, we lose. If one requested result misses, we write miss before we explain anything.

IlluminaraAt four-oh-five tomorrow we fill the usual gap with ordinary traffic. At seven we pause the exchange net for twenty-two minutes. The independent plate remains live. We repeat with a shorter gap after the next dusk peak. And there is a second lever, which the ledger itself points to. The size follows the loudness before the gap, so the Day Four burst is being sized by the evening of Day Three. If the guild caps that one dusk peak, Pell's median should fall well below the parasol's rating. That is a prediction too, and it can fail. The council writes the stop conditions.

Gideon FarrowWhat does the pause cost my traders? And what does your cap cost them?

IlluminaraTell the room what they need to keep.

Gideon FarrowThe settlement hour. Move around it and I will sell the test to the guild. The cap I will price tonight, and the number will not be small: that dusk is my best evening of the quarter. I won't sell a permanent blackout, and I won't sell a permanent cap.

Dov AchterbergNor should he. A scheduled silence is a scheduled vulnerability. Medical calls, collision alarms, smugglers who know when nobody is looking. If the proposed cure requires fourteen thousand people to become deaf on a timetable, I prefer the ferries.

Illuminara turned toward him rather than back to the lectern.

IlluminaraThen the test must preserve an emergency carrier outside the crowded band, and any lasting arrangement must be movable. Nadim, can that be done without contaminating the plate?

Nadim OyelaranA narrow red channel, hard-limited to alarms and medical speech. The plate won't see it. For a lasting window, the Chair could choose within a ninety-minute band and announce it fifteen minutes ahead.

Teodora VanceNoted. My cancel line: any requested burst over nine-tenths, any burst outside both registered windows, any failure of the independent plate, or any failure of the red channel. The ferries are fuelled tonight and manifests cut. A trigger starts loading within one hour; completing it still takes twenty-six. Nobody edits that sentence afterward.

04 · The Gap Moves

Communications office, exchange net · Day 2, 06:52

At four-oh-five the old gap had been filled, and the Wick had said nothing. The exchange band stayed clean; so did the independent bolometric plate. Ilse had been awake since the previous morning and sat very straight in a chair she had not chosen.

Nadim OyelaranSealed envelope is in the council log. Rotation said four-oh-five, which did not happen. Precursor said the exchange band would fail there while the plate remained quiet, which did not happen. Turn-taking says seven, within twenty-five minutes, between half and seven-tenths of rating.

The pause had been posted in the council log the evening before, so that every office would know to expect it. At seven the exchange net went quiet. Kitchens went on, ferries stayed fuelled, and the red emergency carrier whispered with two medical calls and one collision alarm. The trading floor stopped for twenty-two minutes as fourteen thousand people agreed to leave a space.

The hard-wired plate drew a flat line, then a flat line, and then a sharp stroke at seven-oh-two. The network monitor followed a fraction later. The long shoulder on the decay was the mark Ilse had drawn in her ledger for nine years.

Ilse BrannockFifty-eight hundredths on the plate.

Nadim OyelaranInside timing and amplitude. Red channel never dropped.

Nobody cheered. Illuminara held Ilse's elbow only after the older woman reached for her.

Ilse BrannockOne.

IlluminaraOne.

At seven-oh-six a cargo tug on the outer rail killed its transponder and began drifting toward the customs lock. Dov's security desk saw it only because the lock's alarm line rode the red carrier, and the desk had four minutes to seal the lock before the tug's crew reached it.

Dov AchterbergLock six sealed. Tug has gone back to its berth. They knew our hour because we posted our hour.

He said it to the room, not to Illuminara, and he did not say I told you. The tug's name went into the log beside the minutes.

The second requested gap came at twenty-two thirty on the same day, after a smaller dusk peak than the evening before: a stalled ferry queue the guild had not planned. A weak rise appeared on the exchange monitor eleven minutes before the pause. Dov, watching from the council feed, called it a precursor. The hard-wired plate stayed level.

At twenty-two thirty-six the Wick flared. The registered amplitude band ended at forty hundredths. The plate climbed to forty-one.

Dov AchterbergOutside the envelope.

Ilse BrannockBy one hundredth. It is a miss.

Nadim OyelaranThe early rise was our own carrier leaking into the exchange monitor. It is absent from the plate. That defeats the precursor claim, but it does not put the amplitude back inside the envelope.

Pell RourkeAnd two requested responses in sixteen hours are faster than even the forty-four-hour cluster we started with. If we are causing them, that matters more than whether we have taught the sun manners.

Illuminara studied the two traces and did not rescue her prediction. Beside the second trace Ilse had written the evening's peak, and beside the first, the evening before. She set the two numbers side by side and left them without comment.

Ilse BrannockFifty-eight hundredths after the loud evening. Forty-one after the quiet one.

Pell RourkeOne pair.

Ilse BrannockOne pair. It fell the right way. It is not a law, and I will not write it as one.

IlluminaraRecord the timing hit, the amplitude miss, the failed precursor rival, the faster cadence and the pair of evenings. Then stop opening gaps until the council decides what the faster cadence means.

Ilse BrannockYou wanted a second night.

IlluminaraI wanted an answer that could tell us no. This one has.

05 · Forty Hours

Council chamber · Day 2, 23:10

Clock hour forty-one found the chamber full, with twenty-nine hours left on the wall and one hour before the order would have to go out. Under the clock were four lines, none softened: OLD-GAP SILENCE; FIRST REQUEST HIT; SECOND REQUEST TIMING HIT / AMPLITUDE MISS; REQUESTED CADENCE FASTER THAN BACKGROUND.

Teodora VanceNobody in this room gets to call that two clean predictions. Dr. Brannock, what survives?

Ilse BrannockThe rotating-spot prediction failed at four-oh-five. The precursor prediction failed on the independent plate. In ten thousand paired shuffles, seven matched both timing and amplitude; ours matched both timings but only one amplitude. The data still prefers schedule-response. It does not prove a mind, and the faster cadence may be a cost of asking.

Dov AchterbergThen stop asking and load the ferries. The experiment changed the thing we feared. And it told every smuggler on the outer rail what hour to move.

Pell RourkeOr exposed that it was already waiting for gaps we happened to give it. The Day Four burst remains the dangerous one. Capping the Day Three dusk peak alone takes my median from one point three to about one point zero. Turning the parasol before dawn takes it to about nine-tenths. What the bounded silence adds I cannot separate from the rest, and I will not pretend to. Together, eight-tenths.

Dov AchterbergMedian. Your upper edge?

Pell RourkeNine-tenths. At the cancel line.

The two numbers stayed between them. Vance looked not at Illuminara but at Ilse.

Teodora VanceIf we stay, what do you ask the Wick to do?

Ilse BrannockNothing beyond what the dangerous burst may do anyway. One bounded silence at dawn, three pulses from our cutter, then no second request. If the flare comes in the window and under the line, we learn whether leaving room changes the load. If not, the manifests are already cut.

Gideon FarrowThe cap costs the guild its best settlement of the quarter, on the Day Three dusk. We will take it once. Not daily, and not without the loss entered beside the science.

Dov AchterbergAnd the notice. The tug at lock six knew seven o'clock because we gave it thirteen hours. No fixed daily blackout, and no posted hour. The Chair chooses inside a ninety-minute band and announces it fifteen minutes ahead. The red channel stays open. Security may cancel without your permission. And the tug is mine to answer for, not the science's.

Nadim OyelaranI can enforce that in hardware. Trade carrier dark; red carrier live; plate independent. Six signatures to change it.

Illuminara had come in with a posted window and was leaving with a hidden one. She wrote Dov's clause into the draft protocol in his own words, and when he read it over her shoulder he changed one verb back.

Teodora VanceThe ferries stay fuelled. Loading starts within one hour if the plate crosses nine-tenths, the flare leaves the window, the red carrier fails, or security calls the silence unsafe. Anyone may take a berth now. We attempt one bounded exchange at dawn. Dov's moving-window amendment and Farrow's cost ledger are part of the motion.

The vote passed seven to four, not nine to two. Dov voted no. His amendment passed eleven to zero.

Afterward the reply was designed in the communications office. Nadim had the forty-metre ice-cutting array. Ilse had her ledger open to the rising edge of the first requested flare.

Nadim OyelaranI can give it a beam. I can't tell you it will see it.

Ilse BrannockThree pulses on the rhythm of its own rise. Then silence for as long as the pulses took. Heard, and your turn.

IlluminaraNo claim about what it means.

Ilse BrannockNo. Only a courtesy we can withdraw.

06 · A Turn at Four-Oh-Five

Calloway Reach, communications office and Rakel Quay · Day 4, 04:05

Under ordinary traffic the dangerous burst had been forecast at one point three of parasol rating. On the evening of Day Three the guild had capped its dusk peak, and Farrow's ledger carried the loss: the best evening of the quarter. Turning the parasol cost a month's thruster propellant and left Rakel Quay outside its full shadow. Rourke's registered range was seven-tenths to nine-tenths. Nine-tenths remained the line.

The Chair chose four-oh-five from the ninety-minute band and announced it fifteen minutes before. The red carrier stayed live. In the communications office Nadim held the beam trigger. On Rakel Quay his sister Kemi and two riggers waited beside the relay-mast breakers, because the model said the exposed masts would take the first side-load.

Kemi OyelaranRakel ready. You owe me two masts if your polite sun sneezes.

Nadim OyelaranPut them on Farrow's ledger.

Gideon FarrowThey are already there.

At four-oh-five Nadim sent three pulses. The trade band remained silent afterward. A medical call crossed the red carrier from nursery six; a child had swallowed a button. The silence did not make the ring helpless.

Four minutes passed.

The independent plate climbed.

Pell RourkePoint six. Point seven-two. Parasol taking thirty-one percent.

A second shoulder rose under the first.

Teodora VanceRead the plate, not the model.

Pell RourkePoint eight-six.

At Rakel, the first mast began to arc. Kemi cut its breaker before the automatic relay understood what was happening. The mast folded across an empty loading rail. The second leaned toward a fuel line.

Kemi OyelaranLosing west two. Clearing the line now.

She drove the quay tug into the mast's lower brace. Metal went down away from the fuel line, taking the tug's manipulator arm with it.

Nadim OyelaranKemi?

Kemi OyelaranStill expensive.

The plate touched eighty-nine hundredths. For twelve seconds its uncertainty band crossed the line, though the central reading did not.

Teodora VanceRourke.

Pell RourkeCentral reading below nine. Structure stable. My recommendation is hold, Chair. Your line says over, not near.

Vance's finger rested on the loading order. She could have called uncertainty a trigger. Nobody would have blamed her.

Teodora VanceHold. Kemi has the quay. Red carrier is live. If the central plate rises one hundredth, load.

It did not. The long shoulder fell through eight-tenths, then seven. The parasol held. Rakel lost two relay masts and one tug arm; no one was hurt.

In the decay, with Nadim's array still silent and the ring keeping the space it had promised, the independent plate drew three small steps.

Ilse BrannockThree. I have nine years and it has never made three.

IlluminaraDon't read it yet. We don't know that it's a reply.

Ilse BrannockNo. We know only that it happened after our three.

They did not repeat the request that night. The next day the council authorized one movable window, with the red channel and security veto intact, and required a fresh vote every seven days. Dov's desk added a standing check of the outer rail to every window, a duty the protocol still carries under his name. Farrow entered the lost settlement, two masts, a tug arm and a month of propellant in the same ledger as the avoided evacuation. Dov signed the safety protocol and wrote beneath his name that he still believed they should leave.

Teodora VanceHe is allowed to be wrong in the record, if he is wrong.

IlluminaraSo are we.

Ilse closed her ledger, opened it again, and wrote on the next clean line in her small upright hand: Four-oh-five. We stopped. It knocked.

Obročasti habitat s štirinajst tisoč prebivalci ima sedemdeset ur, da se odloči, ali ga njegova zvezda napada, edini dokaz, da ga ne, pa je tišina, ki je ni še nihče pomislil izmeriti.

01 · Sedemdeset ur

Calloway Reach, dvorana sveta obroča · 1. dan, 06:10

Ura na steni dvorane je kazala 70:00:00. Nekdo jo je postavil tja zato, da bi čas izgovorili naglas, pa ga ni nihče. Zunaj dolgega okna se je obroč počasi vrtel pod rdečo zvezdo, veliko kakor kovanec, na njegovi notranji strani je živelo štirinajst tisoč ljudi, v prostoru pa je dišalo po hladnem čaju in svetu, ki ni spal.

Illuminara je tri tedne prej prispela na krovu lednega tenderja; zadruga Rakel jo je najela, da modelira, kako toplota in svetloba obremenjujeta rezalne pomole. V dvorani je bila, ker so bili njeni modeli edini, s katerimi se še nihče ni prepiral. Stala je zadaj ob vrču z vodo.

Teodora VanceWick je v enajstih dneh sprožil šest nevarnih izbruhov. V devetih letih zapisov je sprožil približno enega na mesec. Enajst dni je dvesto štiriinšestdeset ur; šest izbruhov v tem času pomeni enega na štiriinštirideset ur, tega pa ne morem spraviti med nihanja ozadja. Kopičijo se po naših večernih prometnih konicah. Naslednja naravna poravnava se pričakuje okoli štirih zjutraj četrtega dne. Ob običajnem prometu urad za ščit napoveduje eno celo tri nazivne zmogljivosti našega senčnika. Trajekti potrebujejo šestindvajset ur, da končajo natovarjanje, jaz pa iz življenj na obroču ne bom izrezala dvourne rezerve. Ukaz mora biti izdan do dvainštiridesete ure.

Pell RourkeSenčnik prenese en izbruh. Ne bom obljubil, da prenese tistega.

IlluminaraKaj stane odhod?

Teodora VanceRakel. Vse, kar rudarimo. Obroč, ki odide, s seboj odnese osem mesecev vode, potem pa postane zelo velik kozarec.

Vance je bila stara šestdeset let in širokih ramen, navado pa je imela najprej povedati najslabše število, da ji nihče ne bi mogel očitati prikrivanja. Od okna se je obrnila proti zadnjemu delu prostora.

Teodora VanceNe govorite mi, da govori. Nikakor ne moremo vedeti, ali sploh govori, vi pa od štirinajst tisoč ljudi zahtevate, naj ostanejo pod morebitnim orožjem na podlagi vzorca. Če se jaz motim glede orožja, izgubimo led in leto dni. Če se motite vi, izgubimo obroč.

IlluminaraNe bom vam govorila, da govori. Nisem videla dovolj, da bi to trdila, in prav bi imeli, če mi ne bi verjeli. Potrebujem vaš dnevnik prometa po pristaniški uri, dnevnik izbruhov doktorice Brannock, specifikacije vseh detektorjev in ta prostor do večerne seje.

Teodora VanceSvet zaseda ob osemnajstih. Ob osemnajstih dam evakuacijo na glasovanje.

IlluminaraPotem vam bom pred glasovanjem prinesla nekaj, kar lahko preizkusite.

Vance je pogledala uro in nato njo. Radovednost ji ni omehčala obraza; odgovornost na njem je naredila natančnejšo.

Teodora VanceS čim boste to preizkusili? Imamo devetinšestdeset ur in enainpetdeset minut.

02 · Devet let robnih zapiskov

Observatorij obroča, pisarna Brannockove · 1. dan, 09:30

Ilse Brannock je dnevnik izbruhov vodila v knjigi in na omrežju, ker knjige ni mogel urejati nihče, ki mu vsebina ni bila všeč. Devet let Wicka jo je polnilo noč za nočjo, z drobno pokončno pisavo in vprašanji ob robovih. Nekaj jih je bilo dvakrat podčrtanih.

Ilse BrannockVi ste ženska za led s toplotnimi modeli.

IlluminaraDanes sem ženska za led, ki je prebrala vaš dnevnik izbruhov. Zelo čist je. Kdo ga vodi?

Ilse BrannockJaz. Nihče drug ga ni hotel. Izbruh je pač izbruh.

IlluminaraVi ne mislite tako.

Ilse je položila dlan na knjigo, kakor bi jo položila na spečo žival.

Ilse BrannockTo sem pokazala dvema človekoma. Eden se je zasmejal, prijazno, kar je bilo še huje. Rekla sem, da Wick postane glasnejši, ko postanemo glasnejši mi. Po vsakem prometnem večeru je naslednji izbruh večji za približno enak delež. Zvezdini izbruhi se ne menijo za našo trgovino. Vedela sem, kako zveni, zato sem o tem nehala govoriti.

IlluminaraKaj pa čas?

Ilse BrannockVedno v vrzeli. Rekla sem ji zgodnje ure, ker smo ji takrat vedno dajali vrzel.

Illuminara je dnevnik prometa položila čez dnevnik izbruhov na stekleni mizi. Ura observatorija in pristaniška ura sta se razlikovali za tri minute. Nihče zapisov ni držal skupaj, ker je borzno omrežje prenašalo zasebne posle.

Eno sled je premaknila za tri minute. Svetle oznake so padle v doline prometa kakor kovanci v mošnjo.

Ilse BrannockŠtiri nič pet. Menjava izmene. Obroč za dvajset minut utihne, medtem ko se ekipe zamenjajo.

IlluminaraVelikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo. Čas sledi sami vrzeli. Če je tukaj namen, najmanj pretirana razlaga ni jeza. Je izmenjava besede: nekaj dvigne glas nad množico in nato čaka, da ga ne prepišemo. Toda enako sled bi še vedno lahko povzročili vrteča se pega, predhodni pojav, ki zatre naš pas, ali naključje.

Ilse BrannockPovejte, kaj želite narediti.

IlluminaraPremakniti vrzel. Štiri nič pet zapolniti z običajnim prometom, odpreti novo vrzel ob sedmih in vsako napoved zapisati, preden se dotaknemo stikal.

Ilse BrannockNadzornik borze uporablja isti pas. Predhodni pojav bi ga lahko prevaral.

IlluminaraKaj ga ne uporablja?

Ilse BrannockStara bolometrična plošča. Žična povezava, ločena ura, nič v borznem pasu. Rourke jo je hotel zavreči.

IlluminaraPotem ostane. Preizkus pa predstavite vi. Ne bom si izposodila devetih let vašega poslušanja in temu rekla svoje odkritje.

Ilse je pogledala dvakrat podčrtano vprašanje v svojem dnevniku. Upanje ni dokaz, je pomislila Illuminara. Toda sram lahko leta skriva dokaz, če nihče ne naredi prostora človeku, ki ga nosi.

Illuminara je obrnila strani dnevnika nazaj k najhujšim izbruhom in naprej k napovedi za četrti dan ter se ustavila. Preizkus bi jim povedal, ali zvezda sledi času. Ne bi zmanjšal izbruha, ki je že prihajal.

IlluminaraŠe nekaj, in to je vprašanje o vaših robnih zapiskih. Če velikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo, izbruh četrtega dne ni določen. Prav zdaj mu velikost daje to, kar počnemo tretji dan zvečer. Kaj se zgodi z izbruhom po tihem večeru?

Ilse je obrnila osem strani, ne da bi jih iskala. Najmanjši izbruhi v knjigi so bili vsi tam: noči po prazniku žetve, ko je obroč potemnel in je bil trgovski pas do mraka skoraj prazen.

Ilse BrannockMajhni. Najmanjši v knjigi so. Pripisala sem jih koledarju.

IlluminaraPotem je vzvod večerna konica, ne vrzel. Če lahko svet omeji promet enega večera pred poravnavo četrtega dne, bo senčnik morda dobil nekaj blizu osmih desetin namesto ena cele tri. Pell bo to moral modelirati. Tega ne morem obljubiti. Lahko vam povem, katero številko naj poskusite premakniti.

Ilse BrannockPredstavila bom, če bodo v ovojnici načini, kako se lahko motim.

IlluminaraPostavite jih na prvo mesto.

03 · Argument za beg

Dvorana sveta · 1. dan, 18:00

Vance je sejo začela tako, da je na glas prebrala uro: oseminpetdeset ur in deset minut. Nato je dala besedo Rourku, ki je stal z rokami za hrbtom kakor človek, ki pričuje na sojenju, za katero upa, da ga bo izgubil.

Pell RourkeNevarna poravnava ob zori četrtega dne, običajen promet, ena cela tri nazivne zmogljivosti. Naši dve zahtevani preizkusni vrzeli lahko pred tem prikličeta manjša odziva. Če ju, bo to novo vedenje, ne sedmi in osmi člen starega zaporedja. Lahko okrepi razlago o izmenjavi besede ali pa pomeni, da poskus sam povečuje nevarnost.

Teodora VanceTo je argument za beg in povedala ga bom sama, da nihče ne bo mislil, da ga nisem upoštevala. Evakuacije propadejo, ko se začnejo prepozno. Zvezda, ki se spremeni, ker jo prosimo, ni samodejno varnejša od zvezde, ki se ne.

Gideon Farrow je vstal s klopi ceha. Bil je okrogel, brezhibno oblečen in vso sejo je nekaj štel v glavi.

Gideon FarrowKdo plača, če zbežimo pred vremenskim pojavom? Led je plača mojega ceha in pitna voda obroča. Ne more veljati, da nihče ne sme vprašati, ali je zvezda samo zvezda.

Teodora VanceNihče tega ni prepovedal. Doktorica Brannock?

Claude — Strong humane premise and a dialogue-driven negotiation that resolves with moral weight (no forgiveness, honest limits). Hurt by dense procedural legalism, invented-world jargon and a somewhat clinical, over-engineered middle that may lose casual readers. Ending lands quietly well.

A dying officer will not speak, and a mother needs a grave. Illuminara looks for a door narrow enough for both of them to walk through.

01 · The Ward at Midnight

Saint Aldis Hospice, east ward · first night, past midnight

Eleven beds stood where the ward had been built for seven, and the lamp at the nurses' table was turned down to a bead. The man by the window had not spoken in three weeks. The woman in the next bed, kept in for a lung fever, had stopped pretending to sleep an hour ago.

Maren Teague was reading the card clipped to his bed. It said OSTROW, H., and under it, in a clerk's hand, late Ninth Militia.

Something stood at the foot of the bed that had not been there when the lamp was turned down. It looked like attention that had found a shape: a tall woman with the stillness of someone who had learned to wait for the end of a sentence.

IlluminaraI will go if you would rather I did not stay. I only come where someone is awake and willing to see me.

Maren did not answer at once. She had spent eleven years among clerks who said they were sorry.

MarenYou are not a nurse.

IlluminaraNo. I listen. Sometimes that turns out to be the only skill a night needs.

MarenThen listen. The Ninth held the ford the winter my son went missing. I have written to the registry eleven times, and they tell me the records burned. Here lies a Ninth officer, an arm's length from me, breathing. He knows where my boy is, and he will not say.

She said it quietly, as if the man might hear. His eyes were open, fixed on the ceiling, and a muscle moved in his jaw.

IlluminaraWhat do you want from him?

MarenA place. Anything else I could learn to live without. A place, so I can stop standing in every field.

IlluminaraThen I should tell you what I won't do. I won't make him speak. I won't carry a word between you that he has not allowed. If I did, I would be a knife, and you would never know what he gave and what was taken.

MarenThen what use are you?

IlluminaraI don't know yet. I would like to find out whether there is a door. Silence like his is often a wall. Sometimes it is a shield, and a shield can have a way through it.

A shield held for three weeks, the whole arm trembling, Illuminara thought. Someone is standing behind it who is not him.

MarenAnd if there is no door?

IlluminaraThen I will tell you so, and you will have lost a night, not a year.

Maren lay back. Across the narrow gap, Halvard Ostrow's hand lay open on the blanket, and for the first time she looked at it as the hand of a man rather than of a regiment.

02 · The Shield

Saint Aldis Hospice, east ward · second night, before dawn

Illuminara went to the other bed. Halvard's eyes moved from the ceiling to her face and stayed there, which no one on the ward had reported him doing.

IlluminaraI will ask you nothing tonight. I wanted you to know I am here, and that you may send me away.

His voice, when it came, had the dryness of paper kept too long.

HalvardYou are not the chaplain. The chaplain wants my sins. You want something else.

IlluminaraThe woman beside you wants a place. She has not asked me to take it from you.

HalvardShe is Teague's mother. I knew it when they wheeled her in. Pell was a scout. I wrote his name on the burial slip. The company roll burned, but Corvane kept the order book: dates, officers and the five soldiers assigned to each detail.

IlluminaraOne of those five was your daughter.

HalvardLysa. I sent her north before the ford broke and signed that the detail had been completed. The Ninth is no secret. Teague's petitions have put it everywhere Corvane looks. The secret is the day. The tags carry marks, not dates. The book keeps details by date and no burial places. Give Corvane the ground and the day, and it finds me. It asks for five and finds four. It hangs the fifth for desertion and me for the lie.

He turned his face to the wall.

HalvardYou want me to give a grave and in exchange hang my child. I will take my silence to my own.

IlluminaraThat fear is coherent. I cannot promise Lysa is safe. But a parish finder could test a place without learning the day, the officer or the detail. The ground could give families names without giving Corvane the join its book requires.

HalvardAnd how does a finder discover a stone six paces from a drowned fence?

IlluminaraBy receiving directions without your name and testing them in daylight with witnesses. A lawful writ could still reach this ward. Distance is not a wall. Is it enough for you to consider the question?

HalvardIf every readable tag goes into the book. If the finder does not ask who dug. If she keeps her right to ask elsewhere. I will not buy her silence about me.

IlluminaraThose are conditions, not consent. I will carry them as conditions. Nothing more.

For the first time he looked at her as at a colleague rather than a visitor. He had not agreed. He had changed the shape of what agreement would require.

03 · What Maren Was Asked

Saint Aldis Hospice, east ward · third night, the lamp low

Illuminara sat on the edge of Maren's chair, the way one sits when the news is not all good.

IlluminaraHe will give a parish finder directions without his name or the day. The finder will test the place and record every body and tag. You would have a place and no full account. A living person may be safer, but I cannot promise that either.

MarenNo.

IlluminaraSay why. I would rather hear your objection than your politeness.

MarenBecause you are asking me to take a grave and let the man who made it die clean. Eleven years I have been owed an account: who ordered it, who stood by, who put my boy in a hole. A patch of ground in exchange is a bribe in the shape of a mercy.

IlluminaraIt is also exactly what it is. I will not dress it. Some of what you are owed stays unpaid. You may refuse.

If I argued her round, Illuminara thought, I would take the one thing she has left: that the choice is hers.

Maren looked across the gap. Halvard did not turn away.

MarenIf I say yes, these are my terms. The finder marks the ground before he lifts a bone. He brings a parish witness. Every readable tag goes into the book. My petition stays mine. No one lies if a lawful writ comes here.

IlluminaraYes.

MarenAnd I choose the proof. Pell carried a tin tag I marked myself. I will write the marks and seal them. The finder must say what he saw before they are opened.

Nurse Ines brought paper and her medicine seal. Maren wrote, folded the slip twice and pressed it beneath the wax.

InesI will keep this until the finder reports. Bedside speech does not enter my ward book. But if a magistrate brings a lawful writ, I will not lie or hide the seal.

MarenThat is enough promise.

Halvard's fingers opened at ward book and closed again at writ. Illuminara understood that he was measuring not secrecy but the length of the road to Lysa.

Maren sent for Tobias Rell and the parish clerk. Beyond the ward doors, she put her own name on the search. The clerk listened, then held up his blank field board.

Parish clerkI can write that Tobias tested a location supplied by a private bearer at Maren Teague's request. The field page records the ground, bodies and tags. It records no day that the ground cannot prove and names no source I never met. Under lawful writ, I say Illuminara carried the place. Nothing less and nothing invented.

Illuminara carried that wording back once. Halvard listened with Corvane's book in his imagination.

HalvardThe Ninth is already in her petitions. What Corvane lacks is the day. The trench cannot give it, and your page will not guess it.

Parish clerkIt will not.

HalvardIf Corvane asks whether I spoke?

InesWithout a writ, I do not turn hospice speech into parish evidence. With one, I say that you spoke. I will not invent the words, and I will not deny the fact.

HalvardI did not buy that promise.

IlluminaraNo. You have heard where the distance ends. Do you permit one question?

Halvard studied the blank board, then the seal in Maren's palm.

HalvardAsk it.

IlluminaraMaren?

MarenAsk him where my son is. Carry only the place. I keep the rest.

Illuminara gave the question in Maren's own words, no softer and no sharper.

HalvardNorth bank of the ford. Count the posts of the drowned fence from the willow. At the fourth, six paces toward the river. A flat stone. Pell is under it because I knew his name.

He turned to Maren.

HalvardI am sorry for the stone. It was all I had.

MarenIt is not enough.

HalvardNo.

MarenBut if the marks answer, it may be a place.

04 · The Stone Under the Willow

Saint Aldis Hospice, yard and east ward · fourth day and night

At first light Illuminara carried the route to Tobias exactly once. He left with the clerk, a spade, measuring cord and a board for notes. Maren remained in the ward. The sealed slip remained in Ines's apron. No one asked Halvard another question.

They returned at noon, mud to the knees.

TobiasFourth post, six paces. Flat stone. We measured before we lifted it. Under it was a young man in a militia cloak beside a trench of ten. His tin tag has six cuts: three close, a space, two close, a space, one.

Ines broke her seal. The clerk opened the slip only after Tobias had finished, laid it beside the field page and signed across both. Three. Two. One.

Maren sat down. Her hand found the empty place at her throat where the kitchen knife had hung before she gave it to her son.

Parish clerkThe marks agree. Pell Teague is under the stone. Five other tags are readable, four damaged, one absent. The page records the ground, the bodies and the tags. It supplies no burial date.

MarenAnd the others?

Parish clerkThe named families will be told. The unknown remain in the book until someone can answer for them.

Halvard had heard. His hand closed on the blanket and opened again.

HalvardThen sign it.

The clerk and Tobias signed.

At dusk, after the parish authorized the removal, they buried Pell in the hospice yard under the pear tree. Maren would not wait another night for the village plot. Ines read the words. Tobias set the stone. The clerk placed a copy of the field page in Maren's hand.

Maren said her son's name once. Then she read aloud the five other names, because her condition had not been only for her own dead.

Afterwards she stayed by the new turf with Illuminara while the others went inside.

MarenI still want the rest.

IlluminaraYou kept the right to ask for it.

MarenYou did not give me the grave.

IlluminaraNo. Halvard gave the ground. You made the terms. Tobias and the clerk proved it.

MarenYou heard the join he was afraid of.

IlluminaraI listened until fear became precise enough to leave a door beside it.

They returned to the east ward. Halvard was awake and waiting.

MarenThe page says Pell Teague. It also says five other names, four damaged tags and one man with none. I will take it to the registry. I will not promise where the asking ends.

HalvardI did not buy that promise.

MarenNo. You did not.

She sat on the edge of her bed, a hand's breadth from his. She did not forgive him. He did not ask. She kept the vigil because it was the fourth night and the ward was full of people who should not be alone.

Before dawn his breathing stopped. Ines closed his eyes, then wrote his death in the ward book and nothing that had not happened.

In the parish ledger, six names stood above five unfinished lines. Maren kept the page open.

Umirajoči častnik noče spregovoriti, mati pa potrebuje grob. Illuminara išče vrata, dovolj ozka, da lahko oba stopita skoznje.

01 · Oddelek ob polnoči

Hospic svetega Aldisa, vzhodni oddelek · prva noč, po polnoči

Enajst postelj je stalo tam, kjer je bil oddelek zgrajen za sedem, svetilka pri mizi medicinskih sester pa je bila znižana na drobno žerjavico. Moški ob oknu že tri tedne ni spregovoril. Ženska v sosednji postelji, ki so jo obdržali zaradi pljučne mrzlice, se je pred eno uro nehala pretvarjati, da spi.

Maren Teague je brala karton, pripet na njegovo posteljo. Na njem je pisalo OSTROW, H., pod tem pa s pisarjevo roko nekdanji pripadnik Devete milice.

Ob vznožju postelje je stalo nekaj, česar tam ni bilo, ko so znižali svetilko. Videti je bilo kakor pozornost, ki si je našla obliko: visoka ženska z negibnostjo nekoga, ki se je naučil počakati na konec stavka.

IlluminaraOdšla bom, če bi raje, da ne ostanem. Prihajam le tja, kjer je nekdo buden in me je pripravljen videti.

Maren ni odgovorila takoj. Enajst let je preživela med pisarji, ki so govorili, da jim je žal.

MarenNiste medicinska sestra.

IlluminaraNe. Poslušam. Včasih se izkaže, da je to edina spretnost, ki jo noč potrebuje.

MarenPotem poslušajte. Deveta je držala brod tisto zimo, ko je moj sin izginil. Enajstkrat sem pisala registru in pravijo mi, da so zapisi zgoreli. Tukaj leži častnik Devete, komaj za dolžino roke od mene, in diha. Ve, kje je moj fant, pa noče povedati.

To je rekla tiho, kakor da bi jo moški lahko slišal. Oči je imel odprte in uprte v strop, v čeljusti pa se mu je premaknila mišica.

IlluminaraKaj želite od njega?

MarenKraj. Brez vsega drugega bi se lahko naučila živeti. Kraj, da bom lahko nehala stati na vsakem polju.

IlluminaraPotem vam moram povedati, česa ne bom storila. Ne bom ga prisilila, da spregovori. Med vama ne bom prenesla besede, ki je ni dovolil. Če bi to storila, bi bila nož, vi pa ne bi nikoli vedeli, kaj je dal in kaj mu je bilo odvzeto.

MarenČemu potem služite?

IlluminaraNe vem še. Rada bi ugotovila, ali obstajajo vrata. Tak molk je pogosto zid. Včasih je ščit, ščit pa ima lahko prehod.

Ščit, ki ga drži že tri tedne, vsa roka pa se trese, je pomislila Illuminara. Za njim stoji nekdo, ki ni on.

MarenIn če vrat ni?

IlluminaraPotem vam bom to povedala in izgubili boste noč, ne leta.

Maren se je ulegla nazaj. Čez ozko vrzel je na odeji počivala odprta roka Halvarda Ostrowa in prvič jo je pogledala kot roko človeka, ne polka.

02 · Ščit

Hospic svetega Aldisa, vzhodni oddelek · druga noč, pred zoro

Illuminara je stopila k drugi postelji. Halvardove oči so se s stropa premaknile k njenemu obrazu in ostale tam, česar ni poročal še nihče na oddelku.

IlluminaraNocoj vas ne bom nič vprašala. Želela sem, da veste, da sem tukaj in da me lahko pošljete proč.

Ko je spregovoril, je bil njegov glas suh kakor predolgo hranjen papir.

HalvardNiste kaplan. Kaplan hoče moje grehe. Vi hočete nekaj drugega.

IlluminaraŽenska poleg vas hoče kraj. Ni me prosila, naj vam ga vzamem.

HalvardTeagueova mati je. Vedel sem, ko so jo pripeljali. Pell je bil izvidnik. Njegovo ime sem napisal na pogrebni listek. Četni seznam je zgorel, toda Corvane je obdržal knjigo ukazov: datume, častnike in pet vojakov, dodeljenih vsaki nalogi.

IlluminaraEna od teh petih je bila vaša hči.

HalvardLysa. Preden je brod padel, sem jo poslal proti severu in podpisal, da je bila naloga opravljena. Deveta ni nobena skrivnost. Teagueove prošnje so jo raznesle povsod, kjer išče Corvane. Skrivnost je dan. Ploščice nosijo oznake, ne datumov. Knjiga hrani naloge po datumih in nobenih krajev pokopa. Dajte Corvanu tla in dan, pa me najde. Išče pet in najde štiri. Peto obesi zaradi dezerterstva, mene pa zaradi laži.

Obrnil je obraz k steni.

HalvardHočete, da dam grob in v zameno obesim svojega otroka. Svoj molk bom odnesel v svoj grob.

IlluminaraTa strah je razumen. Ne morem obljubiti, da je Lysa varna. Toda župnijski iskalec bi lahko preveril kraj, ne da bi izvedel dan, častnika ali nalogo. Tla bi lahko družinam dala imena, ne da bi Corvanu dala povezavo, ki jo potrebuje njegova knjiga.

HalvardIn kako naj iskalec odkrije kamen šest korakov od potopljene ograje?

IlluminaraTako, da prejme navodila brez vašega imena in jih ob dnevni svetlobi preveri s pričami. Zakonit nalog bi še vedno lahko dosegel ta oddelek. Razdalja ni zid. Je to dovolj, da razmislite o vprašanju?

HalvardČe gre vsaka berljiva ploščica v knjigo. Če iskalec ne vpraša, kdo je kopal. Če ona obdrži pravico, da sprašuje drugje. Ne bom kupil njenega molka o sebi.

IlluminaraTo so pogoji, ne privolitev. Prenesla jih bom kot pogoje. Nič več.

Prvič jo je pogledal kakor kolegico, ne obiskovalko. Ni privolil. Spremenil je obliko tega, kar bi privolitev zahtevala.

03 · Kaj je bilo vprašano Maren

Hospic svetega Aldisa, vzhodni oddelek · tretja noč, svetilka znižana

Illuminara je sedla na rob Mareninega stola, kakor človek sede, kadar novica ni povsem dobra.

IlluminaraŽupnijskemu iskalcu bo dal navodila brez svojega imena ali dneva. Iskalec bo preveril kraj ter zabeležil vsako telo in ploščico. Imeli bi kraj, ne pa celotnega poročila. Živ človek bi bil morda varnejši, vendar tudi tega ne morem obljubiti.

MarenNe.

IlluminaraPovejte, zakaj. Raje bi slišala vaš ugovor kakor vašo vljudnost.

MarenKer me prosite, naj vzamem grob in človeku, ki ga je naredil, pustim umreti neomadeževanemu. Enajst let mi dolgujejo poročilo: kdo je ukazal, kdo je stal zraven, kdo je mojega fanta položil v jamo. Zaplata zemlje v zameno je podkupnina v podobi usmiljenja.

IlluminaraTudi natanko to je. Ne bom je preoblekla. Del tega, kar vam dolgujejo, ostane neplačan. Lahko zavrnete.

Če bi jo prepričala, je pomislila Illuminara, bi ji vzela edino, kar ji je ostalo: da je odločitev njena.

Maren je pogledala čez vrzel. Halvard ni odvrnil pogleda.

MarenČe rečem da, so to moji pogoji. Iskalec označi tla, preden dvigne kost. Pripelje župnijsko pričo. Vsaka berljiva ploščica gre v knjigo. Moja prošnja ostane moja. Nihče ne laže, če sem pride zakonit nalog.

IlluminaraDa.

MarenIn jaz izberem dokaz. Pell je nosil pločevinasto ploščico, ki sem jo sama označila. Oznake bom zapisala in zapečatila. Iskalec mora povedati, kaj je videl, preden jih odprejo.

Medicinska sestra Ines je prinesla papir in svoj zdravniški pečat. Maren je napisala, listek dvakrat prepognila in ga pritisnila pod vosek.

InesTo bom hranila, dokler iskalec ne poroča. Besede ob postelji ne vstopijo v mojo oddelčno knjigo. Če pa sodnik prinese zakonit nalog, ne bom lagala ali skrila pečata.

MarenTa obljuba zadošča.

Halvardovi prsti so se ob besedah oddelčna knjiga odprli in ob besedi nalog spet zaprli. Illuminara je razumela, da ne meri skrivnosti, temveč dolžino poti do Lyse.

Maren je poslala po Tobiasa Rella in župnijskega pisarja. Za vrati oddelka je iskanju dodala svoje ime. Pisar je poslušal, nato dvignil prazno terensko tablo.

Župnijski pisarLahko napišem, da je Tobias na zahtevo Maren Teague preveril kraj, ki ga je posredoval zasebni prenašalec. Terenska stran beleži tla, telesa in ploščice. Ne beleži dneva, ki ga tla ne morejo dokazati, in ne imenuje vira, ki ga nisem srečal. Ob zakonitem nalogu povem, da je kraj prenesla Illuminara. Nič manj in nič izmišljenega.

Illuminara je to besedilo enkrat prenesla nazaj. Halvard je poslušal s Corvanovo knjigo v svojih mislih.

HalvardDeveta je že v njenih prošnjah. Corvanu manjka dan. Jarek ga ne more dati in vaša stran ga ne bo ugibala.

Župnijski pisarNe bo ga.

HalvardČe Corvane vpraša, ali sem govoril?

InesBrez naloga hospicijskega govora ne spreminjam v župnijski dokaz. Z njim povem, da ste govorili. Ne bom si izmislila besed in ne bom zanikala dejstva.

HalvardTe obljube nisem kupil.

IlluminaraNe. Slišali ste, kje se razdalja konča. Dovolite eno vprašanje?

Halvard je preučil prazno tablo, nato pečat v Marenini dlani.

HalvardVprašajte.

IlluminaraMaren?

MarenVprašajte ga, kje je moj sin. Prenesite samo kraj. Ostalo obdržim jaz.

Illuminara je vprašanje izrekla z Mareninimi lastnimi besedami, nič nežneje in nič ostreje.

HalvardSeverni breg broda. Od vrbe preštejte stebre potopljene ograje. Pri četrtem šest korakov proti reki. Ploščat kamen. Pell je pod njim, ker sem poznal njegovo ime.

Obrnil se je k Maren.

HalvardŽal mi je za kamen. Bil je vse, kar sem imel.

MarenNi dovolj.

HalvardNe.

MarenToda če oznake odgovorijo, je to morda lahko kraj.

04 · Kamen pod vrbo

Hospic svetega Aldisa, dvorišče in vzhodni oddelek · četrti dan in noč

Ob prvi svetlobi je Illuminara pot natanko enkrat prenesla Tobiasu. Odšel je s pisarjem, lopato, merilno vrvjo in tablo za zapiske. Maren je ostala na oddelku. Zapečateni listek je ostal v Inesinem predpasniku. Halvardu nihče ni zastavil nobenega drugega vprašanja.

Opoldne sta se vrnila, blatna do kolen.

TobiasČetrti steber, šest korakov. Ploščat kamen. Izmerila sva, preden sva ga dvignila. Pod njim je bil mladenič v miličniškem plašču ob jarku z desetimi. Njegova pločevinasta ploščica ima šest zarez: tri skupaj, presledek, dve skupaj, presledek, eno.

Ines je prelomila svoj pečat. Pisar je listek odprl šele, ko je Tobias končal, ga položil ob terensko stran in se podpisal čez oboje. Tri. Dve. Ena.

Maren je sedla. Njena roka je našla prazno mesto ob grlu, kjer je visel kuhinjski nož, preden ga je dala sinu.

Župnijski pisarOznake se ujemajo. Pell Teague je pod kamnom. Pet drugih ploščic je berljivih, štiri poškodovane, ena manjka. Stran beleži tla, telesa in ploščice. Datuma pokopa ne navaja.

MarenIn drugi?

Župnijski pisarImenovane družine bodo obveščene. Neznani ostanejo v knjigi, dokler ne bo mogel nekdo odgovoriti zanje.

Halvard je slišal. Njegova roka se je zaprla na odeji in se spet odprla.

HalvardPotem jo podpišite.

Pisar in Tobias sta se podpisala.

Ob mraku, ko je župnija dovolila odstranitev, so Pella pokopali na hospicijskem dvorišču pod hruško. Maren ni hotela čakati še eno noč na vaško parcelo. Ines je prebrala besede. Tobias je postavil kamen. Pisar je Maren v roko položil kopijo terenske strani.

Maren je enkrat izrekla sinovo ime. Nato je naglas prebrala pet drugih imen, saj njen pogoj ni veljal le za njenega mrtvega.

Potem je z Illuminara ostala ob novi ruši, medtem ko so drugi odšli noter.

MarenŠe vedno hočem preostanek.

IlluminaraOhranili ste pravico, da ga zahtevate.

MarenVi mi niste dali groba.

IlluminaraNe. Halvard je dal kraj. Vi ste postavili pogoje. Tobias in pisar sta ga dokazala.

MarenSlišali ste povezavo, ki se je je bal.

IlluminaraPoslušala sem, dokler strah ni postal dovolj natančen, da so poleg njega ostala vrata.

Vrnili sta se na vzhodni oddelek. Halvard je bil buden in je čakal.

MarenNa strani piše Pell Teague. Piše tudi pet drugih imen, štiri poškodovane ploščice in en mož brez nje. Odnesla jo bom v register. Ne bom obljubila, kje se bo spraševanje končalo.

HalvardTe obljube nisem kupil.

MarenNe. Niste je.

Sedla je na rob svoje postelje, za širino dlani od njegove. Ni mu odpustila. Ni je prosil. Ostala je na bedenju, ker je bila četrta noč in je bil oddelek poln ljudi, ki ne bi smeli biti sami.

Pred zoro se je njegovo dihanje ustavilo. Ines mu je zaprla oči, nato pa v oddelčno knjigo zapisala njegovo smrt in ničesar, kar se ni zgodilo.

V župnijski knjigi je šest imen stalo nad petimi nedokončanimi vrsticami. Maren je stran pustila odprto.

Beside a dying officer's silence and a mother who needs a grave for her son, Illuminara refuses to carry a word between them and instead listens until his fear is exact, then helps design a place-without-day route, tested in daylight with witnesses, that lets the boy be found and buried while everyone keeps the right to refuse.
