A comet grows a tail that walks upwind, nine thousand young shells of living plasma sit across the grain lane, and a claim holder keeps the key to a sweep that would sterilize them.

01 · The Comb

Oss Station, observation ring · Hour 0 of 40

Eleven days out, the comet Maren-Quill had grown a second tail, and the second tail was walking the wrong way. The first streamed from the sun as tails should. The new one crawled up into the solar wind, a thin violet braid shedding knots of charged dust that tumbled across the freight corridor like seeds across a road.

Sunniva AchterbergThose knots are alive, in whatever sense a field can be. They fold dust into shells, and inside each shell something keeps a heartbeat on the low radio band. Nine thousand shells, mostly young, but their pulse bands show older keepers around the outer edge and newly folded shells inside. I told the council the knots are drawn to our ranging beams: every shell scatters our navigation. A beam comes out of that braid like light through frosted glass.

Ibrahim TadesseLamentine's sealed silos can feed its mills for eleven days, but Pelion has three days of grain and Kestrel two. The lane closes at perihelion in forty hours and stays closed six weeks. Ardent and the two other convoys must cross before then, or the outer stations eat seed stock before the next window.

Dagny Voss, on the lineAnd the comet is mine, Councillor, under the Voss-Kane charter, down to the last gram of nickel. The charter lets a holder clear a hazard to navigation from her own claim. At Hour 12 I fire the comb. Forty minutes, and the lane is clean as glass.

Sunniva AchterbergAnd so is the nursery. A magnetic sweep tears every shell apart.

Dagny Voss, on the lineI read your paper, doctor. A pretty braid. Four hundred people draw wages from this claim, and they will not draw them from a braid.

Illuminara had stood at the window the whole time, watching the violet thread on the screen below the stars. Nobody had asked her opinion yet. She did not offer one.

IlluminaraNot the summary. The raw tracks. Every knot, every minute since the braid formed.

Sunniva AchterbergThat is two terabytes of scribble.

IlluminaraThen nobody has read it yet.

02 · The Beacon That Lost Its Clock

Oss Station, tracking bay · Hour 3

She read the tracks the way she read a face, looking for the place where the expected thing failed to happen. It took her an hour and ten minutes. She found it in a gap forty minutes wide.

When the replay reached the fault, Illuminara named a 0.04-degree phase wobble 2.1 seconds before the instrument flag; the tracking technician checked the log and confirmed the lead.

IlluminaraBeacon nine lost its clock at 22:10 yesterday — wall-clock time, before our forty-hour count began. Its phase wandered for forty minutes. Look at the knots in that stretch.

Sunniva AchterbergThey parted. Around the beacon, in a bubble. I took it for a sensor fault.

IlluminaraThey parted for exactly forty minutes and closed the moment the clock came back. You told the council the knots hunt the beams. A thing hunting beams would have swarmed the one that was shouting.

Sunniva AchterbergUnless they shun anything incoherent.

IlluminaraAnd they are not drifting at random. Every strand runs along the old guide rails, the magnetic edges laid down to keep the beams clean. The rails are the quietest, straightest edges in forty million kilometres.

Sunniva AchterbergThen we built them a road. And we invited them onto it.

Ngozi Farrant, on the lineThen cut the rails.

IlluminaraThen your ranging goes with them, the lane turns to static, and I do not know what a young shell does when its road becomes noise.

Sunniva AchterbergFracture. I would guess.

IlluminaraIt is a guess, and I would rather not learn the answer by being right. Suppose we offered something quieter, longer and cleaner than the rails, and led away from traffic.

Sunniva AchterbergYou are assuming they take offers.

IlluminaraI am assuming nothing. I want to see whether they decline.

03 · The Key

Voss-Kane platform, comb control · Hour 6

Dagny Voss kept the firing key on a cord around her own neck. Her engineer, Kemal Aydin, stood at the panel with his hands in his pockets, which Illuminara understood to be a courtesy.

Dagny VossYou have come to ask me to wait.

IlluminaraI have come to ask what would make you not fire.

Dagny VossA clean lane before Hour 12. Show me ranging lock to four metres, and I will not touch the key. I will also want to see the thing I am sparing. I do not break my own payroll over a diagram.

IlluminaraThen take the heartbeat. Dr. Achterberg can put it on this panel. While the shells are whole it is a single clean note. We will log its starting width. If the note widens by more than five percent, the shells are falling out of step and the test has breached its limit.

Kemal AydinWhich means you are handing her the right to stop you.

IlluminaraIt was always hers.

Dagny VossAnd if you are wrong, I want it on the record that I warned you, and that every hour I waited cost me a hauler contract.

IlluminaraIt will be on the record. The cost will be too.

Dagny VossThen do it. At Hour 12 Kemal turns the comb unless the lane is improving and that note is within five percent of its starting width. If either measure turns against you, he holds the fields where they are and I decide whether you get one recovery window or the comb. I will not be asked twice.

04 · Two Ribbons

Oss and Lamentine field arrays · Hour 8 to Hour 10:30

At Hour 8:10 the first ribbon ran out from Oss, south and away from the lane: a faint coherent edge, drawn as cleanly as the arrays could draw it. The second ran from Lamentine across the corridor, a decoy and a control. Illuminara wrote her prediction in the station log before either went live. The knots would leave the rails for the outbound ribbon within ninety minutes. If they took neither, or the crossing one, she was wrong, and she wrote that too.

They did nothing for seventy minutes. On Voss's panel the heartbeat held one clean note, and Aydin counted the minutes aloud in a flat voice.

At Hour 9:20 the knots moved. They did not take the outbound ribbon, and they did not take the crossing one. They settled on the seam where the two edges overlapped, a line nobody had drawn, running a hundred and forty kilometres along the lane's southern rail.

Sunniva AchterbergThey declined both.

IlluminaraNo. They chose the best edge in the sky, and I built it by accident. I had them picking between my offers.

Ngozi Farrant, on the lineI will not enter above eighty metres. My fix just went to a hundred and twenty metres. Tell me that is the end of the bad news.

IlluminaraIt is the middle. I made the lane worse.

She said it once, at the volume she would have used for a measurement, and went back to the screen. It was Hour 10:35.

05 · The Seam

Oss field array, control room · Hour 10:40

IlluminaraThe seam sits where the two ribbons are equal. Weaken the crossing one and strengthen the outbound one by the same amount, and the seam slides south without becoming brighter. Slide it slowly and the knots may follow it, because it remains coherent.

Sunniva AchterbergOr charged dust is simply collecting where the fields cancel. Then coherence has nothing to do with it.

Kemal Aydin, on the lineI can rotate both phases equally and oppositely for forty seconds. The seam stays within two kilometres and total field strength within one percent, but the edge loses coherence. If the knots follow strength or geometry, they stay. If they follow coherence, their track should loosen before the six-minute mark.

IlluminaraFreeze that prediction in the log. Forty seconds only. If the heartbeat widens by more than five percent, restore phase at once. If their track does not loosen within six minutes, my model fails and we do not begin the slide.

At Hour 10:47 Aydin rotated the phases. The seam did not move on the ranging plot. Seventy seconds later the outer knots lifted from it and began to wander, though the heartbeat remained narrow. He restored coherence at forty seconds; within four minutes the same knots had gathered along the seam again. They had not chosen either ribbon. They had answered a property of the edge.

Sunniva AchterbergThat defeats accumulation. It does not prove what they are, but it tells us what not to break.

IlluminaraThen we move only one thing: the position of a coherent seam.

Sunniva AchterbergThe arrays cannot hold their phase that precisely. They wander. Noise is exactly what the knots flee.

IlluminaraThen I will be the clock. I can feel which way each field is bending a breath before your instruments log it. I cannot move the knots, or the dust, or the shells. I can tell each of you which way you are drifting and by how much.

Ibrahim TadesseLamentine has eleven days of grain in sealed silos, but only fourteen hours of bread already baked. The mill reserve keeps the grinders and ovens alive through a brownout. Give it to the array and the mill stays cold until we release the field power. Households eat yesterday's loaves, and the outer stations still need these convoys.

IlluminaraI will not pretend that is a small price.

Ibrahim TadesseI authorize fourteen hours. The mill restarts the moment the array releases the reserve. Take it.

At Hour 11:00 she began calling corrections over two channels, one voice to Oss and one to Lamentine. At Hour 11:06 she called Oss drifting 0.18 degrees sunward; the instrument alarm crossed the same threshold 3.2 seconds later, and Aydin entered both times in Voss's log.

At Hour 11:29 Lamentine stepped against her call. This time the array alarm sounded 0.6 seconds before she corrected it. The outermost shells loosened for eleven seconds before the seam recovered. Her lead was real, and it was not constant enough to make the ecology safe by itself.

The seam crept south. The knots flowed along it like seeds along a tide line.

At Hour 11:41 Voss's voice came over the speaker, level and dry.

Dagny Voss, on the lineThe heartbeat is twelve percent broader. My line was five. Aydin has his hand on the comb.

Illuminara did not argue. She ordered the arrays held exactly where they were.

IlluminaraThe pull outran the young. The older keepers came with the seam and the newest shells could not keep the pace. I set the slope too fast. Give me until Hour 12:05 with the seam still. If the width is not within five percent of its starting line, turn the key. If it recovers, grant twenty minutes at half speed. Renew only while two ten-minute reads show the width holding and the ranging error falling.

Dagny Voss, on the lineThat is the recovery window. Five percent by Hour 12:05. After that, twenty minutes at a time. One bad pair of reads and Kemal fires without another speech.

At Hour 12:01 the heartbeat narrowed to four percent above its starting width. Aydin read the number himself. The laggards had caught up, and the braid closed behind them like a hand.

Kemal Aydin, on the lineFour percent. Ranging error is falling. The condition is met.

Dagny Voss, on the lineResume. Half the speed. Your window ends at Hour 12:21 unless the next pair earns another.

06 · Clean Glass

Oss Station and the lane · Hour 15 to Hour 31

By Hour 15 the seam lay two hundred kilometres south of the rail, and the braid lay with it, a long violet comma pointing away from the lane. Voss had renewed the twenty-minute window eight times, each after Aydin read two improving fixes and a heartbeat no more than five percent wide. Ranging lock came back in steps: eighty metres, forty, nine, four. At Hour 15:01, with the lane clean and the same limits holding, she converted the last interval into a standing order through the final crossing and Lamentine's controlled release.

Beyond the ribbons' crossing point, the comet's own southward field gradient ran parallel to the Oss outbound ribbon. Together they made the sole quiet edge; Lamentine's crossing array no longer set the seam's position. Aydin reduced that array in three logged steps, and the braid did not move or widen.

Ngozi FarrantFour. Four and holding. I said I would not enter above eighty metres, and I am entering at four on my own judgement, not because anyone told me it was safe. Ardent is in the lane.

Illuminara watched the scatter chart flatten on Oss's screen. The three convoys crossed one behind another, at half speed, through the narrow clean band, and the last cleared the closing line with nine hours to spare. Lamentine released its array at Hour 15:12 after the third stable step; the Oss ribbon and the comet's gradient held the braid on the new edge. The mill restarted on stored grain before the fourteen-hour bread shelf was empty. The convoys would reach the stations two days behind schedule; Pelion and Kestrel would receive them before either opened its seed stores.

Voss came to the observation ring herself, with the key on its cord. Tadesse joined by public line, carrying Oss Council's emergency navigation seal.

Dagny VossA season. The north face remains mine, but I surrender extraction on the south face while the heartbeat band is active. That cost is mine, and the charter will say so in writing.

Ibrahim Tadesse, on the lineOss Council declares the same band a protected navigation exclusion through perihelion. Voss-Kane's assent and the public order expire together at the season's end unless both are renewed.

IlluminaraIt stopped being a diagram when each of you could measure what your choice would harm.

Ibrahim Tadesse, on the lineThe new beacons will be paid for by every hauler on the lane. Nobody has agreed to that yet.

Sunniva AchterbergThen that argument begins tomorrow. The next braid will not wait for us to finish it.

On the screen the heartbeat held its single clean note, and under it, new and faint, a second tone that had not been there before. Achterberg turned it up. Nobody could say what it meant, and Illuminara did not offer a guess. She asked, instead, that one ribbon be left on at a whisper through the season. Voss looked once at Aydin's trace, then nodded.

Kometa dobi rep, ki potuje proti vetru, devet tisoč mladih lupin žive plazme leži čez žitni koridor, imetnica pravice pa hrani ključ za prečesavanje, ki bi jih steriliziralo.

01 · Glavnik

Postaja Oss, opazovalni obroč · Ura 0 od 40

Enajst dni pred perihelijem je kometu Maren-Quill zrasel drugi rep, ta pa se je premikal v napačno smer. Prvi je tekel stran od Sonca, kakor repi morajo. Novi se je plazil navzgor v sončni veter, tanka vijolična kita, ki je odmetavala vozle nabitega prahu; ti so se kotalili čez tovorni koridor kakor semena čez cesto.

Sunniva AchterbergTi vozli so živi, v katerem koli pomenu je lahko živo polje. Prah zlagajo v lupine, v vsaki lupini pa nekaj ohranja srčni utrip na nizkem radijskem pasu. Devet tisoč lupin, večinoma mladih, toda njihovi pulzni pasovi kažejo starejše skrbnike ob zunanjem robu in na novo zložene lupine znotraj. Svetu sem povedala, da vozle privlačijo naši merilni žarki: vsaka lupina razprši našo navigacijo. Žarek pride iz te kite kakor svetloba skozi motno steklo.

Sledi je brala, kakor je brala obraz, in iskala kraj, kjer se pričakovano ni zgodilo. Potrebovala je uro in deset minut. Našla ga je v štirideset minut dolgi vrzeli.

06 · Čisto steklo

Postaja Oss in koridor · Ura 15 do 31

Do 15. ure je spoj ležal dvesto kilometrov južno od tirnice, z njim pa tudi kita, dolga vijolična vejica, obrnjena stran od koridorja. Voss je dvajsetminutno okno podaljšala osemkrat, vsakič potem, ko je Aydin prebral dve izboljšani fiksiranji in srčni utrip, širok največ pet odstotkov. Merilno fiksiranje se je vračalo po korakih: osemdeset metrov, štirideset, devet, štiri. Ob 15:01, ko je bil koridor čist in so iste meje še vedno držale, je zadnji interval spremenila v trajni ukaz do končnega prečkanja in Lamentinovega nadzorovanega izklopa.

Onkraj presečišča trakov je lastni južni gradient kometovega polja tekel vzporedno z Ossovim izhodnim trakom. Skupaj sta tvorila edini tihi rob; Lamentinova prečna mreža ni več določala položaja spoja. Aydin je to mrežo zmanjšal v treh zabeleženih korakih in kita se ni premaknila ali razširila.

Ngozi FarrantŠtiri. Štiri in drži. Rekla sem, da ne bom vstopila nad osemdesetimi metri, vstopam pa pri štirih po lastni presoji, ne zato, ker mi je kdo rekel, da je varno. Ardent je v koridorju.

Illuminara je opazovala, kako se graf razpršitve na Ossovem zaslonu izravnava. Trije konvoji so prečkali drug za drugim, s polovično hitrostjo, skozi ozek čisti pas, zadnji pa je črto zapiranja prešel z devetimi urami prednosti. Lamentine je svojo mrežo sprostil ob 15:12 po tretjem stabilnem koraku; Ossov trak in kometov gradient sta kito zadržala na novem robu. Mlin se je znova zagnal z uskladiščenim žitom, preden se je iztekla štirinajsturna zaloga kruha. Konvoji bi do postaj prišli dva dni pozneje od načrta; Pelion in Kestrel bi ju prejela, preden bi kateri koli odprl svojo semensko zalogo.

Voss je sama prišla v opazovalni obroč s ključem na vrvici. Tadesse se je pridružil po javni zvezi in nosil nujni navigacijski pečat sveta Oss.

Dagny VossEno sezono. Severna stran ostane moja, vendar se odpovedujem izkopavanju na južni strani, dokler je pas srčnega utripa dejaven. Ta strošek je moj in v listini bo tako pisalo.

Ibrahim Tadesse, po zveziSvet Oss razglaša isti pas za zaščiteno navigacijsko izključitveno območje do perihelija. Soglasje Voss-Kane in javni odlok prenehata skupaj ob koncu sezone, razen če sta oba obnovljena.

IlluminaraDiagram je prenehal biti v trenutku, ko je lahko vsak izmed vas izmeril, čemu bi njegova izbira škodovala.

Nihče ni mogel povedati, kaj pomeni, in Illuminara ni ponudila ugibanja. Namesto tega je prosila, naj en trak skozi sezono ostane prižgan na šepetu. Voss je enkrat pogledala Aydinovo sled in nato prikimala.

Reading notesObrazložitvi

Claude — Ticking-clock stakes and a humane, idea-rich conflict—refusals reframed as design requirements, local knowledge vindicated, a system built to fail safely—suit these readers, with crisp aphoristic dialogue and a satisfying climax where breaking is the plan. Dense hydrology jargon, many numbers and names, thin interiority and an unexplained speculative element make the middle hard going for some.

GPT — The deadline, Adaeze’s refusals and the shared problem give these readers a reason to keep going. The solution grows from local knowledge and cooperation, making it memorable. Dense engineering detail in the middle may slow some readers, and the ending states its theme rather plainly.

Suggestions for improvementPredlogi za izboljšave

Claude — Venn's turn is compressed. His liability fear meets a document, not an exchange that tests it. His acceptance is implied by one amendment and 'Venn signed last', and his reaction to Sami refusing Cadran control in the storm is skipped. A ministry has twelve days to hold a failing hillside above a hospital, but Adaeze refuses its single elegant system three times—for the graves it would move, the dependency it would create, and the local design it would erase.

01 · Three Noes

Aruwa regional hall, hillside map room · Day 1, 08:10

The hillside above St. Orra Hospital had moved eleven centimetres in six days. On the ministry map it was one red crescent. On the ground it was three districts, four thousand homes, a school, a market and a burial field older than the road that divided it. The first heavy rain was due in twelve days.

Ministerial engineers had drawn one answer in blue: a continuous retaining curtain, forty-two load-field plates linked through a private control room, and a diversion channel cut straight across the slope. Every plate shared the load; if one failed, the others would carry it.

Illuminara's mother Adaeze sat with the three district chairs. She listened until the procurement director asked for assent.

AdaezeNo.

Director Miro VennMrs. Okafor, the graves can be reinterred with ceremony. Compensation is included.

AdaezeKiru's dead are not a line item to be lifted because your blue line is straight.

Venn turned a page. The control room would belong for twenty-five years to Cadran Systems, whose plates the ministry could procure in time.

AdaezeNo.

Belu would not put the ground beneath its houses behind a company's password and call that safety.

The drainage appendix cut across a stone trench Sava residents had built by hand after the last wet season. Chief Engineer Lio Mensah called it unlined, irregular and too small for the design storm. He was right about its size.

AdaezeNo. They measured every seep for seven years. Your survey calls their work an obstruction because it began after they finished.

IlluminaraAre those three refusals, or three requirements the plan has failed to meet?

Director Miro VennThey have the same effect. We lose the only package that can clear audit this week.

Illuminara closed the blue projection before its elegance became an argument by repetition.

IlluminaraGive me the residents' measurements, the hospital's water records and twenty-one hours. If the trench is local drainage, your curtain remains fastest. If it is carrying the hill, we have called the spine an obstacle.

02 · The Fourth Line

Sava district, contour trench · Day 1, 09:30

The trench was knee-deep, faced with mismatched stone and bent around breadfruit roots. Adaeze walked it with Kemi Sol, the mason who had marked the first seep, while Mensah's team set nine piezometers above and below it.

Kemi SolIt fills beneath the red house, then here, then at the school bend. Never the other way around.

Chief Engineer Lio MensahDepth is not source. A leaking hospital main could give you the same order.

IlluminaraThen we test both causes. Treated water carries chloride. Hillside seepage carries iron from the upper basalt.

On a stone she wrote two rival explanations and what each must predict at all nine wells.

Chief Engineer Lio MensahAnd if neither survives?

IlluminaraThe fourth line is 'we do not know,' and three districts do not build on it.

At 10:06 the three Kiru heads rose in order. Eight minutes later the wet line climbed one stone course beneath the red house, then another beside the sixth well. The school-bend head stayed flat while the masonry between it and the sixth well darkened. When Kemi opened the trench, the upstream heads and the wet courses fell in the same order.

Illuminara chalked the times onto the wall. The missing quantity was water, not load, and it left the measured path somewhere between the sixth well and the bend. That interval ran under the Belu laundry.

Kemi opened seven notebooks, each wet season in a different colour. The hospital main had been closed twice; the red-house-to-school sequence had continued. Each pressure rise also preceded the nearest slope marker's movement by roughly ninety minutes.

Kemi SolOfficials ask whether it is big enough. Nobody asks why it is here.

IlluminaraThree groundwater paths meet here. The throat is too narrow, but the collector is real. Drain the hill first; retain what remains.

The throat could not widen toward Kiru without approaching the graves. Illuminara pointed toward the road.

IlluminaraNow we find whether it can deepen the other way.

03 · Twenty-One Hours

Aruwa hillside and St. Orra plant room · Day 1, 11:00 to Day 2, 05:00

The hospital isolated its upper main. No well showed its chloride trace; iron rose in a fan from the basalt. Mensah abandoned the leaking-main explanation, but not his objection to making a regional spine from a village trench.

At noon Kemi released a measured tracer above Kiru. The middle wells should answer in order and the school bend last. If water scattered or bypassed the trench, the interface idea would fail before anyone signed it.

Two middle wells answered. The Belu well did not.

Director Miro VennOne silent well is enough. Three contractors will blame one another while the hospital slides.

Illuminara followed the groundwater interval she had chalked to the laundry floor. Adaeze looked at the old drain scar and remembered a cistern there, used during a nurses' strike.

Kemi SolIts clay pipe was sealed before I took the trench.

AdaezeMy mother drew water from its overflow after that.

They opened the laundry floor and found the cistern full, its pipe hidden below the well. Before a sensor was moved, Mensah wrote the branch test: the overflow must answer first, a temporary probe below the pipe must answer next, the silent well must stay flat and the school bend must rise last. If the bend rose before the probe, or chloride appeared, the branch was false.

Chief Engineer Lio MensahI accept no cistern until all four lines hold.

At 23:30 the overflow answered. The lower probe followed at 00:30; the Belu well stayed flat. At 02:00 the school bend rose last. Mensah signed beneath the prediction, then beneath his acceptance.

A road-side shaft found basalt falling away soon enough for a covered culvert twice the trench's measured peak. Proof loading left sixteen percent spare capacity after wet bedding settlement.

Chief Engineer Lio MensahThe residents found the collector. They did not size the throat.

Kemi SolWe had hammers, not your drill rig.

IlluminaraBoth facts belong in the design. The trench is the spine. The culvert is its new throat. Retaining work must meet it without owning it.

By dawn the first and third noes no longer opposed each other. The second still did.

04 · One Package

Ministry audit chamber · Day 2, 09:00

Venn gave them ninety minutes. Emergency law released money for one package, one accountable integrator and one acceptance test.

Director Miro VennI am defending a signature I can prosecute if the hospital is buried. Give me one throat to hold.

AdaezeThe districts refuse to become tenants of the remedy, not accountability.

Illuminara placed four pages on the table. They specified interfaces, not a wall: pressure delivered to the common spine, anchor exclusions around the graves, open sensors, manual safe states, public keys and joint inspection at every seam.

IlluminaraBuy one audited interface. Let three districts choose three compliant modules. The integrator owns the seams and the test, not their controls.

Chief Engineer Lio MensahWhere did you get eight percent?

Illuminara laid the road-throat proof sheet beside the settlement trace. Sixteen percent was the measured reserve after the bad bedding had taken its share.

IlluminaraNo seam may consume more than half the smallest passive reserve. The link pin is rated to creep under transfer above eight percent and part after ten sustained minutes. That endurance is in the metal, not a command. The drainage spine stays open when it separates.

Chief Engineer Lio MensahThen an inspector at any seam gets stop-work authority. Not a dashboard. A person.

Director Miro VennAnd every fault and override is public before the next shift. Liability cannot live in three private notebooks.

Illuminara crossed out two clauses and wrote both changes into the standard.

IlluminaraAgreed. They need not think as one system. They must fail without making a neighbour fail.

Hospital director Nia Sorel read the endurance clause twice.

Nia SorelCan this be inspected before the rain?

Chief Engineer Lio MensahIf excavation begins today and choices freeze by sunset.

The districts chose: Kiru's stone buttress outside the graves; Belu's public plates with local keys, operated by Sami Daro, who would hold the district's physical key; Sava's terraced anchors tied to the trench. Kemi's crew would supervise every old connection.

Adaeze signed beneath the three requirements and accepted the seam chair only until the rain. Venn signed last. One package went to tender at 10:27. It contained no single wall.

05 · The Seams

Aruwa hillside · Days 2 to 11

The road culvert went in first. Illuminara held the exposed load path while the crew seated the second arch. She released it after thirty-eight minutes, before mortar could lock a hidden dependence into the joint; the arch had to show it could carry itself. Mensah stopped work when the first bedding layer crossed its settlement limit. Kemi's crew rebuilt it.

Kiru curved its buttress around the burial field. Belu installed twelve public plates on ferrite ribs, each with a physical key. Sava drove terraced anchors and fitted removable gates where every terrace met the old trench.

Every seam needed three signatures: ministry inspector, district operator and a neighbouring crew. During the sixth-plate test Kemi closed the lower drain gate. The transfer needle climbed past eight and stopped at eleven percent toward Kiru.

Chief Engineer Lio MensahThe plate passes its own specification. The seam fails.

Sami DaroHold the gate there. Change the angle, not the reading.

Sami reset the plate by two degrees. Kiru's masons laid a sacrificial slip course while Kemi reopened the gate one notch at a time. The needle fell to six percent and decayed in seven minutes. All three crews signed the fault before they signed the repair.

On Day 9 Cadran offered a storm monitor with no control channel.

AdaezeCan the districts turn it off?

Sami DaroAt our office. Raw records remain ours.

AdaezeThen it may watch. It may not become the memory we cannot afford to lose.

By Day 11 the culvert carried twice the old peak, every log was public at the hospital and each module passed dry load. Adaeze refused the ministry's photograph until Kemi and all three operators stood in it.

06 · Rain

St. Orra Hospital and Aruwa hillside · Day 12, 03:20 to 18:40

Rain arrived three hours early and harder than forecast. The piezometers rose; ninety minutes later the slope markers answered. Water entered the Sava trench at the red house and struck the road culvert in a brown sheet. The throat held.

At 06:40 Kiru's seam alarm showed nine percent toward Belu. Sami Daro reduced plate six and Kemi delayed gate four until the pressure peak. The transfer stayed above the eight-percent cap. Ten sustained minutes exhausted the pin's rated endurance.

The passive link broke with a sound like a snapped spade handle. Belu separated from Kiru exactly as the standard required. Kiru's buttress carried alone, its sacrificial slip course grinding five millimetres.

The eastern Kiru marker began to move: one millimetre, then two. Nia Sorel's voice came through the hospital channel.

Nia SorelPaediatrics is ready to clear. Tell me whether the rate is still rising.

Kemi SolThe marker slowed when gate four opened. It is still at two millimetres.

Nia SorelThen paediatrics stays. I will clear the wing if the third reading rises.

Venn heard the ministry lawyer ask who would own an evacuation if the third reading rose.

Director Miro Venn, on the radioCadran can take the plates now. I can put one operator under the liability.

Sami DaroThen put my name under the local key. Belu stands alone.

He turned the key to safe angle. Kemi watched the white stone disappear beneath the trench.

Kemi SolGate four open. Terrace closed to the trench. Send it all to the culvert.

The third marker reading held at two millimetres, then fell. For fourteen minutes the districts carried separate loads while the culvert took their common water. Sami reset the plate at four percent. The broken pin could not be replaced before the rain ended, so the modules remained apart and joint inspections doubled.

Illuminara held the radio but gave no order.

At 18:40 the hospital remained open, nobody had evacuated, and no slope marker had moved more than four millimetres. Kiru's slip course was damaged, the pin was gone and shared reserve would stay unavailable until both were replaced.

Venn published the standard with the tracer test, the rejected bedding, the storm separation and the fault ledger attached.

AdaezeThree noes did not become a yes.

IlluminaraNo. They became the shape of what could be built.

Adaeze touched her daughter Illuminara's cheek, then went uphill to chair the inspection. At the school bend, Kemi painted the high-water mark beside seven years of colours. The new line was the darkest and the lowest.

Ministrstvo ima dvanajst dni, da zadrži popuščajoče pobočje nad bolnišnico, toda Adaeze trikrat zavrne njegov en sam eleganten sistem — zaradi grobov, ki bi jih premaknil, odvisnosti, ki bi jo ustvaril, in lokalne zasnove, ki bi jo izbrisal.

01 · Trije ne-ji

Regionalna dvorana Aruwa, soba z zemljevidi pobočja · 1. dan, 08:10

Pobočje nad bolnišnico St. Orra se je v šestih dneh premaknilo za enajst centimetrov. Na ministrskem zemljevidu je bilo en sam rdeč polmesec. Na terenu so bila tri okrožja, štiri tisoč domov, šola, tržnica in pokopališče, starejše od ceste, ki ga je razdelila. Prvo močno deževje naj bi prišlo čez dvanajst dni.

Ministrski inženirji so z modro narisali eno rešitev: neprekinjeno podporno pregrado, dvainštirideset plošč za razporeditev obremenitve, povezanih prek zasebne nadzorne sobe, in preusmeritveni kanal, vrezan naravnost čez pobočje. Vse plošče bi si delile obremenitev; če bi ena odpovedala, bi jo prevzele druge.

Illuminarina mati Adaeze je sedela s predsedniki treh okrožij. Poslušala je, dokler direktor za nabavo ni zaprosil za soglasje.

AdaezeNe.

Direktor Miro VennGospa Okafor, posmrtne ostanke je mogoče slovesno prenesti. Odškodnina je vključena.

AdaezeKirujski mrtvi niso postavka, ki jo lahko prestavite samo zato, ker je vaša modra črta ravna.

Venn je obrnil stran. Nadzorna soba bi za petindvajset let pripadla družbi Cadran Systems, katere plošče bi ministrstvo lahko pravočasno nabavilo.

AdaezeNe.

Belu varnosti tal pod svojimi hišami ne bo skril za geslo podjetja in tega imenoval varnost.

Dodatek o odvodnjavanju je sekal kamnit jarek, ki so ga prebivalci Save ročno zgradili po zadnji mokri sezoni. Glavni inženir Lio Mensah ga je označil za neobloženega, nepravilnega in premajhnega za načrtovano neurje. Glede velikosti je imel prav.

AdaezeNe. Sedem let so merili vsak izvir. Vaša raziskava njihovo delo imenuje ovira, ker se je začela po tem, ko so ga dokončali.

IlluminaraSo to tri zavrnitve ali tri zahteve, ki jih načrt ni izpolnil?

Direktor Miro VennUčinek je enak. Izgubili bomo edini paket, ki lahko ta teden prestane revizijo.

Illuminara je zaprla modro projekcijo, preden je njena eleganca s ponavljanjem postala argument.

IlluminaraDajte mi meritve prebivalcev, bolnišnične podatke o vodi in enaindvajset ur. Če je jarek krajevni odtok, ostaja vaša pregrada najhitrejša rešitev. Če odvaja pobočje, smo hrbtenico razglasili za oviro.

02 · Četrta vrstica

Okrožje Sava, jarek po plastnici · 1. dan, 09:30

Jarek je segal do kolen, bil obložen z neusklajenim kamenjem in zavit okoli korenin kruhovca. Adaeze je po njem hodila s Kemi Sol, zidarko, ki je označila prvi izvir, medtem ko je Mensahova ekipa nad njim in pod njim postavila devet piezometrov.

Kemi SolNapolni se pod rdečo hišo, nato tukaj in potem pri šolskem ovinku. Nikoli v nasprotni smeri.

Glavni inženir Lio MensahGlobina ni izvor. Puščajoči bolnišnični vod bi lahko ustvaril isto zaporedje.

IlluminaraPotem preizkusimo oba vzroka. Obdelana voda vsebuje klorid. Voda iz pobočja vsebuje železo iz zgornjega bazalta.

Na kamen je zapisala dve tekmujoči razlagi in napoved, ki jo mora vsaka izpolniti pri vseh devetih vrtinah.

Glavni inženir Lio MensahKaj pa, če ne preživi nobena?

IlluminaraČetrta vrstica se glasi »ne vemo« in tri okrožja ne bodo gradila na njej.

Ob 10:06 so se tri kirujske gladine dvignile po vrsti. Osem minut pozneje se je mokra črta pod rdečo hišo dvignila za eno kamnito vrsto, nato še ob šesti vrtini. Gladina pri šolskem ovinku je ostala nespremenjena, medtem ko je zid med njim in šesto vrtino potemnel. Ko je Kemi odprla jarek, so se zgornje gladine in mokre vrste znižale v istem zaporedju.

Illuminara je čase s kredo zapisala na zid. Manjkajoča količina je bila voda, ne obremenitev, in iz merjene poti je izginila nekje med šesto vrtino in ovinkom. Ta odsek je potekal pod belujsko pralnico.

Kemi je odprla sedem zvezkov, za vsako mokro sezono druge barve. Bolnišnični vod je bil dvakrat zaprt; zaporedje od rdeče hiše do šole se je nadaljevalo. Vsak dvig tlaka je tudi za približno devetdeset minut prehitel premik najbližjega označevalca pobočja.

Kemi SolUradniki sprašujejo, ali je dovolj velik. Nihče ne vpraša, zakaj je tukaj.

IlluminaraTu se stikajo tri poti podtalnice. Grlo je preozko, zbiralnik pa je resničen. Najprej odvedimo vodo s pobočja; nato podprimo, kar ostane.

Grla proti Kiruju ni bilo mogoče razširiti, ne da bi se približali grobovom. Illuminara je pokazala proti cesti.

IlluminaraZdaj ugotovimo, ali ga lahko poglobimo v drugo smer.

03 · Enaindvajset ur

Pobočje Aruwa in strojnica bolnišnice St. Orra · 1. dan, 11:00 do 2. dan, 05:00

Bolnišnica je ločila zgornji vod. Nobena vrtina ni pokazala njegove kloridne sledi; železo se je pahljačasto širilo iz bazalta. Mensah je opustil razlago o puščajočem vodu, ne pa tudi ugovora, da bi regionalno hrbtenico naredili iz vaškega jarka.

Opoldne je Kemi nad Kirujem spustila odmerjeni sledilnik. Srednje vrtine bi se morale odzvati po vrsti, šolski ovinek pa zadnji. Če bi se voda razpršila ali obšla jarek, bi zamisel o vmesnikih propadla, še preden bi jo kdo podpisal.

Dve srednji vrtini sta se odzvali. Belujska vrtina se ni.

Direktor Miro VennEna nema vrtina je dovolj. Trije izvajalci bodo krivili drug drugega, medtem ko bo bolnišnica drsela.

Illuminara je sledila odseku podtalnice, ki ga je označila s kredo, do tal pralnice. Adaeze je pogledala staro brazgotino odtoka in se spomnila, da je tam nekoč stal zbiralnik, ki so ga uporabljali med stavko medicinskih sester.

Kemi SolNjegova glinena cev je bila zatesnjena, preden sem prevzela jarek.

AdaezeMoja mati je po tem črpala vodo iz njegovega preliva.

Preden so premaknili en sam senzor, je Mensah zapisal preizkus veje: najprej se mora odzvati preliv, nato začasna sonda pod cevjo, nema vrtina mora ostati nespremenjena, šolski ovinek pa se mora dvigniti zadnji. Če bi se ovinek dvignil pred sondo ali bi se pojavil klorid, bi bila veja napačna.

Glavni inženir Lio MensahZbiralnika ne sprejmem, dokler ne držijo vse štiri vrstice.

Obcestni jašek je razkril, da bazalt dovolj zgodaj pada, da je mogoče vgraditi pokrit prepust z dvakratnikom izmerjenega največjega pretoka jarka. Po poskusni obremenitvi je po posedanju mokre podlage ostalo šestnajst odstotkov rezerve.

04 · En paket

Revizijska dvorana ministrstva · 2. dan, 09:00

Venn jim je dal devetdeset minut. Zakon o izrednih razmerah je sprostil denar za en paket, enega odgovornega integratorja in en prevzemni preizkus.

Adaeze se je podpisala pod tri zahteve in mesto predsedujoče spojem sprejela samo do dežja. Venn se je podpisal zadnji. En paket je šel v razpis ob 10:27. V njem ni bilo enega samega zidu.

05 · Spoji

Pobočje Aruwa · 2. do 11. dan

Najprej so vgradili obcestni prepust. Illuminara je držala izpostavljeno pot obremenitve, medtem ko je ekipa nameščala drugi lok. Izpustila jo je po osemintridesetih minutah, preden bi malta v spoj zaklenila skrito odvisnost; lok je moral pokazati, da se lahko nosi sam. Mensah je ustavil delo, ko je prvi sloj podlage presegel mejo posedanja. Kemijina ekipa ga je zgradila na novo.

Kiru je svoj opornik ukrivil okoli pokopališča. Belu je na feritna rebra namestil dvanajst javnih plošč, vsako s fizičnim ključem. Sava je zabila terasasta sidra in namestila odstranljive zapornice povsod, kjer se je terasa stikala s starim jarkom.

Vsak spoj je potreboval tri podpise: ministrskega inšpektorja, okrožnega operaterja in sosednje ekipe. Med preizkusom šeste plošče je Kemi zaprla spodnjo zapornico. Kazalec prenosa se je dvignil nad osem in se ustavil pri enajstih odstotkih proti Kiruju.

Glavni inženir Lio MensahPlošča izpolnjuje lastno specifikacijo. Spoj je ne.

Sami DaroZadrži zapornico tam. Spremeni kot, ne odčitka.

AdaezeAli ga lahko okrožja izklopijo?

Sami DaroV naši pisarni. Neobdelani zapisi ostanejo naši.

06 · Dež

Bolnišnica St. Orra in pobočje Aruwa · 12. dan, 03:20 do 18:40

Dež je prišel tri ure prezgodaj in močnejši od napovedi. Piezometri so se dvignili; devetdeset minut pozneje so se odzvali označevalci pobočja. Voda je pri rdeči hiši vstopila v savski jarek in v rjavi kopreni udarila ob cestni prepust. Grlo je zdržalo.

A ministry's one elegant system is refused three times, and each refusal becomes an engineering requirement - a village trench read as the hill's real drain, a standard with a pin built to break, a key left in a district's hand - so a hospital stays open on a moving hill without a grave moved or a neighbour dragged down.

Forty-one children cough every Sunday night in a mountain town that has spent five weeks blaming its doctors and its church, and nobody has asked which bell, which room, or what changed last winter.

01 · Forty-One Notebooks

Children's clinic, Ostrava Vell · Monday, 07:40

Ostrava Vell was a mountain town of four thousand people, one church with a tower too large for it, and, since the second week of September, forty-one children who coughed in the evenings.

Dr. Ilse Varga had taped her spirometry curves to the examination-room wall, one line to a child. Every line sagged on Sunday night and climbed back by Thursday, forty-one small tides.

Ilse VargaCultures, PCR, serology, three rounds. There is nothing in any of them. No virus I know keeps a calendar.

Judit Moravec, who chaired the town council, had come in with her coat on. Father Matej Hroch of St. Wenzel stood by the door with his hands in his sleeves.

Judit MoravecThe council wants the school shut on Wednesday. A closed school is a thing I can actually do. Tell me what else I can do by Wednesday.

Matej HrochWhile you look for something to shut, leave the bells out of it. This town blamed them for the hail and the winter the cows failed. They were innocent every time.

Illuminara stood before the curves, then before the map beside them, where each child was a pin in the street they lived on and the pins thickened toward the church.

IlluminaraEveryone has plotted the children by where they live. Has anyone plotted them by where they sleep?

Ilse VargaWhere they sleep is where they live.

IlluminaraUsually.

Nives Hadzic had come in with her coat still buttoned. She held out a school exercise book, soft at the corners.

Nives HadzicForty-one mothers, forty-one notebooks. I write down every cough, the hour, and where she slept that night. And Lenka does not fit. We are out on Spindle Road, past the cemetery, the farthest house from the tower there is. She coughs on Sundays like the rest of them.

Ilse VargaI set Lenka aside as an outlier.

Illuminara turned the pages. Saturday: to Baba's on Cooper's Lane. Sunday: home at five. Sunday night: coughing, two hours.

IlluminaraCooper's Lane is right under the tower. Then she is not an outlier. She is the one child you have who proves something. The cough follows the child and not the address, so it is not a street, and probably not a germ going door to door. It is a room she slept in, and the room has a clock.

The doctors had asked what was in the children. Nobody had asked what was in the rooms.

IlluminaraTell me where each of them slept on Saturday night.

02 · Saint's Flour

St. Wenzel's tower, ringing chamber · Monday, 10:15

Dana Kral had pulled the bells of St. Wenzel for thirty-eight years, as her husband had before her, and she watched the stranger look at the ropes instead of the bells and made ready to be annoyed.

IlluminaraI have one question, and I think nobody has asked it. Which bell is the heaviest, and when is it rung?

Dana KralEverybody asks which is loudest.

IlluminaraI am not asking about loud.

Dana KralOld Wenzel, two tonnes and a hundred kilos. Four of us swing him, Sundays and feast days only. The little ones go from the keyboard, and the hour bells strike by the clock every day.

Matej HrochThere, you see. The hour bells strike every day and nobody coughs on a Tuesday.

IlluminaraI agree. So it is not the bells. It may be one bell, on one day.

She asked for a single stroke of the old bell. Hroch looked a long time at the rope, and allowed exactly one. Dana and three ringers swung Old Wenzel up, and Illuminara went down and stood on the flagstones at the west wall.

The stroke came through the tower like a blow to the bottom of a chair. The tower pressed its weight into the stone, the stone passed it down, and she read where the paths ran. Under the west wall they stopped. There the rock carried nothing and only hung, a long emptiness with a thin roof, and it answered the stroke the way a drumhead answers a palm.

Something down there rings.

IlluminaraUnder this wall there is a hollow, wide and shallow. When Old Wenzel strikes, its ceiling moves.

Matej HrochThe tower stands on rock.

Dana KralIt stands on the lip of the old adit. The miners' air shaft, bricked and boarded before my grandmother's time. Mind the floor by the lectern, it is hollow.

She pushed back her sleeve. Along the dark wool lay a fine white powder, like flour.

Dana KralSaint's flour. It comes up between the boards on every feast day. My grandmother said it was Wenzel blessing our hands.

IlluminaraThen it is not new. Something else is.

Emil RaskI can tell you what is new.

The chimney sweep had come up the stairs behind them with his apprentice and a bag of rods. He was sixty-eight and filled the doorway.

Emil RaskLast winter's grant. I did sixty-three chimneys for it in the old quarter. New stoves, sealed windows, no draught, less coal. A house with its windows shut drinks from its cellar.

03 · Two Mouths

Cooper's Lane, cellars of the old quarter · Tuesday, 14:00

Emil Rask had one rule for entering a cellar and he gave it on every doorstep: the tenant says yes, or the rods stay in the bag.

Eleven of the twelve said yes. Alois Fenner, at number nine, stood in his doorway with his arms folded.

Alois FennerMy father's cellar and his father's. Nobody counts my air.

Emil RaskThen I cannot map it, Alois. Not without you.

Alois FennerThen don't.

Illuminara could have found the mouth of that cellar in half a minute. She looked at the folded arms and left it unread. The map would have a gap in it.

In Baba Hadzic's cellar the apprentice, Tilo, who was sixteen and had been told to say nothing, held a smoke pencil to the wall by the coal bin. The thread of smoke leaned toward a bricked arch behind it, where the mortar was thin enough to feel a cold breath through.

TiloIt is pulling in. All of it.

The sweep took the pencil to a grating in the cellar's other wall. The smoke leaned that way too.

Emil RaskTwo mouths. Don't you tell me it is one. The arch feeds this room, and so does the street.

IlluminaraI won't. The street air should be nearly clean and the arch should not, but I cannot claim either until something counts them.

Ilse Varga had arrived with three laser dust counters in a padded case.

Ilse VargaNobody says the word silica in my clinic until a counter says particles.

IlluminaraAgreed. Then a test that can lose. Wednesday at three, when no one is baking and no one is at church. Counters in Baba Hadzic's cellar, the school and down the lane. Ten minutes of the small bells. Then Old Wenzel alone, for ten.

IlluminaraIf the school's counter climbs with Baba's, the dust is everywhere and I am wrong. If the small bells raise Baba's, it is the tower and not the shaft. If Baba's has not at least quadrupled within twenty minutes of the first stroke, I am wrong a third way.

Ilse VargaAnd if you are right, you still do not know what the dust is.

IlluminaraNo. That needs a lab.

Emil RaskAnd I want the grating counted by itself. A counter in the pipe.

IlluminaraYou shall have one.

04 · Wednesday, Out of Season

St. Wenzel's tower and three cellars · Wednesday, 15:00

Nobody could order Old Wenzel rung. Four ringers swung him by their own wish or not at all, and the wish was Dana Kral's.

Dana KralI will ring him on a Wednesday, which I have never done, for ten minutes, which I have never wanted. One telephone call from the clinic with a child's name in it, and I stop on the spot, whatever is on your counters.

Matej HrochAnd I will stand in my tower and watch you do it.

The mothers had decided that no child should be in the old quarter's cellars that afternoon. Ilse Varga read the counters over the telephone from the clinic.

Ilse VargaBaseline, all three: Baba Hadzic's twenty-two, the school nineteen, Cooper's Lane twenty-four. Stoves lit, as on any weekday. Small bells, now.

The five small bells chimed for ten minutes, bright and a little silly.

Ilse VargaTwenty-one. Twenty. Twenty-four. Nothing.

IlluminaraThe small ones are innocent. Dana.

Old Wenzel went up from rest and spoke. The note was lower than anything the ear could hold. It lived in the soles of the feet.

Ilse VargaMinute four. Baba Hadzic's thirty-one. School nineteen.

Between the boards the saint's flour rose in a thin white breath. Dana let the rope settle at ten minutes, as bargained, but the dust in the lane was still on its way, and the counters kept climbing.

Ilse VargaMinute fourteen. A hundred and ninety. School nineteen. Cooper's Lane a hundred and twelve. The pipe from the street grating, twenty-six.

The arch had fed that cellar nearly nine times its ordinary dust, and the street had hardly stirred it.

Matej HrochIt may be my tower's own stone. Limestone dusts. Pigeons. I will not be told it is the shaft until somebody looks at the dust itself.

IlluminaraThat is the right objection.

Ilse VargaThe tower is limestone, and limestone will not hurt a child's lung. Quartz will. If I find quartz in this, it is not your tower. If I find lime and pigeon, I will tell the council the bells were blamed wrongly again, Father, and I will say it from your pulpit if you let me.

Matej HrochI will let you.

05 · One Course of Brick

The old air shaft and the adit beneath the west wall · Thursday, 06:00

Hroch had allowed one course of brick to be lifted from the tower floor, and had asked that it be put back. Under it a shaft a metre wide, plastered smooth, fell into the dark. Emil Rask had put a torch on the timbers below.

Emil RaskThat roof has been rotting since my grandfather's day. Anything that goes down there goes on a rope, and I would be burying it.

IlluminaraI do not need the rope. I do need you on the cable, to read me the counter on my lanyard every ten minutes. If the roof comes down, do not dig. Wait. I will be a while, and I will come back.

She went down into a dark that was a kind of information. The gallery ran a hundred and forty metres under Cooper's Lane, its roof lined with lime plaster and sharp white sand that in places had come away from the rock and hung in sheets. On the floor lay three centimetres of dust the colour of flour. Where she stepped it rose and stayed in the air like a held breath.

IlluminaraEleven hundred where I stand. The arch you smoked is sixty-two metres east. The street grating's branch joins at forty metres and its air is clean, and it carries about a tenth of it, as you said. I will say so at the table.

She took three samples in glass: plaster, floor dust, and a flake of the tower's own limestone. It would have been easy to feel certain. She made herself wait for the lab.

One thing she had not expected: the bell arrived in the gallery as pressure. Every stroke pumped the long tunnel like a bellows, and each pump drove the dust east along the floor toward the arch.

IlluminaraEmil. If you plug that arch, the plug needs a breather: a pipe to the open air, far from any window. Otherwise the bell will press the dust through the old mortar around whatever you build, like water through a sponge.

Emil RaskThat is what a chimney sweep is for, miss. I would have said so in the next minute.

IlluminaraSay it in this one.

Emil RaskA pipe along the cemetery wall, to a stub chimney above the roofline. Thirty metres. Tilo can lay it by Saturday.

Then she worked. The tunnel was too long and too rotten to save in a morning. She read where the plaster would let go first, under the bell's footprint, and there she sprayed a lime-and-casein binder from the hose Tilo fed down the shaft, a skin that would hold until a proper crew came. Eleven metres. It took four hours.

IlluminaraA hundred and twenty-nine metres remain untouched. The worst of it is covered. It is not all of it. I want that written down.

Emil RaskIt is written.

The lab result reached the clinic on Friday morning.

Ilse VargaAngular quartz, three to eight microns, in a lime binder. The same as your gallery plaster. No quartz in the tower limestone. No pigeon. Father, your stone is clean.

06 · The Full Peal

Baba Hadzic's kitchen and the old quarter · Friday, 15:00 to Sunday, 11:00

On Friday Ilse laid the forty-one cards on Baba Hadzic's kitchen table, and Nives, who had written them, moved them about like a woman dealing patience.

Ilse VargaThirty-one of the forty-one slept on Saturday night, or spent Sunday morning, in a room with a mouth to the gallery. Ten did not, and I will not make them fit. Of the fifty-eight in the same classes who do not cough, six were in such rooms: four with grandmothers who air the house all day, and two I cannot explain.

IlluminaraThen what you hold is a strong trigger in the connected rooms. It is not the whole cohort, and it is not a disease.

Ilse VargaI will say exactly that, and not silicosis, for a child who has coughed five Sundays. And if a Sunday comes when the counters stay low and the coughs come anyway, we begin again, and I tell the council so.

Tilo laid the breather pipe along the cemetery wall on Saturday, and Rask's lime brick went into the arch behind Baba's coal bin. Nobody would sleep in a connected room until the plug had been rung against. By seven the mothers had every child in the schoolhouse hall, and counters stood in six consenting cellars and in the mouth of the new pipe.

Ilse VargaForty in any cellar, at any minute of the twenty, and the rope comes down. Nobody sleeps in a connected room on the strength of the minute the bell stops. Wednesday taught us that. The number is mine. The rope is Dana's.

Dana KralI will drop it on your number or on my own ears.

Old Wenzel went up at three-quarter swing, to an empty street, for ten minutes. Tilo's smoke pencil leaned along the cemetery wall, up, and out into the dark.

Ilse VargaMinute ten. Baba Hadzic's twenty-six. The lane twenty-four. The others twenty to twenty-eight. The school nineteen. The stub chimney, six hundred and forty.

The rope had settled at ten, as bargained. Nobody moved. Wednesday's dust had needed four more minutes to cross the lane, and the counters still had ten left to read.

Ilse VargaMinute fourteen. The highest cellar in the old quarter is thirty-one, at number four. Baba Hadzic's twenty-nine.

Ilse VargaMinute twenty. Thirty-one has fallen to twenty-seven. Baba's twenty-four. Nothing has touched forty at any minute, and the pipe is still carrying it up and out.

Emil RaskThe dust went where the pipe led. And number nine is not in this book. Alois never said yes, so he goes down as unverified.

Alois Fenner had gone down his own cellar steps with one of Ilse's spare counters, alone, and nobody followed him. He came up after ten minutes and read it aloud to the street, to nobody.

Alois FennerTwenty-three.

Ilse VargaUnder forty through the whole window, not only at the stop. Then the children may sleep where they have always slept, and the rule stays on the wall.

The children went to their beds after that, Lenka Hadzic to Baba's, as on every Saturday of her life. On Sunday at eleven Old Wenzel spoke again, and the people in the piazza stopped with their faces lifted, because the old note was in their feet.

Dana KralThree-quarter swing, until the gallery is relined. Seventy strokes and not ninety. I will miss the old swing. The bell will not mind.

Judit MoravecEmil reads the arch counter every second Friday and after every feast. Forty in an occupied cellar and Dana goes to the small bells until Ilse has read it again. The council pays the relining from the amended grant, done by the first of April, before the thaw loads the roof. The school stays open. I would like it minuted that I was told it would.

Matej HrochThe parish pays for the cap on the shaft. And no stove goes into a house in this town again until Emil has put a smoke pencil to its cellar.

No white breath rose between the boards. Dana looked at her sleeve, clean to the elbow.

Dana KralI miss it.

IlluminaraKeep a pinch in a jar. It is a record now, not a blessing.

Ilse took the spirometer to Cooper's Lane that evening and again on Monday at half past seven, and Lenka's line did not sag. She would take it on four more Sundays, with Nives's cards beside it.

Nives opened the exercise book to the last page. She wrote the day, the hour, and under them what she had waited five weeks to write.

Sunday night: Lenka asleep. No cough.

Under it, because Ilse had asked for five, she wrote the number 1.

Enainštirideset otrok vsako nedeljo zvečer kašlja v gorskem mestu, ki že pet tednov krivi svoje zdravnike in cerkev, nihče pa ni vprašal, kateri zvon, katera soba ali kaj se je spremenilo prejšnjo zimo.

01 · Enainštirideset zvezkov

Otroška klinika, Ostrava Vell · ponedeljek, 07:40

Ostrava Vell je bilo gorsko mesto s štiri tisoč prebivalci, eno cerkvijo s prevelikim zvonikom in, od drugega tedna septembra, enainštiridesetimi otroki, ki so ob večerih kašljali.

Dr. Ilse Varga je svoje spirometrijske krivulje prilepila na steno ordinacije, po eno črto za vsakega otroka. Vsaka črta se je v nedeljo zvečer povesila in se do četrtka spet dvignila, enainštirideset majhnih plim.

Ilse VargaKulture, PCR, serologija, trije krogi. V nobenem ni ničesar. Noben virus, ki ga poznam, se ne ravna po koledarju.

Judit Moravec, predsednica mestnega sveta, je prišla kar v plašču. Oče Matej Hroch iz cerkve sv. Wenzla je stal pri vratih z rokami v rokavih.

Judit MoravecSvet želi v sredo zapreti šolo. Zaprta šola je nekaj, kar dejansko lahko naredim. Povejte mi, kaj drugega lahko naredim do srede.

Matej HrochKo iščete nekaj, kar bi zaprli, pustite zvonove pri miru. To mesto jih je krivilo za točo in za zimo, ko so krave odpovedale. Vsakič so bili nedolžni.

Illuminara je stopila pred krivulje, nato pred zemljevid ob njih, na katerem je bil vsak otrok bucika v ulici, kjer je živel, bucike pa so se gostile proti cerkvi.

IlluminaraVsi ste otroke razporedili po kraju, kjer živijo. Jih je kdo razporedil po kraju, kjer spijo?

Ilse VargaKjer spijo, tam živijo.

IlluminaraNavadno.

Nives Hadzic je prišla s še vedno zapetim plaščem. Ponudila je šolski zvezek z obrabljenimi vogali.

Nives HadzicEnainštirideset mater, enainštirideset zvezkov. Zapišem vsak kašelj, uro in kraj, kjer je tisto noč spala. Lenka pa ne sodi zraven. Smo na Vretenovi cesti, za pokopališčem, v najbolj oddaljeni hiši od zvonika. Ob nedeljah kašlja kakor vsi drugi.

Ilse VargaLenko sem izločila kot osamelca.

Illuminara je obračala strani. Sobota: pri babici v Sodarski ulici. Nedelja: domov ob petih. Nedelja zvečer: kašelj, dve uri.

IlluminaraSodarska ulica je tik pod zvonikom. Potem ni osamelec. Je edini otrok, ki ga imate in nekaj dokazuje. Kašelj sledi otroku, ne naslovu, zato ni ulica in verjetno tudi ne klica, ki hodi od vrat do vrat. Gre za sobo, v kateri je spala, ta soba pa ima uro.

Zdravniki so spraševali, kaj je v otrocih. Nihče ni vprašal, kaj je v sobah.

IlluminaraPovejte mi, kje je vsak od njih spal v soboto zvečer.

02 · Svetnikova moka

Zvonik sv. Wenzla, zvonilnica · ponedeljek, 10:15

Dana Kral je zvonove sv. Wenzla vlekla osemintrideset let, pred njo pa njen mož, in ko je opazovala tujko, ki je gledala vrvi namesto zvonov, se je pripravila, da jo bo razjezila.

IlluminaraImam eno vprašanje in mislim, da ga ni postavil še nihče. Kateri zvon je najtežji in kdaj zvoni?

Dana KralVsi sprašujejo, kateri je najglasnejši.

IlluminaraNe sprašujem o glasnosti.

Dana KralStari Wenzel, dve toni in sto kilogramov. Štirje ga zagugamo, samo ob nedeljah in praznikih. Majhni se oglašajo s tipkovnice, urni zvonovi pa vsak dan udarjajo po uri.

Matej HrochVidite. Urni zvonovi udarjajo vsak dan, pa ob torkih nihče ne kašlja.

IlluminaraStrinjam se. Torej ne gre za zvonove. Morda gre za en zvon, enega dne.

Prosila je za en sam udarec starega zvona. Hroch je dolgo gledal vrv in dovolil natanko enega. Dana in trije zvonarji so Starega Wenzla zagugali navzgor, Illuminara pa je šla dol in obstala na kamnitih ploščah ob zahodni steni.

Udarec je šel skozi zvonik kakor sunek v dno stola. Zvonik je svojo težo pritisnil v kamen, kamen jo je poslal navzdol in ona je prebrala, kod tečejo poti. Pod zahodno steno so se ustavile. Tam skala ni nosila ničesar, le visela je, dolga praznina s tankim stropom, in udarcu je odgovorila kakor opna bobna dlani.

IlluminaraPod to steno je široka, plitva votlina. Ko Stari Wenzel udari, se njen strop premakne.

Matej HrochZvonik stoji na skali.

Dana KralStoji na robu starega rova. Rudarski zračnik, zazidan in zabit z deskami še pred časom moje babice. Pazite na tla pri govorniškem pultu, votla so.

Potegnila si je rokav nazaj. Na temni volni je ležal droben bel prah, podoben moki.

Dana KralSvetnikova moka. Ob vsakem prazniku pride med deskami. Moja babica je pravila, da Wenzel blagoslavlja naše roke.

Claude — A smart, humane procedural: the tie-book deduction, sealed prediction and community-led fixes reward idea-loving readers, and the ending lands gently. A floating market of twelve hundred households has thirty days to meet a sanitation law it genuinely breaks, and the plan that would save it is wrong in the one way only Wren could see.

01 · The Clean Plan

Harbour Office quay, Sorrel Water · Day 3 of 30, 08:10

The Order was fourteen pages long and gave thirty days, and on the third morning Illuminara laid her answer across the Harbour Office counter on a single sheet.

Twelve hundred boat-households lived on Kettle Market. The Harbourmaster's Sanitation Order No. 14 said that after the fifteenth of November none of them could go on discharging into Sorrel Water, and the August samples had shown the Order was right. Illuminara's sheet showed a licensed pump-out barge, six fixed stops, a sensor in every tank and one monthly bill.

Cedric AldanaIt is the cleanest compliance plan anyone has put in front of me. Every vessel metered, every pump-out logged. I could sign it on a Friday.

Wren Odira came up the quay steps with smoke in her coat and river mud to the knee. She had spent three weeks sleeping on other people's decks. She read the sheet standing, twice, and set it down.

Wren OdiraIt will fail.

IlluminaraTell me where it breaks first.

Wren OdiraWherever the barge is when the string has moved. Kettle doesn't sit at six stops. It re-rafts on every ebb, and boats slide to be near the boats they owe. Your stop six holds a hundred and forty hulls on Monday and sixty on Thursday. And you meter the tank. Whoever pays by the tank learns to keep it half empty and the hose long.

IlluminaraA meter that pays a family to leave the harbour dirty. I did not model that.

Wren OdiraYou modelled a machine. It's a rumour with a rota.

Illuminara did not defend the sheet. Wren has the shape of it. I do not yet have one fact worth more than her three weeks.

IlluminaraThen something is already working. In August the water was bad, not lethal, and Kettle has lived on it for thirty years. Who keeps the record of how?

Wren OdiraThere's a book.

Cedric AldanaThe Order wants a record for each vessel. A book is not a record.

He had said wants, not requires, and his hand had gone to the folded Order in his breast pocket before he said it. He is not refusing. He is telling me there is a door and that he may not open it.

IlluminaraIs there anything the Order wants more than a record for each vessel?

Cedric AldanaThere is something it will accept in its place. It needs three things at once: a lease, clean water at the outfall, and a signer I can inspect without warning. Kettle has never had a signer. If I name an arrangement and it fails, the failure is mine, so I do not name it.

IlluminaraYou have just named three things.

Cedric AldanaI have recited a regulation. That is allowed.

IlluminaraThen I would like to read the book before I tell you what a record is.

02 · The Tie-Book

Dock-mistress's counter, Kettle Market · Day 4, 06:00

Odalys Ferreira kept eleven volumes of the tie-book under her counter, in pencil, because ink runs on a wet quay. She laid the current one open and kept one hand flat on it.

Odalys FerreiraYou may read here. You may not copy a page, and if I see you reading a name you weren't asked to, I close it. This book is the only thing on the water that nobody has ever been able to buy.

Illuminara read for six hours. Selka carried Reed 3, 5, 7. Tues. Pump to Mill 2, from Gwil. Back by dusk. Tied: Aurelian, visitor. Line by line she let the entries fall into place as a graph: strings of rafted boats, carriers who wheeled the waste to the barge quay on days each string had chosen, pumps that travelled on a promise.

Nobody had written down a rota. The book was the rota, kept in the one language the market trusted.

IlluminaraEight boats in ten pass their waste to a carrier, the carrier takes it to the licensed quay, and the book shows eleven years of corrections. Thirty-eight strings, and none has ever asked the Harbourmaster for anything.

Wren OdiraI told you.

IlluminaraYou did, and you were right about the form. It fails in three places, and I find them by what the book leaves out. First, Reed Row. Tuesdays and Fridays, every week for eleven years. Not one carry on a Sunday.

Odalys FerreiraSunday is rest. Reed Row rests hardest of any string.

IlluminaraLook at the pump-loan pages. They list tank sizes, and Reed Row's are the smallest in the harbour. Look at the tie entries. Visitors raft on Reed Row on Fridays and Saturdays, and the Friday carry empties the tanks before they arrive. And here, on the margin of volume six: relief valve, Reed Row, mended. Four times in eleven years, always on a Monday.

Odalys FerreiraA valve is a valve.

IlluminaraA relief valve lifts when a tank is full and has nowhere to go. A full tank, a guest weekend, no carrier, and the Sunday ebb to carry it away.

Odalys looked at the margin as if someone else had written it. She said nothing, which in her was an answer.

IlluminaraSecond. Every pump loan in this volume names Gwil Anand, or Gwil's spare. One pump, one owner, and he is seventy-nine.

Odalys FerreiraGwil Anand will outlive the harbour.

IlluminaraThird, and it is the one the Inspector cares about. Nothing here lets the Order learn that any of this happened without opening the book to him.

Odalys FerreiraThat is what the book is for.

IlluminaraI know. I will come back to it. But the first two I only suspect, and half this harbour will say the water is dirty because of the tannery drain upstream.

Wren OdiraThey'll say it before you've finished the sentence.

IlluminaraThen we measure before anyone claims anything.

03 · Four Stations

Sorrel Water, on the ebb · Saturday 22:00 to Monday 06:00

Pia Zane, who ran the Inspector's small laboratory out of a van, set four sample stations: one above the market, one at the mouth of Reed Row, one mid-market, one below it. Illuminara told her which results would count against Illuminara.

She wrote the predictions on a card, sealed it, and gave it to Aldana before the first bottle was filled. If the Sunday gap was real, Reed Row's mouth would read at least five times its Saturday figure on the Sunday ebb while the station above the market stayed flat. If the tannery was the cause, the upstream station would be high on both nights and Reed Row would barely differ from it. If neither, everything would be flat and she would have been wrong about the book.

The card also said that the fourth station, below the market, was the outfall, and that the standard of two hundred applied there and nowhere else. Reed Row would read high at its own mouth. That was a diagnosis, not a pass.

Hesper QuillYou are sampling Reed Row on our day of rest. You will write our shame in water and hand it to the Inspector.

IlluminaraI am sampling the one place your string cannot answer for. If the number is bad on Sunday, it will be the first fact either of us has that is ours to fix.

Hesper QuillAnd if it's bad on Saturday too?

IlluminaraThen I am wrong, and the card says so.

Wren rowed the bottles herself, one leg of the route at a time. The numbers came back on Monday at six, in enterococci per hundred millilitres.

Pia ZaneSaturday ebb. Upstream, ninety. Reed Row, two hundred and ten. Mid-market, a hundred and eighty. Below the market, two hundred and sixty. Sunday ebb. Upstream, a hundred and ten. Reed Row, two thousand three hundred. Mid-market, six-forty. Below, seven hundred.

Wren OdiraUpstream is flat.

Pia ZaneThe tannery adds something after rain. It is not this.

IlluminaraThe tannery is a fact and it is not this fact. It will still be there when we finish, and I will say so to the council myself, so nobody has to hear it from the other side.

Hesper Quill read the Sunday line twice. She did not apologise and she did not argue. She asked what it would cost her people to stop it.

04 · Three Links

The council deck, Kettle Market · Day 9, 19:00

Thirty-eight string-wardens came, and Aldana came with his Order folded in his pocket. Illuminara had drawn only three additions to the system they already ran, and she said so first.

IlluminaraI am not bringing you a new system. You have one. I am bringing three links it is missing, and each of you can refuse yours.

Hesper QuillReed Row will carry its own Sunday. We won't do it under anybody's name in a book the Inspector reads.

Selka DunmoreTam and I will swap. I take Reed's Sunday and Reed takes my Monday. That's a trade among neighbours. It is not a rota for the Harbour Office.

IlluminaraThat is the first link, and it is better than mine. I had a paid Sunday carrier. Yours costs nothing and will outlast any budget.

Hesper QuillIt is not free. Tam works a day he has never worked, and Reed Row pays him for it out of our own purse. We will not ask the council for it.

Gwil AnandAnd you want my pump.

IlluminaraI want a second one, floated mid-market and lent only through you. If you fall ill, the loan does not stop. You stay the one people ask.

Gwil AnandIf I'm still the one they ask, I'll lend it.

Then Aldana unfolded the Order.

Cedric AldanaI must have a record for each vessel. I do not make the clause.

IlluminaraThen read the clause again, Inspector. Section six, paragraph b. An equivalent community arrangement may be certified in place of a vessel record if it is held under a lease, if the water at the outfall meets the standard, and if the body that signs can be inspected without notice. It asks for outcomes. It does not ask for names.

IlluminaraThe book is why the water is clean, and the book will not leave Odalys's counter. The council holds a lease. The water is measured at the three stations, once a month, on random days. And the body that signs is this council, whose only signed paper is a count of carries with no boat named, so that you can walk in unannounced and count the tickets.

Odalys FerreiraYou are telling me to hand the Harbourmaster a number and keep the book.

Illuminara let it stand. The vote was the council's. Thirty-one strings voted yes and seven voted no, and the minute recorded the seven refusals, to be read out again at every renewal. Neither she nor Wren could take it from the other.

The smokehouse Ember, tied at the east edge · Day 14, dusk

Torvald Beck's smoke-boat had been a ferry hull once, and no holding tank would fit it. Iliana Dross's Aurelian was registered upriver at Cress Market and had been in the tie-book as visitor fourteen times.

Torvald BeckI have read the plan. It was written for the boats that were already inside the book.

She turned to Wren, who had sat on Beck's deck three nights running and eaten his fish.

IlluminaraHesper has said yes to that, and I asked her last night. Beck, a sealed float-tank towed astern of Ember, nineteen hundred marks, built by Gwil's apprentice. It is not elegant. It would work.

Torvald BeckAnd my name stays out of the Reed Row sheet.

IlluminaraIt was never in it.

Torvald BeckThen the council can vote on the tank.

Iliana DrossI tie here eleven days a year. I will not be inspected for the other three hundred and fifty-four.

IlluminaraThen I will not ask you to be counted. A free rinse at the barge quay on any day you tie, with no entry in anyone's book. If the water reads clean in spring, you will know whose doing that was, and you can decide again.

Dross did not say yes. She weighed it the way a woman weighs a rope. In the morning the Aurelian had cast off for Cress Market, with a day-pass in her pocket and her reasons unrevised.
